articleTitle: Study an adaptive mean filtering method for differential SAR interferometry
abstract: Aiming at the problem that the traditional mean filtering algorithm has a fixed value in the filtering wind ow, which can not take into account the noise removal and phase information retention of the interferogram, this paper proposes a mean filtering algorithm based on the filtering factor. The algorithm uses the pseudo-coherent coefficient related to the noise distribution and terrain transformation and the two-dimensional Fourier transform spectrum energy to jointly construct the filtering factor. According to the filtering factor, the appropriate filtering window is allocated in different regions of the interferogram. Finally, the measured data are analyzed and verified. The results show that the method can effectively suppress the noise and maintain the phase information, and improve the quality of the interferogram.

articleTitle: A rapid assessment method for jamming situation threat based on signal-level
abstract: Active jamming with diverse types and variable parameters poses a significant threat to the operational effectiveness of modern radars. Accurately and rapidly characterizing jamming threat can provide guidance for radar anti-jamming. From the perspective of the radar anti-jamming closed-loop system, the paper extracts frequency domain features as threat indicators from two aspects: the difficulty of eliminating suppression jamming and the accuracy of deception jamming identification, assessing jamming threat based on the signal-level. Through a consistent simulation analysis of the proposed threat indicators and anti-jamming indicators, it has been quantitatively demonstrated that the threat indicators can represent the adverse effects of jamming on radar anti-jamming systems. Finally, the proposed method has been proven to be effective based on experimental data.

articleTitle: SFDFNet: single-path feature deep fusion network for fast semantic segmentation of SAR images in building areas
abstract: With the SAR satellites have gradually become one of the most important methods of Earth observation, rapid interpretation of SAR images has become particularly important. However, the unique imaging mechanism of SAR makes its interpretation very difficult. In this paper, we propose the SFDFNet, a deep learning-based fast segmentation method for SAR image buildings, to address the problem of difficult SAR image interpretation. A bottleneck layer of buffered large receptive field is designed in the downsampling process. The unique design of the number of channels reduces the amount of computation without affecting the extraction of information. Meanwhile, improving on the ECA module, a two-layer ECA module was proposed to increase the receptive field and improve the linear expression. Experiments show that the proposed network has excellent results in segmentation accuracy and inference speed.

articleTitle: A novel radar emitter fingerprint for multiple path propagation environment
abstract: Mining additional modulation information of signal propagation environment as a new fingerprint feature is more important for modern radar reconnaissance systems. This paper proposes a definition and processing method of a new radar emitter fingerprint from multiple path propagation environment, and demonstrates its application in an improved radar pulses deinterleaving task. For the fingerprint generation, the proposed method reconstructs a reference radar pulse by pulse description words (PDW) and correlate it to intercepted pulse sequence firstly. Then an adaptive threshold is utilized to pick out the main peaks belonging to the same radar. Next all the selected range profiles take a procedure of self-focusing and coherent accumulation among different pulses. Finally, propagation environment fingerprint (PEFP) is obtained after eliminating main-peak by CLEAN in the accumulated results. For the deinterleaving application, a sparse auto-encoder (AE) is used to extract high dimensional features from the generated PEFPs, then the features are combined into traditional PDW as extended features to implement an improved deinterleaving task. Simulation results verify the validity and effectiveness of the proposed fingerprint . The PEFP enhanced deinterleaving processing can improve the precision by 6% in non-cooperative conditions compared with traditional methods.

articleTitle: Open set target recognition based on multi-task compressed sensing using multi-view high range resolution profiles
abstract: This paper focuses on a specific application for a target recognition system. That is, the system input may be out-of-library from an unknown category and multiple observations can be obtained from a small angle interval. To efficiently utilize the multi-view samples for target identification in open-set situation, an open set recognition method using multi-view high range resolution profiles (HRRP) based on Multi-task Compressed Sensing (MtCS) is presented. First, the reconstruction errors of multi-view HRRPs on the over-completed dictionary are obtained by MtCS, and a modified metrics is constructed with the reconstruction error. Next, extreme value theory (EVT) is introduced to model the distribution of the metric s, and then the open-set recognition problem is transformed into a hypothesis test problem. The proposed method can effectively reject the out-of-library samples, and meanwhile exploit the prior information that the multiple observations are strong ly correlated to improve the recognition performance of samples from known targets. The efficiency of the propos ed method is identified through the recognition experiments on the HRRP data generated from MSTAR SAR chips.

articleTitle: Neural network-based self-interference cancellation method for in-band full-duplex system
abstract: In recent years, In-band Full-Duplex (IBFD) has garnered significant research attention in the fields of communications and sensing due to its unique ability to enhance spectral efficiency. However, the strong self-interference signals generated by the transmitter are billions of times stronger than the desired signals. The research and application of IBFD face unprecedented challenges considering radio impairments such as IQ imbalance, phase noise, Gaussian white noise, and power amplifier nonlinearity. To address this issue, this paper proposes a Multi-Domain Self-Interference Cancellation (MDSIC) method and analyzes its fundamental principles. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves approximately 100 dB of self-interference cancellation performance. Although the simulations are based on single-input-single-output (SISO) systems, the proposed MDSIC method can be extended to phased-array or multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) systems. Furthermore, the self-interference cancellation performance of different neural network structures is verified using experimental data. The analysis of the experimental data confirms that the proposed MDSIC method exhibits stronger applicability in suppressing self-interference in broadband signals compared to traditional methods.

articleTitle: Performance analysis of subarray-level STAP for space-based early warning radar
abstract: Compared to airborne early warning radar (AEWR), space-based early warning radar (SBEWR) holds advantages in detection coverage and warning duration. However, the clutter characteristics of SBEWR are more complicated due to factors such as high satellite velocity, long detection range, and Earth's rotation, making clutter suppression more challenging. The SBEWR array consists of numerous antenna elements to ensure sufficient power-aperture product, making it impractical to employ element-level space-time adaptive processing (STAP) methods for clutter suppression. Therefore, it is necessary to divide the array into subarrays before performing subarray-level STAP filtering. This paper focuses on investigating the clutter spectral characteristics of the overlapping uniform subarray and contiguous uniform subarray partitioning methods. A comparative analysis of the clutter suppression performance is conducted, along with an assessment of the achievable upper bound of minimum detectable velocity (MDV) for the above methods. Extensive experiments validate the superiority of contiguous subarray partitioning over the overlapping approach and the robustness of STAP performance of contiguous subarray in the presence of errors.

articleTitle: DST-Net: an algorithm based on multi-scale feature for ship target detection in SAR images
abstract: With the gradual widespread application of Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) images and the continuous development of deep learning, ship detection based on SAR image data has become a research hotspot. However, because the SAR image background is complex and the ship target scale is not uniform, resulting in the network cannot accurately extract the feature information, bringing about detection results of leakage and false detection. To address the above problem, an improved SAR image ship target detection algorithm DST-Net is proposed. Firstly, we adopt a Double Spatial Pyramid Pooling (DSPP) to enhance the ability of the backbone network to extract multi-scale features. Secondly, the S2 MLP Triplet Attention module (ST) is introduced to increase the diversity of features by performing sufficient spatial transformations on the feature map to make the features have better dependence on the spatial and channel dimensions. Experiments were conducted on two datasets, HRSID and SAR-Ship-Dataset, respectively, and the accuracies reached 94.00% and 93.00%, which are better than the detection algorithms at the current stage, proving the effectiveness and robustness of the DST-Net algorithm.

articleTitle: Improving performance with feature enhancement and ranking constraints for radar-based human activity recognition
abstract: Radar-based human activity recognition has been extensively studied using deep learning models. To better suit embedded devices, it is essential to design models that are small in size and computationally efficient. This research paper presents a lightweight model architecture specifically tailored for processing radar micro-Doppler spectrograms. The key contributions of this work include the introduction of a lightweight front-end that employs symmetric depthwise convolution and spectral pooling to enhance features and perform temporal downsampling. In our encoder design, we treat the spectrogram as a multidimensional temporal sequence and exclusively utilize 1D convolution in our model. Additionally, the paper introduces a two-branch temporal modeling module: one branch utilizes attentional LSTM to extract and summarize temporal features, while the other employs a 1D FCN to aggregate features along the temporal dimension. Furthermore, the paper applies ranking constraints to the output of the attentional LSTM, effectively leveraging temporal order information. Experimental results conducted on three HAR datasets validate the effectiveness of the proposed model, with significant performance improvements attributed to the spectral pooling layer. This highlights the importance of addressing temporal redundancy in spectrograms for improved recognition accuracy. The code is available at https://github.com/ZHOUYI1023/ConvLSTM-for-RadarHAR.

articleTitle: Multi-sensor track association and interrupted track association based on deep learning algorithms
abstract: As the radar detection environment of modern battlefield becomes more and more complex, the limitations of traditional radar multi-sensor correlation methods are gradually revealed. The traditional method of radar track correlation is difficult to deal with the environment with high target density and maintain high accuracy. The traditional method of interrupting track correlation is weak in maneuverability and depends on the construction of motion model. To solve these problems, a track association model based on twin neural network algorithm and an interrupted track association model based on depth time contrast algorithm are proposed in this study. The track association model uses bidirectional recurrent neural network with shared weights and interactive attention mechanism to process the feature information to obtain similarity vector, so as to realize the judgment of track association. The interrupted track association model, by extracting the time sequence feature vector of the old and new track, and calculating the similarity of the track depth feature vector, can obtain the similar situation vector of the old and new track, and then realize the correlation judgment of the interrupted track. The accuracy of track correlation model is 98.7%; The average error correlation rate of interrupted track association model is 0.57%. The average missing correlation ra te was 0.1%. The results of this study have certain value to the field of track association, and can be used as a technical reference for multi-sensor track association.

articleTitle: Classification of drones and birds based on integration of local and global features
abstract: Small drones and birds, as typical “low altitude, slow speed and small” (LSS) targets, exhibit a high degree of overlap in spatial position, flight speed, and radar echo amplitude, rendering them difficult to distinguish. However, in the face of the growing threat of drone targets, research on the classification and identification technology of them is necessary and urgent. This paper analyses the target characteristics of rotary-wing drones and birds, and sorts out the features that can be used for their classification. The trajectory, motion, and Radar Cross Section (RCS) features of the targets are extracted at both local and global trajectory levels, and a method for classifying drones and birds based on the integration of local and global features is proposed. Compared with previous methods, the local features extracted by this method more accurately describe the current state of the target. Additionally, some specific actions of drones are detected from a global perspective to improve the success rate of UAV identification. Finally, the effectiveness of this method is verified using real drone and bird targets data obtained from a phased array radar system. Experimental results demonstrate that the classification accuracy of this method surpasses 90%, indicating its superiority over other methods.

articleTitle: A modified strong tracking algorithm based on SRCKF for target tracking
abstract: Aiming at the tracking problem of strong maneuvering target, a modified strong tracking algorithm based on square root cubature Kalman filter (MST-SRCKF) is proposed in this paper. Based on traditional ST-SRCKF algorithm, a new calculation method of the fading factor is proposed, which comprehensively considers all measurement dimensions and reduces the occurrence of false alarm for the abrupt change of the target motion. Furthermore, Chi-square detection is introduced to improve the tracking accuracy when the target state is stable. For maneuvering target tracking case, MST-SRCKF is combined with the improved IMM (IIMM) and the MST-SRCKF-IIMM is given. The simulation results show that the tracking accuracy of the proposed algorithm is obviously improved compared with existing algorithms, and the extended algorithm also has better tracking performance in maneuver scene.

articleTitle: GRU-CNN-based extended Kalman tracking method for small bird targets on Lidar
abstract: Lidar-based tracking and surveillance of small birds is a new key technology for realizing bird monitoring and early warning in airports and the surrounding airspace. However, To the low sampling frequency of Lidar system introduce the problems of large targets tracking errors and low model adaptability, which is challenging to conventional model-driven methods under low sampling rate conditions. In this paper, we propose a GRU-CNN-based extended Kalman tracking method for small bird targets' tracking by fusing the predictive capability of deep learning networks for non-linear motions and the noise reduction capability of extended Kalman filtering. Through transforming the predictions generated by the deep learning network into an explicit state transfer model, the proposed approach establishes closed-loop iterations between prediction generated by GRU-CNN and estimation within the extended Kalman tracking method, and thus the proposed method effectively tracks non-linearly moving bird targets. Simulations on a publicly available pigeon flight trajectory dataset show that the proposed method outperforms traditional tracking algorithms at different sampling frequencies. Notably, our approach exhibits a remarkable improvement in tracking accuracy of approximately 20% at low sampling frequencies, outperforming existing methods.

articleTitle: Feature selection and target classification techniques in imbalanced samples
abstract: The growing issue of maritime security in China necessitates accurate classification and identification of sea surface targets, which is a prerequisite for maritime situation assessment. Ensemble learning methods are widely studied and appreciated for their efficient learning capabilities. However, the accuracy of target classification faces challenges when data samples are imbalanced, and the complexity of the model increases as the number of data features grows. This paper proposes a pre-feature selection technique and sets the model loss function based on class weights. By considering the sensitive matrix of attribute misclassification costs, an integrated framework is established for training the XGBoost model and optimal feature selection, thereby achieving effective target classification. The results of data processing validate the effectiveness of th e proposed method.

articleTitle: Ising formulation and recurrent algorithm for binary weight beamforming
abstract: Binary weight beamforming is a combinatorial optimization problem, where the amplitudes of the weighting vector are constrained by binary values of 0 and 1. It has been widely investigated in resource management of opportunistic array and antenna synthesis of sparse array, while great efforts have been made toward developing heuristic and intelligent algorithms. However, it is challenging for large-scale binary weight beamforming problem to be efficiently resolved by conventional electronic architectures due to its non-deterministic polynomial (NP) computational complexity. Here, we present Ising formulation of this problem. Mappings between the beamforming problems and interaction parameters of Ising spin glasses are deduced. For the first time, a recurrent approach to perform binary weight beamforming with Ising machine is proposed, which could potentially surpass the existed algorithms in execution speed if the Ising machine is efficiently implemented. We mathematically prove that the global optimum of beamforming can be reached with ideal Ising machines which reach ground states with near-unity probabilities. Furthermore, numerical simulation of Ising machine is performed employing simulated annealing method. The probabilities of finding global optimum with the simulated Ising machines are evaluated, while beamforming of random arrays with number of antennas ranging from 18 to 150 is studied.

articleTitle: Joint transmitter/receiver pair selection and power allocation strategy for multi-target tracking in netted radar system
abstract: In this paper, a joint transmitter/receiver pair selection and power allocation strategy is developed for multiple targets tracking in netted radar system. Each transmitting node in this system can simultaneously transmit multiple beams to illuminate different targets, and each receiving node can simultaneously receive and process echo signals reflected by different targets illuminated by all transmitting nodes. The key of this problem is to use optimization technology to select transmit ter/receiver pair and allocate transmit power with the aim of meeting desired multiple targets tracking performance. The predicted Posterior Cramer–Rao lower bound is derived, and subsequently utilized as the performance criterion for the multiple targets tracking. A fast two-step solution technique is proposed to deal with the constrained optimization problem. Simulation results verify the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm and the superiority of netted radar system.

articleTitle: GPR target recognition framework based on low-rank sparse decomposition and hyperbolic scanning
abstract: As a non-destructive detection technology, ground penetrating radar (GPR) has been widely used in the target detection of roads and walls. Strong clutter interference is an important obstacle to affect the accuracy of target recognition, and how to accurately extract the target from the GPR images is a challenging task. This paper presents a target identification framework for GPR. In this method, the low-rank sparse decomposition (LRSD) method is used to extract the target part from the radar image. This method uses the alternating direction multiplier method (ADMM) for iteration. The dictionary learning method uses the dictionary to further process the image with the downward opening. Finally, the hyperbolic point linearization method is used to identify the hyperbola. The proposed method achieves good results in the measured data.

articleTitle: Automatic modulation recognition based on SST and deep learning model
abstract: As the electromagnetic environment in battlefields becomes increasingly complex, automatic modulation recognition for noncooperation radiation source signal is becoming vital and challenging. Most previous works were more likely to cause low recognition accuracy with high computational complexity in low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), and only considered spatial or temporal attributes of signal which ignores the feature interaction. In this paper, we firstly apply synchrosqueezing transform (SST) to extract high resolution and robustness time-frequency feature as one of signal representation, and convert the signal into the in-phase/quadrature (I/Q) components as another signal representation, which enhances the diversity of signal representation. Then, we propose a deep learning model to achieve automatic recognition, which has two streams and each stream consists of the convolutional neural network (CNN), bistatic long short-term memory (BiLSTM) and temporal attention (TAT). It efficiently explores the feature from each signal representation and enhances the key features by the introduction of TAT, furthermore, it implements feature interaction to form a new feature matrix. Finally, experiments and analysis were conducted using the RadioML2016.10a dataset. The experimental results showed that compared to other algorithms, this method has higher robustness and perform better recognition accuracy under low SNR.

articleTitle: SAR image super-resolution and target detection closed-loop network with edge enhancement and feature feedback
abstract: Current super-resolution (SR) methods can effectively restore the global features, but these features may not be relevant to the detection task, which results in constrained improvements in detection results. Given the limitations of existing SR methods, in this paper, a novel SR and target detection closed-loop network based on edge enhancement and feature feedback is proposed. On one hand, a forward connection is established from the SR network to the detection network for a better detection result. Specially, to solve the problem of blurred contours in degraded synthetic aperture radar (SAR) images, an edge enhancement branch is introduced in SR network to provide abundant high-frequency edge information for reconstructed images. On the other hand, the feedback connection from the detection network to SR network transmits spatial and feature information about the target region. The SR network can generate detection-related features based on these feedback features. Extensive experiments on the SAR Ship Detection Dataset (SSDD) show that the proposed method can effectively improve the detection accuracy of degraded SAR images. The average precision is increased by 2.11%, 4.43%, and 5.10% at degradation factors of 4, 8, and 16, respectively.

articleTitle: An improved method for rockfall detection and tracking based on video stream
abstract: Rockfall events occur frequently in mountainous areas. To address the problems of missed detection, false detection, and trajectory interruption when using the deep learning-based online multiple object tracking methods to detect rockfalls, this paper proposes a rockfall detection and tracking method based on video streams. In the detection stage, three-frame difference method is utilized to obtain the moving targets from the video streams, and they are combined with the detection results of the rock detector obtained by the offline-trained YOLOX model. In the tracking stage, data association is firstly performed based on the rockfall detection results. For the existing trajectories that are not matched at the current moment, re-matching is performed by combining the moving object detection results to achieve accurate tracking of rockfalls. Simulations and field experiments prove that the detection method proposed in this paper can effectively separate the rockfalls in the video, and the detected rockfalls have high precision. Besides, it significantly improves the accuracy of rockfall tracking, effectively suppressing phenomena such as trajectory interruption during tracking.

articleTitle: Researches on polarimetric decomposition and 3DCNN for Arctic sea ice classification using Gaofen-3 fully polarimetric SAR data
abstract: Sea ice poses a significant safety hazard during polar navigation, and obtaining accurate sea ice charts is of great importance for safe polar navigation. In this study, we used fully polarimetric sea ice image data from the Gaofen-3(GF-3) satellite and extracted polarimetric features using various polarization decomposition methods. We combined these features with parameters such as backscattering coefficient intensity and incidence angle for classification. Inspired by the operational principles of 3D convolutional neural networks(3DCNN), we constructed a three-dimensional sea ice dataset suitable for 3DCNN to explore whether 3DCNN can capture more information in the "depth" dimension of the dataset and improve the final classification accuracy. We tested the classification performance using both 2D convolutional neural networks (2DCNN) and 3DCNN. The experimental results showed that, under the simple stacking of the bands, the classification performance of the 3DCNN model was comparable to that of the 2DCNN model. This suggests that 3DCNN can be applied to the field of sea ice classification.

articleTitle: A novel point cloud extraction and feature design approach for radar-based object classification
abstract: Radar-based object detection has been extensively studied, with many researchers employing deep learning models like PointNet for processing radar point clouds. However, a common challenge in this domain is dealing with sparse point clouds generated by commercial radar sensors. From a neural network perspective, managing redundant and noisy data is generally more feasible than handling sparse data. Some researchers have attempted to address this challenge by exploring the use of radar raw data, such as Range-Angle-Doppler (RAD) tensors, as input. However, RAD tensors are dense 3D tensors that demand significant memory and computational resources for storage and processing. In our study, we argue that the current point cloud representation is practical, but the point clouds generated by traditional detection pipelines tend to be overly sparse. To tackle these issues, we investigate point cloud extraction and feature design to better align with the requirements of deep learning models. Specifically, we propose a pipeline that employs binary segmentation for point extraction to minimize information loss. Additionally, we leverage local Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) information to assign weights to each point, effectively mitigating the impact of redundant and noisy points. Our experimental results, based on our dataset, demonstrate that using our feature set can significantly enhance the accuracy of the PointNet model without requiring modifications to the model's architecture.

articleTitle: Analysis of uncontrolled geometric positioning accuracy for L-band differential interferometric SAR satellite
abstract: The uncontrolled geometric positioning accuracy is a crucial factor affecting the application potential of L-Band Differential Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar satellite, commonly referred to as "L-SAR". This paper focuses on the research of geometric calibration and high-precision geometric positioning for L-SAR satellite. The Range-Doppler model has been iden- tified as a suitable choice for the geometric positioning of L-SAR satellite. By utilizing this model, various sources of errors that impact the geometric positioning accuracy can be effectively analysed and compensated, thus enhancing the uncontrolled geometric positioning accuracy of L-SAR satellite. Experimental results indicate that: (1) Irrespective of factors such as side-looking direction and ascending/descending orbits, geometric calibration of the L-SAR satellite was conducted using the pulse band width and pulse width as a grouping criterion. After removing the geometric positioning errors induced by orbital inac- curacies, the range error tends to be stable. The standard deviation of range delay about 80MHz/100us and 80MHz/90us of L-SAR satellite can be reduced by 74.8% and 56.2% respectively, compared to before the removal of orbital errors. (2) The geometric accuracy was evaluated using high-precision corner reflectors at calibration sites in Hami, Xinjiang, and California: the root mean square errors (RMSE) of positioning errors for L-SAR satellite about 80MHz/100us and 80MHz/90us have been reduced by 95.6% and 92.7% respectively, compared to before error compensation. This technology of error compensation employed for the L-SAR satellite enables geometric positioning accuracy that can reach, and potentially exceed, the threshold of 1.5 pixels.

articleTitle: Environmental information perception of lidar for autonomous vehicle navigation planning
abstract: Traditional lidar perception algorithms provide limited information and lack target-level details. Therefore, this paper proposes a method that integrates prior environmental information and real-time perception data to construct a local environment model, which guides vehicle navigation planning. Using prior environmental information, the height difference algorithm is employed to reduce the dimensionality of the 3D point cloud data and construct a 2D obstacle grid map. Furthermore, prior feasible regions are used to preprocess the point cloud information, enhancing the speed of map construction. Based on the grid map, a 2D obstacle detection and tracking module is formed, utilizing the distance threshold clustering algorithm, feature extraction, and ROI (Region of Interest) detection. The information generated by this module is incorporated into the grid map, and a perception map suitable for autonomous vehicle navigation and planning tasks is finally constructed. Through simulation and real vehicle experiment, it is confirmed that the algorithm proposed in this paper is capable of constructing the 2D obstacle grid map while ensuring real-time requirements, thereby providing sufficient perception information for navigation planning.

articleTitle: InSAR phase unwrapping method based on neural network and Nesterov accelerated gradient optimization
abstract: Synthetic Aperture Radar Interferometry (InSAR) is an important means of earth observation. It is a technology that can accurately measure the three-dimensional information of the surface. Therefore, it can be used to monitor small surface deformation, such as earthquakes, landslides, glacier movements, topographic mapping, urban land subsidence and other fields. The processing of the Phase Interference Graph is an important part of the data processing flow of the InSAR method. Phase unwrapping is a key link in the Phase Interference Graph processing. Only the accurate unwrapping of the Phase Interference Graph can restore the correct phase, thereby obtaining accurate surface deformation inversion results. However, the traditional phase unwrapping method has the disadvantage of relying on the phase continuity assumption. Using the neural network model to improve the phase unwrapping algorithm, efficient and accurate unwrapping results can be obtained. In this paper, a phase unwrapping method based on neural network and Nesterov accelerated gradient (NAG) algorithm is proposed. The dense connection network (DenseNet) is used to calculate the real phase, and then the NAG optimization algorithm and Smooth L1 loss function are used to correct the calculation results of the neural network to obtain accurate real phase data. Taking the Haerwusu coal mine area in Ordos City, Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region and the Daxing 'anling forest area as examples, good unwrapping results have been obtained. Using neural network to calculate the real phase has higher accuracy and robustness than traditional algorithms.

articleTitle: Comparative analysis of SAR ship detection methods based on deep learning
abstract: Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) is notable for its continuous observation capability, irrespective of the time of day. Advancements in SAR satellite technology have led to a surge in SAR image data, aiding in image interpretation. SAR-based ship detection is pivotal for traffic monitoring and fishery management, becoming a crucial aspect of SAR image interpretation. Despite some success with traditional image processing methods, several challenges remain unresolved. This article delves into six diverse mainstream deep learning models, evaluating their detection efficacy on SAR images, and conducting a thorough comparison and analysis to provide readers with a solid reference for model selection across varying scenarios. The conclusions drawn are as follows: the models 'Explore the limits of Visual representation at scAle using only publicly accessible data (EVA)' and the 'You Look Only Once (YOLO)' series networks demonstrate superior performance in SAR ship detection, with YOLOv8 standing out remarkably by achieving a precision rate exceeding 90%, while keeping the false alarm and miss rates within a 10% threshold. Conversely, Faster Region-Convolutional Neural Networks (Faster R-CNN) and Single Shot MultiBox Detector (SSD) exhibit subpar performance, with precision rates below 75% and a notable miss rate of 78.94% in SSD's case.

articleTitle: Robust low-rank matrix completion under generalized Gaussian mixture model with application to DoA estimation
abstract: This paper considers the problem of noisy low-rank matrix completion (LRMC), presenting a novel and robust LRMC approach that differs from classical methods reliant solely on Lp-norms for handling single noise distributions. Instead, we adopt a model that accounts for the noise using a Mixture of Generalized Gaussian (MoGG) distributions—in both the real and complex circularly symmetric cases—thus accommodating more intricate noise patterns. Our proposed method formulates the LRMC problem as the minimization of the negative log-likelihood coupled with a nuclear norm penalty, which is effectively addressed by the EM-ADMM algorithm devised in this paper. Moreover, the proposed complex-valued LRMC method is applied to tackle the Direction of Arrival (DoA) estimation with incomplete measurements. Specifically, we leverage the developed LRMC technique for imputation of the missing entries and then employ the MUSIC algorithm to estimate the angles of impinging signals. Finally, numerical examples are presented to show the performance improvement of our proposed method compared to some classical ones.

articleTitle: Research on ground clutter polarization suppression algorithm based on prior information
abstract: Low-altitude unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) targets are challenging to detect by radar due to their low flight altitude, which exposes them to strong interferences from complex ground clutter. To address this, this paper proposes a ground clutter polarization suppression method based on prior information, facilitating the effective detection of low-altitude UAV targets. Initially, the method establishes a clutter prior information database and a clutter map according to the actual rad ar application environment, classifying different types of clutter. This serves as the prior information for clutter, supporting detection in th e context of complex ground clutter backgrounds. Subsequently, a linear polarization filtering algorithm optimized based on maximizing the signal-to-clutter ratio (SCR) is proposed for specific clutter environments. A strong clutter point is selected from the clutter map, and the effectiveness of the algorithm proposed in this paper is analyzed and verified using real-world radar data collected from field measurements. The results indicate that the proposed algorithm improves the average signal-to-clutter ratio by 15.39 dB compared to single polarization channels. This method provides a reference for complex ground clutter polarization suppression and polarization detection.

articleTitle: A map construction and maintenance framework for long-term navigation based on LiDAR
abstract: We propose a method for constructing and maintaining a navigation map in dynamic environments using laser scan information. During long-term robot operation, changes in environmental information are unavoidable. Accurate map construction and real-time map updates are crucial for ensuring reliable autonomous navigation over an extended period. Moreover, the dynamic environmental information in the global map can adversely affect the accuracy of LiDAR-based simultaneous localization and mapping algorithms. Given the sparsity of real-time laser scan data in comparison to previous maps, this paper presents a map construction algorithm and a map update algorithm that utilize obstacle-level segmentation. These algorithms demonstrate improved noise filtering capabilities and dynamic information detection, thereby ensuring the accuracy and reliability of the navigation map. We evaluated our approach through experiments conducted in both virtual simulation and real-world physical environments. The results demonstrate its effectiveness in enhancing map construction and map update performance, as well as providing reliable map information for autonomous robot navigation.

articleTitle: A dynamic short-range animal migration forecast model based on weather radar network
abstract: Predicting aerial animal migration has great implications for biological research and conservation, and agricultural production. Animal migration is deeply coupled with spatio-temporal and meteorological factors, however, the existing forecast model is only based on the spatio-temporal features of animal migration and the impact of meteorological factors on migration is not considered. In this paper, we propose a dynamic forecast model to forecast airborne migration from the perspective of the influence of wind field data on migration and makes prediction with the help of neural network. Specifically, we calculate the transition probability matrix using the wind data and the migration spatial field to represent the migration dynamic model, and integrated this model into deep neural network. We use the data of China's weather radar network to verify that our model outperforms the competing methods. In addition, the cause of prediction error at peak value is analysed by visualization results. In future applications, more meteorological factors should be considered to improve the representation of dynamic models.

articleTitle: Pol-ISAR space target component salience characteristic with polarimetric roll-invariant features
abstract: Satellites are typical man-made targets. Polarimetric inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR) can operate all-day and all-weather, making it important for space target surveillance. However, radar target scattering responses are strongly orientation-dependent. Polarimetric roll-invariant features which are independent of target orientations along the radar line of sight exhibit great importance and achieved successful applications in many fields. This work explores the statistic and spatial variance characteristics of space targets from pixel level to component level based on the semantic information. A three-dimension polarimetric correlation pattern (3-D PCP) interpretation tool is utilized and the relationships between different polarimetric roll-invariant features are investigated. Then a Component Salience indicator is proposed to quantitatively measure the feature response to different structures. Experiments demonstrate that the polarimetric roll-invariant features derived from the 3-D PCP have better performance in improving component salience.

articleTitle: Waveform design for integrated sensing and communication in the presence of DRFM forwarding interference
abstract: This paper focuses on the joint design of the integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) waveform and the receive filter in the presence of digital radio frequency memory (DRFM) forwarding interference. We first construct an optimization model by minimizing the integrated sidelobe level (ISL) of the ISAC waveform and the integrated level (IL) of the interference signal, under the constraints of the energy budget, peak loss, and peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR). Moreover, the phase similarity constraint, which minimizes the difference between the ISAC waveform and the communication symbol, is introduced to assure the communication performance. Then, a new decoupled majorization minimization (DMM) algorithm is developed to solve the above formulated non-convex multi-constrained problem. Finally, numerical and simulation results show that the proposed scheme can effectively suppress interference, and also display superior sensing and communication performance.

articleTitle: Robust beamforming method based on FDA-MIMO radar
abstract: In this work, a robust two-dimensional beamforming algorithm based on frequency diversity array multiple-input multiple-output (FDA-MIMO) radar is proposed. The algorithm focuses on scenarios where mainlobe deceptive jamming and sidelobe barrage jamming coexist, taking into account estimation errors in the jamming angle-range. The algorithm initially employs a smoothing technique to eliminate true targets from the samples, utilizing the Mailloux method to expand the null associated with jamming, thereby ensuring robustness against errors. Simulation results confirm the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: The principle analysis of two-element cross-eye jamming based on phased array
abstract: The application of phased array to radar jammer is helpful to improve the effective isotropic radiated power (EIRP) and the ability to counter multiple targets. Two-element cross-eye jammer based on phased array is significantly different from traditional two-element cross-eye jammer (TTCJ) and multiple-element cross-eye jammer (MCJ) in terms of antenna elements layout, circuit architecture and signal processing. However, there are no published literatures to analyse the principle of phased array two-element cross-eye jammer (PATCJ). Therefore, a mathematical model of PATCJ against mono-pulse radar is established in this paper, and the principle and feasibility of applying phased arrays to two-element cross-eye jammer are discussed. The cross-eye gain of PATCJ is derived. Besides, it is verified that the random selection of phase-shifting reference units (PRUs) will not affect the jamming performance of PATCJ. The research results of this paper have guiding significance for the engineering realization of PATCJ.

articleTitle: Research on a method of realizing high performance ultra-long pulse compression processor based on FPGA
abstract: Pulse compression plays a vital role in radar signal processing. With the rapid development of synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imaging technology, the demand for spaceborne SAR imaging processing is becoming more and more urgent, especially the need to support the real-time application of ultra-long pulse compression accelerators. However, limited on-chip resources and memory access bandwidth have always been key bottlenecks restricting the design of ultra-long pulse compression processing. FPGA is widely regarded as a processor that is both highly parallelized and has excellent computing speed. Therefore, this research is committed to proposing a new processor design method based on FPGA to cope with ultra-long point pulse compression processing. First, to be able to effectively handle ultra-long sequence pulse compression up to 1M points, we propose an architecture with careful optimization. Secondly, in order to improve processing efficiency and reduce resource overhead, we propose a fixed-point data fitting implementation strategy. Finally, this study also explores an on-chip storage optimization method for reference function spectrum for linear frequency modulation (LFM) signals, which not on ly effectively reduces the cost of on-chip resources, but also saves storage transmission bandwidth. These innovative designs and optimization strategies will provide strong support for further development in the field of ultra-long-point pulse compression processing.

articleTitle: An autofocus algorithm for moving target with micro-motion in high-resolution SAR image
abstract: SAR (synthetic aperture radar) uses platform motion to observe stationary objects and synthesizes a larger antenna aperture to improve resolution, among which spotlight SAR further improves resolution through a longer synthetic aperture time. However, in this process, defocusing will occur in imaging moving objects, such as cars, ships, and airplanes. At the same time, if part of the moving object is in a different motion state from the subject, the image quality will deteriorate further. Therefore, this paper proposes a multi-PGA(phase gradient autofocus) algorithm for focusing moving target with micro-motion in high-resolution SAR image. Firstly, the PGA algorithm is applied to the defocused image to compensate the phase error caused by the movement of the main bodys of the target. Secondly, the target is divided into regions to focus the micro-motion of the wings. The overlapping parts of different regions are aligned to ensure the stability of the results. Finally, the open SAR data of the Umbra satellite of an moving airplane with vibrating wings is used to test the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Dual-polarimetric Sentinel-1 SAR time series data despeckling using RABASAR with low-rank image
abstract: Polarimetric Synthetic Aperture Radar (PolSAR) sensors can capture images in various polarization states, providing valuable information about target characteristics and scattering mechanisms. However, the inherent speckle noise impedes their analysis and interpretation. In this paper, we present a patch-based low-rank approximation (PLRA) algorithm combined with the RABASAR framework for multitemporal dual-polarimetric SAR image despeckling. The original multitemporal data is first decomposed into four channels, which are then filtered by the PLRA algorithm to compute their corresponding low-rank images. Subsequently, these low-rank images are fed into the RABASAR framework as super-images, from which noise-free channel images are obtained. Finally, these images are combined to produce the ultimate noise-free target image. Experimental results using Sentinel-1 dual-polarimetric SAR datasets demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms other filters.

articleTitle: An improved bistatic radar positioning method based on PCPF
abstract: Target location is one of the important steps in target tracking and recognition. The traditional bistatic geometric positioning method is greatly influenced by measurement error, multipath effect and environmental interference when detecting long- distance targets, which leads to the reduction of positioning accuracy. However, the movement of the target may cause the change of Doppler frequency. By analyzing the Doppler frequency of the target, the state estimation of the target can be obtained, which can improve the positioning accuracy. Based on the rough estimation of target position, this paper deduces the positioning error caused by the estimation of Doppler frequency and frequency modulation. We estimate the moving direction and Doppler frequency of the target by Kalman filter (KF) and product cubic phase function (PCPF). Finally, we simulate the positioning accuracy of the proposed method under different SNR and compare it with the distance-angle positioning method. Simulation results show that the proposed algorithm improves the positioning accuracy by about 25%-30% compared with the traditional positioning method.

articleTitle: Anechoic chamber equivalent simulation method for intermittent transceiver echo based on space target electromagnetic scattering data
abstract: Electromagnetic simulations and anechoic chamber measurements are commonly used to obtain target characteristics. The use of intermittent transceiver in anechoic chamber can effectively solve the problem of the signal coupling at the receiver. However, the method of equivalent simulation between electromagnetic simulation and intermittent transceiver is rarely discussed. In this paper, an intermittent transceiver echo equivalent simulation method in anechoic chamber is proposed based on space electromagnetic scattering data. Then, the characteristics of scattering points of targets under micro-motion conditions are analyzed. Finally, the equivalent relationship and processing flow between electromagnetic scattering data and intermittent transceiver echo are discussed. Simulations are conducted to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Direction finding in partly calibrated arrays considering inter-subarray displacement and subarray inclination
abstract: Direction finding in partly calibrated arrays has garnered significant attention in recent years. Compared to sparse recovery algorithms, classical subspace-based methods have lower time complexity and are better suited for real-time dynamic scenarios. While most of the existing literature primarily focuses on imperfections like inter-subarray displacement, there has been relatively little discussion on subarray inclination. The angle of subarray inclination couples closely with the direction of arrival (DOA) and introduces nonlinear distribution of subarrays, which complicate the issue further. In this paper, we address both imperfections simultaneously and propose a subspace-based gridless method with two stages. We firstly utilize the covariance of sources to estimated the entire steering matrix and then calculate the imperfections and DOAs from the structured array manifold. As the simulations show, our proposed method is capable of achieving robust direction finding and self-calibration in such complex situations.

articleTitle: An improved fusion of SAR and visible images
abstract: The traditional fusion method for SAR and visible images takes high computational complexity and cannot effectively handle the large amount of edge and texture details in high-resolution SAR images. Our team proposed an improved fusion method combining HSV-NSST and adaptive PCNN. Firstly, transfer the visible image into HSV to extract the brightness component V, both SAR and V component image are decomposed into multiple scales using NSST to obtain high and low frequency coefficients. Then, the low-frequency sub-band components are fused through PCNN, the high-frequency multi-band components are fused through SML. Last, the fused image was obtained via inverse NSST and inverse HSV transform. The results shows that NSST(4th)-HSV method outperforms similar algorithms in terms of SSIM, CC, and RMSE metrics, achieving scores of 0.9026, 0.8580, and 0.0089 respectively.

articleTitle: KD-Net: a novel knowledge- and data-driven network for SAR target recognition with limited data
abstract: In recent years, deep learning (DL) has prevailed in the synthetic aperture radar (SAR) target recognition field. It is a data- driven method, which usually requires large-sized labelled data for training. However, different from natural images, SAR images are usually difficult to acquire large-sized labelled data, which significantly limits the improvement of target recognition performance. To address this problem, a knowledge- and data-driven network (KD-Net) is proposed for SAR target recognition. Compared with typical DL-based methods, the proposed KD-Net adopts a knowledge- and data-driven manner for target recognition, which effectively utilizes the prior knowledge of SAR imaging and target characteristics to improve performance. Specifically, in the SAR system, the SAR image is accumulated by different echo characteristics in the azimuth direction. Here, the sub-aperture decomposition is employed to mine the multi-angle observation information in the limited SAR data, which promotes the deep network's ability to acquire discriminative features for different types of targets. In addition, according to the prior knowledge of targets, the multi-scale saliency map is constructed, which enhances target features and suppresses clutter to guide the network focus on salient areas. Here, the multi-scale saliency map acts as a guiding mechanism to further improve the performance by a knowledge-driven method. The experiment results in the MSTAR data set (SOC condition) demonstrate the advantages of the proposed method, which achieved an accuracy of more than 99.4% without data augmentation and transfer learning.

articleTitle: Deceptive jamming suppression based on compressed sensing and slow-time coding via single-channel SAR
abstract: Deceptive jamming suppression in synthetic aperture radar is a problem that urgently needs to be addressed. Due to the coherence of the SAR system, deceptive jamming signals can be well fused with Synthetic-aperture radar images, and have high concealment. This letter proposes a deceptive jamming suppression method that combines slow-time coding and compressed sensing. By using slow-time coding, we divide the SAR transmission signals into two groups and add phase coding to each pulse group respectively. Then compressed sensing is used to separate partial deceptive jamming from echo and image each group signal. Then utilize the difference between the deceptive jamming target location between the two images to remove the remaining deceptive jamming. Compared to some existing methods, this method achieves less jamming residue via a single-channel SAR system with slow-time coding.

articleTitle: Rebar clutter suppression method based on weighted nuclear norm minimization with random SVD
abstract: Through-the-wall radar (TWR) greatly suffers from the wall and rebar clutter, which whelms the targets’ echoes heavily. Since the rebars inside the wall often has the same shape as that of targets, many clutter suppression methods do not work effectively. To solve this problem, this paper utilizes a method based on weighted nuclear norm minimization with random singular value decomposition （SVD） and entry-wise hard-thresholding. For each iteration of the method, different weights are assigned to the singular values, which is used to accurately approximate the rebar clutter. And random SVD is employed to reduce the size of the decomposed data and improve the efficiency. Besides, according to the prior sparsity, entry-wise hard-thresholding is applied to extract the target waves and suppress the remained clutter as well as noise. The effectiveness of proposed method has been verified by the numerical simulation and experimental results.

articleTitle: Deformation inversion and prediction of the Hong Kong-Zhuhai-Macao Bridge (HZMB) combining InSAR and ARIMA-PF model
abstract: Deformation monitoring of bridges is of great significance for the detection of potential bridge safety hazards and the avoidance of accidents. Compared with the traditional bridge monitoring methods, time-series InSAR (Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar) technology has the advantages of wide monitoring range, high accuracy, low cost, no restriction of weather conditions, and continuous monitoring, which is suitable for the deformation monitoring of large-span cross-sea bridges. Taking the Hong Kong-Zhuhai-Macao Bridge (HZMB) as the research object, this paper processed 138 scenes of C-band Sentinel-1 images spanning from 2018 to 2022, extracted the deformation of the HZMB, and predicted the deformation trend of HZMB using the ARIMA-PF model. The average deformation rate of HZMB ranging from -89 mm/y to -72 mm/y during this period. The bridge remained generally stable, except for some settlement funnels observed in the artificial islan d of the Hong Kong Boundary Crossing Facilities (HKBCF). To predict future deformation trends accurately, we employed the ARIMA-PF (Auto Regressive Integrated Moving Average with Particle Filter) model, which proved effective in forecasting HZMB's deformations.

articleTitle: An interference suppression algorithm based on time-frequency features
abstract: Interrupted-sampling repeater jamming (ISRJ) creates a cluster of false targets at the radar receiver, significantly degrading the radar's target detection performance. We investigate a method for suppressing ISRJ based on time-frequency features. Initially, we apply de-chirping processing to the echo signal and use time-frequency transformation to obtain the time-frequency characteristics of the target and ISRJ. To mitigate the impact of noise on the extraction of time-frequency characteristics, we perform binarization processing on the image obtained after the time-frequency transformation. Finally, we utilize two sets of features to achieve the extraction of target information and the suppression of ISRJ. Simulation experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm in suppressing interference.

articleTitle: Knowledge-aided covariance matrix estimation algorithm based on geometric mean in STAP for airborne radar
abstract: The problem of knowledge-aided (KA) covariance matrix estimation in airborne radar space-time adaptive processing (STAP) is studied in this paper. In the traditional KA covariance matrix estimation methods, the insufficient number of available samples and inaccurate prior knowledge can cause serious deterioration of STAP performance. To tackle this problem, a new KA covariance matrix estimation algorithm based on geometric mean is proposed. Specifically, by utilizing the persymmetric structure information as well as the geometric mean in the space of positive definite matrices, a geometric mean estimator is constructed, which is then linearly combined with the prior covariance matrix to obtain a new type of CCM estimators. Simulation results illustrate that the proposed algorithm has good STAP performance with small samples and inaccurate prior knowledge.

articleTitle: SAR target discrimination based on the ensemble projection feature
abstract: The traditional discrimination features for SAR target discrimination are usually extracted in an unsupervised manner, leading to the fact that the description ability of discrimination features are insufficient and the discrimination performance degrades in complex scenes. Aiming at this problem, this paper proposes a supervised SAR target discrimination feature based on ensemble projection. Firstly, the sample prototype sets are automatically sampled from the training samples by using the Max-Min sampling method to represent a series of visual attributes. Secondly, the discrimination function is learned based on eac h prototype of the sample prototype sets. Finally, the samples are projected to the prototype functions and the projection values are concatenated as the final discrimination features. We conduct the target discrimination experiments on the measured data of miniSAR and FARAD SAR, and the results demonstrate that compared with the traditional discriminative features, the proposed discrimination feature can achieve better discriminant performance.

articleTitle: Realization of dual-channel GMTI real-time processing technology based on FPGA
abstract: This paper presents a design of GMTI real-time processing based on FPGA. This scheme uses channel adaptive equalization to calibrate channel phase errors in real time, and realizes on-board real-time moving target detection, reducing false target by secondary condensation, which is suitable for real-time moving targets detection and positioning of dual-channel GMTI radar. In this paper, the FPGA processing architecture is described in detail, and the processing effect is analysed. the actual experiment results show that the presented real-time processor based on FPGA is efficient for dual channels GMTI radar.

articleTitle: Gesture recognition based on fused bi-directional range Doppler information with FMCW radar
abstract: Gesture recognition is increasingly important in human-computer interaction. The research based on millimeter wave radar has the advantages of all-day, all-weather, and good privacy. However, some gesture cannot be distinguished due to their similar range and Doppler features in one direction. In this paper, a gesture recognition method based on bi-directional observation and information fusion is proposed. A vertical and horizontal range-Doppler time map (VH-RDTM) is utilized to extract range-Doppler features in two directions. And then the gesture data is input into the Res-Net for recognition. The experimental results demonstrate that the recognition accuracy is improved from 89% to 98% compared with the traditional unidirectional observation method. Also, the fused one can reflect the motion information of gestures robustly and has better generalization ability for untrained objects.

articleTitle: A high-resolution imaging algorithm for synthetic aperture interferometric radiometry based on unsupervised pulse-coupled neural networks
abstract: High-resolution imaging of synthetic aperture interferometric radiometry (SAIR) has been a research hotspot. Since the spatial resolution of SAIR is limited by array aperture size and the inversion process is a pathological problem, achieving high-resolution image is challenging. In most cases, the target's brightness temperature in SAIR contaminated by noise differs from the brightness temperature of its surrounding pixels, and the noise destroys the correlation between the brightness temperature of adjacent pixels, resulting in low-resolution SAIR images.To address this issue, this paper proposes a high-resolution SAIR imaging algorithm based on unsupervised Pulse-Coupled Neural Network (PCNN) learning. This algorithm adjusts the corresponding brightness temperature of each pixel based on the firing status of the neuron and its neighboring neurons, reducing noise and achieving high-resolution reconstruction of SAIR images. The algorithm does not require a significant amount of training data or prior information, and can achieve the high-resolution reconstruction by using a single image. Simulation and experimental results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm can improve the peak signal-to-noise ratio and resolution of targets.

articleTitle: Application of complex deep neural networks in complex data processing and comparative analysis of activation functions
abstract: The application of deep learning to fast radar data processing has important significance. The effectiveness of complex deep neural networks (CDNNs) has recently been demonstrated, and complex networks are important for processing complex data because they have the ability to handle phases. And the complex-valued activation function introduces a nonlinear transformation to the network, which has a great potential to improve the network performance. In this paper, we test the feasibility of CDNNs and the effect of different activation functions in the framework of complex networks under the goal of retaining more phase information. In particular, we propose a new complex-valued activation RℂReLU based on RℂeLu and test its performance in a classification and auto-encoder context. Finally, we perform radar imaging reconstruction by different activation functions in complex networks, and the results show that RℂReLU is more suitable for processing radar data in CDNNs.

articleTitle: Research on key technologies of portable multifunction battlefield reconnaissance radar
abstract: This article focuses on the demand for combat intelligence reconnaissance in modern high-tech warfare. Firstly, it introduces the operational tasks of multifunctional battlefield reconnaissance radar, and then combines the characteristics of portable multifunctional battlefield reconnaissance radar to analyze its key technologies and provide solutions; Finally, prospects were made for the development of subsequent equipment, which can provide good reference and assistance for the design of multifunctional battlefield reconnaissance radar.

articleTitle: Direction of arrival estimation based on DNCNN in low SNR
abstract: The direction of arrival (DOA) estimation is a key issue of array radar. Improving signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) is essential for DOA estimation, making denoising become a necessary step before DOA estimation. In this letter, de-noising convolutional neural network (DnCNN) is introduced into array radar to realize signal denoising. It adopts residual learning to remove latent noise-free signal, and then outputs noise estimation. Considering that the inputs are one-dimensional complex signals, we adjust the DnCNN parameters such as convolutional channels number, convolutional filters number, convolutional kernel size, and discuss the appropriate network depth. The results show that the DnCNN has remarkable effect on noise filtering, so that accurate DOA estimation can be obtained. In addition, DnCNN has quite strong generalization ability for signals with even lower SNR.

articleTitle: Parameter estimation using compressed distributed polarized sensitive array
abstract: To address the issue of high computational complexity in traditional polarized sensitive arrays for estimating signal direction of arrival (DOA) and polarization parameters, a compression structure has been proposed. The proposed structure involves the addition of a compression network in front of the front-end chains. The compression matrix generated by this network consists of complex Gaussian distributed elements. The compression matrix reduces the dimension of the sample covariance matrix, thereby reducing the complexity of the computation process. The proposed structure achieves higher accuracy in DOA and polarization parameter estimation for a given number of front-end circuit chains. Compared to traditional polarized sensitive arrays, this structure significantly reduces the computational burden in the estimation process, improving the efficiency of DOA and polarization parameter estimation. Numerical simulation results validated the effectiveness of the proposed structure.

articleTitle: Range-ambiguity-free target localization using chirped-FDA
abstract: In this work, we consider the problem of ambiguous range measurements inherent in FDA. We present a novel two-stage scheme that uses frequency diverse array (FDA) with each element transmitting chirp signals. The proposed scheme effectively eliminates the problem by selecting one chirp signal and then performing coarse range estimation within a sparse range grid. In the second stage, we leverage frequency offsets to accurately derive the range value based on the initial coarse estimation. This enables us to employ a dense-grid search within a single range bin, rather than across all bins in the sparse range grid. This scheme also allows us to extend the maximum detectable range theoretically to inﬁnity. Moreover, by adopting this methodology, we are able to simultaneously estimate the direction-of-arrival (DoA) and range through a joint estimation process. To combat the range-angle coupling of FDA, we incorporate coprime frequency offsets. The superior range estimation performance of the proposed scheme, particularly in terms of estimation accuracy, is demonstrated through extensive simulations.

articleTitle: Multi-target high-resolution DOA estimation based on sparse reconstruction for frequency agility radar
abstract: Frequency agility (FA) radar can avoid the frequency band of mainlobe jamming through frequency hopping and has excellent anti-jamming performance. However, frequency hopping also leads to the target signal having an irregular steering vector after pulse integration, which will affect the performance of DOA estimation. To solve this problem, this paper proposes a method of multi-target high-resolution DOA estimation in FA radar based on sparse reconstruction. Firstly, sparse reconstruction method is adopted for high resolution range-doppler reconstruction, realizing the distance and velocity estimation. Afterward, for the received array signal, phase compensation is performed based on the distance and velocity of the multi-target. Finally, using the frequency encoding of different pulses in FA signal to construct an angle estimation dictionary, the high resolution DOA information of multi-target can be recovered. Theoretical analysis and simulation experiments have verified the effectiveness of this method.

articleTitle: Multi-view SAR target recognition based on modified convolutional random vector functional link network
abstract: Due to the problem of the viewpoint-varying scattering feature accompanied by speckle noise in synthetic aperture radar (SAR) images, numerous multi-view deep learning models have been proposed and achieved remarkable performance in SAR automatic target recognition (ATR). However, the performance of these multi-view models is susceptible to the hyper- parameters and the traditional backpropagation is time-consuming. In this paper, we leverage the modified convolutional random vector functional link (IntCRVFL) network to merge the information of multi-view images, then propose a multi-view IntCRVFL (Mv-IntCRVFL) network to simplify the multi-view SAR ATR system. First, the multi-view SAR image features are extracted separately by the fixed convolutional layers with randomly initialized parameters. Then, the activations of the hidden layer under different images are merged through a bunding manner. Ultimately, the connections between hidden and output layers are honed through a closed-form solution, resulting in highly accurate target recognition. The experimental results on the Moving and Stationary Target Acquisition and Recognition (MSTAR) have illustrated the proposed Mv- IntCRVFL network can achieve a desirable accuracy with an improved speed.

articleTitle: Motion modeling and echo Doppler frequency analysis of millimeter wave fuze
abstract: During the process of attacking the target, the artillery shell not only moves in a straight line but also has micro-motions such as spin and conical rotation, which produce micro-Doppler modulation on the echo signal and limit the effectiveness of conventional signal detection algorithms. To eliminate the influence of micro-motion, a warhead motion model is built based on the actual situation. The model determines the positional relationship between the fuze and the target by establishing multiple three-dimensional coordinate systems. It also determines the transformation between coordinate systems according to Rodrigues' rotation formula. Based on the created model, we focused on analysing the micro-Doppler frequency shift caused by micro-motions such as spin, conical rotation, precession, and nutation. The accuracy of the model is verified by simulation analysis, which lays the foundation for using millimeter wave fuze to measure speed and distance.

articleTitle: A novel ground-track FMCW SAR imaging method based on modified wavenumber domain algorithm
abstract: The frequency modulated continuous wave synthetic aperture radar (FMCW SAR) is widely utilised on miniaturized platforms due to its light weight and cost-effectiveness. However, the imaging algorithms for pulse radars may not function well for the FMCW SAR. To deal with this issue, this paper proposes a novel FMCW SAR imaging method based on the modified wavenumber domain algorithm, where the Doppler frequency shift caused by radar motion during the frequency sweep period is compensated firstly. Then, a modified range wavenumber axis scaling transformation is performed, which can effectively reserve the non-stationary phase information, so as to improve the subsequent azimuth focusing performance. Finally, a well-focused SAR image can be obtained after azimuth matched filtering. The simulation results of point targets and the real-measured ground-track FMCW SAR data simultaneously verify the effectiveness and feasibility of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A novel method for micro-motion target detection and ghost track suppression in automotive radar
abstract: Thanks to the robust detection ability in different environmental conditions (light and weather), automotive radar has been widely used in advanced driver assistance system (ADAS). The close-range stationary targets with micro-motion may generate ghost tracks, which can trigger unexpected ADAS alert. Few researches have focused on this issue. To decrease the error alert, a well-designed image processing method based on range-Doppler (RD) image is proposed for micro-motion target detection and ghost suppression. Target detection is realized by ordered statistics constant false alarm rate (OS-CFAR) detector. The image dilation algorithm is applied to cluster the micro-motion targets and their extended parts. The existence of micro-motion target can be predicted according to the number of connected image cells. The ghost track problem can be improved to avoid the extended measurements of the micro-motion target initialing a track. The method is validated by real road test data.

articleTitle: Research on millimeter-wave holographic imaging algorithm based on convolutional integration
abstract: Millimeter-wave cylindrical aperture 3D imaging has been widely researched and applied in the field of security screening because of its advantages of non-ionizing radiation, strong penetrability, omnidirectional scanning and high-resolution imaging. The imaging effect of traditional wavenumber domain algorithms is largely affected by the interpolation accuracy, but the millimeter-wave holographic 3D imaging method based on convolutional integration obtains the millimeter-wave images of targets on the cylindrical surface with different radii by performing convolution operations in the height direction and azimuthal direction, avoiding 3D STOLT interpolation. In this paper, the distance function at part of the radius is calculated and stored in advance, based on which the distance function of the whole imaging region is calculated, finally, the feasibility of the imaging method is verified by computerized imaging simulation of a point target.

articleTitle: A time-variant cross-track error phase removal method for ATI-SAR
abstract: Along-track interferometric synthetic aperture radar (ATI-SAR) is one of the most effective means for obtaining high-precision ocean current fields. In practical scenarios, unstable flight platform attitudes introduce time-variant cross-track baseline components, resulting in error phases in the along-track interferometric phases. This seriously affects the accuracy of obtaining high-precision current field. Therefore, a method for removing time-variant cross-track error phases is proposed. In traditional methods, platform azimuth attitude angle information is generally used in combination with cross-track interferometric measurement principle to estimate and remove error phases. However, residual sub-high-frequency error phase components still exist in this case. To address this issue, the method proposes the use of Empirical Orthogonal Function (EOF) analysis to decompose the error-containing interferometric phase matrix. The interferometric phase is decomposed into a series of orthogonal functions and then recombined, thereby removing the sub-high-frequency error components. This enhances the stability and accuracy of the along-track interferometric current measurement. The effectiveness of the proposed method is verified through simulation experiments and airborne measurement data.

articleTitle: A new dual-frequency polarimetric SAR on helicopter
abstract: Xi'an Institute of Space Radio Technology in China has innovatively proposed a dual-frequency polarimetric synthetic aperture radar system based on helicopter (HD-SAR), with advantages of high integration and easy installation. This system integrates a low frequency band circuit (C-band) and a high frequency band circuit (Ku-band), which can work simultaneously or un-simultaneously. By using a dual-polarized antenna, the Ku-band application can realize full-polarization SAR. This paper firstly introduces key parameters of the radar system, and then installation layouts combined with the helicopter Sikorsky S76 are given. Finally, the results of flight experiment show that the measured resolution of for two operation frequency band application can reach 0.8 m and 0.5 m, respectively, dual-frequency fused image and full-polarization image with more details are also given, which means HD-SAR is applicable to high-resolution microwave remote sensing scenarios.

articleTitle: Sparse spectrum aperiodic waveform design based on Riemannian manifold optimization
abstract: Since the proliferation of electromagnetic devices, the electromagnetic spectrum has become increasingly congested. In order to improve spectrum utilization, radar systems should effectively exploit the discontinuous spectrum gaps in the spectrum across different frequency bands. Nevertheless, the presence of these spectrum gaps worsens the sidelobes performance of the waveform autocorrelation function. This paper introduces a method based on Riemannian manifold optimization for designing waveforms with low autocorrelation sidelobes and specific sparsely allocated spectrum. The objective function, which aims to simultaneously minimize the integral sidelobes level and stopband power, is transformed into a single objective optimization problem using the weighted sum method. Additionally, the feasible regions resulting from imposing the constant modulus constraint on the waveform and unimodular auxiliary variable are complex circular manifolds. Utilizing these manifolds, we construct the Riemannian product manifold, enabling simultaneous optimization of the waveform and unimodular auxiliary variable through the Riemannian conjugate gradient method.
