Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm achieves radar waveform with low autocorrelation performance and specific spectral properties, while maintaining a low computational burden.

articleTitle: Ka-band spaceborne video SAR imaging with Luojia-2
abstract: The utilization of spaceborne video Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) revolutionizes SAR imaging and detection, enabling a transition for SAR images from static to dynamic. This advancement significantly enhances radar's ability to acquire target information for SAR satellite. The Luojia-2 satellite, a Chinese Ka-band SAR satellite launched in May 2023, possesses the capability of obtaining SAR video for up to 30 seconds with a resolution better than 3 meters and a frame rate exceeding 5 Hz. This article focuses on several crucial aspects of spaceborne video SAR imaging, including the modeling of video SAR, the SAR video formation algorithm and its implementation. Additionally, preliminary results from in-orbit testing are presented to show the advantages offered by the Ka-band frequency characteristics in spaceborne video SAR applications. Specifically, it is demonstrated that Ka-band SAR enables high-resolution SAR video with a high frame rate within shorter synthetic aperture time.

articleTitle: Common targets polarimetric calibration technique for long blind range radar
abstract: Many research indicates the importance of polarimetric information in radar systems for purposes such as detection, tracking, and parameter estimation. The calibration process is essential for obtaining precise polarimetric information. However, conducting calibration experiments for long blind range radars can be challenging in fields where ground clutter is prominent. For multi-pulse width switching radar, this paper introduces a polarimetric calibration algorithm by measuring common targets of short- and long-range waveforms. Firstly, we switch between various waveforms to measure the strong echo common targets in the overlapping detection range. The scattering matrices of common targets can be obtained by the short-range waveform calibrated by the conventional method. Then, the polarization error model is built based on the measured scattering matrices of long-range waveform, and the true values of the scattering matrices of common targets are used to estimate the polarization errors of long-range waveform. The effectiveness of the algorithm is validated through simulation results.

articleTitle: Research on non-contact electrocardiogram monitoring based on millimeter-wave radar and residual Unet
abstract: Traditional electrocardiogram (ECG) measurement is one of the gold standards for the clinical diagnosis of cardiovascular disease (CVD), but it require direct contact with skin, which is inconvenience. To overcome this limitation, a non-contact ECG monitoring method was realized for subjects in a seated posture using a millimeter-wave radar in this study. We proposed a two-stage interference suppression method of random body motion and designed a deep learning lightweight network model, i.e., residual Unet (ResUnet), which size is only 17.45 MB. Using a comparative study method, the radar and ECG signals of ten subjects in the sitting state were synchronously collected to construct our database for network training. The experimental results show ResUnet is able to reconstruct the ECG signals with correlation coefficient up to 0.8, even in the presence of random body motion, which are better than the other model.

articleTitle: Discussion on the unified feature parameter extraction framework for multi-polarimetric SAR
abstract: Polarimetric SAR modes include various forms, such as quad-polarimetric, dual-polarimetric, and compact-polarimetric. Different polarimetric modes have different dimensions of observation data, and feature parameter extraction theories and methods are relatively independent. This leads to develop different data processing and application algorithm modules in business applications, making it difficult to meet the comprehensive business needs of various user fields in the future. Therefore, it is necessary to develop a unified processing and application algorithms suitable for multi-polarimetric SAR based on the actual user needs, in order to reduce the cost of algorithm development and maintenance updates in the multi domain business operation process of actual users. This paper explores several ideas for establishing a unified feature parameter extraction framework for multi-polarimetric SAR, which can provide guidance for breaking through the theoretical barrier of multi-polarimetric SAR information processing and establishing a unified multi-polarimetric SAR information processing method in the future.

articleTitle: A separable Wishart dissimilarity in multitemporal PolSAR imagery
abstract: In PolSAR land cover mapping, multi-temporal data can provide land change information over time to improve classification accuracy. Dissimilarity measurement is a typical method to describe the variation of the scattering mechanism, which can provide an important supplement to the scattering information of different ground objects. Furthermore, many studies begin with correlation strength rather than polarization scattering properties, resulting in a lack of polarization information for time- varying features. Aiming at the deficiencies of the Wishart dissimilarity measurement, this paper puts forward one separable Wishart distance measurement to explain the components of Wishart dissimilarity measurement. It is decomposed into three independent variables to quantify the change degree of scattering information of ground objects with coherence decomposition theory. The highest value contains more change information and is sensitive to major changes, the other two change features enhance the change information. To prove the usefulness of this separable Wishart dissimilarity, four ensemble learning methods are implemented for the classification in one UAVSAR dataset, and the classification result of overall accuracy can be improved by 12% compared to the symmetric revised Wishart dissimilarity.

articleTitle: Research on target characteristics and classification technology of small UAV
abstract: In this paper, the RCS of small UAV targets in X-band is modeled and simmulated. Based on this, the target classification technology of small UAV and ground vehicle is studied. The classification method of different RCS targets is studied by using the difference of SNR characteristics. Through this characteristic difference, the classification of the two types of targets is realized, and the false alarm formed by the ground vehicle is better suppressed.

articleTitle: Human target tracking method based on kernelized correlation filter and interactive multiple model
abstract: Through-the-wall radar (TWR) is widely used to locate and track human targets behind walls. However, it is difficult to obtain the prior information such as the position, speed and direction of the human targets, and target images often occur defocusing and deformation with the movement, resulting in difficulty in human targets location and tracking. Aiming at solving these problems, a target tracking algorithm combining kernelized correlation filter (KCF) and interactive multiple model (IMM) algorithm is proposed. In the proposed method, KCF is used to locate the target area on the radar image and obtain the target position measurement. Then, the obtained target position is taken as the input of IMM algorithm, which outputs the final tracking trajectory. Numerical simulation and experimental results show the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Parameters decoupling and estimation in FRaC system
abstract: In light of the rapid and remarkable advancements in autonomous vehicles and transportation infrastructure, a compelling interest has emerged in the realm of dual function radar-communication (DFRC) systems due to the size, cost and resource efficiency. A frequency modulated continuous waveform (FMCW)-based radar-communications (FRaC) system tailored for vehicular applications has been proposed, harnessing sparse MIMO arrays and index modulation (IM) to realize a DFRC system. In this paper, the three-dimensional (3D) parameter coupling problem in the FRaC system is considered. Due to the inherent coupling of the 3D-parameters including range, direction of arrival (DOA) and velocity in the estimating matrix of the FRaC system, the existing estimation algorithms are not well investigated and applicable. A decoupling algorithm is proposed to recover the decoupled estimating matrix by attaching sparsity constraint to the estimating matrix with decomposed atomic norm minimization (DANM) algorithm. Simulation results show that the proposed algorithm exploits the advantage of the virtual aperture in the presence of coupling caused by IM and sparse MIMO array and achieve accurate parameter estimation while concurrently maintaining a low computational complexity.

articleTitle: Research and verification study on airborne distributed coherence-synthetic aperture radar
abstract: Distributed coherence-synthetic aperture radar (DCAR) is a hot research direction in radar surveillance. The detection of DCAR based on airborne platforms is a more complex scene. The present article has researched signal model construction, detection error analysis and coherent synthesis algorithms. The high signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) gain improvement is obtained in the airborne distributed coherence-synthetic aperture radar (ADCAR) detection experiment, which verifies the correctness of the design and the project feasibility of the moving platform DCAR system.

articleTitle: Power equalization model based on neural networks for unequal power DOA estimation
abstract: In the case of unequal power sources, the traditional DOA estimation methods suffer from performance degradation in terms of resolution, especially when the signal angle separation is small. A non-end-to-end power equalization model based on neural networks is proposed to improve the quality of the covariance matrix when unequal power signals are incident, making it look like a power equalization signal. Based on that, we can obtain better estimation accuracy through DOA estimation methods like MUSIC. The numerical experiments demonstrate that the proposed method surpasses the original MUSIC algorithm in terms of success rate under conditions of unequal power sources with small angle separation and exhibits approximately the same estimation accuracy with the other subspace method like ERNS and IPNS. In addition, the method maintain good performance under low number of snapshot and significantly reduces processing time which makes it possible to use in real-time applications.

articleTitle: An approach for multi-beam angle measurement at subarray level
abstract: Aiming at the application of digital multi-beam technology in subarray multi-channel phased array radar, an approach based on MUSIC for multi-beam angle estimation at subarray level is proposed. The approach to form multi-beam by element and subarray weights is introduced. It is derived that the mono-pulse angle measurement can only be used for the multi-beam formed by regular subarrays with uniform weights. The multi-beam angle estimation processing based on MUSIC in subarray-level digital array radar is explained in detail. Employing the detection information of multi-beam, the premise to know the number of targets in MUSIC algorithm has been solved. Simulation results show that the new approach performs well both in a wide SNR range and different subarray formations, compared with the fitting mono-pulse angle measurement.

articleTitle: Enhanced radar target detection with local minimum entropy CLEAN
abstract: In the case of low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), cross term interference generated by time-frequency analysis of multiple targets echo signal are difficult problems in radar detection. In order to reduce the errors caused by cross terms, an improved CLEAN algorithm based on the local minimum entropy criterion is proposed in this paper. The algorithm uses the local minimum entropy of the spectrum to improve the estimation accuracy of sinusoidal parameters, and combines with the CLEAN algorithm to improve the multiple targets detection capability. The simulation results show that the CLEAN algorithm based on the local minimum entropy criterion can detect all the targets when multiple targets interfere with each other.

articleTitle: Space target image deblurring via adaptive motion kernel learning
abstract: Image debulrring has been a challenging task in scenarios where motions occurred to the target or the sensors, such as aerospace explorations and traffic monitoring. Recent years have seen great success of deep learning in image deblurring, however, few of them are specially designed for arbitrary motion conditions, ex., space target debulrring. To solve this issue, in this paper, we propose a novel kernel-learning based framework for arbitrary complex motion condition. The proposed framework is composed for two modules, including a kernel learning (KL) module and an image restoration (IR) module. In KL module, the motion kernel information is learned from the input blurry image. After the KL module, the IR module is employed to generate sharp image by taking blurry image and kernel information as input. The experimental results on three different datasets show that the proposed framework achieves state-of-the-art performance in image deblurring with arbitrary motion kernels. Specifically, it also achieves significantly better deblurring performance while being applying to ISAR images, despite without considering on the radar imaging process. This proves its feasibility and generalization-capacity of dealing with arbitrary motion kernels. The code is available on https://github.com/XYLGroup/AMK-Deblur.

articleTitle: Radar and communication spectral coexistence design under mobile multi-target scenarios
abstract: With the dramatic evolution of intelligent transportation, the radar and communication systems are in competition with each other over spectrum in the mobile scenarios. In this paper, a novel frame for radar and communication spectrum coexistence under mobile multi-target scenarios is formulated, which simultaneously considers the properties of both radar and communication. The controlled degrees of freedom (DoFs) include the receive filter and transmit waveform for radar, also the transmit information matrix the communication system. The established formulation is non-convex with multiple designed variables. To this end, an alternating procedure is proposed on the basis of dual transformation, alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM), and Taylor expansion framework. Finally, simulation results indicate that the presented framework provides superior properties compared to other typical algorithms.

articleTitle: Research on real-time imaging method of spaceborne SAR based on embedded GPU
abstract: Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) as an all-time, all-weather high-resolution imaging radar, can quickly and conveniently acquire the spatial distribution characteristics of a wide range of observation areas by carrying a satellite-borne platform, and it is widely used in military and civilian fields. The data processing mode of a traditional spaceborne SAR system is that the satellite obtains the echo data and transmits it to the ground handling equipment for processing. This processing mode has obvious disadvantages, which greatly reduces the timeliness of acquiring ground information. In this paper, an on-board SAR real-time imaging method based on the embedded GPU is proposed, which can be called improved GPU-CS algorithm. This method combines GPU parallel processing with CS algorithm, adopts zero-copy technology, optimized phase data construction method, GPU-shared memory transpose, and other improved methods to realize fast imaging. Imaging validation was performed on the Jetson AGX Xavier. The improved GPU-CS algorithm is 2~3 times faster than the traditional GPU-CS algorithm and provides method support for on-board SAR real-time imaging.

articleTitle: Low earth orbit satellite-based passive radar target tracking via window sliding processing
abstract: This article provides a brief introduction to a method for tracking targets using LEO satellites as space-based illuminators within a passive radar system. In recent years, the abundance of LEO satellites has made them suitable as illuminators in the passi ve radar system. However, LEO satellites have a lower Power Flux Density (PFD), which can introduce significant errors when tracking targets directly. To address this issue, the paper proposes a tracking method based on a sliding window approach. Initially, this method transforms received echoes into the Range-Doppler (RD) domain and utilizes them as target tracking states. By tracking these states, target tracking trajectories are obtained. Through the use of the sliding window technique, multipl e tracking trajectories are generated over a specific time interval. Finally, the gradient descent method is employed to fuse these trajectories, resulting in an accurate target motion trajectory. The effectiveness of the proposed method is demonstrated by simulations.

articleTitle: Characteristic analysis of high-orbit SAR echo based on spherical earth's surface
abstract: With its wide coverage and short revisit period, high-orbit synthetic aperture radar (SAR) has unique advantages in both military and civilian applications. However, the excessively imaging scene makes the planar scene assumption no longer applicable, leading to inevitable geometric distortion in the imaging results. Aiming at the geometric distortion problem under the spherical earth's surface, this paper analyzes the echo signal characteristics of targets in real spherical scene and pixels in the imaging plane in detail, and determines the equivalent points in the imaging plane that have the same imaging quality as the three-dimensional spherical objects. Finally, by reasonably setting the imaging grids, the Back-projection (BP) algorithm is used to simulate and verify the equivalent relationship. With the experimental results are correct, the problem of spherical ground surface geometric distortion in high-orbit SAR due to the large imaging scene can be solved.

articleTitle: Convex optimization based near field focusing technique
abstract: In ground-penetrating radar, enhancing the radiation capability of the antenna and the underground energy level is of paramount significance for optimizing the detection performance of the ground-penetrating radar. This study focuses on applying convex optimization-based near-field focusing technology to enhance GPR's ability to detect targets near the surface. To streamline computations, all calculations are limited to antennas and observation points in the first quadrant. Convex optimization algorithms outperform traditional phase compensation methods, offering improved focusing accuracy. This approach's effectiveness is supported by thorough simulation validation.

articleTitle: Design of unimodular sequences with good Doppler tolerance with MIMO radar
abstract: Detecting moving targets in multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) radar systems poses a challenge to waveform design due to Doppler frequency shifts. To this end, this paper addresses the problem of designing unimodular sequences with good Doppler tolerance performance for moving target detection in a colocated MIMO radar system. At the modeling stage, an optimization problem is formulated by minimizing the autocorrelation sidelobes and crosscorrelations with the constant modulus and similarity constraints. In order to solve such an NP-hard problem, a majorization-minimization (MM) algorithm combined with a projection method is developed to tackle the resulting constrained non-convex optimization problem, where the Doppler tolerance of the designed waveforms is improved through restricting the sequences to resemble a set of desired waveforms. Numerical results validate the performance of the designed waveforms in the scenario of moving target detection.

articleTitle: Influence of noise and bandwidth on LMS-based adaptive noise cancellation in FMCW radar interference mitigation
abstract: This paper investigates the effectiveness of employing least mean square (LMS)-based adaptive noise cancellation (ANC) for FMCW radar interference mitigation and analyses the influence of white Gaussian noise and radar bandwidth on the LMS-based ANC method. Through numerical simulations, the LMS-based ANC is verified to be an effective method to mitigate the radar cross interference with greatly improved peak to floor ratio (PFR) of the target in the range profiles. Besides, simulation results show that increasing the signal to noise ratio (SNR) and radar signal bandwidth can help to enhance the PFR gain achieved by using the LMS-based ANC and thus improve the interference suppression capability. This research can provide important guidance for practical applications of the LMS-based ANC, which is a promising solution to alleviating the effect of cross interferences in FMCW radars.

articleTitle: Research on high-precision positioning technology of UAV using multi-base station 4G signals
abstract: Based on the detection requirements of low-speed and small UAVs in urban environments, this paper conducts research on high-precision positioning technology for UAVs using 4G electromagnetic signals. The paper analyzes the frame structure characteristics of TDD and FDD in detail, successfully identifies the configuration mode of TDD, and focuses on solving the problem of using TDD downlink signal time window division. The ambiguity function of 4G signals is analyzed, and the side peak is suppressed. Finally, a high-precision detection scene with two transmitters and one receiver is constructed, and two types of 4G base station signals are successfully used as external radiation sources to achieve high-precision positioning of UAVs.

articleTitle: Mondrian conformal prediction enhanced LSTM for birds and drones recognition
abstract: Deep learning has achieved remarkable success in target recognition. However, its efficacy has raised distrust within radar research due to challenges in interpretability and generalization. This study introduces the Mondrian conformal prediction enhanced long short-term memory (MCPLSTM) framework, a pioneering fusion of conformal prediction and deep learning. Applied to the recognition of birds and drones in radar sequences, the MCPLSTM framework offers not only classification results but also the conferral of confidence and reliability for each individual classification. The integration of confidenc e levels into the recognition process empowers precision control, enabling the interpretation of deep learning outcomes through a statistical prism. Empirical validation is realized through extensive analysis of real-world data from an airport bird detection radar system, confirming the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: A novel direction finding method with Y-type baseline interferometer
abstract: This study introduces the principle of direction-finding with short and long baselines for a certain type of interferometer. A tw o-dimensional direction-finding method for a Y-type baseline interferometer was proposed from the perspective of maintainin g accuracy and saving cost. Based on the layout of long and short baselines, the two array antennas on the long baseline are m erged into one array antenna to form a Y-shaped structure.The unfuzzy phase data of the short baseline measurement were use d to calculate the exact phase data of the Y-type baseline measurement and the de-fuzzy process of the Y-type baseline directi on-finding was completed. The accuracy of the Y-type baseline direction-finding was analyzed and simulated. The simulation results show that the Y-type baseline direction-finding method is not only simple in structure, but also has a higher accuracy t han the traditional long and short baseline methods in a certain range.

articleTitle: Extended range detection of sea-surface target based on PRI-agile and frequency-agile waveform
abstract: Due to the limitation of the maximum pulse width, the duty ratio of the low repetition frequency (LPRF) waveform is small when the maritime radar is detecting from a long distance, resulting in a loss of the maximum detection range. To solve this problem, this paper proposes an extended range detection technique of sea-surface target based on PRI-agile and frequency-agile waveform. The technique improves the duty ratio by transmitting a set of medium repetition frequency (MPRF) orthogonal waveforms, and resolves the range ambiguity based on the frequency-domain orthogonal characteristics of the echo signal, thereby suppressing the folding sea clutter. In addition, the pulse repetition interval (PRI) stagger processing is innovatively introduced to eliminate the fixed blind area of intra-frame detection and further improve the radar detection performance. The technique can effectively increase the integration number and extend the radar detection range under the condition of constant pulse energy.

articleTitle: Spaceborne SAR resolution analysis and parameter design method based on wavenumber spectrum
abstract: Geometric resolution analysis and parameter design is a key technology in SAR system design. For Spaceborne SAR, the radar trajectory is three-dimensionally curved, and the Earth's rotation cannot be ignored. The existing resolution analysis methods have problems such as insufficient accuracy, or without analytical expression, which cannot design system parameters. Therefore, a Spaceborne SAR resolution calculation and parameter design method based on BP wavenumber spectrum is proposed in this paper. Since the imaging results obtained by the BP algorithm are usually used as a standard to evaluate the accuracy of a resolution analysis method. Therefore, this paper first derives the two-dimensional wavenumber spectrum expression of the point target after BP imaging, and obtains the two-dimensional wavenumber spectrum width. According to the principle of Fourier transform, the two-dimensional resolution analytical expression of point target is obtained. Then, according to the results of two-dimensional resolution analysis, a design method of bandwidth and synthetic aperture time is given. Finally, the accuracy of the resolution calculation and parameter design method proposed in this paper is verified by comparative simulation.

articleTitle: An improved CLEAN algorithm for multi-target detection in LFM pulse radar
abstract: During the process of multi-target detection with high resolution radar, weak targets are difficult to detect from high range resolution profile as they are masked by the sidelobe leakage of strong targets. This paper proposes an improved CLEAN algorithm based on frequency-domain correlation, addressing the challenges in multi-target detection within linear frequency modulated pulse radar. Similar to the CLEAN method, the improved CLEAN method can precisely estimate the range and radar cross section of the strongest target in the echo signal. The proposed method sequentially eliminates sidelobe interference from strong targets, facilitating the separation and detection of strong and weak targets. In situations with densely distributed targets and significant differences in radar cross section, the proposed method also maintains robust multi-target detection performance. Simulations validate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Resolving range ambiguity via transmit beamforming with time diversity array radar
abstract: Range ambiguity resolution issue is of critical importance in synthetic aperture radar (SAR) for high resolution and wide swath (HRWS) imaging. It is studied in the literature that frequency diverse array (FDA) has the ability in resolving range ambiguity under orthogonal waveform assumption which is non-realistic in practice. In this paper, the time diverse array (TDA) is devised by using time delay modulation among different array elements. The spatial electromagnetic wave distribution characteristics of TDA radar are studied, which reveals that TDA can cover the space with transmitting a single pulse. A space-time two-dimensional matching filtering method based on angle search is proposed. By beamforming at the transmit side, it is effective to utilize the degrees of freedoms (DoFs). Based on the flexible beamforming technology, the element pulse coding (EPC) is applied to resolve range ambiguity signal in SAR. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Retrieval of precipitation intensity by Doppler processing and linear regression using Ka-band CW radar
abstract: A novel precipitation intensity retrieval algorithm based on Doppler processing and linear regression for a Ka-band continuous wave (CW) precipitation radar is proposed. The precipitation radar could be used for surface rainfall measure and monitor. Firstly, the precipitation threshold is presented to determine whether it is rainy. Then the precipitation intensity is directly determined from the droplets echo power, based on the log-linear relationship between the reflectivity factor and precipitation intensity. The droplets echo power is accomplished by Doppler processing. Lastly a loglinear regression problem is modeled with the echo power and the intensity of the laser disdrometer. The experiment results demonstrate the effectiveness of the precipitation intensity retrieval algorithm.

articleTitle: Assessment of refined X-band polarimetric radar technology application
abstract: As an important supplement to the new generation of weather radar systems, X-band polarimetric radar has significant advantages in low-altitude and rapid-update observations. With increased demand on the meteorological services in mega-cities, the refined technology has been used to improve the radial resolution of the existing operational X-band polarimetric radar from 75 meters to 25 meters, aiming to explore and evaluate the potential of utilizing refined resolution X-band radar. The results indicate that after the application of refined technology, the radar can operate in real-time stably, with a sensitivity of approximately 15dBZ at a distance of 50 km. After the application of refined technology, the statistical analysis and standard deviation of various parameters of the radar are within acceptable ranges, and the data quality meets the operational requirements of the business. The data consistency between S-band radar and X-band radar is relatively high within the range of 20-35dBZ. The quantitative precipitation estimation accuracy within the effective detection range for heavy precipitation is higher than the operational resolution. Through application assessment, considerable potential of X-band radar in refined observation can be realized.

articleTitle: A modified genetic algorithm based on the monarch scheme for thinned planar array synthesis
abstract: Narrow main beam width and low peak sidelobe level (PSL) are essential for thinned planar array synthesis. This paper presents a modified genetic algorithm (GA) for thinned planar array synthesis, leveraging the advantage of both the monarch scheme and subarray division. On the one hand, the monarch scheme modifies the genetic operation. In detail, the optimal individual in the current population is crossed over all other even-digit individuals, and a new population is obtained via multi-point mutation. Then, the new population is merged with the current population and sorted according to the fitness function. Thus, the initial population of the subsequent genetic operation is obtained by eliminating the redundant individuals, which keeps the number of individuals constant. On the other hand, the proposed approach can reduce the individual dimension through subarray division with a square grid. The numerical simulation results verify the excellent efficiency of the proposed method in this paper.

articleTitle: Airborne pulse-Doppler radar moving target detection based on generalized image feature and deep learning
abstract: For airborne pulse-Doppler (PD) radar, this paper proposes an intelligent method for detecting moving targets without suppressing interferences (e.g., clutter, jamming, and noise). By analysing the feature difference between the target and interferences on the range-Doppler (RD) image, the proposed method defines a generalized target by combining multipath echoes and different target scatters. Then, the you-only-look-once (YOLO) deep learning network is trained with a simulated dataset to learn the unique generalized target image feature, hence discriminating the target from interferences for fast and reliable detection. Simulation and experiment results show that the proposed method can achieve high detection performance of moving targets.

articleTitle: A fast error phase correction algorithm for imaging radar based on dominant scatterers
abstract: Due to the influence of platform movement trajectory deviation, electromagnetic wave propagation path error and other factors, imaging radar echo data will inevitably contain error phase, causing defocus of imaging results. To solve this problem, this paper proposes a fast phase error correction algorithm for imaging radar based on dominant scatterers. By fully considering the spatial variability of the error phase and solving the problem through operations such as dominant scatterers optimization and azimuth error phases combination. This algorithm ensures the accuracy of error phase estimation while greatly improves the efficiency of the algorithm. Experimental results based on simulation data and measured data demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: A phase filtering method for airborne stripmap SAR based on piecewise polynomials and Akaike information criterion
abstract: Estimation noise can introduce errors in the autofocus results of synthetic aperture radar (SAR), particularly in phase curvature autofocus (PCA) techniques. High-order polynomial fitting is a commonly used approach to address this issue. However, the optimal polynomial order has not been discussed and polynomial fitting may not accurately approximate high - frequency functions. The study introduced Akaike’s information criterion (AIC) to determine the optimal polynomial order and aimed to enhance the inaccurate approximation of high-frequency functions using piecewise Legendre polynomial fitting. The effectiveness of the proposed method was validated through numerical simulations and C-band stripmap SAR real data.

articleTitle: Unsupervised polarization features selection network for polsar image change detection based on attention mechanism
abstract: Polarimetric synthetic aperture radar (PolSAR) can obtain rich polarization characteristics of observed targets. Therefore, its application to land cover change detection has become a research focus. Given the scarcity of polarization SAR data, this paper proposes an improved unsupervised PolSAR image change detection network, referred to as the Polarimetric Feature Selection Network (PFS-Net). In PFS-Net, using the channel attention mechanism, a simple and flexibly pluggable PFS block is designed to augment the polarization parameters of the target. These polarization parameters are fused with the spatial location to achieve the extraction and selection of specific polarization features of different ground objects. Then, the residual backbone network captures advanced semantic features, performs unsupervised clustering on deep features to obtain pseudo labels, and dynamically adjusts the weight of PFS-Net by calculating loss backpropagation through pseudo labels. An experiment based on the fully polarized data obtained from the fully polarised data of RADARSAT-2 on 23 May and 3 August 2013, which covers the farmland area in the Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region of China is carried out. The experiment result shows that the proposed algorithm can effectively improve the accuracy of the change detection results.

articleTitle: An efficient coherence-guided convolutional sparse coding method for interferometric phase restoration
abstract: Recently, complex convolutional sparse coding (ComCSC) has demonstrated its effectiveness in interferometric phase restoration, owing to its prominent performance in noise mitigation and detailed phase preservation. By incorporating the estimated coherence into ComCSC as prior knowledge for re-weighting individual complex residues, coherence-guided complex convolutional sparse coding (CoComCSC) further improves the quality of restored phases, especially over heterogeneous land-covers with rapidly varying coherence. In this paper, we propose an efficient solver to decrease the computational cost of solving the linear system subproblem within ComCSC-based optimization problems. By comparing the proposed method to other state-of-the-art methods using both simulated and real data, the proposed method demonstrates its effectiveness. Additionally, the proposed solver has the potential to improve optimization speed by approximately 10% compared to the state-of-the-art solver.

articleTitle: Micro-Doppler-based method for rotor parameter estimation under short dwell time conditions
abstract: Accurate rotor parameter estimation is crucial for identifying the category and model of aerial targets. Most existing studies rely on continuous target observation, which is challenging for phased array radar systems due to the need to balance tracking an d search data rates, thereby limiting the duration of target observation. To address this, this paper introduces a method for rotor parameter estimation under conditions of short dwell time. A parameterized phase compensation factor is designed based on the mathematical model of rotor target echoes, and phase compensation is applied to the intercepted echo signals. This approach effectively transforms the problem of rotor parameter estimation into one of micro-Doppler signal parameter matching. Simulation experiments conducted in this study demonstrate the feasibility and accuracy of this method. The results indicate that even under conditions of low SNR and short dwell time, this method can accurately estimate parameters such as rotor blade rotation speed and length for various target types, including helicopters and rotor drones. Notably, this method exhibits significantly improved noise resistance compared to existing methods.

articleTitle: Coherent integration for passive radar based on sparse representation and atomic norm minimization
abstract: Passive radar (PR) systems utilize available illuminators of opportunity as signal sources to perform detection, tracking, and imaging tasks. Increasing the coherent integration time is the main way to improve the detection ability of passive radar. Compared with classic coherent integration methods based on cross-correlation, sparse representation (SR) based methods have the advantage of reducing sidelobes. In this paper, we propose an improved SR-based coherent integration method, in which sparse reconstructions are performed separately in Doppler and range dimensions. In Doppler sparse reconstruction, a range migration correction factor is introduced to solve the range migration problem. In the sparse reconstruction of the range dimension, the continuous sparse reconstruction based on the atomic norm is applied to overcome the offgrid problem brought by the traditional SR-based methods. Numerical simulation results show that the proposed method is superior to existing SR- based PR processing methods.

articleTitle: Rotational status inversion of asteroids based on ellipsoidal model
abstract: Optical telescopes and ground-based radar are essential tools for celestial object detection. Optical data can be used to infer the rotational characteristics of asteroids but cannot provide small-scale three-dimensional shapes of asteroids. Ground-based radar can offer high-resolution delay-Doppler images, allowing for the reconstruction of small-scale asteroid structure and rotational characteristics. However, this inversion method relies on initial values provided by optical measurements regarding the rotational state. For asteroids without long-term accumulated optical data, the parameter range to be inverted increases dramatically with existing methods. Moreover, due to significant parameter coupling, the inversion accuracy significantly decreases. To address this issue, we propose a method for initializing rotational parameters using ellipsoidal shape representation in the absence of optical data. We apply the PSO optimization algorithm and validate the effectiveness of this method through numerical simulations. Index terms—Delay-Doppler images, ellipsoid, shape modeling, rotational measurement.

articleTitle: A single-frame velocity disambiguation algorithm for FMCW radar with high-precision ranging
abstract: Velocity ambiguity is a common problem in detecting high-speed moving targets for automotive frequency-modulated continuous-wave (FMCW) radars. The traditional velocity estimation algorithm ignores the walking information of the distance so that the velocity information is only extractable from the phase. The 2π periodicity of the angle limits the phase, so the velocity ambiguity phenomenon will appear. This paper proposes a single-frame velocity disambiguation algorithm for FMCW radar with high-precision ranging. The proposed algorithm utilizes the velocity information in the frequency term by high-precision ranging to avoid velocity ambiguity. In addition, the Crámer-Rao bound (CRB) for velocity estimation is derived, and simulation experiments verify the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Frequency-converted injection-locked optoelectronic oscillator based on delay matching
abstract: A frequency-converted injection-locked optoelectronic oscillator (OEO) with delay matching to eliminate the additional phase noise introduced by the externally-injected signal is proposed and experimentally demonstrated. In the OEO, the modulated signal from a dual-drive electro-optic modulator driven by both the oscillation signal and the injected signal is divided into two branches, where one branch is used to maintain the oscillation in the cavity, and the other one after frequency conversion in a photodetector is used to generate a pure frequency-converted injection signal. Owing to the frequency-conversion-based injection locking effect, the side-mode suppression ratio of the proposed OEO can be greatly improved. In addition, the phase noise deterioration induced by the externally-injected signal can be effectively eliminated when the time delays of the two branches are well matched. In the experiment, a pure single-tone microwave signal at 9.99686 GHz is generated, where the side-mode suppression ratio and the phase noise are measured to be 82 dB and −130 dBc/Hz@10 kHz, respectively.

articleTitle: High frequency data acquisition design algorithm based on hierarchical optimization of GNSS-InBSAR
abstract: In the Global Navigation Satellites System-based bistatic Interferometry Synthetic Aperture Radar(GNSS-InBSAR) system, the resolution of the imaging results is affected by the bistatic configuration, while the bistatic configuration is affected by the time, satellite illuminate source, and the location of the detection area, which leads to high-precision uniform deformation observations of the detection area are very poor for the majority of the one repeat-pass period. In order to uniformly observe the surface deformation of the detection area, this paper proposed a high-frequency data acquisition design algorithm based on hierarchical optimization of GNSS-InBSAR. First, based on the high-frequency data acquisition optimization model, the experimental time is calculated. Second, uniform grouping of experimental times by using the acquisition time interval as constraint. Third, a group of the time uniformity maximization is calculated by Position Dilution of Precision(PDOP) as constraints and replacement of periods that do not meet the PDOP threshold using the nearest replacement principle, so high-frequency acquisition time that meets the requirements can be obtained. The high-frequency deformation retrieval monitoring of the region is realized, Finally the measured data verifies the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: NR-ADMM-Net: a noise robust time-frequency enhancement method
abstract: Time-frequency analysis is often used to process the echoes of micro-motion targets. However, the traditional time-frequency analysis methods have some problems, such as low time-frequency resolution and poor noise robustness. In this paper, a method based on deep unrolling technique is proposed to realize time-frequency enhancement of micromotion signal. Firstly, the time-frequency distribution model of micro-motion signal is established and solved by the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) algorithm. Secondly, the ADMM algorithm is developed into a deep network using deep unrolling technology. In order to realize the robustness of the network to noise, a hypernetwork is introduced to learn the parameters of the algorithm, and a new loss function is proposed. Finally, the performance of the proposed method is tested on the 5-20dB simulated data set, and the reconstruction performance and robustness to noise of the proposed method are verified.

articleTitle: Three-dimensional imaging based on L-shaped antenna array with vortex electromagnetic wave
abstract: The vortex electromagnetic three-dimensional imaging method based on linear distributed antenna array has the problems of resolution deterioration under large elevation conditions. In order to solve this issue, the bistatic observation model of L-shaped array is proposed, then the echo signal model based on L-shaped array is derived and an improved three-dimensional imaging method is given. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed imaging method is verified by simulation experiments. The simulation results show that the proposed method significantly improves the resolution under large elevation conditions of elevation resolution.

articleTitle: Spatially varying sidelobe suppression for spaceborne SAR terrain matching curved imaging
abstract: The terrain matching curved (TMC) imaging is a promising technique to observe the long curved terrain efficiently. By adjusting the beam in azimuth and range simultaneously, a curved swath matching with the long curved terrain can be generated, achieving high efficient data acquisition. However, due to the complex beam steering in the TMC imaging, the Doppler bandwidth and the sidelobe direction of the image are spatially varied among the long curved terrain, resulting in a failure of sidelobe suppression using the sidelobe suppression traditional method. To solve this problem, a new spatially varying sidelobe suppression method is proposed in this paper. By calculating the Doppler history of targets during the beam illumination, a spatially variable window adapting to the Doppler bandwidth variation can be designed accurately, achieving sidelobe suppression in the TMC imaging effectively. The validity of the proposed algorithm is verified by simulation.

articleTitle: Surfacelet-IHS transform-based fusion of SAR and optical video
abstract: SAR and optical videos can provide complementary information about the area of interest. The traditional video fusion method has the problems of temporal information loss, image artifacts and large computation. In order to better display the fusion effect of 3D video signals, a new video fusion algorithm based on Surfacelet-IHS transform is proposed. The source video is subjected to IHS and Surfacelet transforms[1]. Meanwhile, the fusion rule based on structural similarity and brightness difference is applied to the obtained low-frequency components, while the fusion rule based on improved Laplacian energy is applied to the high-frequency components. The fusion result is then obtained by Surfacelet and IHS inverse transforms. Experimental results show that the fusion videos obtained using this algorithm have significantly improved visual effects and evaluation metrics. Additionally, spatial structure information and spectral information are effectively preserved, which is helpful for subsequent target detection and recognition tasks. In addition, the proposed algorithm is highly efficie nt and thus has practical application value in the field of real-time video fusion.

articleTitle: A novel azimuth ambiguity suppression algorithm for ship monitoring
abstract: The azimuth ambiguity causes undesired false targets on the synthetic aperture radar images, which impacts the ship monitoring and detection. Traditional filter-based methods that aim to suppress the azimuth ambiguity rely on tedious processing parameters to construct filters. The suppression performance declines when the parameters applied for the filter calculation deviate from the nominal values. To remove the false alarms that disturb the ship monitoring, a novel azimuth ambiguity suppression algorithm based on deep learning is proposed to achieve stable and reliable azimuth ambiguity suppression and improve the ship detection. The proposed algorithm applies the specially designed ambiguous energy estimation network for the ambiguous energy estimation in the range-Doppler domain. The mean shift algorithm is used to select the less polluted sub-spectra based on the estimation result. The less polluted sub-spectra are extrapolated to the complete spectrum. After the inverse Fourier transform, the optimized image is obtained, of which the ambiguous energy is supressed and the resolution is maintained. Experiments based on the TerraSAR-X images are carried on to verify the performance of the proposed algorithm and the improvement on the ship detection.

articleTitle: SARViT: vision transformer for SAR image interpretation with efficient model compression for time-real processing
abstract: The synthetic aperture radar (SAR) images provide all-time and all-weather observation for the earth, which has become one of important techniques for remote sensing (RS). Recently, the large-scale vision transformers (ViT) have made significant progress for natural image processing due to their good scalability and representations. However, how to deploy the ViT for SAR image processing has not been explored. In this paper, we firstly resort to ViT with large-scale SAR images for model pretraining and then attempt to fine-tune the model tailored to downstream tasks for investigating how such large models perform. Moreover, in order to meet the requirement of online time-real processing on the satellite, we then develop a method of the knowledge distillation for model compression from 320M to 36M, which can significantly reduce the computational cost and memory footprint while reserve good representations. The experimental results of downstream tasks including scene classification, object detection and building segmentation show state-of-the-art performance compared to existing methods. Further experiments for compressed models also show the competitive results in terms of accuracy and computational complexity.

articleTitle: Retrodirective cross-eye jamming based on the phase-conjugating array
abstract: Monopulse technology is widely employed in various fields such as target tracking and missile guidance, due to its exceptional accuracy in angular measurement and its robustness against interference. Relevant countermeasures have become a hot topic in the field of modern electronic warfare. Among them, cross-eye jamming (CEJ) stands out as the most effective pattern against monopulse radars, as it artificially enhances the angular glint with a long effective jamming time and high reliability. Nevertheless, the classic CEJ technique based on the Van Atta array suffers from certain limitations, including significant delays and limited applicability to certain radar types. To improve the applicability of CEJ systems, the incorporation of a phase conjugate array (PCA) is considered. Theoretical analysis and simulation experiments of the PCA-based retrodirective CEJ (PCA-RCEJ) are performed, building upon a review of the classic theory of two-element retrodirective cross-eye jamming (TRCEJ). The results demonstrate that PCA-RCEJ offers distinct benefits in terms of delay and applicability scenarios when compared to the classic CEJ technique. However, the adoption of PCA-RCEJ requires dealing with a more intricate system structure and facing challenges in parameter selection.

articleTitle: Deep unfolding network for sparse SAR imaging based on compound regularization
abstract: How to get an accurate image of multi-class targets scene is the key to synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imaging research. In sparse SAR imaging, compound regularization constrains multi-class target features by setting multiple regularizations prior to the model. However, the solution method based on a traditional iterative algorithm needs to set parameters manually and has a large number of iterations. In this paper, a novel SAR imaging method for the l1 norm and the total variation (TV) compound regularization based on a deep unfolding network (DUN) is proposed. The l1 norm and TV compound regularization can promote the sparsity and despeckle at the same time. Besides, the deep unfolded network can learn iteration parameters in a data-driven manner to speed up convergence. Finally, real SAR data experiments can verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Efficient beamforming method in IRS-assisted sparse UAV swarms
abstract: The intelligent reflective surface (IRS) is considered a potential technology in future radar systems. In this paper, we investigate the application of multiple IRSs to improve the unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) detection performance. The purpose of our design is to reduce the cost of an aerial large-aperture array system while enhancing the beamforming ability in the target direction. A signal model is established for the target detection by hanging IRS on the UAV, taking the presence of obstacles between the transmitter and the target into account. The theoretical analysis shows that the received power can be maximized by setting the IRS in the positions near the transmitter. Moreover, a novel sparse-based IRS distribution optimization method is proposed using a genetic algorithm and Gaussian process regression. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms the conventional methods in terms of performance and computational efficiency.

articleTitle: Calibration method for gain-phase errors of HFSWR based on sea clutter
abstract: We propose a passive calibration method for gain-phase errors of HFSWR by using the sea clutters as candidate calibration sources. We regard the sea clutters as interesting signals and introduce an extraction method which can be divided into two steps. The first step is to extract the first-order sea clutter spectrum based on the signal-to-noise ratio, and the second step is to extract the single-source spectrum points in the first-order sea clutter spectrum. Based on the single-source sea clutter points, we estimate the value of the gain-phase errors by the iterative calibration method. Experimental results demonstrate the correctness of our proposed method: the DOA estimation result after calibration is closer to the azimuth of the real target, and the amplitude of the spatial spectrum is also higher.

articleTitle: Radar HRRP clutter suppression method based on cascade of anomaly detection and binary accumulation
abstract: In the field of automatic target recognition (ATR) for radar high-resolution range profile (HRRP), the effectiveness of recognition is usually limited by the signal-to-clutter ratio (SCR), which is mainly due to the influence of clutter on the target features during feature extraction, resulting in the extracted features not being entirely from the target, but a mixture of target and clutter features. To address this problem, this paper proposes an HRRP clutter suppression method based on cascade of anomaly detection and binary accumulation, which first excludes the isolated clutter with outlier features in the HRRP, and then removes the remaining clutter with noise characteristics on this basis to obtain a more robust target HRRP. Based on the simulated comparison with the real data, the algorithm of this paper is applied to the HRRP of the corner reflector and truck has better clutter suppression effect and smaller computation amount, which has strong engineering practical value.

articleTitle: Estimation and calibration of UAV trajectory deviation for through-wall radar detection
abstract: The small Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) equipped with Frequency-Modulated Continuous Wave (FMCW) Radar can flexibly detect the enclosed environments within high-rise buildings by through-wall detection and thus has been widely studied recently. However, mini-UAVs are susceptible to large and complex trajectory deviations caused by environmental disturbances. Such deviations with complex pattern significantly affect both the envelope and phase of the radar echoes. Traditional algorithms for compensating motion errors are ineffective. This article introduces a self-focusing algorithm that relies on Back Projection (BP) imaging results. The algorithm performs iterative optimization based on the linear properties of the wall and the image contrast of the distributed multi-objectives behind the wall. Instead of estimating the 2D space-variation phase error, trajectory deviations in the line-of-sight direction and along the heading are estimated and compensated in two steps. In cases where the trajectory deviates larger than the range resolution, the algorithm can effectively estimate and compensate for large deviations, achieving estimation accuracy at the range resolution level.

articleTitle: High-precision DSM-based algorithm for SAR absolute radiation calibration
abstract: Radiation calibration is crucial for synthetic aperture radar (SAR) images, but it faces limitations due to the limited availability of corner reflectors. In this paper, we introduce an innovative algorithm to determine the absolute radiation calibration coefficient for SAR images using high-precision Digital Surface Model (DSM). This algorithm adapts to more common observation scenarios, reducing its dependence on reflectors. Firstly, the DSM is employed for target geolocation, providing precise local incidence angle information closely tied to the backscatter coefficient. Secondly, specific land cover types (such as forests, bare soil, or water bodies) are estimated based on a priori scattering model and local incidence angle. Finally, the absolute radiometric calibration coefficient is calculated by comparing observed and theoretical backscatter coefficients. This study utilized the DSM product and SAR image from China's first interferometric spaceborne synthetic aperture radar (InSAR) system, "Tianhui-2," to validate the algorithm's accuracy. Experimental results demonstrate an estimation accuracy exceeding 0.3 dB for the absolute radiation calibration coefficient.

articleTitle: A polarization HRRP target classification method based on one-dimensional convolutional attention neural network
abstract: High resolution range profile (HRRP) signal can represent the structure information of observed targets, and it can be easy obtained. And for the polarization HRRP signals, the polarization information can further display the symmetry, spatial orientation and physical property. Using HRRP signals to classify targets has been widespread concern and has been applied in military and civilian fields. Traditional classification methods always extract handmade features, and then choose a classifier for target classification. With the extensive performance improvement of neural network in fields, this paper introduces the neural network into HRRP classification and proposes a polarization HRRP target classification method based on one-dimensional convolutional attention neural network. Considering the data representation on HRRP, the proposed method employs one-dimensional neural network operators. The network backbone is composed of spindle-shaped residual blocks. And in the spindle-shaped residual blocks, an attention module is added to enhance the target representation. Experiment results show that the proposed method obtains more high classification accuracy than traditional methods in multiple datasets.

articleTitle: Foundation PIT deformation measurement technique based on ground-based interferometric radar
abstract: The deformation monitoring data of foundation pit is an important criterion for forecasting and strengthening measures in the field of building safety. During the construction period, the foundation pit will be affected by load, temperature change, random disturbance and other effects to produce deformation. Due to the complex deformation process of foundation pit, it is hard to accurately describe and separate the load trend deformation and elastic thermal deformation by mathematical expression. Excessive thermal deformation may cause cracks in the surrounding pavement and affect the judgment of load deformation. This paper first introduces the deformation measurement method of foundation pit based on differential interferometry technology using ground-based interferometric radar. Based on the obtained deformation type, the simulation verifies the separation effect of wavelet transform on different deformation trends and periodic components. Through the foundation pit deformation monitoring experiment of Tongzhou infrastructure project, the wavelet transform method is used to decompose the foundation pit deformation curve, and the extracted periodic component has good consistency with the temperature information.

articleTitle: Automatic fusion method of SAR image and electronic road map based on road network extraction
abstract: Effective fusion of SAR (Synthetic Aperture Radar) image and electronic road map could provide more abundant battlefield information for battlefield surveillance and command system during the process of ground reconnaissance. While poor fusion effects are usually obtained due to the invalid extraction of road network from SAR image. In order to improve the performance of such fusion and further provide battlefield target information promptly, this paper presents an automatic fusion method of SAR image and electronic road map based on road network extraction. Automatic edge detection algorithm of main road network from real-time SAR image is first developed. And then road line elements are extracted and connected based on Hough transform and region growing algorithm, respectively. Based on the above results, image matching of main road network and electronic map is realized, followed by which, registration and fusion of such road network and electronic road map is conducted. This method could complete automatically detection and extraction of main road network from SAR image which is provided by imaging system, and further provide comprehensive combat scenario situation to assist pilot in emergency response, real-time strike, and evaluation of damage effects.

articleTitle: A multi-agent jamming decision-making method based on SP-HASAC
abstract: In the study of the multi-UAV penetration mission decision method, the Heterogeneous Agent Soft Actor-Critic algorithm uses the HAML framework and the maximum entropy principle to enable UAVs to have stronger anti-jamming capability and exploration capability. However, it is difficult to accurately evaluate the action value of UAVs and the training stability is poor. To address this issue, this paper proposes a multi-agent based on the state prediction-HASAC (SP-HASAC) jamming decision method. Based on the idea of advantage function decomposition and environmental dynamics model, the state prediction network is designed to extract more abundant spatial information of penetration battlefield and achieve accurate evaluation of the action value of multi-UAV. Combining with the negative domain activation theory, the ReLU function is improved to realize the stable training of multi-UAV. The simulation results show that in the electronic penetration scenario of three UAVs against a single radar, the training convergence time of the proposed improved algorithm is reduced by 22% compared with the original algorithm. Three UAVs penetration to twice the burn-through distance still has more than 70% penetration success rate.

articleTitle: Modular subarrayed large-element-spacing array design utilizing gradient optimization
abstract: This paper proposes a novel modular subarray design composed of large-element-spacing elements. The large-element-spacing array technique is a way to reduce the cost of phased radar. However, the traditional large-element-spacing array design is always non-modular, which brings about inconvenience for design, manufacture, assembly, and maintenance. The proposed design uses basic module units of one type to form the whole aperture and can, therefore, reduce the cost while achieving modularity. By rotating the basic unit and adjusting the subarray's position in the basic unit, an array with an arbitrary shape is formed, and the grating lobe is suppressed. Gradient algorithm is utilized to optimize the array structure. Numerical simulations and analysis are provided to verify the effectiveness of the proposed design.

articleTitle: Respiration estimation for indoor human via commodity WiFi based on time-frequency analysis
abstract: In this article, we use WIFI signals to estimate the human respiratory rate. We propose a method for estimating static human respiration rate using CSI signals. We perform continuous wavelet transform on the CSI signal to obtain a time-frequency graph, and propose the Breath-net to learn the features related to respiration in the time-frequency graph. Finally, the Breath-net estimates the respiration rate. The results show that the average absolute error of this method for predicting respiratory rate can reach approximately 0.2 bpm.

articleTitle: Joint location design and resource allocation for integrated sensing and semantic communication
abstract: In this paper, the problem of fair semantic spectrum efficiency optimization for an integrated sensing and semantic communication is investigated. In the considered model, an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) is served as a base station to serve multiple users, where the UAV simultaneously senses the target and transmits information to the users. Due to limited wireless resource, both sensing accuracy and limited communication resource constraints are involved. This joint communication, sensing, and computation optimization problem is formulated as an optimization problem whose goal is maximize the fair spectrum efficiency of the system through optimizing the transmit beamforming, semantic compression ratio, power allocation, and UAV location. To solve this problem, an alternating algorithm is proposed with optimizing four subproblems iteratively, i.e., user allocation subproblem, semantic compression ratio optimization subproblem, UAV trajectory optimization subproblem, and integrated sensing and semantic transmission beamforming optimization subproblem. Simulation results verify the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: An optical to SAR transformation method for SAR image augmentation
abstract: Compared to optical images, synthetic aperture radar (SAR) data is more expensive to acquire and SAR imaging is susceptible to factors such as azimuth angles, wavelength, and polarization, resulting in insufficient SAR data. However, with the widespread application of deep learning techniques in SAR interpretation, there is a growing demand for larger SAR datasets. Therefore, utilizing optical data for SAR data generation holds significant practical value.This paper proposes a SAR image augmentation method by transforming optical images to SAR images through a transformer framework. In order to make the generative network better keep geometric and scattering characteristic, SIFT keypoints are extracted from optical and generated SAR images, respectively, for similarity measurement. Contrastive learning is also introduced into the network to refine the quality of the generated SAR images. In this paper, experiments have been conducted on optical dataset VEDIA, and a SAR dataset collected in Zhuzhou, Hunan, China. The quality of the generated SAR images is evaluated by calculating the scattering intensity difference and attribute scattering center (ASC) similarity between the original and generated SAR images. Experiments show that the scattering intensity difference for the proposed method is lower than 3.13 dB, and ASC similarity is higher than 82.67% , which means the proposed optical-to-SAR tranformation method is effective.

articleTitle: CPU+GPU architecture radar real-time signal processing method based on signal description technology
abstract: Due to the rapid development of information technology, high requirements for radar real-time performance. The real-time processing technology of the radar signal based on the CPU+GPU architecture has greatly improved the system simulation speed, but there is still room for optimization and progress. Use signal description word technology to further accelerate the simulation by reducing the number of interaction and interaction content between the CPU and the GPU. While ensuring the accuracy of the radar signal processing, the effectiveness of the method is verified through the comparison of the CPU, GPU, and GPU data transmission time. In the end, this method is more than 2.3 times faster than the traditional CPU+GPU calculation method.

articleTitle: A new estimator for the number of high-dimensional signals using ratio of higher-order moments
abstract: This paper provides a novel estimation procedure for determining the number of high-dimensional complex-valued signals embedded in Gaussian white noise. Initially, this problem is formulated as a sequence of nested hypothesis tests. To enhance the decision performance, we introduce new test statistics based on the ratio of the fourth- and square second-order moments of the population covariance eigenvalues. This enables us to leverage higher-order moments information in the observed data, distinguishing it from conventional tests that rely solely on the first and second order moments. In the context of high-dimensional, complex-valued data and within a sub-sphericity testing framework, unbiased and consistent estimates are derived for these two higher-order moments. Subsequently, we conduct an asymptotic analysis to incoporate these estimates into the construction of the test statistics and the design of our proposed estimation scheme for determining the number of sources. Finally, numerical examples are presented to show its effectiveness and superiority over several classical estimation methods.

articleTitle: Optical knowledge assisted unsupervised cross-domain SAR target detection
abstract: Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) based synthetic aperture radar (SAR) target detection methods have garnered attention in recent years. However, labeled SAR images are scarce and expensive to acquire, making training CNNs challenging. In this paper, an unsupervised cross-domain SAR target detection method with the assistance of the knowledge of the labeled optical domain is proposed. Our method gradually improves the performance of the detector in the unlabeled SAR target domain from three stages. At the first stage, to reduce visual dissimilarity between optical and SAR images, the Optical-to-SAR generative adversarial network (GAN), namely Opt2SAR GAN with skip layer is proposed to generate labeled fake SAR images. At the second stage, the adversarial learning strategy is employed to make the detector learn the domain invariant features between the two domains. At the last stage, to alleviate domain-bias problem, we use pseudo-labels predicted by the detector of the second stage to learn more discriminative representations of the SAR domain. To further alleviate the impact of wrong pseudo-labels, we select confident pseudo-labels according the image uncertainty and proposal uncertainty. Experiments on two cross-domain detection datasets of vehicles and ships demonstrate the effectiveness of our method.

articleTitle: Threshold-free adaptive open-set classifier for SAR target recognition
abstract: Many synthetic aperture radar (SAR) automatic target recognition (ATR) techniques are constrained by the closed-set environment assumption, resulting in a failure to detect targets from novel categories. To address the challenges of SAR ATR in an open world, we propose a threshold-free adaptive open-set classifier (TfAOsC) for SAR open set recognition (OSR). With the help of generative adversarial network (GAN), the proposed TfAOsC adaptively transforms the OSR task into a K+1-way classification problem, achieving both known class classification and unknown class identification without a predefined threshold. First, to generate diverse SAR images of unknown classes, Kullback–Leibler (KL) divergence is leveraged to enlarge the difference between generated image pairs sharing the same label. Moreover, we design a multi-task optimization loss to enhance the recognition performance of the proposed method. Experimental results on moving and stationary target acquisition (MSTAR) and synthetic and measured paired and labeled experiment (SAMPLE) datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method over some state-of-the-art open-set SAR target recognition approaches.

Index Terms: Area Under Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve

articleTitle: Joint frequency and PRF agility waveform design and signal coherent accumulation against cross-pulse repeater deception jamming
abstract: Active deception jamming plays a dangerous role for the moving target detection in modern radar system. The false target generated by active deception jamming is extremely confusing for target identification. Frequency and pulse repetition frequency (PRF) agile waveforms have been widely applied in radar systems to improve anti-jamming capabilities of radar. However, the random phase fluctuation caused by frequency and PRF agility leads to the range -azimuth coupling of echoes, which makes it difficult to estimate motion parameters and achieve target coherent accumulation. In this article, in order to improve the detection performance of moving target in interference environment, we propose a novel joint frequency and PRF agility waveform (JFPAW) with characteristics of equivalent coherent waveform (ECW). In especial, the echo signals are divided into different groups according to the PRF of ECW, and then coarse velocity estimation of the target is performed based on minimum image entropy in the coherent echoes of ECW. After range walk correction in all groups by coarse velocity, an improved nonuniform discrete Fourier transform (NDFT) algorithm for coherent integration of the JFPAW is proposed to effectively detect the moving target in complex electromagnetic environments.

articleTitle: An adaptive OS-CFAR detector for dynamic group targets
abstract: Effective detection of group targets is of great significance to people's livelihood and national security. Flocks of birds, UAV swarms and other group targets are closely spaced in the radar beam and have high dynamics, which can easily lead to the mismatch of the traditional detector parameters and missed detection. Therefore, in this paper, to solve this problem, we established the detection model of the corresponding scene, derived the probability density function expression of the threshold, and proposed the OS-CFAR detector parameter correction method with the expectation of the maximum number of detected targets as the optimization criterion. Taking the OSPA distance as the detection performance index, the detection performance under different detection parameters is compared to verify the effectiveness of this algorithm, and the experiments show that the algorithm proposed in this paper can effectively reduce the target missed detection in the group targets scene.

articleTitle: A long-time coherent integration method for marine moving target detection with GNSS-S radar
abstract: A frequency bin second-order Radon Fourier transform (FBSoRFT) long-time coherent integration method is proposed in this paper, and it is used for GNSS scattered signal-based radar (GNSS-S radar) detection of marine moving targets. FBSoRFT algorithm firstly searches and compensates Doppler rate for the echo after pulse compression in the slow time-range frequency domain, and then realizes the coherent integration of the target energy by fast Radon Fourier transform (FBRFT). Standard SoRFT method realizes the coherent integration of target energy through the three-dimensional parameter search of initial distance, Doppler center frequency and Doppler rate, while FBSoRFT only needs to carry out one-dimensional parameter search of Doppler rate. Compared with the standard SoRFT, the computational efficiency is greatly improved. An experiment using GNSS-S radar for marine moving targets detection is conducted, and it verifies that the FBSoRFT can effectively improve the detection capability of marine moving targets.

articleTitle: Weak energy interference suppression in InSAR image using semantic segmentation network
abstract: Spaceborne interferometric synthetic aperture radar (InSAR) satellite, serves multiple industries, including land management, earthquake analysis, mapping, environmental monitoring, disaster reduction, and forestry. However, the presence of radio frequency interference (RFI) makes it difficult to obtain high-quality digital elevation model (DEM) and to perform deformation monitoring. In this paper, a RFI suppression model based on Residual Attention UNet (RA-UNet) is proposed for the Lutan-1 ground processing system, which is capable of processing massive images quickly and efficiently. The model combines attention mechanism and residual block to quickly focus on the changes in the local interference region, and uses UNet to extract the interference features in the spectrum to distinguish the interference. Under different RFI conditions, a wide range of experimental results are provided in different scenarios of the real measured data of Lutan-1, including single-pass and repeat-pass modes. The experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness, efficiency and robustness of the proposed method in interference suppression.

articleTitle: A novel illumination normalization based on 2D recursive convex optimization
abstract: Illumination normalization is fundamental and critical to image preprocessing in terms of improving Signal to Clutter Ratio (SCR), contrast, etc. Whereas previous studies mostly focused on image sequence, we propose in this paper a new approach that deals with a single image with uneven illumination.
