The proposed approach firstly performs image division based on the Auto Regressive Moving Average (ARMA) model and then implements illumination normalization separately for different types of backgrounds applying a two-dimensional recursion convex optimization method. Unlike techniques based on consecutive frames, this method is capable of treating images with drastic changes in background yet requiring only mild assumption on the image, making it adaptable to various situations. Simulation results show its effectiveness in improving the contrast and SCR of an image.

articleTitle: Deformation field products generated using Lu Tan-1 over China
abstract: Lu Tan-1 (LT-1) has finished its in-orbit test at the beginning of 2023. We started to collect the data over China since June 22<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup> and have finished the second coverage on August 20<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup>. That allowed us to generate the differential interferometric SAR (DInSAR) products which are defined as deformation field. We have generated the deformation field product using DInSAR using 14546 stripmap 1 images and 1521 stripmap 2 images. In this paper, we show the initial results of the deformation field over China, and the typical deformation phenomena. GNSS data were used for accuracy assessment. The result is expected to be useful in geohazard monitoring.

articleTitle: A fast method for focusing azimuth cyclically interrupted SAR echo via deconvolution
abstract: Azimuth cyclically interrupted Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) echo exists in regard of novel radar task or sensor geometries. To focusing interrupted SAR echo, a number of algorithms based on solution of ill-posed problem are proposed. However, solving ill-posed problems usually consume large computing resource. In order to solve this issue, a novel fast method for focusing cyclically interrupted SAR echo is raised in this paper. The investigated method processes interrupted SAR echo by adding zeros operation, range migration based focusing, Point Spread Function (PSF) estimation and fast azimuth restoration via Richardson-Lucy deconvolution method. The proposed method can reduce illusory targets caused by azimuth interruption and operates much faster than method on basis of complex deconvolution via Complex Fast Iterative Shrinkage-Thresholding Algorithm (FISTA). Experimentations of simulation and veritable SAR data processing demonstrate the validity of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Compressive spectral imaging and its application
abstract: This paper introduces spectral imaging based on compressive sensing and its potential application. The principle of compressive sensing, modelling of Coded Aperture Snapshot Spectral Imaging (CASSI) system as well as reconstruction model of spectral images are introduced. To improve the reconstruction results, various coded apertures are proposed. The aperture design and its development are compared and summarized. Finally, the potential for application in other fields especially in aerospace field is analysed.

articleTitle: Computationally efficient coherent integration algorithm based on DBO for weak maneuvering target
abstract: In addressing the challenges of compensating for distance migration and Doppler frequency migration during long-time coherent integration, the generalized Radon-Fourier transform (GRFT) requires a multi-dimensional, joint parameter search to accurately detect the motion parameters of moving targets. However, this necessitates a geometric increase in computational complexity as the order of the echo signal model rises. To mitigate this, this paper proposes an optimization of the GRFT integration process based on the Dung Beetle Optimizer (DBO). This optimization technique swiftly fine-tunes the objective function parameters, thereby reducing both computational time and load to satisfy the requirements of real-time signal processing applications. The effectiveness of the proposed method is validated through simulation experiments and compared to Genetic Algorithms (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), which shows that the proposed method can efficiently obtain the integration results with low computational burden.

articleTitle: Interference mitigation for automotive radar in continuous wavelet transform domain
abstract: Interference mitigation is a crucial aspect of automotive radar research, especially in dense vehicle scenarios, where radar detection performance needs enhancement. This paper proposes a novel interference mitigation algorithm, the continuous wavelet transform and morphological component analysis (CWT-MCA). By converting the time-domain signal to the time-frequency domain, CWT-MCA achieves direct separation of target and interference components without requiring interference detection and identification. The paper compares the proposed algorithm with the traditional linear prediction method. Numerical simulations show that our algorithm excels in interference mitigation performance and computational efficiency, making it well-suited for real-time implementation in automotive radar systems.

articleTitle: A novel 3-D geometry reconstruction method of space target based on joint optical-and-ISAR observation
abstract: For a space target with unknown motion, it is difficult to reconstruct the three-dimensional(3-D) geometry without the prior information of the instantaneous attitude. To tackle this problem, this paper proposes a novel 3-D geometry reconstruction method based on a joint optical-and-inverse-synthetic-aperture-radar (ISAR) observation system. Firstly, the key points and mask of the target are extracted from each ISAR image and optical image. Then, the Doppler information is estimated from each ISAR image, followed by the 3-D orientation and length estimation of the key components of the space target combined with the isochronous optical image. Meanwhile, two-dimensional(2-D) alignment of the isochronous optical-and-ISAR images is performed. Next, the rotation and translation relationships of the space target between adjacent observation instants are derived, and 3-D alignment is subsequently executed. After that, the 3-D space is divided into small 3-D voxels and a voxel candidate will be judged as a real part of the space target if the projection positions of the voxel candidate are located in the target regions of each ISAR and optical image. Finally, all the reserved voxels constitute the 3-D geometry of the space target. Experimental results based on electromagnetic simulation data verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Research on radar image change detection based on weight denoising and discrete coefficient k-means clustering
abstract: Radar image change detection is to obtain the change information of ground objects according to the difference between images by analyzing and comparing two or more radar images in different periods of the same area. In the radar image change detection, the multiplicative speckle noise caused by the change of the echo intensity of the image itself pollutes the difference image, which increases the difficulty of detecting the deformation of the ground object. Therefore, this paper analyzes and studies the fusion and denoising of difference images in coherent coefficient image change detection. In this paper, a transform detection method based on wavelet transform difference image fusion based on weight denoising is proposed. This method combines the advantages of various difference images. Through wavelet decomposition and weight denoising, the processed wavelet coefficients are reconstructed to generate the final difference image. Finally, k-means based on discrete coefficients is used for clustering to obtain change detection images. Use the actual data of a mining area for change detection. The results show that the method proposed in this paper removes a large amount of noise, improves the robustness of the difference map construction, makes it easier to cluster, and the clustering results are more accurate.

articleTitle: A novel method for suppressing dense repeated jamming in frequency agile radar based on sparse recovery
abstract: Dense repeated jamming is highly correlated with radar transmitted signals, it produces both suppressive and deceptive interference effects, seriously threatening the detection efficiency of combat radar. Frequency agile radar greatly reduces the radar's anti-interference ability by rapidly changing the carrier frequency between pulses, but cannot completely suppress dense repeated jamming. To address this problem, a suppression method for dense repeated jamming is proposed based on sparse recovery. Firstly, the echo models of the target and dense repeated jamming are established under the frequency agile radar system, and the Kronecker product is utilized to transform the solving problem of multiple measurement vector models into single measurement vector models. Secondly, based on the partial pulse forwarding equivalent model of the interference signal under the frequency agile radar system, effective estimation of the direction of arrival (DOA) and time delay of the target and interference is achieved through sparse recovery algorithm. Then, based on the parameter estimation results, dense repeated jamming is reconstructed and removed from the radar echo. Finally, the effectiveness of the algorithm proposed in this paper is verified through simulation experiments.

articleTitle: Generalized sparsely index modulation OFDM for integrated sensing and communication waveform design
abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) is an attractive technology for efficient utilization of spectral and hardware resources, while designing the ISAC waveforms in meeting both radar and communication requirements is a critical issue. In this paper, orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) with generalized sparsely index modulation (OFDM-GSIM) is proposed. In the proposed OFDM-GSIM, subcarrier indices of in-phase and quadrature components are first activated independently, then the amplitude shift keying constellations are mapped to the active subcarriers to carry extra bits. Compressive sensing (CS) is implemented in active subcarriers at the radar receiver to realize the successful recovery of target parameters. Furthermore, an improved CS is applied to estimate the information carried by the real and imaginary components of OFDM-GSIM signals at the communication receiver. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed waveform improves the reliability and the peak-to-average power ratio.

articleTitle: Class-incremental SAR automatic target recognition using simulated data
abstract: Synthetic aperture radar automated target recognition (SAR ATR) approaches based on deep neural networks (DNN) have made great progress in recent years. However, the effectiveness of DNN models depends on a large number of independent and identically distributed measured SAR images, which is contrary to the SAR ATR in practice. Furthermore, while learning a series of new classes, DNN models suffer from catastrophic forgetting. Simulated data can be produced independently of measured data. We introduce simulated data into the class incremental learning of SAR ATR to address these issues. Specifically, we aim to continuously learn a sequence of new classes with a small amount of measured data and a large amount of simulated data. We found that simulated data can produce good performance in short-term incremental learning rather than long-term incremental learning. Then, we provided a novel class incremental learning method that uses feature regularization to reduce the distribution discrepancy between measured and simulated data and uses feature distillation to alleviate the catastrophic forgetting. Experimental results obtained on the MSTAR benchmark dataset and the Fast 3D-ISAR simulated dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of using simulated data in class-incremental SAR ATR.

articleTitle: A TRPCA based mutual interference mitigation method for FMCW millimetre-wave radar
abstract: In recent years, with the surge in the number of vehicles and the rapid development of autonomous driving technology, it has become a matter of great concern to perceive the surrounding environment to avoid traffic accidents. Millimetre-wave radar has become the mainstream of vehicle-mounted sensors with its unique advantages. However, the current automotive radar frequency band is limited to 76GHz-81GHz, the spectrum resources are quite intensive and will inevitably lead to mutual interference between radars, which is not conducive to further target detection, and even threatens the safety of public transportation. Therefore, this paper studies mutual interference between automotive frequency modulated continuous wave (FMCW) radars, and suppresses the mutual interference through an interference suppression algorithm based on tensor robust principal component analysis (TRPCA). Numerical experiments show that the proposed algorithm has a good interference suppression effect, and the performance of the proposed method is better than other related methods.

articleTitle: An ultra-low phase-noise frequency synthesizer in a package
abstract: This paper presents a low phase-noise 4 GHz frequency synthesizer designed for radar applications. The entire circuitry is encapsulated within a ceramic casing, achieving a compact form factor while maintaining minimized phase noise and spur levels. The design utilizes a step recovery diode (SRD) to implement a comb spectrum generator, achieving a 40-fold frequency multiplication of the reference signal. This direct high-order frequency multiplication method enhances phase noise performance. Additionally, the filtering circuit is implemented using film bulk acoustic resonator (FBAR) filters, This approach guarantees minimal spurious emissions in the output signal and enables module miniaturization. The measured phase noise performance is -127.98 dBc/Hz at 1 kHz offset from the carrier frequency of 4 GHz.

articleTitle: A quantitative estimation method of migrating insects using weather radar by high resolution radar joint observation
abstract: The main migration animals in China are insects, and a large number of large-scale seasonal migration insects have a great impact on ecology. The establishment of a comprehensive early warning system for migratory insects necessitates the implementation of large-scale macro monitoring. Among the array of methodologies available, weather radar stands out as an efficacious tool for facilitating extensive macro-level monitoring. Nonetheless, several unresolved challenges persist in accurately quantifying the density of vast insect populations on a large scale. This article introduces an innovative method for insect quantification through the collaborative use of weather radar and high-resolution phased array radar for insect target observation and joint data analysis. This novel method harnesses the collective observational data derived from both weather radar and high-resolution radar systems, harmonizing the temporal and spatial dimensions of these datasets. By establishing a nuanced mapping correlation between insect density and weather radar reflectivity, this method enables the determination of insect density within specific geographical regions. In the final part of this article, joint observation experiments were conducted to examine the experimental data collected from operating weather radar and specialized phased array radar systems. A total of 244 days of data were analysed, and the proposed method was rigorously validated.

articleTitle: Full aperture phase error estimation for spaceborne spotlight SAR
abstract: Spaceborne spotlight SAR adjusts beam direction in real-time through electrical scanning. Due to the fact that the virtual phase centers of the antenna with different beam directions are not completely consistent, a phase error that varies with the beam direction will be induced in the received echo. When the resolution is low, the impact of this phase error is always ignored. However, as the azimuth resolution reaches the sub meter level, th is phas e error will leads to azimuth defocusing. Accurate estimation of this phase error is necessary for high-precision imaging of s potlight SAR. Therefore, this paper proposes a high-accuracy full aperture phase errores timation method based on spotlight SAR echo. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of this method.

articleTitle: A track initiation method based on the combination of Kalman filtering and the transformer model
abstract: Aiming at the problem of track initiation of multiple moving targets in a strong clutter environment, this paper proposed a track initiation method based on the combination of Kalman filtering and the Transformer model. Firstly, Kalman filtering is used to filter the radar measurement data to generate a temporary track set containing real and false tracks, then the temporary track set is mapped into a set of spatio-temporal vectors that can reflect the track characteristics, and finally, the spatio-temporal vectors are input into the Transformer model for classification, so as to get real tracks to complete the track initiation. The Transformer model uses a position-coding layer and self-attention mechanism so that the model can directly capture the dependencies in the sequence and extract the motion characteristics of the target efficiently. The experimental results show that compared with t he traditional sequential processing methods and batch processing methods, this method can not only complete the track initiation in a shorter time but also has a higher track initiation rate and a lower error rate in the strong clutter environment, which is of great significance to target tracking.

articleTitle: Building structure reconstruction with UAV-borne through-wall radar
abstract: Through-wall radar (TWR) building structure reconstruction holds significant practical significance and research value in various fields, such as counter-terrorism operations, disaster relief, and surveillance. However, traditional TWR is a hand-held or vehicle-mounted equipment, which is challenging to use in tower blocks and complex terrain scenes. To solve the limitations of traditional TWR systems, this paper utilizes a TWR system equipped on a small multi-rotor unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) to perform synthetic aperture radar (SAR) mode scans and reconstruct building structures. First, this paper reviewed back-projection (BP) and range-Doppler (RD) algorithms for building structure reconstruction. Then, UAV-borne TWR was used to efficiently collect radar echoes from the front and side of building. Finally, BP and RD algorithms were employed to image wall layout with high-quality. The experiments show that UAV-borne TWR offers higher efficiency and convenience in complex scenes. The performed experiment further extends the conventional imaging scenarios. This paper demonstrates that building structure reconstruction with UAV-borne TWR is a feasible approach and has wild applications.

articleTitle: Joint design of the transmit and receive beamforming via non-iterative optimization for MIMO radar
abstract: The joint design of the transmit and receive beamforming for multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) radar systems is considered in the background of signal dependent interference. An optimization model using signal-to-interference-plus-noise-ratio (SINR) as a performance metric is designed under similarity cone, power, and energy constraints. An algorithm for simultaneous updating of transmit and receive (T-R) beamforming is presented, that bypasses the conventional T-R iteration and initialization, thus avoiding premature termination of the iteration or poor initialization. Simulation experiments verify the effectiveness of the method.

articleTitle: A high-resolution SAR imaging method with multi-frequency pulse diversity mode
abstract: To achieve the ultra-high-resolution Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) imaging, it is necessary to obtain ultra-wideband signals. However, it is difficulty for the traditional system to transmit ultra-wideband signal directly, which might increase the requirement of system hardware. In this paper, a method based on multi-frequency pulse diversity (MFPD) mode is proposed to ultra-high-resolution SAR imaging. In MFPD mode, a single channel transmits multiple waveforms from different frequency bands, and several receive channels which satisfy the condition of displaced phase center antenna. Thus, the echoes from different receive channels correspond to different subbands. Then, an ultra-high-resolution imaging can be obtained by spectrum splicing. In addition, a window function is designed for overlapping spectrum to achieve a better imaging performance. Simulation results demonstrate the excellent performance of this method.

articleTitle: A multi-frequency GPR data fusion technology based on end-to-end deep neural networks
abstract: As one of the most important non-destructive testing technologies, ground penetrating radar (GPR) technology detects the internal electromagnetic characteristics and distribution by transmitting electromagnetic waves. High-frequency electromagnetic waves have high resolution but shallow detectable depth, while low-frequency electromagnetic waves have wide detectable range but terrible resolution. In order to obtain GPR signals with both high resolution and great detectable depth, we propose a GPR multi-frequency data fusion technology based on end-to-end deep neural network. In the first part, the features of the A-scan echo signals at different scales are obtained through the convolutional layer. In the second part, these features are fused using maximum values. Finally, the high-dimensional information is decoded to return the A-scan signal. In our paper, compared with the original single-frequency signal, the fusion signal achieves higher resolution at greater depth.

articleTitle: Mainlobe deceptive jammer suppression based on quadratic pulse coding in FDA-MIMO radar
abstract: The problem of suppressing mainlobe deceptive jammers that spoof the radar systems by generating multiple false targets. To tackle this problem, the frequency diversity array-multiple-input multiple-output (FDA-MIMO) radar system is utilized. Firstly, by applying a quadratic phase code (QPC) in transmitted pulses of different elements, the true and false targets can be discriminated in the joint Doppler-transmit-receive frequency domain. Then, after decoding and principal range compensation, the jammers are equivalently distributed in the sidelobes of Doppler-transmit-receive domain. Finally, the jammers are suppressed by data-dependent Doppler-transmit-receive three-dimensional beamforming using singular spectrum analysis (SSA) technique. Numerical simulations demonstrate the performances of the developed jammer suppression method.

articleTitle: A new framework for extracting and using polarization information from fully polarized entomological radar
abstract: The fully polarized entomological radar is an effective tool for monitoring insect migration by obtaining target orientation, body length, and mass through polarization information. However, most previous methods for calculating insect parameters are obtained through the analysis of microwave anechoic chamber data, which often resulted in poor accuracy in the actual process. In this paper, we summarized the recently proposed polarization calibration methods, orientation estimation, and mass estimation methods for the fully polarized entomological radar and summarized a new entomological radar polarization signal processing framework. The proposed framework is applied to a fully polarized entomological radar and long-term accurate observation data has been obtained.

articleTitle: High-resolution sliding-spotlight spaceborne SAR imaging algorithm for Ka-band
abstract: High-band spaceborne SAR offers image-like optics and broadens the application range of microwave remote sensing on space-based platforms. The sliding-spotlight mode fulfils the high-resolution detection requirements for target recognition in remote sensing and has gained significant attention and application in the industry. Given the differences between high-band spaceborne SAR data processing and traditional low-band spaceborne SAR data processing in terms of orbital accuracy analysis, key parameter calculation of imaging, algorithm acceleration, and parallelization, this study conducts an analysis of data accuracy, imaging, and image quality using real data from Luojia-2. The results demonstrate that the proposed imaging process method achieves high-precision imaging of the sliding-spotlight SAR real data from Luojia-2.

articleTitle: An algorithm for separating moving targets from ground clutter based on beam pattern amplitude
abstract: Millimetre-wave sensors have become one of the core sensors for unmanned vehicles due to their advantages of being all -day, all-weather, miniaturized and low cost. Due to the motion of the unmanned vehicle platform, and the ground clutter an d the target change as the platform moves, resulting in uneven background noise and poor agreement. Meanwhile, many de - cluttering algorithms based on the consistency of the background cannot be applied. In this paper, we propose a beam pattern amplitude-based algorithm for moving target and ground spurious separation, which can effectively achieve moving target detection without increasing the computational effort. Both simulated and measured data demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: SAR imaging with traveling wave array antenna
abstract: Traveling-wave array antenna (TWAA) has the outstanding advantages of wide-band and low cost compared with standing-wave array antenna (SWAA). TWAA has been widely adopted by searching radars, but seldom adopted by synthetic aperture radar (SAR) because its beam dispersion characteristic makes the imaging processing very complicated. In this paper, the azimuthal beam dispersion problem has been focused for SAR imaging using TWAA. At first, the effect of azimuthal beam dispersion on SAR imaging has been analysed and based on which the imaging algorithm is developed for SAR with TWAA.

articleTitle: The Monte Carlo simulation of the radar received wave of the hypersonic vehicle with plasma sheath
abstract: Based on the physical optics a fast Monte Carlo method is introduced. It can simulate the radar received signal from the hypersonic vehicle with plasma sheath, and the interactions between the electromagnetic wave and plasma with complicate time or space dependent. Compared with other numerical algorithms and analytic solutions, the mean error of the results by this method is 1.5dB smaller than the others. In addition, for the hypersonic speed target, the deviation between the measured and the simulated radar received signals is very satisfied.

articleTitle: Counter-reconnaissance performance analysis of amplitude coded modulation radar waveform
abstract: The electronic reconnaissance systems can obtain intelligence information from technical parameters of radiation sources. Then, anti-radiation missiles can be used to destroy radiation sources, seriously threatening the survival of radar systems. To improve radar counter-reconnaissance capability, various waveforms are proposed. Among the waveforms, amplitude coded modulation (ACM) can divide the pulse into many short pulses. The signal sorting may fail so that the signal is difficult to be recognized. Therefore, the ACM signal can improve the counter-reconnaissance performance. However, the signal counter- reconnaissance performance has not been discussed. Thus, the uniform and non-periodic ACM model are proposed in this paper. Time-frequency distribution entropy and intercept probability of ACM signal are utilized to evaluate the counter-reconnaissance performance. Simulations are conducted to verify the accuracy of theoretical analysis.

articleTitle: Geosynchronous SAR 3-D target reconstruction based on multi-angle observation
abstract: Geosynchronous synthetic aperture radar (GEO SAR) has the ability of multi-angle observation, and the potential to reconstruct the three-dimensional (3-D) structure of target. To fully utilize this ability, a 3-D target reconstruction method based on multi-angle observation and forward projection is proposed. The core idea of the proposed method is to determine whether target exists on a 3-D position by forward projecting the 3-D position onto the multi-angle SAR images. The proposed method is well validated via simulation and real data experiment.

articleTitle: Optical and SAR image registration based on the intersection of shallow and deep scale feature points
abstract: There exist significant nonlinear radiometric differences between optical and SAR images, which often lead to the inability to select significant feature points. To address this issue, this paper proposes a refined registration method for optical an d SAR images based on the intersection of shallow and deep scale feature points. The method consists of three steps. Firstly, scale spaces are constructed for both optical and SAR images, and shallow-scale corners as well as deep-scale extreme points are extracted. Secondly, the Siamese Cross-Stage Partially Dense Network (Siamese-CSPDenseNet) is utilized to extract robust feature descriptors. Finally, feature points matching are performed on descriptors, and RANSAC is applied to remove outliers, then the final registration result can be obtained. The proposed method is evaluated on public datasets. The results demonstrate that the proposed method is superior to other state-of-the-art methods.

articleTitle: Hierarchical cross attention model for multi-modal HRRP recognition
abstract: The ease of processing, small data size, and rich target structural information associated with High-Resolution Range Profile (HRRP) have consistently positioned it as a research focal point in the Radar Automatic Target Recognition (RATR) field. However, most existing methods primarily focus on a single time domain (amplitude) feature, neglecting the time -dependent and multi-domain features of HRRP. In this regard, this paper proposes a multimodal hierarchical cross-attention model that combines recurrent and co-attention neural networks. Initially, the time and frequency domain representations are processed using a set of bidirectional recurrent neural network layers with self-attention, which can transform the dual-domain information of HRRP into fixed-dimensional embeddings. Additionally, the incorporation of co-attention layers integrates contextual information from both modalities, with the layer attempting to weigh the utterance level embeddings relevant to the task of HRRP target recognition. Finally, the neural network parameters in the time domain layer, frequency domain layer, and multimodal co-attention layer are hierarchically trained for the HRRP target classification task. The experimental results indicate that the algorithm can effectively learn the multi-domain temporal correlations of HRRP, thereby enhancing target recognition performance.

articleTitle: An improved FMCW synthetic aperture ladar imaging algorithm
abstract: Synthetic aperture ladar (SAL) is the combination of microwave synthetic aperture technology and laser coherent detection technology, which has better resolution than synthetic aperture radar (SAR). For SAL system, frequency modulated continuous wave (FMCW) is usually used to achieve large time-bandwidth product. In this article, an improved two-dimensional (2D) imaging method based for FMCW SAL is proposed. Firstly, we describe the FMCW SAL system structure. Secondly, a signal model of strip SAL imaging is established. Based on FMCW SAL features, the ωk algorithm is improved to compensate the intra pulse motion error and residual video phase (RVP), and the phase gradient autofocus (PGA) algorithm is introduced into SAL for motion compensation. Finally, 4km ground-based and airborne SAL experiments are completed, and the imaging results are displayed. The imaging results verify the effectiveness of the proposed method, which demonstrates the application potential of SAL in remote high-resolution earth observation.

articleTitle: Flexible multi-generator model with fused spatiotemporal graph for trajectory prediction
abstract: Trajectory prediction plays a vital role in automotive radar systems, facilitating precise tracking and decision-making in autonomous driving. Generative adversarial networks with the ability to learn a distribution over future trajectories tend to predict out-of-distribution samples, which typically occurs when the distribution of forthcoming paths comprises a blend of various manifolds that may be disconnected. To address this issue, we propose a trajectory prediction framework, which can capture the social interaction variations and model disconnected manifolds of pedestrian trajectories. Our framework is based on a fused spatiotemporal graph to better model the complex interactions of pedestrians in a scene, and a multi-generator architecture that incorporates a flexible generator selector network on generated trajectories to learn a distribution over multiple generators. We show that our framework achieves state-of-the-art performance compared with several baselines on different challenging datasets.

articleTitle: An improved measurement pixel selection method of GB-MIMO radar image applied for bridge vibration measurement
abstract: Ground-based multi-input multi-output (GB-MIMO) radar has significant advantages in bridge structural vibration parameter measurement due to its non-contact, high frame rate, and high-precision measurement characteristics. Due to the complexity of the environment, traditional methods of selecting pixels based on permanent scatterers (PS) cannot accurately obtain bridge structure pixels. This article proposes an improved classification method of the PS deformation curves to accurately select vibration pixels of bridge structures. Firstly, prescreen those PSs with small deformation amplitude as the first category. Secondly, for the screened PSs, the principal component analysis method is used to reduce the data dimension of their deformation curves to reduce the time consumption of clustering. Finally, the K-medoids algorithm is used to classify the screened PSs based on the dimensionality reduction data, and the Davis-Bouldin index is adopted to overcome the problem of local optimization. The experimental results of a large-scale bridge prove that the method proposed in this paper can effectively improve the speed of data processing while ensuring accurate pixel selection of the bridge structure.

articleTitle: A modified altitude estimation method for airborne SAR by multi-channel Doppler spectrum sharpening
abstract: A modified altitude estimation method for airborne SAR is proposed in this paper by multi-channel Doppler spectrum sharpening, to enhance both the along-track measurement resolution and the estimation robustness. A certain along-track measurement resolution is realized by Doppler sharpening, and the robustness of the estimation is improved by multi-channel clutter spectrum averaging. Simulation results show that this method has both good measurement resolution and robust estimation accuracy of the relative altitude for airborne SAR radar with both forward-looking view and down-looking view illuminations.

articleTitle: Joint pulse signal detection and DOA estimation algorithm based on eigenvalue distribution of sample autocorrelation matrix
abstract: Under the condition of Nyquist sampling, direction finding algorithm generally uses all time domain or frequency domain snapshots for direction finding, which is difficult to apply to passive applications where the time -frequency domain of the signal is unknown or the signal-to-noise ratio is very low. Aiming at the problem that the direction finding of pulse signal is without guidance in time domain, this paper proposes a direction estimation algorithm combined with pulse detection. The algorithm first determines the position of the pulse signal in time domain by using the largest eigenvalue distribution of the sample autocorrelation matrix, and then guides the direction finding in time domain. The joint estimated Cramer-Rao Bound is also derived. Simulation results show that the estimation performance of the proposed algorithm is significantly better than that of the direction finding algorithm without pulse detection.

articleTitle: An extended frequency nonlinear chirp scaling algorithm for high-speed high-squint SAR with curved trajectory
abstract: The imagery of High-Speed High-Squint (HSHS) synthetic aperture radar with curved trajectory is a challenging task due to the existence of acceleration, the azimuth-dependent range migration, and azimuth-dependent Doppler parameters. Although existing imaging algorithms can deal with most of high-squint scenarios based on a nonlinear trajectory, these algorithms will be invalid when speed and resolution are increasing. Thus, an extended frequency nonlinear chirp scaling algorithm is developed to handle this issue. First, a more accurate range model is established. Then, a pre-processing is made to eliminate the impact of 3-D acceleration on the Doppler parameters and range-azimuth coupling. Subsequently, a spatial-variant acceleration phase calibration is implemented for range focusing based on bulk range cell migration correction (BRCMC) and extended secondary range compression (SRC). Finally, an extended frequency nonlinear chirp scaling (EFNCS) algorithm is derived for azimuth compression. The effectiveness of the proposed algorithm is verified by computer simulations.

articleTitle: A signal reconstruction algorithm for distributed multichannel squint missle-borne SAR
abstract: With the increase of velocity of missile-borne platform, it is difficult for a single antenna to meet the minimum antenna area constraint of synthetic aperture radar (SAR) system, and the contradiction between range ambiguity and azimuth ambiguity is irreconcilable. In order to make full use of the surface space of missile-borne platform, a distributed multichannel squint SAR system is proposed in this paper, which can relatively increase the total antenna area. Different from the general linear multichannel SAR, the space-time spectrum of distributed multichannel SAR is nonlinear and range-variant, which brings difficulties to the spectrum reconstruction. In order to solve this problem, a distributed multichannel squint SAR signal spectrum reconstruction algorithm is proposed. Firstly, the nonlinear range-variant characteristics of space-time spectrum are analyzed through the signal model of distributed multichannel SAR. Then, a space-time preprocessing operation based on the two-step range variant phase compensation is proposed to obtain the analytical space-time spectrum of distributed multichannel SAR. Finally, the spatial filtering operation is performed through the analytical expression of space-time spectrum, and then the single-channel unambiguous signal with equivalent high pulse repetition frequency (PRF) is obtained. Simulation results verify the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm. The proposed method is easy to implement for its low computation complexity, through the two-step phase compensating, the complex space-time spectrum is corrected to a straight line, thus the conventional methods can subsequently be used to resolve the Doppler ambiguity.

articleTitle: An efficient range migration algorithm for high resolution MEO SAR in highly squinted condition
abstract: There are many challenges in high resolution and highly squinted medium-earth-orbit synthetic aperture radar (MEO SAR) imaging process, such as wide swath, curved orbit, severe range walk and range-azimuth-coupled. In this paper we propose an efficient range migration algorithm for high resolution MEO SAR in highly squinted condition. Firstly, we analyse the key aspects of high-resolution MEO SAR processing, including slant range model, derivation approximation and range-azimuth coupling, and the range migration algorithm (RMA) algorithm is selected. Secondly, the range-splitting is conducted and the hyperbolic range equation (HRE) model error is compensated. Additionally, the range cell migration correction and quadratic Doppler rate error are further compensated, which decreases the number of range block. Finally, simulations are carried out to validate the effectiveness of the presented algorithm.

articleTitle: Interrupted-Sampling Repeater Jamming (ISRJ) suppression method based on segmented FRESH filtering target detection
abstract: Interrupted-sampling repeater jamming (ISRJ) based on digital radio frequency storage has coherent characteristics, which can generate a large number of false targets after pulse compression, making radar detection ineffective. To solve this problem, an algorithm based on segmented FRESH filtering and target detection is proposed. On the basis of Pulse Doppler processing of the received signal, the algorithm detects the range Doppler matrix and obtain the range positions of multiple targets. According to the detection results, the received signal is processed by piecewise parallel adaptive cyclic stationary filtering. The multi-group filtering results are intercepted and spliced to achieve ISRJ suppression in complex electromagnetic environment. The simulation of the real field environment shows that the method can productively suppress the jamming and has good anti-jamming effect when the false target and the real target are distributed in different positions.

articleTitle: Waveform design for pulse radar based on interrupted coding modulation
abstract: Coding modulation is utilized to design radar waveform to obtain complex properties so that the waveform is difficult to be recognized. However, traditional coding modulation brings high sidelobe in target range profile which makes the detection performance decrease. To solve this problem, the interrupted coding modulation is proposed in this paper based on the interrupted transmitting and receiving. The signal model is provided and the low sidelobe property of range profile is discussed. Constant false-alarm rate (CFAR) is utilized to evaluate the detection performance of interrupted coding modulation waveform. Simulations are conducted to verify the low sidelobe property and detection performance of the proposed waveform.

articleTitle: Surface deformation pattern recognition in the urban environment using MT-InSAR and LSTM
abstract: Multi-temporal Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Rada is a new Earth observation technology. It can generate large-scale time series data, the characteristics of these data can reveal the patterns and driving mechanisms of surface deformation in diffe rent regions of the city. This provides early warning for urban geological disaster prevention and control. However, if manually identifying these surface deformation patterns is time-consuming and labour-intensive, we adopt a LSTM neural network with STL to explore the potential value of MT-InSAR data, in order to efficiently and accurately identify urban surface deformation features. Our work can provide a solution for future urban surface deformation monitoring.

articleTitle: Anti-range deceptive jamming method via polarization reception design
abstract: With the rapid development of self-defensive jammers, the range deceptive jamming shows high efficiency for jamming energy and is widely utilized in the field of electronic countermeasures, making it difficult to realize effective jamming discrimination via signal processing methods in the traditional domains of time, frequency and spatial for radar. To address this issue, this paper proposes a novel method to discriminate the range deceptive jamming in polarization domain. Particularly, the polarization scattering matrix (PSM) of the selected target is measured based on the stretch processing firstly. Then, the radar transmitter generates the random polarized signal and the receiver can suppress the selected target echo in polarization domain with the measured PSM. Finally, the number of peaks after matched filtering indicates the result of jamming discrimination. Several numerical simulations are provided to evaluate the validity and feasibility of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Joint design of transmit waveform and receive filter for dual-function radar-communication systems
abstract: This paper considers the joint design of transmit waveform and receive filter for a dual-function radar-communication (DFRC) system based on a multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) array. The system involves a dual-function multiple-antenna base station (BS), which detects the radar target in a signal-dependent interference environment and serves multiple single-antenna communication users. Different from the traditional frame for designing the radar transmit beampattern, we effectively use the degree of freedom of the radar receiver to maximize the radar signal to interference plus noise ratio (SINR). Meanwhile, we aim to minimize the multi-user interference energy to ensure regular communication for downlink users. By introducing weighting coefficients, a composed summation objective function is constructed. An iterative algorithm based on the alternating framework is proposed to solve multivariable optimization problems with constant modulus constraints. Moreover, the similarity constraint is introduced to make the transmit waveform have good ambiguity properties. Finally, the availability of the proposed method is evaluated by simulation results.

articleTitle: Systematic error measurements in object height estimation for automotive radars
abstract: The paper deals with two algorithms to improve automotive radar sensors alignment and road object height estimation. The first algorithm is based on the elevation angle measurements accumulation using the least squares method for error correction. The second algorithm based on difference estimation between elevation angles, each of them derived from direction finding method and Doppler beam sharpening method respectively. The proposed algorithms were both tested using test field measurements and road datasets.

articleTitle: Multi-false-target deceptive jamming based on FDA for SAR real target cancellation
abstract: Different from traditional single-element and phased-array antennas, Frequency diverse array (FDA) antenna introduces a frequency increment between neighbouring array elements making beam distance-angle coupling, which provides a promising paradigm for the development of novel deceptive jamming approaches against the SAR imaging. This paper proposes a method of deceptive jamming to SAR using FDA jammer. Two-dimensional intermittent sampling of intercepted radar signals and corresponding amplitude-phase compensation are performed by the FDA jammer. Instead of adding additional frequency modulation like other echo cancellation methods, real targets in the imaging scene can be eliminated by setting the frequency increment appropriately. The signals emitted by each FDA array element have different frequencies, so using this method can produce a larger number of false targets than ever before. The theoretical analysis and simulation show that there are only a large number of false targets in the imaging results.

articleTitle: Research on remote sensing satellite image compression and evaluation methods based on GAN
abstract: Image compression technology plays an indispensable role in the field of remote sensing satellite; however, existing methods often struggle to avoid loss of fine details in remote sensing satellite images. This paper introduces a remote sensing satellite image compression model based on Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs). The core objective of this model is to effectively preserve image details during the compression process and generate high-quality reconstructed images. Additionally, we incorporate object detection as part of the evaluation method for the compression model to comprehensively explore the feasibility and effectiveness of different compression methods in practical applications. Extensive experimental results on a real remote sensing satellite image dataset demonstrate that our model can maintain high-quality image reconstruction while reducing data volume, particularly excelling in object detection performance.

articleTitle: Unsupervised saltlake water extraction using DEM and dual-polarization SAR
abstract: Salt lakes contain rich natural resources, but the surrounding ecological environment is fragile. The area changes of water i n salt lakes are closely related to resource reserves and environmental changes. This paper proposes an unsupervised water extraction method that combines the Digital Elevation Model (DEM) and dual-polarization synthetic aperture radar (SAR) data. We calculate the gradient of DEM data and design a DEM correction factor to correct the polari zation decomposition features H/A/Alpha of dual-polarization SAR. Then the corrected polarization features are fused to one dimension by applying principal component analysis, and finally, water extraction is achieved using threshold segmentation. Compared with the traditional K-means method or single polarization feature segmentation method, the proposed method can effectively remove the mountain areas on from the segmentation results. The segmentation accuracy in complex scenarios has been improved by about 7%.

articleTitle: Ground penetrating radar target detection method based on optimized faster RCNN and k-means clustering
abstract: Ground Penetrating Radar (GPR) technology is a widely used detection technology for underground target objects, which can perform non-destructive detection of underground targets. Due to the complexity of the underground environment and the interference of clutter, manual processing of GPR data is a time-consuming and laborious task. Therefore, an accurate and fast automatic underground target detection method is urgently needed. We propose a method that can achieve fast goals in complex multi-goal situations. The simplified ResNet-50 network is used to detect dense intersecting hyperbolic curves and reduce the computation of the network. At the same time, we use k-means clustering algorithm to optimize the anchor in faster-Rcnn based on the characteristics of GPR hyperbola. In addition, this method is also suitable for target detection on GPR images under random media.

articleTitle: Water extraction using spaceborne Ka-band SAR images
abstract: The Luojia-2 satellite is a Chinese Ka-band SAR satellite launched in May 2023. This article presents high-resolution Ka-band SAR images captured and collected by the Luojia-2 satellite, which include multiple scenes of flood disasters, and compared Sentinel-1 C-band SAR images to to show the unique image characteristics of ground objects at Ka-band. Finally, we established the first Spaceborne Ka-band SAR flood dataset, and used three classical deep learning semantic segmentation networks to achieve intelligent segmentation and extraction of water bodies, which initially demonstrated the advantages of Spaceborne Ka-band SAR images in water extraction and water conservancy monitoring.

articleTitle: HRRP target identification method based on joint feature extraction and stacking model classification
abstract: This paper introduces a radar target recognition method for High Resolution Range Profile (HRRP). The method uses 1D Convolutional Neural Network (1D-CNN) to extract the deep features of HRRP, and combining with a variety of non-parametric features of HRRP for feature-level fusion, so as to obtain a more comprehensive feature characterization. In addition, the Stacking integration model is used to integrate multiple basic classifiers at the decision level, further improving the recognition accuracy and robustness of the model. Finally, the recognition and classification results are obtained through experiments with simulation data and measured data, and the performance of the proposed method is further verified by comparison with other deep learning algorithms, indicating that the method has certain practical application value in the field of radar target recognition.

articleTitle: Cramér-Rao bound assessment for manned-unmanned bistatic airborne radar
abstract: The Manned-Unmanned Teaming concept involving the utilization of cost-effective, attritable Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) in conjunction with a manned aircraft, is a novel concept of operation for future air combat. As an early-warning platform, it presents distinct advantages, including superior intelligence compared with single UAV swarm, enhanced detection ability and improved survivability compared with monostatic manned aircraft. Therefore, more efficient and reliable capabilities for moving target detection in complex environments can be achieved. In this paper, the parameters estimation accuracy on a new detection platform, i.e., Manned-Unmanned bistatic airborne radar (MUBAR), is discussed in detail. In the MUBAR, the manned aircraft is used as transmitter and the V-type formation UAV swarm mounted end-fire antenna array is utilized for receiving. The expression of Cramér-Rao bound (CRB) for parameters estimation accuracy on this platform is derived and validated through computer simulation.

articleTitle: An insect swarm segmentation algorithm based on Mask R-CNN
abstract: Radar has become an important tool for continuously observing insect migration, measuring and recording the biological and behavioural information of aerial insects crossing beams at different heights. Insects usually actively choose their migration time and height according to the environment, gather in swarms at specific time and height ranges, and exhibit some similar behavioural characteristics. Extracting the insect swarm and combining them with information of individual insects in the swarms provided by the high-resolution insect radar to study insect migration is becoming a new research path for radar entomology. Therefore, this article proposes an intelligent insect swarm segmentation algorithm based on the difference of insect spatiotemporal distribution. Firstly, the spatiotemporal distributions of insects measured by high-resolution insect radar are presented in the form of heat maps. Then, the Mask R-CNN network is used to segment the image based on the aggregation degree of insect individuals to identify the aggregated insect swarm. Finally, the aggregated swarms are extracted by matching the original data based on the pixel coordinates of the segmentation results. The good performance of the proposed method was verified based on simulation and experimental data.

articleTitle: An ISAR imaging method for maneuvering target based on fast iterative shrinkage thresholding algorithm-particle swarm optimization
abstract: Non-cooperation of targets is the main difficulty in inverse synthetic aperture radar imaging (ISAR). Target maneuvering during ISAR imaging severely interfere with image quality. The existing ISAR imaging algorithms for maneuvering targets suffer from many defects such as low computational efficiency, poor noise robustness, and inapplicability to echoes with sparse aperture. Therefore, this article proposes an ISAR imaging method for maneuvering target based on fast iterative shrinkage thresholding algorithm-particle swarm optimization (FISTA-PSO). Specifically, maneuvering target imaging can be viewed as an least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) problem with unknown rotational parameters. We adopt FISTA to solve the LASSO problem efficiently and adopt PSO to estimate the rotational parameters. Finally, alternating iterations of FISTA and PSO resulted in well-focused maneuvering target imaging results. Comparing with traditional maneuvering target imaging methods, FISTA-PSO has higher computational efficiency and is applicable to sparse aperture echo. Experimental results based on simulation datasets proved this conclusion.

articleTitle: Periodic ISRJ suppression with convolution generative network in delay-Doppler domain
abstract: Based on digital radio frequency memory (DRFM), interrupted sampling repeater jamming (ISRJ) poses a serious threat to radar systems by generating false targets after matched filtering. The suppression of jamming has become an intriguing topic in recent years. In this paper, the distribution feature of false targets in the delay-Doppler domain is derived by analyzing the target operator and performing Fourier series expansion on the periodic sampling pulse of ISRJ. The solution for suppressing ISRJ is then transformed into a matrix fitting problem, which may require two-dimensional convolution and feature extraction. With the aid of convolutional generative network (CGN), the delay-Doppler matrix of false targets can be reconstructed and cancelled with the original jammed matrix. The ISRJ-suppressed pulse compression output can finally be extracted from the jamming-cancelled matrix. Simulation experiments on three kinds of common radar waveforms are conducted to confirm the effectiveness and universal applicability of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Near-field millimetre wave SAR imaging for non-destructive testing
abstract: Millimetre wave imaging has the advantages of high resolution, high precision and no need for physical contact, which makes it a promising solution to non-destructive testing (NDT). In this paper, a near- millimetre wave synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imaging system is proposed and its performance for NDT is experimentally investigated. A millimetre wave SAR is established using the commercial TI radar operated with a bandwidth of 4 GHz (77-81 GHz), based on which a matching filter together with a sliding window energy detection method is proposed to construct the image. In the experiment, the imaging of a mental plate is demonstrated to verify the high-resolution imaging capability, and the imaging of carbon fibre reinforced plastic (CFRP) boards is implemented to imitate the NDT of occluded objects. In addition, the imaging of a printed-circuit board (PCB) is performed with the results showing good potential of the system to identify and locate the components of different materials, which is highly required in NDT applications.

articleTitle: A study of ghosts generated by tangential reflectors in traffic radar
abstract: Multipath propagation is an important problem in radar-related research. A significant approach to address the multipath problem is to model the reflecting surfaces in the scene, predict the ghost targets, and then identify and suppress the multipath. However, existing studies have mostly focused on considering radial types of reflecting surfaces, such as road barriers or the ground, without taking into account the influence of tangential types of reflecting surfaces. This article considers a novel tangential type of reflecting surface and its possible reflection paths, establishes an accurate model,and derives the distance and velocity characteristics of ghost targets. These characteristics is helpful to further identify and suppress ghost more accurately and perfectly.We also propose a targeted ghost target recognition and suppression algorithm, and the effectiveness of the algorithm is verified by the measured data. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first modeling study on the impact of tangential types of reflecting surfaces on radar.

articleTitle: STCA radar multi-dimensional ambiguity function characteristics optimization
abstract: Space-time coding array (STCA) radar provides new application capabilities and potentials due to its beam-wide airspace coverage capability. As radar ambiguity function (AF) is an effective tool to analyze the range (time delay) and Doppler resolution characteristics of various radar systems, this paper derives and analyzes the STCA radar Multi-dimensional AF characteristics in a general way. These characteristics provide some insights into optimal STCA radar parameters design. Furthermore, this paper optimally designs the STCA radar AF with array element coding and subarray division method, reducing the side-lobe level (SLL) in the range of waveform. Two kinds of subarray techniques are employed: uniform and non-uniform. Numerical results verify all derived expressions and methods.

articleTitle: Scale-aware memory-augmented autoencoder for hyperspectral sub-pixel anomaly detection
abstract: Hyperspectral anomaly detection (AD) exhibits promising performances in hyperspectral image processing, and autoencoder (AE) has shown great potential with its network more challenging to reconstruct the anomaly. Unfortunately, as AD algorithm automatically detects abnormal targets that are significantly different from the background, abnormal targets which are less than one pixel on the image, mixing with the features of the background, have brought challenges to the tasks and AE also faces the problem of the increasing ability to reconstruct the anomaly. This article proposes a scale-aware memory-augmented AE(SMAE) to resolve the above two problems via sending the different scales features in the encoder to the corelative decoder by the memory module. Given an input, SMAE firstly obtains the embedding from the encoder and then u ses it as a query to combine the most relevant memory items to retrieve the new features, which occurs in all depth of the network, prompting the ability to process diverse size targets, and memory-augmented design can strengthen the reconstructed errors for anomaly detection also increasing its sensitive to detect the sub-pixel anomaly targets. Experiments on various datasets prove the high precision of our proposed method.

articleTitle: Dual band HRRP scattering center estimation via atomic norm minimization
abstract: High resolution range profile (HRRP) obtained through air-to-ground radar provides information on the target structure, which is widely used in military and aviation fields. On the other side, dual band radar is able to improve the performance of target detection and recognition by fusing the information of different band. In this paper, we propose a dual band HRRP scattering center estimation method based on atomic norm minimization (ANM). Due to the fact that dual band information reflects the characteristics of the same target, it is modelled as the multiple measurement vector (MMV) and incorporated into the modelling process to effectively utilize the correlation of dual band information and sparse reconstruction. This method estimates in a continuous domain, avoiding the problem of base mismatch. According to the experimental results, this method exhibits outstanding advantages in accuracy and robustness.

articleTitle: Multiband iterative coherent processing method based on the ADMM framework
abstract: Multiband radar bandwidth extrapolation is an effective way to broaden bandwidth, which can realize high resolution at low cost and is of great significance for the detection and identification of large-range unmanned aerial vehicle clusters. Due to system error and multiband measurement deviation, an incoherent factor is often present between multiband data, which has a negative effect on the quality of multiband fusion. This paper proposes a new method for multiband coherence process by making use of alternating direction method of multipliers algorithm and Levenberg-Marquardt iterative approach. The simulation and measured data are used to verify the proposed algorithm. The results show that compared with the traditional method, this method can improve the estimation accuracy.

articleTitle: Scene-adaptive infrared small target detection method
abstract: Infrared small target detection plays an important role in the tasks of public safety and area monitoring. However, there are often few target pixels in the image output by the system and the existing algorithm mainly accommodate the following shortcomings: (1) Insufficient robustness of the complex scenes. (2) Noise causes higher false alarms. To solve these problems, a scene-adaptive infrared small target detection method based on low-rank matrix recovery is proposed in this paper. Firstly, the infrared block image model is proposed to suppress the background and highlight the target. Secondly, adaptive parameters tuning model is designed to improve the robustness of the algorithm under complex background with various noises. Finally, the Kalman filter parameter estimation and update strategy using multi-frame information is established to suppress background clutter false alarm and enhance target detection effect. Compared with the existing infrared target detection methods, the proposed algorithm is more robust and has better detection effect.

articleTitle: A novel phase-only pattern nulling algorithm
abstract: In order to obtain low probability of intercept, it is required to form nulling in the transmit pattern for the phased radar. To solve the problem, a novel phase-only pattern nulling algorithm is proposed in this paper. First, dummy interferences are introduced according to the nulling angles, and the interference covariance matrix is calculated; then the mathematical model for forming nulling is established by minimizing the array output power; last, the phase-only weight can be obtained by the single coordinate algorithm. The experimental results demonstrate the correctness and effectiveness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Evaluation and refinement of interferometric baseline of LT-1 SAR during the in-orbit testing phase
abstract: Lutan-1 (LT-1) stands as China's pioneering L-band radar satellite constellation, primarily geared towards surface deformation measurements. In this study, we harness ascending and descending orbit Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) data acquired by the LT-1 satellite within the Yunnan region. Our objective is to conduct a comprehensive examination, elucidating the spatial characteristics and governing factors of the phase ramp detected in the LT-1 differential interferogram due to orbit-related errors. Our analysis points to the primary culprit behind the orbit phase ramp as the estimation error in the change rate of the parallel baseline component. In response, we've pioneered an advanced baseline estimation methodology rooted in Iterative Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) to surmount the limitations of existing techniques. The outcomes underscore the efficacy of this innovative approach in achieving precise baseline and change rate estimations, resulting in differential interferograms devoid of conspicuous residual orbital phase artifacts. Furthermore, we've conducted a succinct evaluation of LT-1 data coherence and the accuracy of Digital Elevation Model (DEM) calculations. The results reveal that LT-1 data exhibit exceptional coherence, even in densely vegetated regions. Moreover, the DEM accuracy aligns closely with theoretical expectations, affirming its reliability.

articleTitle: ISAR imaging method for space maneuvering target based on parameter estimation
abstract: Due to the complex movement of the space maneuvering target, the received radar signal has time-varying characteristics, which causes the traditional range-Doppler imaging method to fail. Therefore, it is necessary to investigate the ISAR imaging method of the space maneuvering target further. To solve this problem, an ISAR imaging method for space maneuvering targets based on parameter estimation is proposed in this paper. First, the received signal in each range unit is modeled as a multi-component cubic phase signal (CPS) after range compression and translation compensation; Second, use a high-order ambiguity function (HAF) to reduce the CPS to a multi-component chirp signal; And then use the coherent integrated cubic phase function (CICPF) to achieve parameter estimation, reconstruction of the original signal to achieve ISAR imaging. Compared with the existing methods, the proposed method can simultaneously estimate the second-order and third-order parameters of the cubic phase signal, and has higher computational efficiency. Finally, simulation experiments are given to verify the validity of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A high-precision platform positioning method based on InSAR interferogram matching
abstract: The SAR/INS positioning and navigation system employs Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) image matching for platform positioning and to compensate for platform drift caused by Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU) errors. Images obtained by SAR are matched with digital landmark data. In scenarios where landmarks are absent, this article introduces a novel high-precision positioning method based on interferogram matching. Interferogram contains terrain elevation information and are less susceptible to seasonal variations compared to the SAR/INS system. Interferogram generated through real-time Interferometric SAR (InSAR) processing and interferogram simulated using a Digital Elevation Model (DEM) are matched. Subsequently, the three-dimensional positioning model of the platform is established by the unit look vector decomposition approach. Through real-data experiment, the presented method demonstrates its capability to achieve accurate platform positioning when Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) signals are unavailable.

articleTitle: Research on oil spill detection algorithm for marine radar echo image
abstract: Marine radar detection is one of the effective means to solve the problem of oil spill detection. This article proposes an oil spill detection algorithm. Taking the oil spill explosion accident that occurred in Dalian New Port in 2010 as an example, after obtaining the radar echo image of the accident waters, the oil spill detection algorithm was used to detect the oil spill in the accident waters and extract its edge. On the basis of the algorithm design, the influence and selection of various parameters in the algorithm are discussed, and the results obtained by this algorithm are analyzed.

articleTitle: 3D sparse SAR imaging based on complex nonconvex penalty function
abstract: Combining sparse signal processing with imaging can improve different types of SAR image quality. The L1 penalty function is an effective and typical sparse prior representation in sparse reconstruction. However, as a convex optimization function, L1 penalty function often introduces bias in sparse signal reconstruction. Therefore, in this paper, nonconvex penalty function is used to obtain high-quality and high-precision 3D SAR images. In order to improve the accuracy of sparse reconstruction, we adopt complex valued smoothly clipped absolute deviation penalty (CSCAD) for sparse reconstruction. Compared to the existing sparse reconstruction method with L1 penalty function, the proposed method not only improves the quality of array SAR images, but also reduces bias effects. In addition, the variant of alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) framework is used to achieve 3D sparse reconstruction, which can effectively reduce the computational complexity compared to traditional ADMM. The experiment is implemented to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: ISAR imaging of maneuvering targets using synchronous extraction transformation under low SNR
abstract: Inverse Synthetic Aperture Radar (ISAR) holds a significant position in the field of radar imaging, with the Range-Doppler (RD) algorithm being a common method used in ISAR imaging. However, traditional Range-Doppler algorithms encounter difficulties in focusing ISAR images when faced with low SNR of the received echo signals and the time-varying Doppler caused by the complex motion of maneuvering targets. Time-frequency distributions such as Short-Time Fourier Transform (STFT) suffer from low time-frequency resolution or interference from cross terms, making them unsuitable for real-time imaging of maneuvering targets. The recently proposed ISAR imaging based on Synchronous Squeeze Transform (SST) effectively addresses the time-varying Doppler problem brought by maneuvering targets. However, SST is essentially a post- processing operation of STFT, achieved by squeezing all the time-frequency coefficients in STFT. Some irrelevant signals are also squeezed, leading to a lower concentration of time-frequency energy. To address these issues, this paper proposes a new method of ISAR imaging of maneuvering targets based on Synchronous Extraction Transf orm (SET) under low SNR. Firstly, the echo signals of maneuvering targets, which have undergone translation compensation and Keystone transformation, are segmented at each distance unit. The segmented signals at the same distance unit in different azimuths undergo SET transformation. Compared to SST transformation, the obtained echo signals have better robustness to noise without sacrificing image resolution. Finally, the effectiveness of the algorithm is validated through computer simulation and actual data measurement.

articleTitle: Semantic enhanced image blending for spaceborne SAR airport targets
abstract: As the extensive application of deep networks and the increasing complexity of functionalities, there is a growing demand for training samples. In most publicly available SAR target detection datasets, the number of target instances is limited. Theref ore, SAR sample synthesis becomes an effective approach to enhance the target detection capability of deep models. In the task of image synthesis, image blending aims to smoothly integrate objects from source images into other background images in a natural manner. This paper proposes a semantic-enhanced image fusion method for achieving high-fidelity and reliable sample augmentation. Firstly, an object feature separation method is introduced, which separates the target features into key textur es and secondary content. Secondly, Poisson blending and style transfer are applied separately to these two feature parts, with controllable degrees of feature fusion achievable through different parameter settings. Finally, deep fusion is performed on the entire image to further enhance the appearance realism of samples. Experimental results demonstrate that semantically enhanced fusion images can be used for sample augmentation and significantly improve the recall rate (R) of classical detection networks.

articleTitle: Refined coherent parameters estimation based on iterative Chirp-Z transform for DCAR on moving platforms
abstract: The Distributed Coherent Aperture Radar (DCAR) offers significant advancements in long-range and high-power detection capabilities by coherent synthesis. However, achieving coherent synthesis in DCAR relies on the precise estimation of Coherent Parameters (CPs). Conventional algorithms typically focus solely on the estimation of time-delay and phase CPs, which is unsuitable in scenarios of moving platforms with Doppler frequency deviations between channels. Additionally, the deviations cannot be effectively compensated for using the Doppler frequency parameter estimated by common algorithms due to the off-grid problem. To address these issues, a refined CPs estimation algorithm based on the iterative Chirp-Z transform (ICZT) is proposed for DCAR on moving platforms. The proposed algorithm can effectively mitigate the mismatch between the target signal and the centre frequency of the Doppler filter, reducing residual phase errors and ensuring accurate CPs estimation. The effectiveness of the proposed algorithm is verified by the simulation experiments.

articleTitle: Spectral–spatial attention fusion transformer for hyperspectral image classification
abstract: In view of the limited generalization and poor local feature information modeling ability of vision transformer model(ViT) in hyperspectral image classification, a Spectral-Spatial Attention Fusion Transformer (SAFT) method for hyperspectral image classification is proposed in this paper. The proposed method includes two key modules: Spectral-Spatial Feature Extraction Module (SSFE) and Multi-Head Attention Fusion Transformer Module (MAFT). The SSFE module is a lightweight network. It contains a 3D convolution block and a 2D convolution block, which can efficiently obtain local feature information. Based on the proposed attention fusion structure, the MAFT module designs an improved transformer encoder. It improves the generalization ability of the model on the premise of obtaining global information. In this paper, two datasets of HyRANK are used for experiments. The experimental results show that this method is superior to other HSI classification methods.

articleTitle: Adaptive detectors with enhanced selectivity properties in the compound Gaussain clutter with generalized inverse Gaussian texture
abstract: In this paper, the problem of adaptive detection of signals in the compound Gaussian clutter when the signal mismatch occurs is discussed. The texture follows the generalized inverse Gaussian distribution which includes inverse Gaussian, inverse gamma and gamma as three special examples. To increase the mismatch rejection performance, the binary hypothesis test is modified and a fictitious signal is introduced under the null hypothesis. Two adaptive mismatch selective detectors are derived according to the maximum a posteriori test and generalized likelihood ratio test. The performance evaluation shows that the two proposed adaptive detectors have stronger mismatch rejection performance than the conventional detector.

articleTitle: Deceptive interference suppression with a novel FDA-PMIMO radar
abstract: The deceptive interference suppression with a novel frequency diverse array-phased multiple-input multiple-output (FDA-PMIMO) radar is studied in this article. Unlike the existing method focusing only on the receive side with FDA-MIMO radar, a novel method focusing on the joint processing in both the transmit and receive sides is presented, which enhances the performance of interference suppression significantly. In this regard, the signal model of FDA-PMIMO radar is derived, where the array is partitioned to multiple subarrays. In this case, the output signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) can be improved by the transmitting coherent processing gain. Subsequently, a robust suppression method with a low calculation cost is developed, where the processed data dimension is effectively reduced by a sequential suppression way. Furthermore, in order to improved the suppression performance further, a transmit design method is also studied by optimizing the subarray number. Numerical simulations highlight the superiority of the proposed methods.

articleTitle: Ship detection in SAR images based on data augmentation and attention mechanism
abstract: Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) images are significantly affected by the presence of a substantial amount of speckle noise and sidelobe interference, which can degrade the performance of ship detection. This paper introduces an approach that combines data augmentation and improvements to the object detection model.
