By incorporating the Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM), the detection model is enabled to learn feature information in both spatial and channel dimensions. CBAM serves to suppress the acquisition of background features, thereby enhancing the model's capacity to acquire ship target features in complicated backgrounds. Furthermore, a generative adversarial technique is employed to inhibit sidelobe interference and produce images for augmenting the training dataset, thereby enhancing the model's capability to discern sidelobe interference. Lastly, the paper introduces the SIoU loss function, which redefines the loss function through vector angles between bounding box regressions, thereby effectively improving detection accuracy. Results from a series of experimental evaluations using the SSDD dataset indicate that the method provides higher performance in ship detection for SAR images with significant interference. Compared to the standard YOLOv5 model, the proposed approach achieves a recall increase of 0.027 and a mAP increase of 0.006.

articleTitle: Joint accuracy evaluation method of multiple scenarios for GNSS-based InSAR system
abstract: GNSS-based InSAR system utilizes navigation satellites and PS-InSAR to monitor surface deformation, which is a flexible, efficient and high-precision method. When measuring deformation in a single scene, the system can obtain high-precision measurement results. When measuring deformation in multiple scenes with a large range, due to the relativity of the measurement in a single scene, directly fusing the single-scene measurement results leads to erroneous evaluation accuracy. This paper introduces a calibrator dedicated to GNSS-based InSAR system. The calibrator is composed of a navigation signal transponder and a GNSS signal receiver rigidly connected. The measurement results can be obtained through signal transponder, and the real deformation at target points can be obtained through GNSS signal receiver. It can improve the accuracy of deformation measurement using measurement results and real deformation.

articleTitle: Vegetation descriptors derived from dual-polarization SAR imagery for monitoring agricultural crop growth
abstract: Monitoring crop growth through synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imagery is vital in conducting comprehensive crop yield analysis. However, existing SAR vegetation indexes do not comprehensively exploit the polarimetric and intensity information in dual-polarization SAR data, resulting in incomplete SAR information extraction. Therefore, this paper introduces an innovative approach to derive vegetation descriptors from dual-polarization SAR images. This approach combines the covariance matrix elements with backscatter intensity, comprehensively representing vegetation's polarization characteristics and scattering mechanisms. Initially, three vegetation descriptors are introduced, including the co-pol purity parameter (mcp), pseudo-scattering angle (θcp), and pseudo-scattering entropy (Hcp). Subsequently, a new unsupervised clustering framework is developed based on θcp and Hcp to assess the dynamic growth processes of various crop categories. Finally, the performance of our method is validated using the Carman test site. Experimental results demonstrate the sensitivity of mcp, θcp, and Hcp to different crop growth stages. From the initial sowing of wheat to its maturity, sampling points transition from the low to medium entropy co-pol zone to the High entropy vegetation zone. Therefore, the vegetation descriptors and clustering framework effectively monitor crop growth processes, providing technical support for scientific agricultural management.

articleTitle: A coherent weak signal direction finding method based on anisotropic coupling
abstract: Conventional spatial spectrum estimation algorithms often fail to estimate the direction of arrival (DOA) of weak signals when the power of the signals differs greatly. In this paper, aiming at solving the problem of coherent weak signal direction finding under the suppression of strong signals, in the case that the direction of arrival of the strong signal, the corresponding di rection vector and amplitude, and the initial phase are unknown but the signal waveform is known, the waveform information of the direction of arrival of the strong signal is used to enhance the direction finding capability for coherent weak signals in different unknown directions. In the case of the Minimum Variance Distortionless Response (MVDR), Multiple Signal Classification (MUSIC) and other modern spatial spectrum estimation and direction finding methods, it is difficult to find the direction of the weak signal. Because it is suppressed by strong signals in nearby directions, and coherent with strong signals. The Wiener filter vector and the MVDR filter vector determined by the waveform information of the direction of arrival of the strong signal are combined to form a set of coherent vectors and anisotropic coupling coefficients to achieve the purpose of decoherent direction finding and improving the accuracy of weak signal direction finding. The simulation results show that compared with the conventional spatial spectrum estimation algorithm, the direction finding accuracy of the method proposed in this paper is mu ch higher for weak signals.

articleTitle: Accuracy and influencing factors analysis of tree height extraction for different tree species based on UAV remote sensing
abstract: The rapid advancement of Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV)remote sensing has greatly facilitated forest resource monitor ing. In order to investigate the single tree identification rate and tree height extraction accuracy of UAV when faced with different tree species, this study focuses on four common tree species in Guilin City. The combination of watershed segmentation algorithm and local maximum value algorithm was employed to segment individual trees and extract tree heights. The results indicate that the single tree identification rate and tree height extraction accuracy vary when dealing with different tree s pecies. Among the four tree species, the Osmanthus trees exhibits the highest single tree identification rate and tree height extraction accuracy, with identification rates and correlation coefficients (R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) of 87.6% and 0.962, respectively. On the other hand, th e Pine trees has the lowest single tree identification rate and tree height extraction accuracy, with identification rates and correlation coefficients of 78.0% and 0.851, respectively. The Eucalyptus trees and Banyan trees fall in between these two. This study validates the reliability of UAV in extracting tree heights from different tree species, providing robust support for the application of UAV in forest resource monitoring.

articleTitle: Maneuvering target imaging and motion parameter estimation based on improved maximum likelihood estimation
abstract: In synthetic aperture radar (SAR), long-time coherent integration may induce range migration and Doppler frequency migration, resulting in the defocusing of the moving target. To this end, a new method to estimate motion parameters of maneuvering target is proposed in this paper. In this method, the second-order keystone transform is utilized to correct the range curvature. Then, the Radon transform is used to estimate the slope of the range migration, from which radial velocity of the target can be obtained. Next, an improved algorithm based on Maximum likelihood (ML) is applied to estimate motion parameter of the maneuvering target. Finally, a well-focused image of a moving target can be accomplished by compensating Doppler frequency migration according to the estimated motion parameters. Compared with ML, this method can reduce computational complexity. Compared with other traditional method, this method can estimate motion parameter of the target more accurately.

articleTitle: Passive radar direct wave signal reconstruction method based on fractional domain blind source separation
abstract: The direct wave signal reconstruction is a prerequisite for passive radar to realize effective detection. However, when the passive radar receives multiple linear frequency modulated (LFM) signals with similar parameters from different radars, multi-source pulse signals may be aliased in the spatial domain and time-frequency domain simultaneously, which leads to the degradation of signal parameter estimation performance and the invalidation of direct wave signal reconstruction. In order to solve the problem of signal multi-domain aliasing and realize wave signal reconstruction, this paper proposes a novel method based on fractional domain blind source separation (FD-BSS) for passive radar. Firstly, apply fractional Fourier transform (FrFT) for the received direct wave signal to accumulate the intra-pulse energy. Then, FrFT filtering is completed and the filter width is controlled by least square fitting. Subsequently, the multi-channel BSS is performed to separate the signals with different optimal transform orders in FrFT domain successively. Finally, the separated signals in time domain are obtained via inverse fractional Fourier transform (IFrFT) and the parameters estimation can be achieved to reconstruct the signals. Simulation results prove the validity and reliability in direct wave signal reconstruction using the proposed method.

articleTitle: Exploring the potential of ultra-low latency spiking neural network in remote sensing image classification
abstract: With the rapid advancement of artificial intelligence, the depth of artificial neural networks (ANN) has increased, resulting in higher power consumption and resource utilization. To address these concerns, researchers have begun to explore spiking neural networks (SNN) as an alternative. SNN offers the potential for improved energy efficiency while achieving comparable performance. In recent years, there has been a growing interest in applying SNN to remote sensing classification scenarios. However, one major challenge hindering its widespread adoption is the high latency associated with real-time processing. To address this challenge, we adopt a novel hybrid training approach that combines ANN-SNN conversion with backpropagation through time. We evaluate the effectiveness of our approach on three publicly available datasets: MSTAR, AID and UC-Merced. Our experiment results demonstrate that the proposed ultra-low latency SNN achieves classification accuracy rates of 99.05%, 91.36%, and 92.62%, respectively, with a single time step. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first time to apply ultra-low latency SNN to remote sensing image classification tasks. Our findings suggest that this innovative approach has significant potential for future research in the deployment of these models for on-board processing.

articleTitle: A Deramp Doppler parameter estimation method for spaceborne sliding spotlight SAR
abstract: Sliding spotlight mode is a widely used working mode for spaceborne synthetic aperture radar (SAR) systems. It can realize a higher azimuth resolution than the stripmap mode and a wider observation swath than the spotlight mode. For sliding spotlight SAR, due to the higher azimuth resolution, the accuracy of the Doppler parameters is of great importance since it affects the construction of the azimuth matching filters and further impacts the focusing quality of the final image. While most of the existing Doppler estimation methods are not applicable for sliding spotlight mode since they do not consider the azimuth spectrum aliasing problem. In this paper, we conduct a detailed analysis of the variation of azimuth time-frequency relationship during the azimuth preprocessing of the two-step focusing process for spaceborne sliding spotlight SAR. Based on the analysis, we propose a new Doppler parameter estimation method dedicated to azimuth preprocessing. We also present our experimental results of real data which can verify the effectiveness of our proposed method.

articleTitle: Suppression of mainlobe deceptive jammers using multi-domain coding
abstract: This paper deals with the problem of suppressing mainlobe deceptive jammers by using the Multi-Domain Coding (MDC). At the design stage, by coding in the spatial, slow-time and fast-time domains, the MDC radar is capable of separating the transmitted signals from various transmit elements and discriminating the true target from the mainlobe jammers in the joint transmit-receive spatial frequency domain. Furthermore, the mainlobe jammers can be eliminated by nulling at the equivalent transmit beampattern via an appropriate coding coefficient. Simulation results corroborate the effectiveness of the proposed MDC scheme for the mainlobe deceptive jammer suppression.

articleTitle: Active and passive cooperative tracking method based on weighted least squares
abstract: In modern battlefield, a single radar tracking system needs to continuously send electromagnetic waves to the outside world, which is easy to expose itself, and the tracking system with active and passive radar working together can effectively solve this problem. In order to improve the real-time and accuracy of the active radar control in the cooperative tracking system, the active and passive cooperative tracking method based on weighted least squares is proposed. In this method, the motion equation of the target is estimated by the weighted least squares method combined with the measurement noise when the active radar is turned on. After the active radar is turned off, the new residual generated by the fitted “measurement” and the filtered predicted value is used as the evaluation factor. The simulation results show that the active radar startup time of the proposed method is reduced and the collaborative tracking accuracy is improved when high concealment is required.

articleTitle: A simplified processing method for angle measurement of broadband phased array
abstract: For the broadband multi-beam systems, using the time delay compensation method would result in a large amount of equipment. A simplified parallel processing method of different directions in the complex electromagnetic environment is researched in this paper. Firstly, the phase- shifting method is used for beamforming. For multi-beam case, the gain loss of the non-center frequency narrow band signal is small, but the angle is shifted. And then the angle sensitivity curve of non-center frequency can be obtained through the transformation of the angle sensitivity curve to realize accurate angle measurement. Finally, the purposes of multi-beam and multi-direction parallel process are achieved. The simulation is provided to verify the effect of angle measurement. The obtained conclusions have reference significance for engineering practice.

articleTitle: An addition network with ResNet for fine-grained visual classification in SAR images
abstract: Military target Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) images classification is a fine-grained visual classification task that has higher difficulty than the classification of optical images. Due to the widespread application of radar imaging in military, the classification of military target SAR images is well worth exploring. Currently, convolutional neural network (CNN) is widely used for target classification. The performance of traditional CNN is not ideal for SAR images of ground military target, which is mainly because that the network does not learn enough about the refined features of targets and the serious confusion of similar targets. We propose a refined feature extraction additional FPN network with ResNet as the backbone in this paper. The network can extract the refined features of the target by selecting regions of interest on various feature dimensions and fuse them with the backbone features to increase the diversity of features. The method of this paper obtained 98.6% on the MSTAR and 84.5% on the CircularSAR-FAST-Vehicle, which is 0.7% and 6.8% higher than the equal scale backbone network.

articleTitle: A SBL-based unrolled deep network for high-resolution ISAR imaging
abstract: This paper introduces the CVEM-Net, which combines a sparse Bayesian learning (SBL) based reconstruction algorithm with a data-driven deep neural network. The CVEM-Net presented in this study excels at high-resolution inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR) imaging, even in low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and incomplete data scenarios. It also demonstrates robustness to variations in SNR and data loss rates. Firstly, we establish a sparse ISAR observation model and a statistical model. Secondly, the model parameters are estimated using the variational expectation maximization (VEM) algorithm. Subsequently, we unroll the iterative VEM algorithm into a deep network and train it using backpropagation. Lastly, the trained network, in combination with maximum likelihood estimation, iteratively estimates the ISAR image and phase errors. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in achieving well-focused ISAR imaging across various SNRs and data loss rate scenarios.

articleTitle: ISAR imaging of IFDS echo based on GPU parallel processing
abstract: The Intermediate Frequency Direct Sampling (IFDS) mode in Inverse Synthetic Aperture Radar (ISAR) imaging preserves the original information of the echo signal and radar system characteristics. However, the massive data accompanying this mode imposes considerable computational burdens on subsequent steps. As a result, traditional ISAR imaging algorithms and implementations face challenges in achieving fast, real-time imaging in IFDS mode. This paper presents the design and implementation of an IFDS echo ISAR imaging system based on parallel computing using Graphic Processing Unit (GPU). The efficiency and effectiveness of the proposed system were validated on the simulated data. Significant performance improvements compared to traditional CPU-bound ISAR imaging systems were demonstrated in the results. These improvements were achieved with minimal impact on the final quality of the two-dimensional ISAR image.

articleTitle: Three-dimensional scattering center reconstruction for single-frequency MIMO arc array radar
abstract: Reconstructing scattering centers based on MIMO radar technology is a research hotspot in the field of RCS measurement technology for near-field targets. As the basic input to generate the echo of the target, the three-dimensional scattering center of the target has the advantage of thoroughly describing the electromagnetic scattering characteristics. However, traditional scattering center reconstruction methods require wideband data input, which greatly limits the efficiency of echo simulation with the increase of dimension. In this paper, we propose a three-dimensional scattering center reconstruction method based on single-frequency MIMO arc array radar. Based on the three-dimensional echo data obtained by single-frequency MIMO arc array radar, the proposed method respectively uses the MDL algorithm, the MUSIC algorithm and the least square method to estimate the number, position and amplitude of scattering centers, realizing the three-dimensional reconstruction of scattering centers. The proposed method can reconstruct the three-dimensional scattering center quickly and accurately. Finally, Numerical simulation verifies the three-dimensional scattering center reconstruction effect of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A closed-form solution for target localization and clock refinement in distributed MIMO radar systems under inaccurate clock synchronization
abstract: Due to limitations in clock synchronization technology and sensor non-ideal clocks, achieving accurate clock synchronization for distributed multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) radar systems is not feasible. This paper addresses the issue of target localization and clock synchronization in the systems under inaccurate clock synchronization. Firstly, the problem is approached by deriving the Cramer-Rao lower bound (CRLB) of the measurement model and analyzing the increase in CRLB of target location to illustrate the necessity of considering clock synchronization error when locating the target. Then, a closed-form solution is proposed to locate the target and refine clock parameters. Specifically, based on the maximum likelihood and maximum a posteriori estimation theory and the best linear unbiased estimation theory, the calculation formulas to estimate the clock synchronization error and the target location are derived stepwise, where the former depends on the estimate of the latter. Finally, simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method provides better target localization accuracy than state-of-the-art algorithms and can effectively present the estimates of the unknowns under moderate noise level.

articleTitle: Learning-empowered frequency-domain single-snapshot DoA estimation in FMCW automotive radars
abstract: Automotive radars demand precise angle estimation, and this task is coupled with matching targets' range and velocity es- timates. To better address this need, we design a learning-empowered framework for direction-of-arrival (DoA) estimation using frequency-domain single snapshot. The proposed framework starts with initial steps of two-dimensional fast Fourier transform and constant false alarm rate operations, which are applied to received signals to select the frequency-domain snapshot associated with the target range-Doppler bin. Signals from different channels are used to create a covariance matrix, subsequently refined by a customized convolutional neural network. To ensure interpretability, the process of DoA estimation employs the well-established model-driven algorithm of root multiple signal classification (root-MUSIC). Sim- ulation results demonstrate the framework's ability to yield markedly reduced root mean square error compared to baseline methods in typical signal-to-noise ratio settings, thus substantiating its potential in practical scenarios.

articleTitle: Research on α-β filtering algorithm on tracking high-speed AMMO
abstract: The α-β filtering is a usually estimation method for radar target tracking. This paper introduces a new adaptive gain α-β filtering algorithm employing recursive method, which could improve tracking accuracy of high-speed ammo. Therefore, we make simulation experiments that evaluates the performance of proposed α-β filtering algorithm, according to comparison between constant gain α-β filtering and Kalman filtering. The simulation results indicate that the adaptive gain α-β filtering can guarantee convergence to a stationary value for velocity rapidly with less fluctuation.

articleTitle: A false points eliminating method of bearing-crossing localization in passive radar based on Hough transform
abstract: The bearing-crossing localization technique of passive radar has been widely used in modern electronic warfare. However, when the passive radar locates multiple interference sources, a large number of false points will be generated. The traditional false points eliminating methods exist the problems of low positioning accuracy and high computational complexity. In order to eliminate false points more effectively and ensure the tracking performance of passive radar to interference sources, a false points eliminating method for passive radar cross location based on Hough transform is proposed in this paper, which combines the advantages of angle correlation method and Hough transform method to eliminate false points. The experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed false points eliminating method. Compared with the traditional false points eliminating methods, the proposed method not only presents higher positioning accuracy for interference sources, but also can effectively reduce the computational complexity of the algorithm.

articleTitle: Open set recognition of radar active jamming signals based on relative entropy
abstract: It is of great significance to recognize radar active jamming signals in complex electromagnetic environment. However, the existing methods are mainly based on expert knowledge and a closed set, which are affected by environmental factors and unrealistic. In this paper, an open-set recognition method for active jamming signals is studied based on relative entropy. First of all, after performing the short-time Fourier transform (STFT) and moving target detection (MTD), the time-frequency and Range-Doppler (RD) map of the active jammers are obtained. Then, two deep learning-based jamming recognition branches, including the time-frequency and the RD, are trained and validated, where recognition probabilities are obtained for both branches with the same input. Furthermore, the relative entropy between the recognition probability and the ideal probability is utilized as the confidence level, and the open set recognition is realized through a voting mechanism which recognizes the probability and relative entropy. Numerical simulations show that the recognition probability can reach over than 90% at jammer-to-noise ratio (JNR) higher than 10dB.

articleTitle: YOLO-MSSD: multi-scale ship detection in SAR images based on spatial and channel attention
abstract: Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) plays a crucial role in ship detection from remote sensing images, but the detection performance often deteriorates due to the varying scales of ships and complex background interference. It is challenging to extract effective features from multi-scale ship targets, leading to high missing alarm rate. To solve the problem, we propose a multi-scale SAR ship detection algorithm, named YOLO-MSSD. In YOLO-MSSD, a new Spatial and Channel Attention Module (SCAM) is designed during the stages of feature extraction and fusion. SCAM is designed to dynamically combine contextual information from both spatial and channel dimensions. It achieves this by computing the correlation between maps at various positions and across different channels. This process enhances the representation of features at multiple scales, resulting in a more robust and comprehensive feature representation. Therefore, SCAM can effectively extract spatial and semantic information. Meanwhile, YOLO-MSSD also extracts abundant contextual information to suppress complex background interference in SAR images. The experimental results based on Synthetic Aperture Radar Ship Detection Dataset demonstrate that YOLO-MSSD achieves superior detection accuracy, with the AP, AP50 and AP75 values being 5.7%, 1.9%, and 5.7% higher than several existing state-of-the-art methods.

articleTitle: Surface mounted high-power directional coupler based on ceramic quad flat no-lead package
abstract: In this paper, a surface mounted high-power directional coupler is designed based on High Temperature Co-fired Ceramics (HTCC) technology and Ceramic Quad Flat No-lead (CQFN) package. The parallel coupled lines are imbedded in ceramic medium. The simulated and measured results demonstrate that the directional coupler has low insertion loss (⩽0.3 dB), high directivity (⩾17.5 dB), and stable coupling (39.5 dB±0.5 dB) in the frequency band of 485-495 MHz. The high-power tests show that the directional coupler can withstand 400-W continuous wave, and can be easily integrated with other high power circuits.

articleTitle: A variational bayes based extened object tracking method for 4D radar
abstract: Compared with traditional low-resolution 3D automotive radar, emerging 4D automotive radar has the significantly enhanced environmental perception capability and can provide richer point clouds, making it possible to estimate the object extension accurately. However, the radar measurements in polar coordinates exhibit a nonlinear relationship with the object motion and extension state modelled in the Cartesian coordinate system. To deal with the nonlinearities in the measurement equation, a novel extended object tracking algorithm using radar measurements is proposed. With the utilization of variational Bayesian inference, the approximate analytical estimation of the motion and extension state densities for the assumed elliptical extended object is obtained recursively. Furthermore, combined with the global nearest neighbour algorithm, the proposed method is generalized to the multiple object tracking scenarios, where the position gate adjusts its size according to the object extension estimation. By doing so, the occurrence of false associations can be reduced effectively when the tracked objects are closely spaced. Finally, the effectiveness of our approach is validated using the real test data of 4D radar.

articleTitle: Analysis on the minimal number of uniform sub-bands for wideband adaptive beamforming
abstract: Sub-band adaptive processing is a useful approach for real-time wideband adaptive beamformer, which converts a wideband problem to multiple narrow sub-band problems. Narrower bandwidth of sub-band has a better performance in wideband adaptive beamforming. However, narrow bandwidth results in large number of sub-bands, which increases computational complexity of the beamformer. In this paper, we analyse the effect of sub-bands number on the performance of wideband adaptive beamformer and propose a method to determine the minimal number of uniform sub-bands. By limiting the maximum sub-band beam pointing error to a quarter of half-power bandwidth (HPBW), we provide the accurate minimal number of sub-bands configuration for wideband adaptive beamformer with enough performance and low computational complexity. The numerical simulation results are presented to verify the effectiveness of the method we proposed.

articleTitle: Design of asymmetric beam antenna and its gain jitter optimization method
abstract: An asymmetric beam comb-antenna for automotive corner radar is designed in this paper, which is realized by adding parasitic element to achieve maximum gain at -45°. In addition, a novel periodic structure is designed to reduce azimuth gain jitter of antenna with radome and bumper. The simulation and measurement results show that antenna achieves maximum gain at -45° and azimuth gain jitter reduced from 13dB to 5dB within ±60° with radome and bumper.

articleTitle: Enhancing GPR full waveform inversion imaging accuracy through deep learning-based stochastic clutter suppression
abstract: In Ground Penetrating Radar (GPR) detection, uneven subterranean media distribution often leads to stochastic clutter interference, degrading the quality of ensuing imaging and impairing the precise identification of anomalous targets. This paper introduces a novel technique, Context Feature Fusion Module-Convolutional Block Attention Module-Residual Network (CFFM-CBAM-ResNet), tailored to suppress such interference in GPR data. Once processed, this GPR data facilitates enhanced Full Waveform Inversion (FWI) imaging. Both synthetic and experimental GPR data substantiate the algorithm's viability and underscore its potential in bolstering FWI imaging accuracy.

articleTitle: Distributed array radar system high precision jamming cancellation method based on sub-sampling interval time delay compensation
abstract: The distributed array radar system can effectively suppress the mainlobe jamming based on the high angle resolution provided by multiple independent radars. However, the excessively large equivalent aperture size may lead to time delay errors from system time asynchrony because the distance between the independent radars are too far. The jamming cancellation performance will severely decline when these time delay errors exist. Precision of traditional compensation methods such as the correlation method are limited by the sampling interval, and other methods such as the sub-band beamforming method cannot completely eliminate the influence of time delay errors either. In this paper, a new method is proposed to compensate for the sub-sampling interval time delay in the distributed array radar system to improve jamming cancellation performance. In the proposed method, the receiving signal of each radar is processed in frequency domain to overcome the precision limitation. Then the linear fitting method is utilized to reduce influence of noise to achieve high estimation accuracy. Simulations and experimental results illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed method on distributed array radar system jamming cancellation.

articleTitle: An ADMM-based low-complexity algorithm for atomic norm minimization in DOA estimation
abstract: In the array signal processing field, the DOA estimation algorithm based on sparse recovery has evolved from gradually transitioning from using a partitioned overcomplete grid dictionary for basis matching to solving semidefinite programming problems in the continuous frequency domain through atomic norm minimization. This transition aims to mitigate the grid mismatch caused by discretization, leading to improved DOA estimation accuracy. Currently, the interior-point method utilizing the CVX solver SDPT3 is commonly employed for solving this problem, but it exhibits high computational complexity and is unsuitable for real-time processing. This paper introduces the Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM) into the solution of the atomic norm minimization problem. By employing an augmented Lagrangian expansion and alternating iterative updates of variables, this approach decouples the multivariable coupled unconstrained convex optimization problem, thereby significantly reducing computational complexity. Theoretical analysis and simulation results demonstrate that the ADMM-based atomic norm minimization DOA estimation method achieves both accurate estimation and lower computational complexity.

articleTitle: SSA-LSTM urban surface deformation change predictive model research based on timing InSAR
abstract: In recent years, due to the rapid development of urban infrastructure construction, to varying degrees of ground settlement in urban areas, it has brought a huge threat to environmental protection and social development. The Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) neural network can achieve prediction and analysis of ground settlement. However, the time and space evolution of urban ground settlement is easily affected by human and natural factors. It is difficult to accurately obtain non-linear characteristics of time sequence data through traditional LSTM neural networks, resulting in low accuracy of urban ground settlement prediction and analysis. Therefore, this article uses Small Baseline Subset Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (SBAS-InSAR) technology to monitor time sequences of the ground settlement of the main urban area of Hohhot from 2017 to 2023. A SSA-LSTM neural network prediction model based on Sparrow Search Algorithm (SSA) is proposed, compared with the predictive results of the LSTM neural network model. The results showed that SSA-LSTM neural network model's predictive accuracy on time serial transformation data is better than traditional LSTM models, which has good predictive performance, and can improve its computing efficiency and robustness.

articleTitle: K-Means Clustering based Sparse Cross-Entropy Minimization algorithm for DOA estimation
abstract: Aiming at the problem that traditional greedy class compressed sensing algorithms are influenced by noise in the estimation of direction of arrival (DOA), this paper proposes the K-Means Clustering based Sparse Cross-Entropy Minimization (KMCSCEM) algorithm. First the algorithm selects atoms by minimizing the sparse cross-entropy to improve the accuracy of atom selection at the low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). Subsequently, K-mean clustering is added in each iteration to reduce the range of atom selection, which further improves the estimation accuracy. Finally, the speed of convergence is improved by introducing an orthogonal least squares (OLS) criterion. Simulation experiments show that the proposed algorithm has an exact estimation ratio close to 90% when the SNR is less than -5 dB.

articleTitle: Few-shot radar active deception jamming recognition: spatial-graph aggregated feature fusion based on transfer learning
abstract: Deep learning (DL) has demonstrated remarkable proficiency in classifying radar active deception jamming (ADJ). Yet, its effectiveness relies on the presence of ample training data. Regrettably, gathering such data is not only costly and time- intensive but also infeasible. Contrarily, natural image datasets like ImageNet and mini-ImageNet, distinct from ADJ, offer a wealth of texture and structural details. Facilitating efficient knowledge transfer between these diverse datasets holds substantial potential for enhancing the precision of ADJ classification. This paper proposes a classification network for jamming recognition, which extracts jamming spatial-graph aggregation fused features based on transfer learning (FSLVGCN). To begin with, a carefully designed VGG is employed for few-shot learning (FSL) on the mini-ImageNet dataset to acquire transferable knowledge. Then, to leverage the relationships between jamming signals, graph aggregation information is extracted by graph convolutional network (GCN). Finally, the spatial information of jamming is fused with the graph aggregation information, providing a more comprehensive and enriched representation of jamming features. Experimental results demonstrate that FSLVGCN achieves higher classification accuracy for jamming under very limited samples compared to Advanced jamming classification models.

articleTitle: A robust method for estimation of velocity in chirp-subpulse stepped frequency radar
abstract: In ISAR imaging of chirp-subpulse stepped frequency radar, a key step is estimating the velocity, which is the determinant of wideband synthesis. In this paper, a method of two steps is proposed, that is more robust for interferences in practices. Fir stly, the coarse estimation is obtained based on the fact that the profiles of target from same frequency are similar. Meanwhile, for eliminating the disturbance from jam, some estimations from different frequencies are comprehended. After correcting migration through resolution cell based on the prior estimation, some stronger cells are selected and the high resolution range profiles of each cells are achieved through IFFT (Inverse Fast Fourier Transformation). And based on these, the more precise velocity is estimated. Finally, the validity and the robustness of the method are validated through the practical radar dataset.

articleTitle: Joint power and beam allocation strategy based on CI fusion in networked collocated MIMO radar system
abstract: In this paper, a joint power and beam allocation strategy (JPBAS) is proposed in the networked collocated multiple-input and multiple-output (C-MIMO) radar system for distributed multi-target tracking (MTT). Each radar node that adopts a multibeam working mode in this network can generate limited beam and power resources. Firstly, a square-root cubature Kalman filter-covariance intersection (SRCKF-CI) fusion architecture is developed to process information between radar nodes. In addition, the target comprehensive threat evaluation model and the posterior Cramer-Rao lower bound (PCRLB) for the CI fusion rule are derived to evaluate the global MTT performance. Then the optimization model subject to power and beam resource constraints is established. A two-step algorithm is presented to solve the problem. Numerical results indicate that the proposed algorithm can effectively improve tracking accuracy and achieve a more reasonable resource allocation compared to other allocation strategies.

articleTitle: Airplane symmetry-based convolutional neural network for airplane detection in remote sensing image
abstract: Airplane detection in remote sensing image has attracted increasing attention in recent years owing to the successful applications of civil and military. Usually, the structure of the airplane is symmetrical in order to ensure the flight safety, and this inherent character would benefit target detection from complex background. This paper proposes a novel airplane detection algorithm based on symmetry-based region proposal (SB-RP) method and convolutional neural network (CNN). Firstly, pre-trained convolutional neural network is used to extract the high-level features from the training data set that include positive samples (airplane) and negatives (background). Then a symmetry-based region proposal (SB-RP) method is developed to extract the regions of interest from the complex remote sensing image. At last, the convolutional neural network trained by high-level features is exploited to detect the airplane from these regions of interest. The major contribution of SB-RP CNN method is that the interference of background clutter is greatly decrease for the regions of interest are reduced significantly for the background isn’t symmetrical. The extensive experiments are induced and the experimental results show that the SB-RP CNN method could greatly improve the performance of airplane detection in remote sensing image.

articleTitle: Gridless DOA estimation for automotive radars with various array geometries: the non-Vandermonde atomic soft thresholding approach
abstract: This paper is centered on gridless direction of arrival (DoA) estimation for single-snapshot data collected by non-uniform linear arrays (NLAs) in the context of automotive applications. While recent single-snapshot DoA estimation algorithms rooted in grid-based compressed sensing (CS) offer super-resolution capabilities, they are notably sensitive to discrepancies between the assumed sparsity basis and the actual basis. Furthermore, the existing atomic soft thresholding (AST) algorithm, a promising gridless sparse recovery technique within the Toeplitz model, is constrained to uniform linear arrays (ULAs) exhibiting Vandermonde structure in their array manifolds. However, in automotive scenarios, it becomes imperative to efficiently apply gridless DoA estimation to NLAs featuring non-Vandermonde array manifolds. In this paper, we introduce the non-Vandermonde atomic soft thresholding (NVAST) algorithm and employ it for DoA estimation in NLAs. The novel algorithm establishes a link between Vandermonde and non-Vandermonde atoms by decomposing non-Vandermonde vectors and addressing them using semi-definite programming (SDP). Simulation and measurement experiments conducted with automotive radars underscore the remarkable performance of our proposed method.

articleTitle: Design and ground experiment of asteroid internal structure detection radar (AISDR) onboard Tianwen-2 mission
abstract: China will launch Tianwen-2 mission targeting a small near-Earth asteroid and a main-belt comet. Asteroid Internal Structure Detection Radar (AISDR) is one of scientific payload onboard to investigate the asteroid internal structure. Giving consideration to penetration depth and range resolution, AISDR operates at low-frequency channel, 130-170MHz, and high-frequency channel, 300-1500MHz. Besides simulation and scale models experiments, a prototype has been field tested in two different geological settings, frozen lake and sand dunes.

articleTitle: Ground-based distributed radar synchronization with long coherence time
abstract: Ground-based distributed radar has received increasing attention and research from scholars due to its strong aerospace targets detection capability. However, due to its unique distributed configuration, the differences in frequency sources among stations can cause great synchronization trouble for imaging. In low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) echo environment and with long coherence time, the SNR gain provided by pulse compression is insufficient to extract the range history of the significant point. This makes traditional echo-based synchronization methods no longer applicable. In this paper, a novel synchronization method based on significant point under low SNR is proposed, and simulation has verified its effectiveness.

articleTitle: Distributed wireless radar system with application to through the wall radar
abstract: Nowadays, distributed radar network system has become a hot research issue because its performance is superior to monostatic radar in target positioning accuracy, detection probability, detection range. The distributed radar network is made up of N(N>=2) active radar nodes, and each radar has its own clock, therefore, time synchronization is important issue for cooperative detection. In this paper, we have developed a distributed wireless radar network, which is a portable prototype composed of three pseudo- random coded radars (N=3). The processing flow of distributed wireless radar data is introduced for the positioning and tracking of the target inside the wall. A wireless radar signal time synchronization scheme is proposed, the fast time synchronization is based on the arrival time of the direct coupled wave of the antenna, and the slow time synchronization is based on the state matching of a moving target, a template matching algorithm is used to estimate the time bias. Based on the multi-station radar data, Levenberg-Marquardt algorithm is applied to determine the location the target, and the Kalman filter algorithm is used to track the moving target.

articleTitle: Multi-frequency PolSAR image classification based on cross attention ViT
abstract: In the land cover classification of multi-frequency Polarimetric SAR (PolSAR) images, the classification performance highly depends on the effectiveness of feature fusion. Currently, linear fusion methods are widely employed in multi-frequency PolSAR land cover classification. However, linear fusion methods do not introduce extra interactions between the features from different bands, thus failing to fully exploit the advantages of fused features. To address this issue, a feature fusion method based on cross-attention is proposed. The proposed method is based on the Vision Transformer architecture. We enhance the model's capability to extract multi-frequency fusion features by introducing additional cross-frequency feature interactions within the self-attention module. Experimental results demonstrate that using the proposed cross-attention module significantly improves the model's performance in multi-frequency PolSAR image classification without introducing extra parameters or computational costs.

articleTitle: Azimuth ambiguity suppression for single look complex image based on block sparse representation
abstract: Azimuth ambiguity affects image quality seriously, which poses a great challenge to post-processing methods. However, existing ambiguity suppression method mainly deals with the azimuth ambiguity in raw data or utilizing multi-channel information. This paper proposes a blind adaptive method for single-look complex (SLC) images with less prior information. The energy of azimuth ambiguity will be sparsely spread in each sub-look image by multi-look processing on the SLC image. Through robust principal component analysis, useful information embedded in each sub-look image is effectively reconstructed and the azimuth ambiguity is removed. By applying sub-look synthesis, the problem of azimuth resolution loss caused by sub-look images is effectively avoided. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Integrated radar and communication waveform design based on spaceborne one-bit SAR system
abstract: The explosive growth in the number of communications and radar satellites has been accompanied by a rapid depletion of satellite orbital and spectrum resources. Given the similarity of radio systems in terms of underlying structures, integrated radar, communication and navigation satellites are gaining attention. Radar-communication integrated waveform design is one of the more critical technologies, integrating radar transmission signals and communication information and transmitting them through the same hardware system. Since SAR signals have high requirements for the accuracy of the transmitted signals, it is more difficult to superimpose random communication information directly on the existing SAR system. In recent years, the 1-bit SAR system, in which only the symbol bits of the echo samples are retained at the quantizer, has been rapidly developed, which greatly simplifies the SAR receiver and the digital transmission system, and at the same time reduces the constraints on the accuracy of the transmitted signal. In this paper, the frequency scan SAR transmit signal is improved by using phase shift keying modulation of chirp signals. Preliminary calculations and simulations show that the system is capable of downlinking the acquired echo information in real time while ensuring that there is no significant degradation in imaging resolution.

articleTitle: Polsar ship detection based on neighborhood polarimetric tensor
abstract: Using polarimetric Synthetic Aperture Radar (PolSAR) imagery for ship detection is a prominent research area within the realm of marine surveillance. The predominant approach in current practice encompasses the employment of super-pixel techniques and neighborhood matrix methodologies. Nonetheless, these methods may not fully capitalize on the spatial information. In this paper, the authors propose an innovative detection methodology by employing a neighborhood polarimetric tensor. This tensor encapsulates the entirety of polarization data within the pixel's neighborhood, with its constituent elements implicitly encoding spatial information. Furthermore, this research introduces the Kernelized Support Tensor Machine (KSTM) as the designated detection algorithm. KSTM, an extension of the conventional Support Vector Machine (SVM), unveils both polarization and spatial characteristics embedded within the neighborhood polarimetric tensor. Experiments were conducted utilizing PolSAR data acquired from Radarsat-2. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of the neighborhood polarimetric tensor in achieving precise ship detection.

articleTitle: A thin tunable absorbing metamaterial for intelligent stealth in L band
abstract: Absorbing metamaterials trigger great interests due to their potential applications in stealth. Plenty of absorbers have been proposed to achieve radar cross section (RCS) reduction. However, the contradiction between bandwidth and thickness is hindering their development. The intelligent stealth is a new method for achieving broadband absorption. The intelligent stealth system controls the absorption frequency of the absorber according to the detection signal received by the antenna. In this paper, a thin tunable absorbing metamaterial is proposed for intelligent stealth. It integrates antenna and absorber with a thickness of 0.028λ. By controlling the varactor diode loaded on the absorbing metamaterial, the antenna and the absorber can operate in 0.9 ~ 2.19GHz and 0.86 ~ 1.82GHz respectively. Simulated results prove that our method offers an effective strategy to design thin tunable absorbing metamaterial for intelligent stealth.

articleTitle: Simulation methods and development trends of radar target motion features
abstract: Radar is an important part of missile weapon system. Doppler physical reproduction technology runs through the design, development and acceptance of radar system. Based on the application background, the Doppler feature physical reproduction technology is divided into three types according to the simulation mode: platform simulation, active simulation and passive simulation. The development status of these three types of reproduction technology at home and abroad is introduced, their advantages and disadvantages are analyzed, the development direction of this field in the future is prospected, and the new progress in the field fo radar target motion feature simulation technology is elaborated.

articleTitle: Intelligent identification method of migratory animals based on weather radar
abstract: Weather radar echoes encompass precipitation, biological data, and other pertinent information, rendering them valuable tools for aeroecological monitoring. Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) can effectively categorize echo images, whereas Fully Convolutional Networks (FCNs) excel in pixel-level classification of organisms and precipitation within these echo images. We leveraged a comprehensive dataset replete with extensive echo data spanning a significant spatiotemporal range to train the FCN-8s network. The empirical findings underscore the remarkable capabilities of FCN-8s in elevating the average accuracy and recall rate for the biological component to levels exceeding 0.9. Achieving a balanced equilibrium between classification accuracy and recall rate holds paramount significance in augmenting the precision of aeroecological monitoring via weather radar.

articleTitle: Binary code design for pulse-Doppler radar performance enhancement via slow-time modulation
abstract: To improve the detection performance of pulse Doppler radar in the presence of interference, this paper proposes a slow-time modulation scheme and considers the design of binary slow-time modulation codes based on signal-to-interference-plus-noise-ratio maximization. To tackle the nonconvex nondifferentiable binary optimization problem, a two-step approach is developed. First, we relax the binary code constraint with a unimodular constraint and use the minorization-maximization (MM) algorithm to tackle the unimodular quadratic programming problem. In addition, we use the fast iterative shrinkage-thresholding algorithm to accelerate the MM algorithm. Then, the binary codes are synthesized from the optimized constant-modulus waveforms with a randomization process. Numerical examples demonstrate that the performance of the proposed algorithm is superior to that of the semi-definite relaxation algorithm and the coordinate descent algorithm.

articleTitle: Improved cardinalized probability hypothesis density filter for multitarget tracking using formation priors
abstract: Effective observation of group targets (bird flocks, etc.) has significant importance in aviation safety and ecological research. Closely spaced group targets with swarm intelligence can form huge and complex linear formations. Tracking radar must feature a narrow beam and high bandwidth to discriminate different targets within the formation. However, there are two major problems in formation target tracking. First, the number of targets within the beam may fluctuate with the change of radar-target geometry; second, false measurements may be detected from the distributed Doppler spectra. This paper proposes a cardinalized probability hypothesis density (CPHD) filter for multitarget tracking using the formation priors form a scanning radar. The model of false measurements is optimized based on the experimental data of birds. The densities of new targets and the probability of target death are set according to the formation priors of group structure and radar-target geometry. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is verified by experimental results.

articleTitle: Joint optimization of transmit waveform and mismatched filter for jamming suppression in distributed radar
abstract: In this paper, we focus on the issue of coherent performance deterioration caused by Interrupted Sampling Repeater Jamming (ISRJ) in Distributed Coherent Aperture radar (DCAR). To address this problem, we propose an algorithm based on joint optimization of transmit waveform and mismatched filter to suppress the jamming. We present a dual-variable optimization model concerning the integrated sidelobe level (ISL) of transmit waveform and the integrated level of ISRJ after mismatched filtering with constant-modulus constraint. By iteratively optimize two sub-problems, we can get the analytical solution. Finally, the efficiency of the algorithm is verified by simulations and the improved coherent performance is presented.

articleTitle: MoPPE: a moment-percentile Pareto estimator for sea clutter
abstract: Modern radar data frequently contain a mixture of relevant and irrelevant information. Sea clutter is a common non-interest information in many radar use cases. Enhancing the radar system's ability to process received signals necessitates a comprehensive understanding of sea clutter characteristics. Researchers have observed that a majority of sea clutter conforms to the Generalized Pareto Distribution (GPD). Consequently, the estimation of parameters in GPD holds significant importance in contemporary radar research. In this study, we initially introduced a Moment-Percentile Feature (MPF) encompassing six moments and nine percentiles. Secondly, we proposed the Moment-Percentile Pareto Estimator (MoPPE), a novel method employing convolutional neural networks and MPF for precise estimation of the shape parameter in GPD. Finally, we conducted a series of experiments to empirically demonstrate MoPPE's substantial advantages over conventional approaches and other machine learning methodologies.

articleTitle: Hierarchical adaptive gate array-based Kalman filter for multisensor integrated navigation system
abstract: Kalman filter based algorithm is generally used in integrated navigation to provide estimation of the state parameters. But the estimation accuracy is affected by the measurement noise parameters. In multisensor navigation system, a single method based adaptive Kalman filter shows limited improvidence in reducing on dependency on initial noise parameters of different types of sensors. In this paper, a hierarchical adaptive gate array-based Kalman filer is proposed to improve sate estimation. The filter bank is designed by different integrated couples of sensors with a set of adaptive filters. The filter array is generated and updated hierarchically with weights in gating networks. Simulation results prove the feasibility and performance improvement of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: A dirty paper forcing zero multi-beamforming algorithm for Ka-band radar
abstract: Multi-beamforming technology in radar system is a spatial filtering method, which ADAPTS to the rapid growth of detection demand through spatial reuse of spectrum resources. In practical application, multi-point beamforming in digital domain can suppress the interference among multi-users.In this paper, the Ka-band radar system faces the problem of severe rainfall attenuation during transmission. Based on the typical Zero Forcing (ZF) and Regularized Zero Forcing (R-ZF) precoding methods, A Regularized-Zero Forcing-Dirty Paper Code (R-ZF-DPC) method is proposed, and the difference between deterministic coding order and random coding order is analyzed simultaneously. The complexity of dirty paper regularized zero forcing algorithm is significantly lower than that of dirty paper coding.

articleTitle: SMSP interference suppression method based on time-domain interference matching
abstract: The existing smeared spectrum (SMSP) interference suppression algorithms are mainly operated on the transform domain other than the time domain. The operation object is an interfered echo segment with the same duration as the radar-transmitted signal and mostly does not involve multipulse processing in a coherent processing interval. To address these problems, this paper proposes a SMSP interference suppression method based on time-domain interference matching under the background of self-defence interference in pulse Doppler radar. The autocorrelation of the echo signal is first calculated, and the interval between the horizontal coordinates of neighbouring peaks is calculated by peak searching, which is related to the duration of the sub-waveform. Next, the frequency modulation slope of the interference sub-waveform is calculated, and then the sub-waveform matching signal is constructed to do matched filtering with the echo signal, Finally, interference reconstruction or filtering is used to suppress SMSP interference. The simulation results show that both the reconstruction method and filtering method can suppress the SMSP interference effectively, and the two methods are equivalent when the threshold is the same.

articleTitle: Effective velocity estimation method for passive location based on virtual aperture
abstract: As an important part of electronic reconnaissance, radiation source location technology has always attracted much attention. With the deployment of low-Earth orbit satellites and the development of 5G communication, the realization of 5G radiation source location has important military and commercial significance. In recent years, researchers have introduced synthetic aperture technology into passive location to improve the location accuracy. The algorithm uses the Doppler information of the received signal to locate the radiation source. To solve the influence of satellite orbit curvature and earth curvature on the location model under the spaceborne condition, the effective velocity is introduced. In this paper, an effective velocity estimation algorithm based on matched filtering is proposed. The received signal is filtered by the matched filter constructed by solving the positions of the emitter corresponding to different velocities. Different from the existing effective velocity estimation methods, this algorithm is less dependent on the geometric model, so the approximate estimation process is less and the estimation error is smaller. The simulation results show that the proposed algorithm can effectively improve the positioning accuracy and has better location performance than the traditional single-satellite location method.

articleTitle: Extraction of glacier surface flow velocity field based on multi-source SAR imagery in the Igong Tsangpo basin
abstract: The study of glacier surface flow velocity field in the mountainous area of southeast Tibet is of great significance for understanding the material changes and local climate formation in the middle and upper reaches of the Yangtze River. In this paper, we use multi-source satellite-based Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) images, analysis the advantages and disadvantages of the current glacier surface flow velocity field extraction methods, choose the feature tracking method to complete the extraction of the glacier surface flow velocity field in the Igong Tsangpo basin, and analysis the error of the calculation process with mathematical analysis and physical meaning. The results show that the glacier surface flow velocity in the basin is 0-464.6 ma-1 in 2003, 0-515.4 ma-1 in 2007, 0-492 ma-1 in 2010, and 0-447.5 ma-1 in 2015, which is consistent with the results of other studies in the region, and the results are credible. The use of multi-source satellite-based SAR images is an effective means of extracting the surface flow velocity field of mountain glaciers under severe climatic conditions.

articleTitle: Research on SAR image matching based on SAR-Harris detector and adaptive locally-affine matching
abstract: Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) image matching is an essential step in SAR image processing. The synthetic aperture radar- scale invariant feature transform (SAR-SIFT), which combines the ratio of exponentially weighted averages (ROEWA) operator with multiscale Harris detection and employs Random Sample Consensus (RANSAC) for matching and filtering, has shown promising results. However, SAR-SIFT suffers from low matching efficiency in specific scenarios, and RANSAC exhibits strong randomness and potential problems of non-convergence. To address these problems, this paper introduces an approach that combines scale-space layers reduction in the SAR-Harris detector with the efficient Adaptive Locally-Affine Matching (AdaLAM) to enhance SAR image matching performance. The proposed SAR-SIFT-AdaLAM method is experimentally evaluated on two sets of different SAR images for matching, and the results indicate an improvement of approximately 25% in the number of matching points compared to the SAR-SIFT, along with a reduction of about 30% in matching time, demonstrating its effectiveness.

articleTitle: Forwarding false target jamming suppression method based on peak distribution characteristics
abstract: Both digital radio frequency memory (DRFM)-based interrupted-sampling repeater jamming (ISRJ) and full pulse forwarding jamming (FPFJ) utilize the coherence of radar signals to form multiple false targets by sampling, storing, processing and forwarding the received signals. In order to improve the radar's ability to restrain forwarding false target jamming, this paper proposes a forwarding false target jamming suppression method based on the characteristics of the peak distribution of high-resolution range profiles (HRRP). False targets have a distribution pattern of approximately equal intervals during forwarding, while the distribution of targets has no regularity. Therefore, a peak interval threshold is designed to achieve false target jamming recognition and suppression. Finally, the effectiveness of the method is validated through simulations.

articleTitle: Task scheduling of radar constellation for continuous area monitoring
abstract: This study presents a time-dependent search task scheduling method of a radar constellation, dedicated to continuous monitoring of a large area under strict power constraints. Radar constellations are designed based on the observation area and the field of view (FOV) of radar. The scenario time and observation area are discretized by the search data rate and radar beam size, respectively, and the dwell time of radar is calculated as the cost of scheduling. A rescheduling method and a reassignment algorithm are developed to eliminate the out-of-power and over-allocated satellites due to the ‘nearest scheduling’ (simply assign tasks to satellites with the minimum dwell time), and reduce the requested system resources. In simulation, consecutive observation of an over 20 million km<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> irregular area is conducted for 35 hours with a search data rate of one minute. The results show that: the proposed method reduces the quantity of operational satellites from 57 to 51, fulfilling all power limit constraints. Besides, the requested system resources like satellite battery capacity, solar array size, and radar power-aperture can be further diminished by properly choosing the parameters of the reassignment algorithm.

articleTitle: An adaptive CFAR detector based on binary neural network and its FPGA implementation
abstract: The Constant False Alarm Rate (CFAR) algorithm is a method used for radar target detection. However, it is designed for specific clutter distributions and radar operation scenarios, which makes it challenging to guarantee detection performance in continuously changing environments. To overcome this limitation, this paper proposes an adaptive CFAR detector based on a binary neural network (BNN) to enhance radar target detection in various scenarios. BNN performs pattern recognition on the echo signal, judges the current operation environment of the radar, and guides the CFAR processor to choose the optimal detection algorithm for the corresponding scene. An energy entropy-based feature extraction algorithm is proposed to obtain the pattern feature map of the signal under different scenes through energy analysis. The simulation results demonstrate that the proposed feature extraction algorithm significantly improves the recognition accuracy and generalization ability of BNN, resulting in only a small performance loss compared to the full-precision parameter network. Finally, the CFAR detector is deployed on FPGA, and the experimental results show that BNN-CFAR significantly reduces memory usage and computational overhead during hardware implementation, achieving approximately 10 times network computational acceleration.

articleTitle: Space-time adaptive processing algorithm via reciprocal-filter for airborne passive radar
abstract: Due to the continuous random and non-periodic characteristics of the passive signal, the different modulation information within each equivalent pulse will exacerbate the performance of space-time adaptive processing (STAP) algorithm in airborne passive radar (APR). In this paper, an appropriate STAP method based on reciprocal-filter and Sparse Bayesian Learning (RFSBL-STAP) is proposed for clutter suppression of APR. The advantage of the algorithm is that it cannot only address the impact of the modulation information mismatch in each equivalent pulse, but also achieve accurately space-time spectral estimation with small samples. A series of simulations are conducted to verify the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Joint classification of hyperspectral and SAR data using asymmetric residual cross transformer
abstract: With the increasing amount of remote sensing (RS) data obtained from satellites or airborne platforms, The combined use of multimodal remote sensing data to improve classification performance has been widely concerned. Therefore, a new transformer-based hyperspectral and synthetic aperture radar (HS-SAR) data joint classification network ACCT was proposed in the paper. Combining the strengths of convolutional neural networks (CNN) and transformer, focus on extracting specific and common features from HS and SAR data. In addition, adding layer scale to the output of each residual block can learn diagonal matrix and improve the dynamics of training. Then, combining the advantages of residual join and asymmetric convolution kernel, the parameters are reduced while the feature information is fully learned. Experiments in this paper are carried out on two famous multimodal fusion datasets: Augsburg (AU), and Berlin (BL) datasets. Results show that ACCT achieves better classification accuracy than several existing models. OA reaches 97.20%, and 85.02% on the two datasets.

articleTitle: Few-shot class-incremental SAR target classification based on class-aware bilateral distillation
abstract: Due to the difficulty of acquiring synthetic aperture radar images, it is difficult to acquire a large number of images to train synthetic aperture radar automatic target recognition (SAR-ATR) models like optical datasets. In addition, in an open environment, how to learn and identify new categories quickly and accurately is also an urgent problem for SAR-ATR model to solve. To tackle this problem, this paper proposes a new few-shot class-incremental SAR-ATR model based on class-aware bilateral distillation. Specifically, we draw from two complementary teachers. One is a model trained on large amounts of SAR image data from base classes that have a wealth of general knowledge that can be used to mitigate the overfitting problems of current new classes. The other is the updated model of the last incremental session, which contains the adapted knowledge of the previous new session to mitigate their forgetting. The experimental results on the commonly used MSTAR dataset show that the SAR-ATR model based on class-aware bilateral distillation has significant advantages in few-shot class-incremental recognition task.

articleTitle: Development and application analysis of low-cost decoy target aircraft
abstract: With the rapid development of unmanned and intelligent, the future war had higher and higher requirements for low-cost unmanned system products and equipment, and how to meet the complex environment, especially the use of low-cost unmanned decoy target system in the combat environment was also crucial. This paper first introduced the overview of decoy target system and its development at home and abroad. Then the combat mode and development trend of low-cost decoy target system were introduced. Finally, the key technologies of low cost decoy target system were analyzed. The research ideas and methods were suitable for the development, design and application of low-cost unmanned target aircraft systems in engineering.

articleTitle: Research on decorrelation analysis and image registration method for UAV InSAR
abstract: In recent years, Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) interferometric synthetic aperture radar (InSAR) has become a research hotspot due to its advantages of being lightweight, and portable. However, during the UAV InSAR multi-pass interferometry, various decorrelation factors reduce the coherence between images. Among these factors, the baseline length and undulating terrain cause the spatial characteristic offsets between SAR images, resulting in mismatch decorrelation of the region, and traditional InSAR registration methods fail to address this issue. This paper firstly analyses the effect of different decorrelation factors. In addition, based on the analysis above, an image registration approach is proposed. Firstly, the images are uniformly divided into a number of sub-blocks, and different regions of undulating terrain are segmented based on correlation coefficients. Then, each region is independently extracted to cross-correlation registration. Finally, the registration results of regions are combined and fused. The effectiveness of the proposed approach is verified by using the measured data.

articleTitle: An angle measurement method of sum-difference beams for machine-scanning VHF radar
abstract: The angle measurement method of sum-difference beams for machine-scanning VHF radar is studied in this paper. The particularity of wide beamwidth and long wavelength of VHF radar is analyzed, and the improvement and realization method of sum-difference beams angle measurement is discussed. On this basis , the signal processing flow to realize the angle measurement function are designed. Finally, the different situations are simulated, and the angel measurement performance of machine- scanning VHF radar is evaluated, and engineering tests are carried out. The simulation and engineering tests verify the correctness and effectiveness of the improved method.

articleTitle: PMBM filter with tree trajectory model for spawning extended target tracking
abstract: In extended target tracking, target spawning is a significant event. The conventional Poisson multi-Bernoulli mixture (PMBM) filter encounters challenges in determining the prior distributions for spawning extended targets and experiences a degradation in tracking performance within clutter environments. This paper proposes a modified PMBM method known as the Extended Target Tree Trajectory PMBM filter (ET-TrPMBM). This method entails the representation of the complete trajectory’s continuous information and genealogies of an original extended target, as well as its subsequently spawning descendants, as a tree trajectory variable, which is employed as an input within the PMBM recursion process. To effectively extract the trajectory of an individual spawning target from the intricate tree trajectory, an independent and identically distributed (IID) Bernoulli cluster is deployed. This cluster operates as an approximation tool for the posterior distribution of the tree trajectory, and the optimal approximation is achieved by the KL divergence minimisation. Furthermore, this study encompasses the application of gamma Gaussian inverse Wishart (GGIW) distribution within the context of tree trajectories, and provides the close-form solutions for the ET-TrPMBM filter. Simulation results verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A LiDAR localization method based on spatio-temporal fusion and quality filtering
abstract: Vehicle localization is one of the primary challenges in autonomous driving. LiDAR, due to its wide detection range and high distance accuracy, has been widely applied in the localization tasks of autonomous driving. Traditional LiDAR localization algorithms rely solely on the pose obtained from matching the current single-frame point cloud. However, due to the sparsity of point cloud, single-frame matching methods struggle to avoid localization errors. To solve this problem, this paper proposes a LiDAR localization method based on spatiotemporal fusion and quality filtering. Firstly, a spatiotemporal fused pose set is constructed to take advantage of spatiotemporal connectivity between LiDAR data. Then, a quality filtering process is applied to select the best poses from the pose set. Finally, the best poses are further optimized to improve the localization accuracy. The performance of the proposed method is evaluated using both open-source data and real-world measured data, validating the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Analysis of polarimetric distortions of radar waves in magnetized plasma sheath
abstract: The high velocity reentry objects suffer from the plasma sheath, which will affect the propagation characteristics of the radar signal. The existing research mainly focuses on the time-frequency characteristics of the radar signal neglecting the influence of geomagnetic environment. In this article, the polarimetric distortions of radar wave in magnetized plasma sheath are analyzed and the influence of geomagnetic field is evaluated. Based on the Appleton-Hartree (A-H) formula, the refractive index of the plasma sheath considering the geomagnetic field is derived and analyzed. Then, the error model of the polarization rotation (PR) for radar wave is established. For the radar system, PR will cause the offset in polarization plane, resulting in the distortion of the polarimetric characteristics and the attenuation of the echo amplitude. Simulating with the typical parameters, the influences from the electron density, the collision frequency and the radar frequency are analyzed respectively. According to measured data, for C-band radar signals, when the geomagnetic field is 60000 nT, the PR can reach 0.006°, and the PR attenuation can reach −5×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−8</sup> dB. In addition, the increasing electron density expands them, whereas the radar frequency and the collision frequency play the opposite role.

articleTitle: Exploring the deep incremental learning for radar target recognition
abstract: In the practical applications of radar, a large amount of data is dynamically obtained during the operation of radar systems. Constructing the incremental learning capability for radar target recognition in the open environments has become a research focus. This work studies to use the incremental learning method for improving the radar target recognition models in open and adversarial scenarios. For this purpose, we construct a High Resolution Range Profile (HRRP) dataset, design a new deep convolutional neural network based on one-dimensional ResNet, and conduct extensive data analysis with incremental learning for radar target recognition. The experimental results in this paper demonstrate that: (1) For HRRP data used in radar target recognition, there exists a basic data volume requirement. The model accuracy remains stable when this requirement is satisfied. (2) The impact of sample imbalance on recognition performance is related to the target characteristics. (3) Considering the low-density characteristics of radar in HRRP, through the construction of non-forgetting samples, we effectively reduce the amount of data samples used for model training without affecting the accuracy of target recognition.
