This work significantly helps the construction of effective radar recognition training data, and realizes robust radar target recognition through incremental learning.

articleTitle: An interpulse ship discrimination method in bistatic radar system
abstract: In this paper, an interpulse ship discrimination method is proposed in a bistatic radar system, utilizing the distinct spatial scattering properties of ships and corner reflectors. First, raw data from two radars is locally preprocessed to extract complex envelope sequences of targets. Subsequently, a correlation test is conducted with threshold estimation using bistatic radar linked data, enabling target discrimination based on the correlation coefficient and threshold. Finally, the fused data can be utilized to output the target position parameters. The effectiveness of the proposed algorithm is demonstrated through on-site experimental data verification.

articleTitle: Complex-valued cross-domain few-shot learning network for PolSAR image classification
abstract: Gathering reliable labeled samples for polarimetric synthetic aperture (PolSAR) image classification is laborious. Moreover, applying a trained classifier to new domains often leads to noticeable performance degradation due to domain disparities. Therefore, this paper proposes the novel complex-valued cross-domain (CD) few-shot learning classification (CCFSLC) method for PolSAR images to address these issues. Firstly, the transferrable knowledge learning module (TKLM) with a complex-valued feature encoder (CVFE) is trained using source data with sufficient labeled samples. Then, the deep few-shot learning module (DFSLM), constructed using the pre-trained CVFE, is trained by episodes in both source and target domains, with only minimal target labeled samples. Meanwhile, the adversarial domain adaptation module (ADAM) is employed to eliminate domain shift. The proposed CCFSLC mainly focuses on exploring discriminative information from raw PolSAR data, while reducing the domain gap to recognize novel categories in unseen domains with only a few annotated samples. Experiments on typical PolSAR datasets validate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Noise-assisted multivariate successive variational mode decomposition
abstract: Multi-dimensional Variational mode decomposition (MVMD) has shown great potential in analyzing multichannel signals. However, the requirement of presetting the number of extracted components diminishes the analytic property of both VMD and MVMD methods. We propose the Noise- assisted Multi-dimensional Successive Variational mode decomposition (NA-MSVMD) for multivariate signals denoise. We extend SVMD to multiple dimensions and use the alternating directional multiplication method(ADMM) to solve the multi-dimensional optimization problem. In addition, we combine the multi-dimensional SVMD with the noise injection paradigm to obtain the noise-assisted multi- dimensional successive variational mode decomposition (NA-MSVMD). In contrast to MVMD, our method implements adaptive decomposition and eliminates the reliance on the parameter K. We performed simulated signal experiments, EEG signal denoising tests and bearing troubleshooting tests to verify the effectiveness of our proposed method.

articleTitle: Application of ground penetrating radar 3D detection in tunnel engineering
abstract: In order to accurately forecast and quantitatively analyze groundwater, karst and other bad geological bodies, the 3D imaging technology of ground penetrating radar (GPR) has become one of the main technologies of tunnel engineering geological detection. In order to explore the application of GPR 3D detection technology in tunnel engineering, this paper designs the GPR 3D system through the point detection mode and the radar wave directional radiation distribution data acquisition system. Based on the detection results of ground penetrating radar, the characteristics of rock mass in different ranges from the palm face are analyzed. Through MMS multi-wave and multi-component detection, the three dimensional imaging technology of ground penetrating radar and seismic wave detection method are mutually verified. The results show that the detection range of GPR 3D imaging technology is large, the detection speed is fast and the detection results are accurate.

articleTitle: An autofocus network for multi-channel phase errors with application to tomoSAR imaging
abstract: Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) tomography (TomoSAR) has garnered significant attention due to its capability for three-dimensional reconstruction. Compressed sensing (CS) methods are widely employed to address the TomoSAR inversion challenge. Nevertheless, practical applications reveal phase errors among different channels, resulting in defocusing and blurring when relying solely on CS for 3D reconstruction. Current state-of-the-art autofocus techniques suffer from prohibitive computational complexity, limiting their applicability to large-scale 3D imaging. In pursuit of efficient TomoSAR 3-D autofocusing, we proposed ASAMP-Net, an innovative deep unfolding network. Operating within a two-step framework, each layer comprises two stages: phase error estimation and iterative scattering coefficient reconstruction using the sparse adaptive matching pursuit (SAMP) algorithm. Additionally, phase error estimation is obtained through mathematical derivation, while challenges associated with fixed sparsity and limited efficiency in conventional methods are mitigated through deep learning techniques. Simulation experiments and real data validation affirm the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Unsupervised anomaly detection for radar active deception jamming based on denoising diffusion implicit model
abstract: Detection of radar active deception jamming signals is essential for effectively countering potential threats. Currently, the detection performance in supervised learning partially depends on the training samples with correct jamming annotations. However, there are substantial types of active jamming in modern battlefields, posing a significant challenge for radar systems to capture a satisfactory number of jamming samples with definite annotations for training. Moreover, the existing unsupervised anomaly detection (UAD) methods have limited performance in high-accuracy detection. In this paper, we propose a UAD method based on the denoising diffusion implicit model (DDIM), aiming to automatically mark jamming- related anomalies and then score for the marked patches. Compared to representative unsupervised models, the simulation results demonstrate the remarkable superiority of the proposed method in the application of UAD.

articleTitle: Gradient test for double subspace signal detection
abstract: In this paper, we consider the detection problem for double subspace signal detection and devise an effective detector according to the criterion of gradient test, which possesses the constant false alarm rate (CFAR) property with respect to unknown noise covariance matrix. Numerical examples show that the proposed detector can achieve better detection performance than existing ones. We also show the factors which can affect the detection performance.

articleTitle: Single pulse target detection method based on a two-stage convolutional neural network
abstract: In order to quickly and accurately detect targets in radar echoes, this paper studies a single pulse target detection method based on the convolutional neural network. This method fully utilizes the feature extraction ability of neural networks and divides the target detection task into a two-stage regression task. Similar to the process of human detecting targets, the network first quickly scans the entire echo to determine the approximate position of the target, and then conducts precise searches within a specific range. This not only ensures the accuracy, but also achieves a faster detection speed than conventional neural network detection methods. After experimental verification, the method proposed can achieve a detection probability of over 80% when the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) is only -3dB, and its running speed is fast enough for practical use.

articleTitle: Characteristics analysis of stepped frequency chirp signal using uniform interrupted modulation
abstract: The co-modulation is beneficial for increasing the anti-reconnaissance potential of radar waveform. Stepped frequency chirp (SFC) signal has the characteristics of both linear frequency modulation (LFM) signal and stepped-frequency waveform (SFW). Uniform interrupted modulation (UIM) can increase the complexity of the signal in the time domain. Therefore, the characteristics of the SFC signal with UIM are deduced in this paper. First of all, the processing method of the SFC signal is introduced. Then the characteristics of the SFC signal with UIM are analysed emphatically. The high-resolution range profile (HRRP) of the inter-pulse and intra-pulse interrupted modulation are both deduced respectively. It is concluded that the UIM between pulses brings the HRRP of the SFC signal multiple pseudo peaks extending along the range profile. However, there is no pseudo peak in the HRRP of the intra-pulse interruptedly modulated SFC signal. Signal simulation experiments are carried out with MATLAB to verify the accuracy of the theoretical analysis.

articleTitle: An improved two-dimensional CFAR detector for moving target detection in complex ground clutter scenarios
abstract: The CFAR detectors have been used widely in radar detection. Multi-dimensional CFAR detectors outperform one-dimensional CFAR detectors in many scenarios. CFAR detectors achieve optimal performance when the cells in the scenario are independent and identically distributed (I.I.D.). In scenarios with severe ground clutter, pulse-Doppler (PD) radar usually employs a high-pass finite impulse response (FIR) filter and coherent integration to detect moving targets. The filter has a limited passband width, breaks the I.I.D. in the Doppler dimension, and restricts the usage of multi-dimensional CFAR. This paper proposes a two-dimensional CFAR detector that is suitable for PD radar detecting moving targets under heavy ground clutter scenarios. It incorporates the magnitude response of the filter to the reference cells selection of the CFAR detector. These cells are more likely to be I.I.D. and can be used to estimate the interference level across Doppler bins. This detector does not require massive calculations. Based on a set of measured data with spatiotemporally varied ground clutter, this detector demonstrates more stable detection performance and fewer false alarms compared to traditional one-dimensional CFAR detectors.

articleTitle: CAP-Net: a cross-attention prototype network for robust few-shot ISAR target classification
abstract: Classification for inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR) target remains a challenging task due to insufficient training samples and unknown image deformations. To achieve robust feature extraction and accurate classification, a cross-attention prototype network, namely CAP-Net, is proposed in this article. Different from existing few-shot learning frameworks, the spatial transformation network (STN) is integrated into CAP-Net to achieve adaptive adjustment of unknown deformations, and the cross-attention module (CAM) is also designed to build a bridge between support and query samples for effective information interaction. Experimental results on multi-class ISAR satellite dataset demonstrate that the proposed method can significantly improve the accuracy of few-shot ISAR target classification compared to other state-of-the-art methods.

articleTitle: A computationally efficient sparse SAR imaging network based on ADMM
abstract: For the problem of SAR imaging resolution degradation under sparse sampling and phase error conditions, we propose a computationally efficient depth unfolding network for high-resolution SAR imaging. The proposed algorithm introduces an approximate observation operator based on the traditional sparse SAR imaging method, which reduces the size of the measurement matrix and improves the computational efficiency of the algorithm using the Kronecker property. The method designs the algorithm iteration process as a corresponding network layer, which makes up for the drawbacks of poor interpretability of data- driven network-based methods in SAR imaging, reduces the difficulty of parameter setting in traditional sparse imaging methods, improves the imaging speed, and is expected to achieve high-precision real-time imaging of SAR. The experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness and applicability of the method.

articleTitle: Inter-pulse carrier frequency agile design for cognitive radar
abstract: This paper deals with the joint design of inter-pulse frequency and receive filter to reduce the Doppler sidelobe for cognitive Frequency Agile Radar (FAR) working in search and confirmation modes. At first, we introduce an inter-pulse coherent processing method that integrates phase compensation with Weighted Non-Uniform Discrete Fourier Transform (W-NUDFT). Then, a multi-parameter non-convex optimization model is established based on the issue of high Doppler sidelobes caused by inter-pulse non-uniform accumulation. Subsequently, we develop an alternating iterative optimization algorithm that combines Coordinate Descent with Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (CD-ADMM) to tackle the resulting non-convex optimization problem. Finally, through numerical simulations, the effectiveness of the waveform via the application on weak targets detection accompanied by strong targets is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Close-loop EMS emulator with 3-D RCS map and geographical information based propagation modelling
abstract: A close-loop EMS emulator for EM environment and threat simulation is introduced in this paper. Using the 3-D RCS map and EM wave geographical propagation modelling during the generation of multiple signal and threat targets echo signal, can help increase the fidelity of the EM environment and threat simulation in actual operation for the purpose of mission effectiveness verification.

articleTitle: A novel algorithm for maneuvering target coherent integration based on second-order keystone and radon fourier transform
abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel coherent integration algorithm for the maneuvering target detection with constant acceleration. We first deduce the signal expression after pulse compression (PC). After PC, there exists range walk and curvature in the target's trajectory, and the phase can be modeled as a quadratic signal. In the following, we conduct the second-order keystone transform (SOKT) to correct the range curvature. After the SOKT, the target's trajectory become a slant straight line, i.e., only range walk is residual, whereas the phase signal is still quadratic. Borrowing the idea of Radon Fourier transform (RFT), we determine the target trajectory along straight lines by only searching the range and velocity and conduct the discrete chirp Fourier transform (DCFT) to estimate the phase parameters along the determined trajectory, and then construct a reference function. Finally, we accumulate the target signal in the searching range-velocity domain with multiplying the reference function. The real Ku-band radar data are processed to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm. Performance comparisons with other typical algorithms, i.e., GRFT, RFRFT, RLVD, validate that achieving the similar detection ability, our proposed algorithm is more computationally efficient and beneficial for CFAR detection.

articleTitle: Defect recognition method of digital twin power line image based on improved TridentNet
abstract: The detection of defects in Power Line images plays a vital role in timely and effective identification of equipment flaws, thereby preventing equipment failures. Current methods for transmission image defect detection need further algorithmic research to improve their capability to detect defects at different scales. In this paper, we propose an improved method for the TridentNet network specifically designed for transmission line inspection scenarios. We optimize the scale-based training strategy by adjusting the selection range to enhance the model training effectiveness. We introduce a new dimension in the backbone network to improve feature extraction efficiency. Additionally, we design a weight normalization process in the feature extraction part of the network to accelerate model convergence and improve accuracy when training data batches are small. These enhancements contribute to improved accuracy and recall rates for multi-scale defect detection in the same image. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness and accuracy of our proposed method.

articleTitle: Research on the influence of array configuration and non-ideal factors on the interference suppression performance of distributed array radars
abstract: Interference suppression is an important research topic in radar signal processing. Distributed array radars have strong interference suppression abilities, which can solve the problem of main-lobe interference suppression. The interference suppression performance of the distributed array radar is affected by array configuration and non-ideal factors. This paper studied the influence of array configuration and non-ideal factors. The impact of array configuration elements, including the distribution of the positions of arrays, the ratio of the area of the main array to the auxiliary array, and the baseline length of the distributed array, on interference suppression performance was studied through simulation analysis. The influence of non- ideal factors, including amplitude and phase errors, time synchronization errors, and auxiliary array beam pointing errors, on interference cancellation performance in different interference scenes was studied by simulations.

articleTitle: Length estimation of ships through dual-radar collaborative observation
abstract: The length of ships plays an important role in target classification and recognition, but to estimate ships' length in real time is difficult by traditional single radar observation. To solve this problem, the dual-radar collaborative observation method is proposed in this study to jointly calculate the ship length, by using the obtained HRRP (High Range Resolution Profile). The effect of SNR (signal-to-noise ratio) on estimation error of system parameters and the ship length estimated is simulated. The results show that the method can estimate the ship length effectively, the estimation error of the ship length is not more than one meter under high SNR (more than 10dB), which provides a reference for feature extraction and target recognition of ships.

articleTitle: Retrieval of nearshore bathymetry from spaceborne SAR data combining NRCS and Doppler shift
abstract: Research of nearshore bathymetry retrieval based on relationship between SAR NRCS and current gradients has been ongoing for over 30 years. But NRCS-based method is still far from practical application, because NRCS can reflect no actual current velocity but current gradients. Considering Doppler shift can provide with actual current velocity, this paper presents a method for retrieval of nearshore bathymetry using the NRCS and the Doppler shift from spaceborne SAR in order to compensates for the limitations of relying solely on NRCS. The retrieval method is based on Newton-GMRES method solving large sparse systems of nonlinear equations. The proposed method is applied to detect sandwave features at mesoscale(>10km) from spaceborne SAR simulation data. Under appropriate tidal and radar parameter conditions, the RMSE and MRE of the retrieval method combining both NRCS and Doppler shift is 2.14m and 10.14%, respectively, which outperform the performance based solely on NRCS (4.17m and 20.26%).

articleTitle: Wall clutter suppression for through-wall radar on hovering drone
abstract: Moving targets detection of through-wall radar (TWR) has attracted a significant amount of research interest in recent years. Most previous studies of moving target detection mainly focused on stationary platforms, like hand-held TWR. Moving-human target information can be detected on the echo map by moving target indicator (MTI). The combination of drones and TWR improves the detection area of radar. However, the TWR on hovering drones is unstable, which causes wall-scattered clutter submerging the moving human signal. This paper employed a wall clutter suppression technique based on robust principal component analysis (RPCA) to remove the stationary clutter of TWR. We first give the signal model of linear frequency modulation continuous wave (LFMCW) radar. Then, an RPCA algorithm is introduced to attenuate wall clusters. Finally, a field experiment of TWR on a hovering drone was performed and validated the effect of RPCA on UAV-borne TWR data. This paper approved that moving human echoes can be detected in drone TWR echoes.

articleTitle: The first demonstration of DEM generation using stereo SAR technique with ascending and descending LuTan-1 SAR data
abstract: Stereo synthetic aperture radar (SAR) observation is a method for digital elevation model (DEM) generation. Stereo SAR includes ipsilateral and heterolateral observation modes. Due to the inherent ambiguity caused by SAR imaging and shadowing effects from different viewing angles, matching in complex mountainous regions becomes challenging. In this paper, we introduce external DEM data to aid in the matching process and enhance matching accuracy through multiple iterations. Experimental observations were conducted in the mountainous regions of Northeastern China using the recently launched LuTan-1 SAR data. The resulting DEM, when differenced with the SRTM DEM, yielded an average discrepancy of -1.189 m and a Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 9.971 m. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of employing heterolateral stereo observations from the LuTan-1 satellite for effective applications in challenging mountainous terrains.

articleTitle: The video SAR simulation algorithm based on the DEM and SBR
abstract: This paper presents a rapid video synthetic aperture radar (SAR) simulation algorithm aimed at addressing the challenge of acquiring video SAR images. The proposed method independently simulates both targets and ground clutter. Background clutter is generated using a digital elevation map (DEM), while target echoes are simulated using Shooting and Bouncing rays (SBR). By employing ray tracing techniques, occlusion areas for both background clutter and targets are computed, thereby ensuring that the simulation results are adaptable to various algorithm development requirements. Ultimately, through a series of fast algorithms and GPU acceleration, significant reduction in simulation time is achieved, enabling rapid simulation of multiple video SAR images. This research provides abundant data sources for the study of video SAR detection, tracking, and recognition algorithms, offering robust support for practical applications.

articleTitle: A novel signal presence detection strategy in beamforming spectra for weak signal detection
abstract: In complex electromagnetic environments, passive radio direction determination often encounters a challenge where distant weak signals and nearby strong signals are difficult to separate in both the time and frequency domains. Weak signals are often masked by the presence of strong signals, making detection and localization problematic. To address this issue, this paper presents an approach that leverages the spatial spectrum generated by conventional beamforming techniques, utilizing its spectral valley features as confidence indicators for the rapid evaluation of spatial spectrum-based direction determination results. This method significantly enhances the detection probability of weak signals in the presence of strong signals, while simultaneously reducing false alarms when weak signals are absent.

articleTitle: Unsupervised feature representation for ocean-going ship detection
abstract: Feature representation plays a crucial role in ocean-going ships detection with remote sensing imagery. The robustness of traditional hand-craft features is heavily influenced by prior knowledge, and modern deep neural network models require a large amount of annotated data. In this case, the large field of view characteristic of remote sensing imageries leads to high and challenging annotation costs. Here, we investigate an unsupervised feature representation method, utilizing the spatial context of similar affinity to enhance local descriptors. The refined local descriptors are embedded into a subspace constructed by learned landmarks, aiming to achieve a linear approximation and derive equivalent feature representation. Further, visual cosine similarity is utilized for labelling similar samples in a large-scale data environment. Compared with one-shot object detection methods with classical hand-craft features, the experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves superior detection efficiency with little training instances.

articleTitle: Radar jamming state prediction method based on CNN-LSTM
abstract: By setting the strategy, the jammer adaptively transmits the appropriate jamming against the received radar signal, which poses a great threat to modern radar. Moreover, they also provide the potential for predicting jamming in radar systems. Radar jamming state prediction is crucial for the effectiveness and real-time performance of anti-jamming, and accurate prediction for the future state of jamming can guarantee the initiative of radar in electronic warfare. In order to better explore the effective information contained in the radar countermeasure data, a radar jamming state prediction method based on Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) is proposed for the characteristics of nonlinearity and time series of jamming state data. By incorporating the received jamming characteristics, including jamming type and parameters, along with the current radar status information as inputs into the network, the prediction of future jamming states can be achieved. Multiple comparative simulations have demonstrated the effectiveness of the proposed method, as well as its advantage in terms of time-consuming tasks.

articleTitle: Research on imaging coordinate system of time-domain algorithm in BI-SAR system
abstract: The time-domain imaging algorithm can meet the imaging requirements of bistatic synthetic aperture radar(Bi-SAR) system with flexible and complex configurations, and establishing the imaging coordinate system is the key step especially for Fast Time-Domain algorithms. In this paper, to simplify the establishment of imaging coordinate system, the orthogonal elliptical mapping polar (OEMP) coordinate system is proposed and used in the frame of the fast factorized back projection(FFBP) algorithm. Compared to the orthogonal elliptical polar(OEP) coordinate system, the proposed coordinate system has simpler coordinate solving, and can also reduce the computational burden of the FFBP algorithms. The applicability and performance of the OEMP-based FFBP algorithm is verified through simulation experiments.

articleTitle: A phase synchronization device and method for distributed receiving radar based on orthogonal signals
abstract: Phase synchronization of radar carrier is key issue to realize for signal coherent processing of distributed multiple receiving radars. A novel phase synchronization method and a synchronizing device, which is based on a group of orthogonal synchronization pulse signals, are proposed. Each orthogonal synchronization pulse signal is simultaneously sent to the other receiving stations by a omnidirectional synchronization antenna. The Doppler effect can be eliminated. The phase synchronization errors between each two receiving stations can be quickly extracted. And then the phase errors of radar echoes can be compensated, the coherent processing gain of multiple echo signals and target detection can be achieved.

articleTitle: Air target threat assessment using latent features enhanced Bayesian networks
abstract: Threat assessment technology, which analyzes various potential threat factors in the aerial combat environment, can assist combat personnel in quickly identifying important targets and taking timely combat countermeasures. Bayesian network is one of the most effective model in representing and reasoning with uncertain knowledge, particularly suitable for addressing the problem of threat assessment under the open and volatile battlefield information. However, their capability to uncover and express latent features is limited. To achieve enhanced assessment capabilities in complex battlefield environments, this paper proposes a threat assessment technique based on latent features enhanced Bayesian networks. We first define the explicit features and latent features of air targets. Then, we utilize a deep learning approach with Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) to extract the latent maneuvering features of air targets from detection data. Finally, the latent features along with the explicit features, are jointly employed as inputs to the Bayesian network, resulting in the air target threat probabilities. Experimental results demonstrate that the latent features enhanced Bayesian network improves the accuracy of threat assessment results.

articleTitle: A scattering mechanism analysis model for vessels in polarimetric SAR images
abstract: Vessels are usually paid much attention to in polarimetric synthetic aperture radar (PolSAR) images. Analyzing the detailed polarimetric scattering mechanism of vessels can provide guidance for the subsequent feature extraction and target detection. In this paper, a scattering mechanism analysis model is proposed, which can be used to simulate PolSAR images of vessels under various observation conditions and to analyse the scattering mechanism. Based on the high frequency approximation techniques, ray tracing is applied to calculate the backscattering coefficients. Simulated echo signal and image can be obtained by convolving the backscattering coefficients with original echo signal of PolSAR system. Through this simulation analysis model, a lot of data acquisition costs can be saved, and the polarimetric scattering mechanism of vessels under any observation condition can be freely analysed. The experimental results show that the model can effectively obtain the simulated PolSAR image of vessel and be used to analyse the scattering mechanism, which provides help for the subsequent feature extraction and target detection.

articleTitle: A machine learning burned area extracting method based on dual-polarization Sentinel-1 images
abstract: Aiming at the problem that it is difficult to perform accurate burned areas mapping with a single polarization feature, we propose a machine learning burned area extraction method based on dual-polarization sentinel-1 images, which aims to make full use of the parameter changes in backscattering intensity, polarization decomposition, and texture features caused by forest fires. In this paper, we first construct a feature parameter dataset for the polarization feature and texture feature changes caused by forest fires. On this basis, the optimal combination of features that best reflects the changes in the burned area is determined by combining feature importance and correlation analysis. We used a random forest (RF) model for burned area mapping. For verifying the feasibility of the model and algorithm, Sentinel-1 images before and after the forest fire were selected for the Xichang fire in 2020 to carry out experiments. The experimental results show that the accuracy of combustion area extraction of the method in this paper is 93.68%, and the Kappa coefficient is 0.7955.

articleTitle: A deep neural network full-flow imaging method for SAR moving targets
abstract: This paper introduces a deep neural network imaging method for SAR moving targets. The full flow of the method includes model construction and defocused imaging, training dataset generation, and imaging network construction. Firstly, we establish a moving target imaging model to achieve defocused imaging of multiple moving targets under different motion parameters, and construct a high-quality and rich radar image dataset, then, based on the generated dataset, we propose a deep neural network-based SAR moving target imaging method. Finally, through comparative simulation experiments, we verify the effectiveness and superiority of the method. The results not only prove the correctness of the simulation method, but also show the great potential of the method in supporting the research of SAR moving target indication, classification, and recognition.

articleTitle: High-speed maneuvering target detector based on deep residual network
abstract: Range migration and Doppler frequency migration lead to severe coherent integration loss and worse target detection performance in high-speed maneuvering target detection. In this paper, a deep residual network detector (RND) is proposed for high-speed maneuvering target detection. The RND is used to replace the Doppler processing and hypothesis testing components in the conventional signal processing procedure. By training, the RND is capable of effectively achieving a nonlinear mapping from range-compressed signals to target detection results, demonstrating that the proposed detector exhibits excellent detection performance. Finally, numerical experiments validate that the detection performance of the RND is better than that of the KT-MF algorithm in the scenario of higher signal-to-noise ratio, and the computational complexity is much lower than that of the KT-MF algorithm, which can demonstrate the RND can achieve a trade-off between detection performance and computational complexity.

articleTitle: Sparse representation based DOA estimation of mixed circular and non-circular signals
abstract: In this paper, the problem of direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation for the mixture of circular and non-circular signals is considered and a new sparse signal recovery (SSR) based method is proposed. The estimation process consists of two steps. First, the DOAs of non-circular signals are retrieved by formulating and solving a one-dimensional SSR optimization problem based on the elliptic covariance matrix of the array output. Then, with the steering vectors corresponding to the estimated non-circular signals, the DOAs of the remaining circular signals can be retrieved by similarly formulating and solving a one-dimensional SSR optimization problem based on the covariance matrix of the distinguished array output. Compared with the existing methods, the setting of the regularization parameter is not involved in the constructed SSR problems. Moreover, the computational complexity of our proposed method is considerably alleviated since the proposed method avoids the two-dimensional SSR structure required in previous work. The improved performance of the proposed method over the existing methods in terms of resolution capability and estimation accuracy is verified by simulation results. Particularly, the simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method maintains robust estimation performance in challenging scenarios, such as few available snapshots or very low SNR (signal-to-noise ratio) levels.

articleTitle: Hybrid integration detection of moving target with moderately fluctuating RCS
abstract: Compared to the classical Swerling model, the moderately fluctuating model can be seen as a more general model to describe the practical target's radar cross section (RCS). To achieve the optimal signal-to-noise (SNR) gain, this paper proposes a hybrid integration method for detecting moving target with moderately fluctuating RCS. It is shown that the correlation of moderately fluctuating RCS is decreasing with the time lag between different pulses. Therefore, after the range migration correction (RMC), the echo in the coherent processing interval (CPI) is divided into several sub-apertures. In each sub- aperture, the coherent integration is applied, while between different sub-apertures, the non-coherent integration is applied. The validity of the proposed algorithm is confirmed by the signal-level example and Monte Carlo simulations.

articleTitle: The syntheses design of an S-band 32-channel broadband filter and monitoring network
abstract: An S-band 32-channel broadband filter monitoring network is designed, which integrates low-pass filtering, channel monitoring and broadband power combiner, and with high integration and low loss characteristics. The design, simulation, and measured results of low-pass filters, monitoring coupling circuits, and wideband power combiner networks are introduced .The measured results show that the standing wave of the main channel is less than 1.3, the transmission loss is less than 0.5dB, and the out-of-band rejection is better than 37dB, which achieves the expected purpose within 25% broadband of the S-band. This design idea and method have broad application prospects.

articleTitle: Multi-channel HBM parallel storage controller for spaceborne SAR imaging system
abstract: With the continuous development of remote sensing technology, Spaceborne Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) is gradually evolving towards acquiring information in space and real-time on-board processing. Therefore, the real-time processing requirements for its imaging processing system are becoming increasingly stringent. The data bandwidth of the existing imaging processing systems cannot meet the high real-time processing demands. To address the aforementioned issues and satisfy the high bandwidth requirements of on-board SAR imaging processing systems, this paper proposes a multi-channel High Bandwidth Memory(HBM) parallel storage controller for Spaceborne SAR. It enables parallel data reading and writing for 16 data channels. The overall hardware design is based on the Virtex UltraScale+ HBM VCU128 FPGA platform. Through testing and verification, under the same clock frequency, the data bandwidth has been improved by approximately 10 times compared to existing solutions, achieving around 80GB/s of ultra-high bandwidth data read-write capability. Additionally, this design solution holds significant potential for further development, making it of considerable value and significance for the design of on-board SAR imaging processing systems.

articleTitle: An improved range migration algorithm based on azimuth time resampling for automotive SAR with curved trajectory
abstract: The automotive Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) can obtain two-dimensional (2-D) high-resolution images compared with millimeter-wave (MMW) radar which the azimuth resolution is limited by the antenna aperture in the automatic driving system. However, the existence of acceleration causes the vehicle’s motion trajectory is no longer a straight trajectory, so the traditional range model and SAR imaging algorithm are not suitable. To solve these issues, this paper first proposes an equivalent range model to describe the curved trajectory for the little turn case. Then an improved Range Migration Algorithm (RMA) is proposed based on the range model, which combines the azimuth preprocessing with RMA. The azimuth time preprocessing employs a resampling method to eliminate the effect of acceleration. Simulation and experiment results verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Polarization domain coordinate mapping cancellation method based on least norm solution of compatible non-homogeneous linear equations
abstract: When the main lobe interferences and the desired signal have close polarization angles with the same frequency and direction of arrivals, the output signal to interference ratio of the oblique projection polarization filter (OPPF) will be degraded. Therefore, a polarization domain coordinate mapping cancellation method (PDCMCM) based on the minimum norm solution of compatible non-homogeneous linear equations is proposed to get better interference suppression performance in this paper. To achieve the purpose of suppressing the specific parameter signal, by constructing the suppression optimization matrix, the coordinate transformation is performed in the original parameter domain of received signal, and the orthogonal projection is done in the transformed parameter domain. Compared with the traditional polarization filtering method and OPPF, the proposed method has higher signal-to-interference ratio and strong robustness.

articleTitle: LandSAR software testing method for Lu Tan-1 SAR standard product generation in natural resource monitoring
abstract: LandSAR software is first developed by the InSAR group of the Land Satellite Remote Sensing Application Center (LASAC) in 2015, which is designed for Chinese differential interferometric SAR satellite constellation application. It is used for interferometric applications such as DEM and deformation product production. After Lu Tan-1 satellites were launched in 2022, LandSAR entered the systematical testing phase. In this paper, the testing flow of LandSAR was introduced. In the systematical testing phase, we carried out unit testing method (UTM), integrated testing method (ITM), system testing method (STM), and acceptance testing method (ATM), verifying the function and performance of the 177 modules at all levels. We use a multi-factor testing flow (MFTF) to test the software. Until now, about 80 modules of the software have been distributed to 53 users from multi-province nationwide for trial. By testing, the software has been continuously optimized. In order to ensure the quality of data processing results, after repeated systematical testing and acceptance testing, we have formed the key steps of InSAR and DInSAR data standardization processing flow with ideal data results. Next, we will rely on the standard processes mentioned to declare SAR data processing standards and carry out data business production of LuTan-1 satellites. The standardization will be helpful for various industries to carry out natural resource monitoring and supervision work.

articleTitle: Optimization method of inter-pulse phase agility waveform
abstract: Inter-pulse phase agility (IPPA) waveform attracts widespread attention for its capability to resolve range ambiguity and suppress clutter and jamming. Due to the superiority of IPPA, a waveform design method based on ambiguity function is proposed in this paper, which regularizes the optimization of weighted integrated sidelobe level (WISL) and peak sidelobe level (PSL) in interested range segments of ambiguity function under the same framework. The proposed method simplifies the objective by majorization-minimization method, then eliminates the constant modulus constraint through variable substitution and solves it with BFGS. Besides, an acceleration scheme for the proposed method is also raised. Through numerical simulations, the effectiveness of the proposed method is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Time reversal MIMO detector in clutter environments
abstract: The time reversal (TR) technology can explore the rich scattering in a multipath signals environment to improve the radar detection performance by adaptively matching the propagation channel to achieve the space-time focusing effect. However, in the scenario where the clutter exists, the detection performance of the TR technology on the multipath utilization will be degraded. Unlike the phased-array radar systems, the multiple-input multiple-out (MIMO) radar can transmit diverse waveforms across the transmitters. In this paper, a MIMO radar detector based on the TR technology and the power allocation method is proposed in the clutter and the multipath signals environment. The numerical simulations demonstrate that the proposed detector outperforms the conventional statistical MIMO detector.

articleTitle: A high-integrated Ka-band phased array antenna for radar application
abstract: This paper presents a high-integrated Ka-band active phased array antenna based on the low temperature co-fired ceramic technology. The presented active phased array antenna integrates the antenna array, RF feeding network, power supply network and digital controlling network. The novel antenna element and RF passive devices using multilayered structure are designed and simulated. Also, the sum-difference networks and beamforming circuits are mentioned in this paper. The presented antenna array has a wide operating bandwidth performance from 31 GHz to 35 GHz, and more than 60°beam scanning rang in azimuth and elevation directions without grating-lobe. Both high integration and light weight are achieved during the design to support the miniaturized active phased array radar applications.

articleTitle: An approach to weak signal extraction under ignorance of direction of arrival
abstract: The radar working in the complex target environment and electromagnetic spectrum environment is affected by various jamming sources, which leads to the deterioration of its target detection performance. In the case of the antenna array and the radar colocated, the pulse signals radiated by the radar are much stronger than the signals radiated by the jamming source, and the two overlap in the time and frequency domain, where the pulse signals radiated by the radar are str ong and the signals radiated by the jamming source are weak, leading to difficulties in extracting the jamming source signals from the signals received by the antenna array. To solve this problem, this paper uses the known incoming direction of the radar signal to design an optimal spatial filter for extracting the jamming source signal, which is also known as weak signal.

articleTitle: Radar high resolution range profile open set recognition of UAV target
abstract: In the field of radar target recognition, non-cooperative targets are often encountered in practical applications. In this case, it is necessary to use an open set recognition method to deal with the problem. This paper proposes an open set recognition method based on high resolution range profile (HRRP) of UAV that trains the network through a distance loss and forces the sample feature output by the model to form a close category cluster. Then it fits the boundary of each category according to the distance between the output vectors and corrects the SoftMax score of samples to achieve rejection. This method does not rely on the threshold to effectively distinguish the boundary between the known class and the unknown class. It can identify the known class samples with a high recognition rate under different sample set openness. Additionally, the rejection accuracy of unknown class samples exceeds 95%, which indicates good open set recognition performance.

articleTitle: Theoretical limit of varying pulse interval ability to spaceborne SAR terrain matching curved imaging
abstract: Spaceborne synthetic aperture radar (SAR) terrain matching curved (TMC) imaging featured by adopting an adaptive continuous curved swath to achieve high efficiency for imaging a long curved terrains. Pulse interval (PI) design is to generate a pulse repetition frequency (PRF) sequence for high-quality data acquisition. Varying PI is used to satisfy the drastic slant range variation of the TMC imaging, resulting in a higher requirement for the number of varying PI segmentation. However, there is few discussion about the relationship between the varying PI ability and the requirement of terrain. In this paper, the theoretical limits of varying PI ability to spaceborne SAR TMC imaging is discussed in detail in two aspects: First the influential factors on the number of varying PI segmentation is analysed. Then a method for calculating the minimum number of varying PI segmentation is proposed. The minimum number varying PI segmentation is analysed with different geometric configuration.

articleTitle: Orbit error estimation in ground-based radar lunar 3D imaging based on minimum entropy
abstract: Ground-based (GB) radar is an effective approach in lunar observation. In GB radar lunar three-dimensional (3D) high-resolution imaging, orbital measurement error will degrade the image quality, and should be estimated and compensated. In this manuscript, an orbit error estimation and compensation method for GB radar lunar 3D imaging based on minimum entropy is proposed. First, echo model considering orbit error is established. Thereafter an autofocus algorithm based on back projection and minimum entropy is proposed to acquire fine-resolved image. Furthermore, particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm based on dynamic inertia weight is used to estimate the optimal compensation parameter to minimize the image entropy. Finally, computer simulation results validate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: SAR-DARTS: a convolutional neural architecture search for SAR scene classification
abstract: In recent years, the collaborative service architecture of cloud computing and edge computing to reduce the demand for computing, storage and other capabilities of artificial intelligence methods has developed rapidly, but their application in synthetic aperture radar (SAR) image scene classification is still immature. In this paper, we propose a neural architecture search and pruning model for SAR scene classification. By introducing network morphisms and path regularization method, we can reduce the unfair competition between cells on the basis of expanding the search space. The model approach is applied to the FUSAR-Ship and OpenSARShip datasets for performance evaluation. The proposed method can achieve higher accuracy with fewer parameters.

articleTitle: Fully polarized ground penetrating radar imaging and scattering information extraction
abstract: Chinese Martian rover, Zhurong is equipped with the Full Polarimetric Mars Rover Surface Penetrating Radar, marking the first instance of utilizing this technology to analyse the subsurface structure of Mars and search for potential water ice. In this paper, we present an imaging approach for fully polarized radar data, utilizing multi-channel data to transform radar images into false-colour representations that enhance underground features. Additionally, we derive the scattering characteristics of subsurface structures based on the physical scattering process, enabling the differentiation of materials with similar dielectric constants. The effectiveness of this method is demonstrated through the validation of both simulated and in-situ experimental data, affirming the applicability of the imaging algorithm and scattering feature extraction technique in processing fully polarized ground-penetrating radar data.

articleTitle: Design and verification of radar system based on MBSE
abstract: At present, there is a problem of focusing on the scheme and ignoring the requirement in radar system development, especially in complex systems. To solve this problem, the Model Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) method is introduced into the radar design process. This paper uses Harmony SE methodology to carry out radar system requirements, function analysis, architecture design and simulation verification. In order to facilitate the research, the radar system prototype is first established, and a variety of modeling methods are applied according to the function and complexity of the radar system prototype. The radar architecture design is further carried out, and the requirements of the radar system and subsystems are verified by black-box state machine and white-box state machine respectively. Finally, the simulation verification tool chain is built. The verification of the system working process, which can only be carried out in the system hardware debugging stage in the past, is advanced to the design stage.

articleTitle: An efficient waveform design algorithm for transmit energy focusing and DOA estimation with colocated MIMO radar
abstract: In this paper, we propose an efficient algorithm to design waveforms for angle estimation with multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) radar. Since the orthogonal waveforms transmitted by conventional MIMO radar result in an omnidirectional transmit beampattern and the transmit power dispersion, we aim to design waveforms to focus the transmit energy within the angular sector of interest. Moreover, to enable the utilization of efficient angle estimation algorithms, we minimize the maximum matching error between the virtual transmit steering vectors and the desired ones to guarantee the rotational invariance poverty. To tackle the associated waveform design problem, we propose a method based on alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM). Numerical results show that the proposed algorithm has a comparable performance to the interior point method but with a much lower computational complexity.

articleTitle: Radar target recognition based on data-level fusion of radar multi-dimensional information
abstract: Radar target recognition plays an important role in battlefield situational awareness system, which has attracted more and more attention in recent years. The radar multi- dimensional information, (e.g., the radar cross section (RCS) data, the high-resolution range profile (HRRP) data, and the inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR) image), has been extensively studied to achieve the purpose of radar target recognition. Typically, the existing algorithms, which mainly focus on the decision-level or feature-level fusion to identify radar objects, often face the problem of many types of deep neural network models in the processing procedure of feature extraction of radar multi-dimensional information, such as one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D CNN) for the HRRP data and two-dimensional convolutional neural network (2D CNN) for the ISAR image. To overcome this problem, a data-level fusion algorithm for radar multi-dimensional information is proposed in this paper. The main idea is that the HRRP data can be transformed into a 2D grayscale image, and then is used as input to the CNN along with the ISAR image. Experimental results validate that the proposed radar target recognition approach, which is based on data-level fusion of radar multi-dimensional information, can provide robust and outstanding classification performance with a more simpler and unified recognition model architecture than other related methods.

articleTitle: Development demands for remote sensing information processing technology: inspired by the US PWSA
abstract: This article analyzes the overall characteristics, hierarchical structure, and main mission objectives of the proliferated warfighter space architecture proposed by the United States Space Development Agency. It primarily focuses on two layers of equipment: the tracking layer and the guardian layer, and analyzes the key technology requirements in the field of space information processing, exerting a certain influence on the development of related technologies.

articleTitle: Subarrayed array thinning using iterative FFT
abstract: This paper proposes a fast-Fourier-transform-based iterative technique for the synthesis of a large thinned planar array with a subarray. Unlike array thinning at the element level, for array thinning at the subarray level, the overlapping of subarrays should be examined. In each iteration, the proposed algorithm is applied to the set of all possible subarrays to select some nonoverlapping subarrays with excitation similar to the expected excitation. The selected subarrays constitute the optimal thinned array with the lowest sidelobe level. Numerical experiments involving a thinned planar array with regular and irregular subarrays showed the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: SAR absolute radiometric calibration method based on offshore wind farm
abstract: Radiometric calibration of synthetic aperture radar (SAR) establishes a crucial connection between image digital numbers and target backscattering coefficients. Natural stable point targets have gained prominence in SAR radiometric calibration since they don't require any additional construction or maintenance expenses compared to artificial calibrators. However, the existing point targets utilized for calibration are not sufficiently concentrated and regularly distributed and are subject to high levels of interference from background clutter. Offshore wind farms, characterized by stable scattering properties and a concentrated distribution at sea with minimal clutter influence, hold promise as calibration targets. This paper presents an absolute radiometric calibration approach based on offshore wind farm. First, suitable offshore wind farms for calibration are chosen based on the length of time since completion and the number of offshore windmills they contain. Then, stable offshore windmills are determined by analyzing parameters such as signal-to-clutter ratio (SCR), radar cross-section (RCS), and RCS temporal stability. Finally, calibration coefficients are calculated using the relationship between the response energy of the windmills in the uncalibrated image and the RCS values obtained from the calibrated image. Experiments using Sentinel-1 data demonstrated that the deviation between nominal calibration coefficients and those calculated using this method falls within the range of 0.21-0.76 dB.

articleTitle: A classification method for group targets and extended targets based on SSA
abstract: With the development of UAV coordination technology, UAV cluster can simulate the morphological flight of large transport aircraft. In the perspective of broadband radar, both of them are multiple scattering points on HRRP, which is difficult to distinguish. To solve this problem, a classification method of group targets and extended targets based on singular spectrum analysis is proposed in this paper. In this method, the main scattering points are eliminated by singular spectrum analysis, and the HRRP features are extracted and imported to SVM for training, and the trained SVM is used to classify group targets and extended targets. The simulation results show that the classification accuracy of this method is greatly improved compared with the traditional method.

articleTitle: An adaptive scheduling algorithm for multi-target ISAR imaging radar based on greedy algorithm
abstract: With the increasing number of airborne targets and the shift towards clustered combat modes, radar systems are facing the challenge of dealing with a large number of targets within limited time. Effectively utilizing time resources to image as many targets as possible has become an urgent problem to address. This paper firstly investigates the impact of target motion on t he quality of ISAR imaging. Subsequently, an adaptive scheduling algorithm for multi-target ISAR imaging radar based on greedy algorithm is proposed.The algorithm begins by analyzing the changing trends in the equivalent rotational angular velocity of multiple targets relative to the radar system. This information is then used to determine the optimal observation period for each target. By considering target characteristics in conjunction with the optimal observation period, the greedy algorithm is applied to achieve optimal scheduling of multi-target imaging by the radar system.Simulation results demonstrate that the algorithm proposed in this paper can improve the success rate of radar imaging on multiple targets while ensuring imaging quality.

articleTitle: Precise simulation of ground penetration radar data on inhomogeneous media
abstract: The Current approaches to Ground Penetrating Radar (GPR) numerical simulation for road applications predominantly revolve around the construction of homogeneous layer models. However, due to the inherent heterogeneity of road materials, such as asphalt mixtures, electromagnetic wave scattering in these mediums is significantly more pronounced when compared to uniform materials. This complexity hinders the applicability and realism of existing simulation algorithms. In this study, we address this gap by introducing a multiphase stochastic discrete medium modelling method based on the Finite-Difference Time-Domain (FDTD) technique. An open-graded friction course (OGFC) model is constructed, taking into account the volume fractions of each phase, and employs the FDTD method to perform GPR simulation. This proposed algorithm’s efficacy and accuracy are validated through synthetic data and laboratory results. Comparative analysis with numerical outcomes from the Random Sequential Adsorption (RSA) model highlights the proposed algorithm's enhanced capability to accurately capture signal characteristics in GPR detection within heterogeneous mediums, thus providing a more realistic simulation for GPR applications in roads.

articleTitle: Design and implementation of a multi-core parallel low illumination enhanced target detection system
abstract: In this paper, we propose an embedded deployment method for low illumination enhancement to address vision-based techniques. Low illumination enhancement of pictures, videos and camera images is achieved by multi-core parallel computation using a Phytium multi-core CPU. Target detection is performed on low illumination enhanced images using YOLO-Fastest network and model inference is accelerated by multi-core parallelism. Low illumination enhancement of camera 1920*1080 images and target detection is implemented with 181% multi-core CPU usage and even distribution of usage across cores. After multi-core acceleration for 1920*1080 video, the inference time per video frame is reduced from 570ms to 300ms, which is about 50% speedup.

articleTitle: A high-efficiency partitioned integration method for GNSS-based passive radar moving target detection
abstract: The Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS), as an illumination source with broad coverage capabilities, is considered to have great potential for passive radar detection. However, due to the low signal power density, long-time integration is required to obtain a satisfactory signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). The long-time integration of moving target will cause range migration and Doppler frequency shift. To solve the problem, this paper proposes an efficient partitioned integration method. Within the subblock, FFT is deployed to quickly achieve focusing. Across subblocks, coherent integration is realized through parameter searching and phase compensation. Finally, moving target motion compensation and imaging are achieved in the RD domain. A car target detection experiment has been carried out using GPS L5 signal. The results show that the SNR of the peak value is slightly lost, but the time consumed is shortened by 79 times, which achieve a balance between integration performance and computational efficiency.

articleTitle: Wideband radar echo cancellation based on joint azimuth interrupted-sampling and frequency modulation
abstract: Echo cancellation is an ingenious method that protects the target of interest (TOI) by cancelling target echo at radar receiver with an active source. In this paper, a wideband radar echo cancellation method using joint azimuth interrupted-sampling and frequency modulation is proposed. The proposed method can not only cancel the target echo, but also generate false targets along the azimuth direction, which will protect the TOI more efficiently. Besides, the frequency modulation is added to cancel the echo with the 0 order false target instead of the -1 order one, then the modulation energy gets more efficiently utilized. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Performance analysis of sub-object partition method for linear formation targets
abstract: The structure of bird formation is complex and variable. Traditional sub-object partition methods cannot match different types of linear formations, leading to a degradation of performance. Recently, a new sub-object partition method applicable to different formations has been proposed. However, the performance of the method has not been analyzed and verified thoroughly. This paper analyses the effectiveness of the proposed method. The statistical rules are proposed to evaluate the performance of the sub-object partition. A series of simulations are conducted using the method of controlling variates, with several important parameters of the method and formation being chosen and discussed separately. And the quantitative results of partition accuracy are demonstrated and the impact of each parameter on partition performance is discussed. Based on the conclusion above, an empirical method for parameter initialization is proposed, which guides the practical applications.

articleTitle: Clutter suppression method of wind farm for airborne array radar based on multi-channel data joint processing
abstract: Wind power has been concerned by the countries around the world. The performance of airborne array radar may be affected by the reflected echoes of the wind farms. Therefore, the research on wind farm clutter suppression technology is of great significance for improving the performance of airborne array radar. Compared with the ground-based radar, the number of wind farm clutter samples is limited for the airborne array radar and it can also be affected by the strong ground clutter. For the above problems, the wind farm clutter suppression method for airborne array radar compatible with ground clutter suppression is proposed in this paper. In this method, the ground clutter is first suppressed by the space-time adaptive processing technology, and the weighted least squares (WLS) criterion is used to recover the corresponding space-time data of the array radar. Then the wind farm clutter can be suppressed by using the extended factor approach (EFA) under the condition of the limited clutter samples. The experiment results verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A high-precision sliding spotlight and TOPS SAR geo-location method
abstract: The target’s imaging position time of sliding spotlight or TOPS SAR will change with the azimuth scaling or de-ramping parameters in two-step imaging algorithm or sub-aperture imaging algorithm. Based on imaging position analysis in a selected two-step imaging algorithm, the mathematical expressions between target imaging position time and orbital position time related to imaging parameters is established, and a useful high-precision geo-location method with the fast inverse Range-Doppler model for sliding spotlight and TOPS SAR is provided. Simulation and real data results show the effectiveness of the proposed location method.

articleTitle: Spectrum-decomposition based fast-time domain algorithm for SAR ECHO generation
abstract: Time-domain synthetic aperture radar (SAR) echo generation algorithms are widely employed due to their independence from azimuth invariance assumptions and high performance in accuracy. However, it will involve huge computational burden for large scenario applications. To address this problem, a spectrum-decomposition based on fast-time domain algorithm for SAR echo generation (FTDEG) is proposed in this paper. The FTDEG is based on the aperture segmentation and sub-image downsampling process. Firstly, the spectrum of the scenario SAR image corresponding to the full-aperture is shifted to zero frequency by utilizing a spectrum alignment operation. Then the full-aperture is split into small sub-apertures and the sub-images corresponding to the sub-apertures are obtained by segmenting the spectrum and downsampling the original image without spectral burring. The sub-aperture segmentation and the sub-image down-sampling process are implemented in a designed recursive framework without huge complex interpolations, and the algorithm has a significant improvement in efficiency for the large scene echo generation. Simulation experiments are provided and analyzed to validate the high performance of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Parameter estimation for compound interrupted sampling and repeating jamming
abstract: With the increasing complexity of the electromagnetic environment in the battlefield and the rapid development of active jamming technology, radar is facing unprecedented active jamming, especially the threat of compound jamming. Accurate estimation of the key parameters of compound jamming is crucial for anti-jamming. In recent years, compound interrupted sampling and repeating jamming (ISRJ) has been emerging as one of the primary jamming patterns. Therefore, accurately estimating the key parameters of compound ISRJ has become increasingly crucial for enhancing radar anti-jamming capabilities. This paper proposes a compound ISRJ parameter estimation method that identifies signal amplitude distribution based on histogram curve fitting and estimates key parameters using transceiver mechanism of ISRJ. The proposed method is capable of adapting to various complex jamming scenarios and exhibits high computational efficiency. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A Doppler spectrum folding removal method for high resolution squinted SAR
abstract: With the increase of resolution, SAR systems operate on wider bandwidth. When SAR works with squint angle, signals of different frequencies will generate different Doppler offset at the same squint angle. As the squint angle increases, the Doppler variations caused by different signal frequencies become more significant. Besides the Doppler bandwidth corresponding to the beam width, the variation changes the position and the distribution of the original Doppler band. This problem causes the extension of Doppler bandwidth and results in the Doppler spectrum folding. For high-resolution SAR with squint angle, this paper proposes a pre-processing method to overcome the problem of Doppler spectrum folding which leads to the image quality degradation. The method contains Doppler spectrum reshaping and support domain extension. In this paper, the processing procedure of the method are presented and the effectiveness of this method is verified by simulation results and the real data results.

articleTitle: Parameterized radar target RCS model with spherical harmonics series
abstract: Radar target scattering characteristic can be used to improve the radar system performance, including target detection and target recognition, but existing radar target scattering models often occupy huge memory, which is an obstacle for real applications. In this paper, we study a parameterized model of radar target scattering characteristic through the widely used spherical harmonic (SH) series. An algorithm based on the truncated singular value decomposition (SVD) method is presented to find the coefficients for the series. Numerical results with two 3D models show that the spherical harmonic series can approximate the target spatial response well in most situations and the average compression rate of the proposed model can reach more than 20%.

articleTitle: Refocusing of moving ships based on deep learning for high altitude platform SAR
abstract: Imaging maritime vessels in synthetic aperture radar (SAR) systems has long been a challenging task. The translational and six-degree-of-freedom complex motions of vessels introduce imaging artifacts such as shifts and defocusing. Conventional approaches typically require estimation of motion parameters to refocus. In contrast, deep learning methods cast the refocusing problem into a regression framework. However, existing deep learning refocusing approaches mostly address short aperture times and are tailored to airborne or spaceborne platforms where vessel-induced shifts and defocusing are relatively minor. However, for slow-moving high-altitude platforms (HAP) with extended aperture times, these approaches become less effective. Hence, this paper derives an analytical expression for the signal model in the image domain after pulse compression for maritime vessels with six-degree-of-freedom motion. Various parameters affecting the complex motion are analyzed, and the derived model is utilized to generate subsequent training set images. Subsequently, a refocusing approach based on Resnet50 is proposed, incorporating a feature fusion module that utilizes the generated images from the analytical expression for training. Finally, through comparative analysis with other networks, the proposed approach demonstrates superior refocusing performance for SAR images with significant defocusing under long apertures in slow-moving, high-altitude platforms.

articleTitle: A network compression method based on network architecture search for SAR target detection
abstract: With the development of high-resolution satellites, real-time processing of satellite data has become a major development trend. However, due to the limitations of onboard resources, onboard real-time processing faces problems such as insufficient storage space, insufficient operating memory, and high computational complexity. To address the above issues, we propose a Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) image detection algorithm based on neural network structure search. By designing efficient and flexible search spaces, search strategies, and subnet evaluation modules, lightweight detection networks that meet specific task requirements can be searched from the original detection network. The proposed method was tested on three SAR ship datasets, and the results showed that the proposed method can reduce model complexity and improve inference speed while keeping detection accuracy nearly lossless.

articleTitle: Design of non-uniform frequency-phase hybrid modulation radar waveform and segmented complementary mismatch filtering
abstract: With the development of electronic countermeasures, radar systems need to embrace innovative modulation techniques to enhance signal intricacy and bolster counter-interception capabilities. The time width and bandwidth of the code of the existing conventional frequency-phase hybrid modulation signal are constant, and the range sidelobe level is relatively high. This paper approaches the aforementioned problems from two perspectives: optimizing the transmission signal and processing hybrid modulated signal. Firstly, a novel approach is introduced involving non-uniform frequency-phase hybrid modulation radar signal. The signal is optimized by using the principle of coordinate descent and cost function diversity. Secondly, to further mitigate the impact of range sidelobes on target observation, an intrapulse segmented complementary mismatch filtering technique is proposed, built upon the foundation of hybrid modulated signal. Notably, the influence of actual Doppler frequency shifts is taken into account. Finally, the effectiveness of the algorithm is verified through simulation. Compared to conventional interpulse complementary mismatch filtering, the hybrid signal and processing techniques presented in this paper lead to reduced signal processing times and the realization of range sidelobe suppression for moving targets.

articleTitle: Orbit determination error analysis and compensation for multi-static GEO SAR imaging
abstract: The high orbit altitude of Geosynchronous Synthetic Aperture Radar (GEO SAR) introduces a significant challenge of long synthetic aperture times, which restricts the application of rapid imaging. A multi-static GEO SAR system consisting of multiple satellites flying along track can be employed to jointly image, and thus, to reduce the synthetic aperture time, but the orbit determination errors of different satellites will bring serious defocusing effect to the sub-image synthesis. In this paper, the effects of orbit determination errors on sub-image offset, defocusing and constant phase errors are analyzed in the multi- static GEO SAR system, and an orbit determination error correction method based on phase gradient autofocus (PGA) and interferometric phase estimation is proposed. Simulation results validate the effectiveness of the method.

articleTitle: Development of a drone-borne GPR system for ICE thickness detection
abstract: In this study, we build a drone-borne ground-penetrating radar (GPR) system for ice thickness detection. The GPR system is composed of a portable vector network analyzer (VNA), a Vivaldi antenna, a GNSS receiver, and a microcomputer. The whole system could be easily mounted on an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV). Then, laboratory experiments were conducted to test the performance of the GPR system. Results show that the radar system can accurately detect the thickness and the relative errors are 3.7% and 2% for the ice samples with actual thicknesses of 5.4 cm and 45.0 cm.

articleTitle: Multi-model KalmanNet for maneuvering target tracking
abstract: The performance of traditional target tracking algorithms usually depends on the selection of preset motion models. When the real motion model of the target is mismatched with the preset model, the performance of the filter will degrade. How to dynamically update motion models to mitigate performance degradation caused by model mismatches has become an important issue. In this paper, we propose Multi-model KalmanNet, which is a multi-model network based on KalmanNet and can dynamically update motion models. While retaining the Kalman filter framework, it can learn the similarity between the target's motion model and the network's preset motion models, and uses the similarity as the weight of each preset model. By continuously updating the weights, it can alleviate the filtering performance degradation caused by model mismatch.

articleTitle: Three-dimensional imaging of spatial spinning group targets based on extended Kalman filter and inverse Radon transform
abstract: Ballistic missiles have become an important weapon in modern military wars by their strong penetration ability, wide striking range and high accuracy in hitting targets. In the mid-course, the missile releases warheads, debris and decoys, which form a spatial group targets. And each of them usually achieves spatial orientation by spinning motion. This complex motion brings great challenges to the radar imaging. Based on the extended Kalman filter and inverse Radon transform, a three-dimensional imaging method for spatial spinning group targets is proposed in this paper. First, the sine curves in the range-slow-time plane are separated by extended Kalman filter, and the height coordinates of scatterers are estimated by the offset of the curves. Then the spinning angular velocity of each scatterer can be analyzed by the empirical mode decomposition, which reveals the number of sub-targets. Finally, on the basis of above estimation, the three-dimensional reconstruction of each sub-target is carried out by the inverse Radon transform. This algorithm reduces the dimensionality of traditional search with curve separation techniques, thereby significantly improving the computational efficiency. Simulation results verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: FDA radar target detection under the array phase errors
