abstract: In this paper, the problem of target detection for frequency diverse array (FDA) radar under array phase errors is studied. To address this problem, a practical signal model for the FDA radar is developed, wherein the phase errors are included. Furthermore, the frequency reliance of the target amplitudes on FDA signal is considered in this model. During the detector design process, obeying the criterion of the generalized likelihood ratio (GLR) test, an adaptive detector is proposed. Note that the proposed detector does not require the aid of the training data. The derivation indicates that the proposed detector also has the constant false alarm rate (CFAR) property with respect to the noise covariance matrix. Simulation results indicate the benefits of the proposed signal modeling and verify the performance of the adaptive detector.

articleTitle: High-success-rate ISAR imaging of maneuvering targets with a robust optimal imaging time interval selection algorithm
abstract: The complex time-variant Doppler frequency of maneuvering targets leads to serious defocusing of inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR) imaging results. It indicates the maneuvering motion poses great challenges to traditional ISAR imaging algorithms. To address the problem, a robust optimal ISAR imaging time interval selection algorithm is proposed in this paper to improve the imaging success rate of maneuvering targets. The proposed algorithm evaluates the imaging results of different imaging time intervals by multiple criteria, and uses Dempster-Shafer (DS) evidence theory to fuse the multiple criteria to select the optimal imaging time interval. Moreover, the proposed algorithm is able to balance the contradiction between resolution and image focusing quality, providing a robust imaging time interval selection performance to obtain well-focused ISAR images of maneuvering targets. The experimental results of both simulated and real data illustrate the effectiveness and necessity of the proposed algorithm to improve the ISAR imaging success rate of maneuvering targets.

articleTitle: Retrieval of ocean surface current from GF-3 SAR imagery using Doppler shift
abstract: Ocean surface current (OSC) is one of the key oceanic dynamic elements that play a crucial role in global carbon and heat cycles. Spaceborne Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) enables the acquisition of information about ocean surface current by measuring Doppler centroid anomaly caused by sea surface motion. In this paper, we utilize Chinese Gaofen-3 (GF-3) single-look complex (SLC) data to retrieve OSC based on the Doppler centroid anomaly method. The SLC data are uniformly divided into sub-blocks, and the Doppler centroid of each sub-block is calculated using the time-domain Doppler estimation method. In terms of the Doppler grid pixel spacing and estimation accuracy, the selection of sub-block size is investigated. For the study case in this work, the optimal size of sub-block is 200*250, corresponding to Doppler grid pixel spacing of 1km. With the Doppler shift information obtained, the CDOP model is utilized to remove the contributions of wind-driven waves to obtain the ocean surface current field. The retrieval results are validated against the HYCOM current data. It is suggested that the root mean squared error between the retrieved ocean surface current velocity from GF-3 and the Hycom current velocity is 0.51 m/s.

articleTitle: An earth-based radar high resolution imaging technology of the moon based on sub-aperture delay Doppler algorithm
abstract: The delay Doppler algorithm is the earliest developed and the most used frequency-domain imaging algorithm for the moon, which is suitable for low resolution imaging. Howeaver, this algorithm usually assumes that the Doppler phase induced by the rotation of the target is only first order. This assumption is not suitable for high resolution imaging with long-term observation. In this paper, an earth-based radar high resolution imaging technology based on sub-aperture delay Doppler algorithm is proposed. This paper first analyses the basic constraints of the sub-aperture division, which avoid the ARU and ADU effects in each sub-aperture and ensure that the Doppler phase is linear. Then, the sub-aperture delay Doppler imaging is performed to obtain the sub-aperture images. Then, multiple sub-aperture delay Doppler images can be projected into the geographic coordinate system based on the RD positioning model. Finally, multiple sub-aperture images can be coherently fused to obtain a full-aperture image. Computer simulation results and experimental results based on a distributed coherent radar prototype system validate the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Auto-focused learning imaging network for MIMO radar in the case of model mismatch
abstract: In the last decade, compressive sensing (CS)-based and deep unfolding network (DUN)-based methods have attracted much attention for multiple-input and multiple-output (MIMO) radar target imaging due to the advantages of high resolution and low sampling burden. However, when the established signal model is mismatched, the performance of CS-based and DUN- based imaging methods decrease significantly. In this study, we propose an auto-focused learning imaging network (AFLI-Net) to solve this problem. The AFLI-Net uses a stacked convolutional auto-encoder (SCAE)-based image focusing network (IF- Net) to follow a memory-augmented DUN-based LI-Net, helping to focus the defocused targets caused by model mismatch. Simulation results validate the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed learning imaging method comparing to the CS- based and DUN-based imaging methods.

articleTitle: Fully polarized radar target detection and waveform optimization under rainy condition
abstract: Polarization and waveform optimization can significantly improve the detection ability of fully polarized radar. However, in practical scenarios, atmospheric particles frequently induce depolarization effects on radar waves, thereby influencing precise target detection, a phenomenon predominantly observed with raindrop particles. This paper establishes a target detection model for fully polarized radar in rainy condition. Subsequently, a joint transceiver iterative optimization algorithm is devised, utilizing the maximum output signal-to-interference plus noise ratio (SINR) of the system as the benchmark, and imposing dual constraints of energy and resemblance on the transmitting waveform. Ultimately, the effectiveness of the proposed method under rainy condition is validated through simulation, and recommendations for engineering applications are provided based on the analysis.

articleTitle: A baseline distribution scheme for swarm UAVs multi-static SAR tomographic imaging
abstract: In radar imaging applications, using unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) equipped with radar systems for imaging has the characteristics of low cost and high efficiency. Using a system composed of multiple UAVs to achieve true 3D highresolution imaging in a single flight, the cost is lower compared to linear array SAR (LASAR) and tomographic SAR (TomoSAR). However, the commonly used linear distribution of baselines is limited by the maximum unambiguous height, resulting in close spacing between UAVs, which is not conducive to the safe flight of UAVs. Excessively close baseline spacing can affect the stable flight of UAVs. Regarding this issue, A distribution scheme for swarm UAVs Multi-Static SAR is proposed which meets both the minimum spacing requirements for safe flight and the maximum spacing requirements for the maximum unambiguous height. This scheme aims to increase the straight-line distance between UAVs as much as possible while ensuring the imaging quality. Within this condition, the UAVs do not interfere with each other and a good 3D SAR imaging result is ensured. The simulation results are provided to verify the effectiveness of the scheme and demonstrate the imaging effect.

articleTitle: Realization of remote sensing image classification algorithm based on SOPC
abstract: Recently, Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have made significant progress in the field of remote sensing image scene classification. However, commonly used CNN models are mainly deployed on GPU, which is bulky and power-hungry, making them unsuitable for customized requirements of on-board embedded applications. To meet the needs of on-board embedded applications, this study selects System On a Programmable Chip (SoPC), known for their low power consumption and compact size, as the processing platform for accelerating CNNs. Employing the knowledge distillation method, this paper uses the classical CNN scene classification algorithms to create lightweight models. These optimized models are then deployed on resource-constrained ZCU104 SoPC hardware platform. Experimental results demonstrate that the optimized lightweight models achieve image classification tasks with over 95% accuracy on SoPC hardware platform. Furthermore, due to minimal impact from quantization errors, the accuracy drop is less than 1%. Compared to GPU (GTX1650), the throughput on SoPC is increased by 96.43%.

articleTitle: A human posture recognition method for millimeter wave radar sparse point cloud
abstract: Millimeter-wave radar has received considerable attention for its applications in human activity recognition in residential environments due to its insensitivity to lighting conditions and strong privacy features. However, the direct application in posture recognition is hindered by the sparse nature of the point cloud data generated by millimeter -wave radar, along with the presence of considerable noise points. To address these issues, this study proposes an intelligent posture recognition method for sparse point cloud data. Firstly, a multi-frame accumulation technique is employed to generate point cloud data containing the complete posture movements. Subsequently, the DBSCAN algorithm is applied to perform noise reduction on the accumulated data. Finally, a signal-to-noise ratio based weighing approach is utilized to enhance the feature representation of the sample data. To enhance recognition accuracy, this study employs 4-dimensional point cloud data that includes velocity information as input, utilizing an expanded PointNet architecture for posture recognition. Experimental outcomes show that the proposed method effectively reduces noise and achieves a remarkable average recognition accuracy of 96.1% for four distinct postures: falling, hunkering, bowing and jumping.

articleTitle: A novel acceleration compensated alpha-beta filter
abstract: Alpha-Beta filter is widely used in radar tracking, but it has an inherent weakness of the large dynamic lag error when tracking maneuvering targets and ballistic targets, especially at a low data rate. In this paper, we propose an improved alpha-beta filter called IMA filter based on complex control technology. By introducing acceleration compensation to the traditional alpha-beta filter, the dynamic lag errors of position and velocity tracking are significantly degraded. Theoretical derivation and simulation analysis show that the IMA alpha-beta filter has better dynamic tracking accuracy.

articleTitle: A lightweight SAR ship detection method based on improved YOLOv8
abstract: The complex background and small size of targets pose challenges for ship detection in SAR (Synthetic Aperture Radar) images. Currently, deep learning-based methods have been widely used for SAR ship detection. However, the neural networks involved in these methods have a large number of parameters, which hinders their practical applications on resource-constrained platforms. This paper proposes a lightweight SAR detection algorithm specifically designed for small ship targets in SAR images. Firstly, we adopt a decoupling strategy to reconstruct the backbone network, effectively reducing the number of parameters. Secondly, a new regression loss function MPDIoU is proposed to enhance the detection accuracy of small ship bounding boxes and improve the regression speed of the model. Finally, we conduct experiments on the SSDD and HRSID datasets, and the results show that our proposed method achieves improvement in mAP (mean average precision) by 97.8% and 89.2% respectively, while the model weight parameters is only 72.5% of the standard YOLOv8n.

articleTitle: Research on ISAR imaging method of long-distance high-speed space targets
abstract: Space targets imaging based on space platform is a research hotspot in recent years. In this paper, according to the relative motion characteristics of space targets in the imaging process of space platform, we analyzed the ISAR imaging method of long-distance high-speed space targets and summarized the influence of frequency, distance, speed and multiple targets on several classical ISAR imaging algorithms, including Range Doppler Algorithm, Polar Formation Algorithm and the STFT- based imaging method. An improved Doppler center tracking method based on unified calibration datum was proposed to realize high-precision phase compensation and azimuth focusing for high-speed space targets. At the same time, the imaging resolution and running time of several methods were compared. Through the comparison of simulation experiments, simulation results were presented which confirmed that the Range Doppler Algorithm could achieve distance alignment with high resolution when the space platform imaged long-distance and high-speed space targets.

articleTitle: A novel image fusion method for joint ISAR-and-optical observation combing NSCT and PADCPCNN
abstract: Inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR) images and optical images reflect the scattering characteristics of the observed target in different frequency bands. In order to obtain more structure and details information of the observed target, a novel fusion method of the ISAR image and the optical image is proposed. Firstly, the ISAR-and-optical image registration is achieved based on the theory of homography transformation. Secondly, the non-subsampled contourlet transform (NSCT) is utilized to decompose the ISAR and optical images into a low-pass sub-band and a sequence of band-pass directional sub-bands, respectively. After that, the low-pass sub-bands of the ISAR image and optical image are further fused by using the rule of low-frequency image information features, while the band-pass directional sub-bands are fused by using the parameter-adaptive dual-channel pulse-coupled neural network (PADCPCNN). Finally, the fused image is constructed from the fused sub-bands by applying inverse NSCT. The experimental results show that the proposed algorithm can effectively fuse the detail features of ISAR images and the contour features of visible images through qualitative evaluation and Quantitative Evaluation.

articleTitle: Demonstration of P band UAV bistatic SAR experiment and imaging processing
abstract: UAV Bistatic SAR (UAV BiSAR) distributes the transmitting and receiving system on different UAVs, which has the advantages of anti-reconnaissance, powerful crypticity and anti-interference capability. However, due to problems such as channel delay, radio frequency interference(RFI), and synchronization error, it is difficult to perform 2D imaging on the UAV BiSAR real data. Therefore, the results of UAV BiSAR real data are rare in the existing literature. The P-band UAV BiSAR real data based on two-way convection performed in this paper can well solve the above problems. Next, we will demonstrate the P-band UAV BiSAR two-dimensional imaging experiment. Finally, some imaging results are given to verify the P-band UAV BiSAR mode and processing method.

articleTitle: A rockfall motion parameter estimation method based on TDM-MIMO radar with combined double/multi-pulse channels
abstract: MIMO(Multiple-Input Multiple-Output) radar can be effectively applied to the real-time detection of rockfalls, but it is challenging to balance the measurement range of unfuzzy velocity and the real-time detection performance when using TDM(Time Division Multiplexing) waveform. Besides, the estimation accuracy of DOA(Direction-Of-Arrival) of rockfalls is easily disturbed by the motion phase. Aiming at solving the above problems, a rockfall motion parameter estimation method based on TDM-MIMO radar with combined double/multi-pulse channels is proposed in this paper. Firstly, by designing the time sequence of TDM signals, the problem of mutual limitation between the detection range of velocity and real-time detection performance is solved. Secondly, the problem of inaccurate angle estimation caused by Doppler frequency is solved. When there is only one target in the range unit, the motion phase should be compensated first. When multiple targets are located in the same range unit, the velocity of these targets is used to judge the corresponding azimuth, and then velocity-azimuth decoupling is completed. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is verified by simulation experiments.

articleTitle: TDM radar target angle and velocity estimation with forward and reverse transmission patterns
abstract: Time division multiplexing multiple-input multiple-output (TDM-MIMO) radar is widely used in vehicle applications, but it suffers from the problem of velocity and angle coupling when measuring moving targets. In order to eliminate the influence of TDM on parameter estimation, it is necessary to design a new transmission pattern and corresponding processing method. In this paper, a forward and reverse transmission pattern is proposed together with the parameter estimation method. The forward and reverse transmission are used to obtain the sum and difference of target velocity and angle phases respectively, and the independent parameters are solved from the coupled phases. Different from the commonly adopted random TDM schemes, the transmission pattern of proposed forward and reverse transmission is determined, and the estimation algorithm mainly involves only two-dimensional fast Fourier transform (FFT) on uniformly sampled data matrixes. The asymptotic estimation accuracy and the multi-target resolution is equivalent to that of multiple-input single-output (MISO) radar with the same aperture, which means that the proposed method overcomes the coupling problem in TDM radar.

articleTitle: Waveform design for netted colocated-MIMO radar systems
abstract: The paper investigates the transmit waveform design for a netted colocated Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) radar system to enhance the performance of target detection under clutter interference. The objective is to optimize the Signal-to-Clutter-and-Noise Ratio (SCNR) and waveform ambiguity characteristics under the constant modulus constraint, so as to ensure hardware compatibility and good pulse compression performance. In addition, the spectrum of each transmitter is limited to ensure that the angular waveforms have low cross-correlation level. The resultant problem is a non-convex optimization problem. By reformulating the initial non-convex problem equivalently, we propose a polynomial-time iterative approach involving the resolution of a series of convexified subproblems. Finally, the performance of the proposed algorithm is validated through simulation experiments.

articleTitle: Online trajectory planning of bistatic SAR based on regularised extreme learning machine
abstract: As a special bistatic configuration, the maneuvering platform bistatic SAR using GEO transmitter (GEO-BiSAR) can provide long-duration and wide beam coverage over the target scene. This bistatic configuration can continuously observe targets during flight and obtain target recognition and tracking information from images. The imaging performance of bistatic SAR depends on the observation geometry, which is determined by the trajectory of the maneuvering platform receiver. Therefore, it is necessary to design the flight trajectory of the receiver. However, during the flight, the trajectory of the receiver is vulnerable to external disturbances and generates certain offsets. The original trajectory can't meet the actual imaging requirements, and a new trajectory needs to be re-planned in real time. To address the above issues, this paper models the problem as a multi-objective optimisation problem and proposes a new framework for online trajectory planning using Regularised Extreme Learning Machine (RELM). The framework first obtains the planned trajectory as a dataset through multi-objective optimisation. Then train the dataset into RELM to achieve online trajectory planning, and the results meet the requirements of real-time and effectiveness. Experimental studies demonstrate the rapidity and effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A robust high-resolution sparse ISAR imaging method based on deep unfolding network
abstract: Aiming at the problem of performance drop of ISAR imaging method caused by the changeable echo signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and loss rate in ISAR imaging, this paper proposes a sparse ISAR high-resolution imaging method based on deep unfolding network to improve the robustness of the network under echo SNR and loss rate. Firstly, the imaging iterative algorithm 2D-ISTA is unrolled to be a unfolding network including a gradient descent layer (GDL) and a proximal mapping layer (PML). Secondly, in order to improve the noise and defect robustness of the imaging network, a controllable proximal mapping block (CPMB) based on controllable units is introduced, and the controllable units are used to modulate the output of the residual network according to the echo loss information. Finally, CPMB is embedded in PML to form a controllable proximal mapping layer (CPML), then the sparse ISAR high-resolution imaging network is constructed. Experimental results based on simulation and measured data verify the effectiveness and superiority of the method.

articleTitle: Urban area extraction based on polarimetric features using DP-UNet
abstract: Urban area extraction based on polarimetric synthetic aperture radar (PolSAR) data is challenging as oriented building area can easily lead to misinterpretation as vegetated area. In this letter, a dual path UNet (DP-UNet) network is designed inspired by UNet, and the polarimetric features obtained by the improved five-component decomposition method are introduced as input. First, the improved polarimetric decomposition method is used to obtain scattering characteristics. Second, one branch of the DP-UNet is designed to learn different polarimetric features including surface, double-bounce and volume scattering. While urban feature is extracted by the other branch. Finally, the different feature layers learned are integrated to be used to extract buildings. The performance of our proposed method is verified by RADARSAT-2 C-band data using randomly chosen samples. The results show that our method has better effect on building extraction.

articleTitle: Design and experimental research on vibration damping for missile-borne radar antenna system
abstract: Missile-borne Radar system is one of the core functional unit of the radar seeker, which working at the forefront of the missile platform and withstanding a large amount of randomness vibration load. To order to improve the mechanical environment adaptability of the missile-borne radar antenna system, Analysis of structural characteristics, vibration damping design methods ,selection method of absorber , design method of damping parameters had been carried out in turn. The effect in random vibration environment of the damping deign methods had been studied by experiment. Tests on vibration reduction efficiency showed that the design scheme can control the high frequency vibration efficiently, especially the frequency after the resonance point, and the damping efficiency in X /Y/Z directions can reach to 57.3%, 54.7%, and 54.9%. Tests on array displacement showed that there are significant variations among the displacement amplitude range in X/Y/Z directions, and the results are (-0.6, 2)mm, (-2, -1) mm, and (-0.1, 1) mm. Tests on array deflection showed that the variation range of deflection angle α/β/γ are (-0.1, 0.2)°,(-0.15, 0.15)°, and (-0.1, 0.02)°.

articleTitle: A two-channel multi-stage feature fusion method for SAR synthetic aperture radar classification
abstract: Deep learning technique plays a significant role in the society of Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) target recognition. However, most of existing SAR target classification methods do not take the physical properties of SAR image into account, merely adopting an end-to-end model to classify the target. In this paper, we propose a two-channel multi-stage feature fusion (TMSF) model for SAR target recognition, which contains three modules: an attributed scattering centers extraction module denoted by ASC module, a feature extraction module denoted by AE module and a feature maps fusion module, denoted by MF module. The AE module generate the estimated feature maps of the attributed scattering centers (ASCs) and vanilla input, respectively. The MF module is utilized to fuse the extracted feature, while the TMSF network recognizes the targets through the fused outputs. Under the MSTAR dataset, extensive experiments evaluate the recognition performance of the proposed method, which super passes the existing methods in terms of MKSFF and CA-MCNN. The code is available on https://github.com/XYLGroup/TMSF.

articleTitle: Research on satellite-ground collaborative location of spread spectrum signal
abstract: Addressing the problem of insufficient adjacent satellite location conditions and difficulty in estimating time-frequency difference parameters of spread spectrum signals in dual satellite location, this paper proposes a Satellite Earth cooperative location technology. Based on spread spectrum code sequences , reconstructs user spread spectrum signals, Use the received satellite interference source side lobe signal and reconstruct the signal to extract TDOA(time-frequency difference of arrival) parameters, and complete the location. Simulation results show that the proposed satellite earth cooperative spread spectrum signal location method is effective, It can extract TDOA of DSSS(Direct Sequence Spread Spectrum) signal with negative 40dB SNR (signal-to-nosie ratio), and the location accuracy conforms to the theoretical analysis results.

articleTitle: Automotive radar interference mitigation using principal signal component estimation
abstract: Wide usage of Frequency Modulated Continuous Wave (FMCW) radar systems as part of Advanced Driver Assistance Systems in recent years have led to the problem of mutual interference mitigation between radars on the road. Modern interference mitigation algorithms should keep their high performance in different road conditions during various strength interference and simultaneously not distorting the useful signal and its complete processing in predictable time limits. This paper proposes an algorithm of interference detection and signal recovery based on principal signal estimation for FMCW radars satisfying specified requirements. Principal signal estimation is used to replace the task of interference detection in the presence of strong reflected target signal with the task of interference detection in the presence of the noise-like weak reflected target signal. Using the principal signal estimation as a source signal for signal recovery allows to mitigate artefacts, that are caused by interference zeroing in Range-Doppler map, to avoid false alarm and missing targets masked by these artefacts. The provided performance assessment and real road tests verify that the proposed interference mitigation solution benefits existing iterative solutions, i.e. better signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio improvement and less missed and false detections. It ensures a predictable processing time due to non-iterative structure.

articleTitle: Preliminary results of GNSS-InBSAR deformation retrieval using Beidou MEO repeated-orbit sequence
abstract: Global Navigation satellite-based bistatic interferometric synthetic aperture radar (GNSS-InBSAR) is a new type of surface observation system, which can simultaneously use the reflected echo signals of multiple navigation satellites to obtain three-dimensional deformation information of the target scene. The number of MEO satellites of Beidou navigation system is more than that of IGSO satellites, which can form a richer GNSS-InBSAR system configuration, provide observation information from more angles of the target scene, and combine with the observation information of IGSO to further improve the accuracy and frequency of deformation monitoring of the target scene. Based on five sets of MEO multi-satellite repeated-orbit images of GNSS-InBSAR in a certain urban area of Jinan, this paper obtains preliminary deformation monitoring results, which confirms the feasibility of long-term deformation monitoring based on Beidou MEO satellite, and lays a foundation for the research of Beidou MEO-IGSO cross-orbit deformation monitoring.

articleTitle: Wideband MIMO radar transmit beampattern design via manifold optimization embedding with momentum information
abstract: The waveform design for transmit wideband beam- pattern with Constant Modulus Constraints (CMC) is the key technology in Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) radar systems. Most existing methods solve the problem by relaxing the objective function or the CMC, which leads to relaxing error. To address this issue, we notice that the original problem is a quadratic unconstrained problem over Complex Circle Manifolds (CCM). Based on this, a Manifold Optimization Embedding with Momentum Information (MOEMI) method without relaxation is proposed. To be specific, we first derive a momentum update strategy by adaptively updating the step size and the descent direction based on the momentum over the CCM. Then, we use the strategy to solve the problem and insure a non-increase of the objective function. Numerical results are provided to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Integrated waveform design for MIMO dual function radar-communication system via MM-ADMM method
abstract: An integrated waveform design problem is investigated for a dual function multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) radar communication system, in the presence of signal-dependent interference. Taking into consideration both the radar signal detection performance and the communication data rate, an optimization problem that maximizes the signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) with constrained multi-user interference (MUI) energy is formulated. In addition, practical constraints on the energy and the peak-to-average ratio (PAR) of the probing waveform are also considered to comply with the radar power budget and the current power amplifier technology, respectively. The resulting constrained optimization problem is non-convex and NP-hard, which is challenging to solve analytically. An iterative algorithm based on majorization- minimization (MM) and alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) techniques is proposed accordingly. It is shown by numerical examples that compared with existing results in the literature, the proposed method achieves higher SINR performance and much faster convergence rate, which implies a better trade-off between performance and complexity.

articleTitle: An airborne P-band polarimetric synthetic aperture radar tomography campaign in hilly areas
abstract: Tomographic synthetic aperture radar (SAR) has great application potential in forestry, ice and snow detecting, and urban modelling for its ability to extract vertical structure information of the target and reconstruct the illuminated area. To fulfil the requirement from forestry users, a P-band tomographic SAR campaign was carried out in Zhaoqin, Guangdong Province in 2022, by the No.38 Research Institute, China Electronics Technology Group Corporation (CETC38). In this paper, the P-band SAR system is introduced briefly, and the flight design is presented. The airborne SAR imaging algorithm for this tomographic campaign is described. Particularly, the phase errors caused by topography are compensated by introducing the digital elevation model (DEM) from shuttle radar topography mission (SRTM). To evaluate the phase accuracy for the tomographic SAR images, two of them are co-registered and generate interferogram and coherence maps. It is illustrated that the coherence is improved greatly after topography-dependent motion compensation. In the conclusion, further work is expected.

articleTitle: Sparse SAR target classification based on transfer learning
abstract: Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) is a high-resolution microwave remote sensing observation system. Due to the development of deep learning, automatic classification has become a hot topic in the applications of SAR image during these years. However, collecting labeled SAR images is difficult and comes at high cost compared with abundant labelled datasets in optical images. In this paper, a novel sparse SAR target classification method based on transfer learning (TL) is proposed to alleviate the problem of low classification accuracy due to limited samples. In addition, a novel data separation method is designed to avoid over-fitting and improve the robustness of classification framework. Firstly, a novel iterative soft thresholding (BiIST) algorithm is used to acquire sparse images with better quality than traditional SAR images based on MSTAR dataset. Then a shallow convolutional neural network (CNN) is pretrained by simulated SAR image dataset. Finally, with sparse SAR dataset being the input of CNN, we evaluate the performance of transfer learning in sparse SAR target classification by transferring different numbers of layers, and find out the most suitable transfer learning method. Comparative experiments between sparse SAR dataset and traditional MSTAR dataset are carried out as well. Experimental results show that the proposed method has higher classification accuracy than training from scratch under standard operating conditions (SOC), especially in the case of small sample.

articleTitle: SAR-communication integration based on FBMC-OQAM waveforms
abstract: The integration of radar and communication can achieve target detection and wireless communication simultaneously with high spectrum utilization. It responds to the development of emerging applications including internet of vehicles/things (IOV, IOT), smart city/transportation and self-driving. In establishing system-level integration, the integrated waveform plays a fundamental role. However, the state-of-art integrated waveforms, which are based on Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (OFDM) techniques, suffer from Doppler frequency bias. This drawback is mainly introduced by the excessively high sidelobes of the OFDM subcarrier. For this sake, a novel integrated waveform based on Filter Bank Multicarrier with Offset Quadrature Amplitude Modulation (FBMC-OQAM) is proposed. It has lower sidelobes of subcarriers and thus becomes insensitive to frequency bias. It also has better robustness against multi-path fading and higher spectral efficiency. Particularly, the stepped frequency chirps are introduced into FBMC as pilots. Apart from acting as Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) imaging signals, these pilots can track channel changes and assist communication. More significantly, to avoid the intrinsic interference between pilots and data symbols, auxiliary pilots (APs) and compensation algorithms are proposed. Theoretical analysis and simulation results illustrate the feasibility of this waveform scheme.

articleTitle: Typical active jamming performance analysis of triangular FMCW
abstract: Frequency modulated continuous wave (FMCW) radar is widely used in commercial and military applications because of its simple structure and low probability of intercept. Based on digital radio frequency memory (DRFM) technology, this paper analyses the effects of typical active jamming methods on triangular FMCW radar, including coherent noise, time-delayed forwarding, interrupted sampling repeater, and frequency shift modulation jamming. By comparing the effects of various jamming techniques, a more effective two-segment frequency shift modulation jamming approach is proposed. Coherent noise jamming blankets the target at a high jamming-to-signal ratio (JSR), interrupted sampling repeater jamming is hard to control, time-delayed forwarding jamming fails to affect the velocity dimension, and conventional frequency shift modulation jamming only affects the velocity dimension. By contrast, the proposed two-segment frequency shift modulation jamming can affect both the range and velocity dimensions, forming a false target at the expected position. Finally, simulations are given to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Aerial target classification method based on clutter suppression and fully connected neural network
abstract: In this paper, the problem of robust and accurate recognition of aerial radar target is considered. The strong clutter and difficulty in mining effective features have a significant negative impact on the recognition accuracy. To improve the recognition performance of radar for aerial targets, an aerial target recognition method based on fully connected neural network (FCNN) is proposed. The method first extracts the multi-pulse echo data of the range bin where the radar detection target is located, and then obtains the time domain echo data mainly composed of the target micro-Doppler component through clutter suppression and the eliminate of the radar target airframe components based on the improved CLEAN algorithm. Then the features such as time and frequency domain central moments, waveform entropy, frequency domain amplitude normalized variance and L1 norm of the target are extracted, and finally the extracted features are used to t rain and test the designed fully connected neural network to realize the recognition of three types of typical aerial targets, namely, jet, helicopter, and propeller aircraft. The experimental results of the measured data demonstrate that the proposed FCNN method performs better than traditional classification method.

articleTitle: SAR deformation vehicle target recognition based on improved transformer network
abstract: Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) possesses advantages such as all-weather, all-day capabilities, and high-resolution compared to optical sensors. In the military field, SAR is widely applied to target jamming, military monitoring, and military strikes, and has become an important means of battlefield reconnaissance and situational awareness. Through a more comprehensive investigation into automatic target recognition (ATR) in SAR imagery, its potential for widening and enhancing the scope of SAR image applications becomes apparent. However, SAR ATR confronts the challenge of low accuracy in recognizing deformed targets due to factors such as the high depression angle of the carrier and imaging system of SAR. Consequently, this paper introduces an innovative SAR ATR approach that combines convolutional neural networks (CNN) and transformers, aiming to address the challenge of recognizing deformed SAR targets. Additionally, validation is conducted on both the publicly available the moving and stationary target acquisition and recognition (Mstar) dataset and a self-developed Full aspect stationary targets-Vehicle (FAST-Vehicle) dataset. Experimental results show that the proposed method can enhance the accuracy of recognizing SAR deformation targets.

articleTitle: SAR image classification using pseudo-siamese network and supervised contrastive loss
abstract: Deep learning has emerged as the predominant research direction for Synthetic Aperture Radar Automatic Target Recognition (SAR ATR). However, SAR image classification encounters the challenge of obtaining sufficient clear training samples to ensure the generalization ability of neural network, primarily due to the difficulty and considerable cost associated with acquiring SAR images in real battlefield environments. To address this issue, this paper proposes a method based on a pseudo- siamese network and supervised contrastive loss. This method aims to alleviate the problem of insufficient training samples and the subsequent rapid decline in network performance caused by a gradual reduction of training samples. The comparative experiments demonstrate that the proposed method achieves higher classification accuracy when compared to the network or method under evaluation on the Moving and Stationary Target Acquisition and Recognition (MSTAR) dataset. Furthermore, the target classification accuracy does not significantly deteriorate even when the number of training samples gradually decreases. Notably, the proposed method achieves a classification accuracy of 87.74% when utilizing only 20 SAR images per class from the MSTAR training set.

articleTitle: Non-contact radar vital signs detection based on DBO-VMD and coefficient discrimination
abstract: The detection of heartbeat signals will be significantly hampered by respiratory harmonics when the human target is far away from the millimetre wave radar. Additionally, before using Variational Mode Decomposition (VMD) algorithm to decompose vital signs signals, it is necessary to set relevant parameters. To solve these problems, we propose a new method. We use Dung Beetle Optimizer (DBO) algorithm to optimize VMD algorithm, and then coefficient discriminant method is used to select the decomposed modes. The experimental results of simulation and measured data show that the proposed method converges faster than other optimized VMD methods in parameter selection. Moreover, it is more accurate than the correlation coefficient method in mode selection. Especially, it can accurately identify respiratory harmonics and heartbeat signals, and improve the accuracy of heart rate detection.

articleTitle: Quantum fast iterative shrinkage thresholding algorithm for radar image recovery
abstract: Considering the high computational complexity of the classical sparse recovery algorithm, a quantum Fast Iterative Shrinkage Thresholding Algorithm (QFISTA) is proposed with the advantage of exponential speedup or quadratic speedup of quantum computation. In this paper, after analysing the iteration process of FISTA, the QFISTA and its quantum circuit is proposed. Among them, the frame diagram of the quantum circuit of the quantum matrix multiplication algorithm (QMMA) and quantum state preparation (QSP) is presented. The computational complexity of QFISTA is given. In the simulations experiments, the synthetic aperture radar (SAR) and inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR) image is reconstructed by the proposed QFISTA.

articleTitle: Detecting vertices of hyperbolas in GPR data using fully convolutional neural network
abstract: Hyperbola is a distinctive pattern in the B-scan image of ground penetrating radar (GPR). Accurate and automatic localization of the hyperbolas' vertices is of great importance for the interpretation of GPR B-scan data, however, which is still a challenging problem due to the irregular hyperbola shapes in complex detection scenarios. In this paper, a novel method for detecting the vertices of hyperbolas in GPR B-scan image is proposed using a modified fully convolutional neural network (FCN). First, a simulated training dataset approximating the real data is created, which ensures the reliability of the network for real measurements. Second, a lightweight network based on fully convolutional architecture is proposed to mask the vertex regions of the hyperbolas, without resizing the input B-scan image. Finally, the density-based spatial clustering of applications with noise (DBSCAN) algorithm is employed to cluster the masked results, thereby obtaining the coordinates of the hyperbola vertices. The effectiveness of the proposed method is validated by simulations and experiments.

articleTitle: Regionalized energy function segmentation method based on GMTRJ algorithm
abstract: As an improved algorithm of the Reversible Jump Markov Chain Monte Carlo (RJMCMC), Generalized Multiple-Try Reversible Jump (GMTRJ) algorithm can design the weight functions to overcome the quality issues in solving model parameters by the RJMCMC algorithm. To precisely segment Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) image, a regionalized energy function segmentation method based on GMTRJ algorithm is proposed. Firstly, the geometric tessellation and unconstrained Gibbs probability distribution function are combined to construct a regionalized energy function segmentation model under the energy function segmentation framework. Then the GMTRJ algorithm is applied to simulate from the model to solve its parameters, where the weight function is designed to improve the quality of parameter solution. The proposed and compared methods are tested on simulated and real SAR images. These results show that the proposed method can segment simulated and real SAR image better. Further, it can be verified that the weight functions in GMTRJ algorithm can improve the quality of parameter solution.

articleTitle: Regularized orthogonal matching pursuit based airborne tomographic SAR inversion
abstract: As an extension of synthetic aperture radar (SAR), SAR tomography (TomoSAR) has the ability to decrease the overlap in two-dimensional (2-D) image, achieves the multi-scatterers separation, improves the three-dimensional (3-D) modeling capability, and hence obtains the high-resolution 3-D image of the interested area. Recent studies have proved the feasibility of airborne TomoSAR for acquiring 3-D image of urban building. However, its imaging performance still requires to be further improved, particularly when the limited number of baselines are available and the baselines are time-varying. In this paper, to address the above problems, we introduce a novel compressive sensing (CS) based algorithm, regularized orthogonal matching pursuit (ROMP) into airborne tomographic SAR inversion, and achieve 3-D imaging of artificial buildings in Yuncheng and Emei, China. Compared with traditional spectral estimation algorithms, such as beamforming, ROMP realizes the super-resolving imaging in the elevation direction. While compared to the existing CS based method, such as orthogonal matching pursuit (OMP), the proposed method improves the accuracy of 3-D reconstruction and filters out the interference of false or weak scattering points.

articleTitle: Fast and efficient K-D frequency estimation for multiple complex sinusoids
abstract: Frequency estimation of complex sinusoids under a white Gaussian noise is widely used in many applications, including radar, sonar, and communications. In this paper, we propose a fast and efficient algorithm for K-dimensional (K-D) frequency estimation of multiple complex sinusoids, where K is any integer larger than one. The proposed algorithm uses the discrete Fourier transform to realize the coarse estimation, and an iterative interpolation structure is designed to obtain the fine frequency estimation of multiple complex sinusoids. This algorithm has low computational complexity, and numerical results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Improved propagator method for range and angle estimation with FDA-MIMO radar
abstract: The multiple input multiple output (MIMO) radar with frequency diverse array (FDA) has been widely studied in radar fields because it can produce range-angle-time beampattern. However, many existing parameter estimation algorithms show the lower estimation performance and larger computational complexity, which are based on large amounts of sampled data and eigenvalue decomposition (EVD) or singular value decomposition (SVD). In this paper, the improved propagator method for joint range and angle estimation with FDA-MIMO radar is proposed. The traditional covariance matrix decomposition operation is replaced by building block matrix and adopting matrix multiplication to reduce the complexity. Different propagators are constructed to achieve angle and distance estimation by transmitting and receiving dimensions respectively. Several experimental results are provided to verify the effectiveness of proposed method.

articleTitle: Time domain echo simulation of airship-borne weather radar based on ground-based radar data
abstract: In order to test the designed radar system, it is first necessary to conduct radar echo simulation work as a basis for validating the newly developed system and signal processing algorithms. Therefore, a time-domain simulation program will be developed to simulate a real meteorological scenario using radar data, and echo simulation based on the autocorrelation function of rainfall echoes. Due to the lack of airship-borne radar measured data, but in order to verify the effectiveness of the radar system and signal processing technology designed on the airship-borne radar, the ground radar measured data is used as the input data of the simulation to simulate the echo simulation of the airship-borne radar detecting the ground radar data, so as to carry out other related tasks such as resolving range ambiguity and data quality control.

articleTitle: GEO-correction method for micro-deformation monitoring radar image and DEM fusion
abstract: The micro-deformation monitoring radar system has been widely used in the field of surface deformation monitoring, which is of great significance to the determination and identification of disaster hidden points in the monitoring area. Aiming at the problem that the positioning error of the Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) on the starting and ending points of the aperture will lead to the deviation of the position of the radar image mapped to the Digital Elevation Model (DEM) data, this paper derives the matching error formula of the fusion of the micro-deformation monitoring radar image and DEM, establishes the error correction model according to the matching error, and proposes a geo-correction method for the fusion of radar image and DEM. The feasibility and effectiveness of the model and the geo-correction method are verified by the measured data.

articleTitle: Landslide displacement prediction based on time series and GRU-ATTENTION neural network
abstract: Landslide displacement prediction is an important component of landslide monitoring and warning. Neural networks are gradually being applied to landslide displacement prediction. In order to enhance the extraction and capture of historical information to make predictions more accurate, this paper proposes a Gated Recurrent Unit neural network with attention mechanism (GRU-ATTENTION) for predicting landslide displacement. Firstly, the complete ensemble empirical mode decomposition with adaptive noise (CEEMDAN) algorithm is used to decompose the landslide displacement into trend and periodic terms. Then, the GRU-ATTENTION is used to fit the trend and period terms of landslide displacement with noise. Finally, considering the influence of rainfall and reservoir water level factors, the periodic and trend terms of the landslide displacement are predicted in Bazimen landslide. Compared with the prediction results of other traditional neural networks, the results indicate the GRU-ATTENTION can better capture historical information features, and achieve better prediction results, which provide a new technical method for landslide prediction.

articleTitle: Edge detection in PolSAR images based on polarimetric nonsubsampled contourlet transform
abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel edge detection method for polarimetric synthetic aperture radar (PolSAR) images based on polarimetric nonsubsampled contoured transform (PolNSCT). Nonsubsampled contourlet transform (NSCT) can provide flexible multiscale and directional decomposition, but it is susceptible to noise interference. In order to overcome this problem, we propose PolNSCT by combining multiscale polarimetric information in a new fashion. More specifically, in the multiscale decomposition, the coefficients of the nonsubsampled pyramid in the PolNSCT are calculated by measuring the polarimetric differences in polarimetric domain between the adjacent sub-band levels, instead of using the polarimetric contrast only or the differences in primary domain of the adjacent sub-bands. In this way, the proposed method detects edges more effectively in complex texture regions and produces less false alarms. Experimental results on an AirSAR image demonstrate the effectiveness and great potential of the proposed method.

articleTitle: CNN-GRU–based single-channel blind source separation of complex signals
abstract: A single-channel blind source separation method is proposed in this study to address the low accuracy and poor robustness of traditional methods in handling complex mixed signals composed of radar, communication, and jamming signals. The method combines a convolutional neural network (CNN) with a gated recurrent unit (GRU). The training phase involves normalizing the dataset, segmenting the sample sequence, extracting spatial features using a CNN, mining the temporal pattern using a GRU, and performing fully-connected feature fusion. The model parameters are trained and saved multiple times. In the testing phase, the algorithm verification and testing are conducted using the test set and the trained model to obtain a separated signal. The experimental results are compared with a traditional single-channel blind source separation algorithm and a deep learning blind so10urce separation algorithm with a single network structure. The proposed algorithm demonstrates high accuracy, a low distortion rate, and superior separation performance for complex mixed signals.

articleTitle: Design of agile multi-beam wave control system based on Ka phased array antenna
abstract: In recent years, China's space test missions have increased year by year, and satellite users have also increased year by year, and the requirements for inter-satellite, satellite-ground communication capabilities are getting higher and higher. Wideband array multi-beam antennas are widely used because of their advantages of large bandwidth, large dynamic range, high sensitivity, high gain and beam coverage agility. This paper introduces a method, which can meet the requirements of the harsh space environment of the space-borne phased array antenna, and can realize the rapid on-orbit switching of all wave positions of the multi-beam phased array antenna to meet the increasingly complex functional requirements of the antenna system.

articleTitle: Preliminary result of time delay estimation method based on range vernier technique
abstract: High-precision time delay estimation based on radio source signals is the core of accurate transmitting and receiving coherence technique of distributed coherent aperture radar. This paper introduces a time delay estimation method based on the range vernier technique and demonstrates an experiment based on measured data including system introduction, experiment design and preliminary results.

articleTitle: Mainlobe deceptive jamming suppression with polarimetric characteristic FDA-MIMO radar
abstract: This paper investigates the adaptive beamforming method based on the Polarimetric Scattering Matrix (PSM) of targets to suppress deceptive jammings located in the beampattern mainlobe. In our algorithm design, the cross dipoles are selected in the transmit and receive antennas, and the extra range-dependent degrees-of-freedom is introduced in the transmit and receive domains. A typical form of mainlobe deceptive jammings are considered, where multiple false targets are generated in the same range ambiguity region. In this respect, the parameters of all targets are estimated and the false targets are discriminated from the true target in the range-PSM domain. Furthermore, the false targets of the beampattern mainlobe are suppressed based on the adaptive beamforming method. The effectiveness of PSM in identification for the true and false targets is verified and the performance of mainlobe deceptive jamming suppression is evaluated by comparing with the existing systems via simulation results.

articleTitle: Thinned array anti-jamming angle measurement technology based on oblique projection
abstract: A new method for suppressing main lobe jamming and angle measurement using thinned array radar is proposed. Firstly, the received data of symmetric thinned array is synthesized into subarrays to reduce the processing complexity. Then, the ADBF method combined with oblique projection technology is proposed for jamming suppression, and the covariance matrix whitening formula of non-uniform subarrays is derived. Simulation results show that the proposed method has better angle discrimination surface and smaller angle measurement error than the four channel method under the specific main lobe jamming condition.

articleTitle: Multi-carrier LFM signal fusion for radar interference suppression
abstract: In this paper, a method for fusing multi-carrier linear frequency modulation (LFM) signals is presented and its application in radar interference suppression is demonstrated. The proposed method utilizes digital channelization in the receiver to separate the multiple subcarriers and implements dechirp processing to each subcarrier independently. The multiple dechirped signals are then fused using a sparse reconstruction algorithm to get a full-band response covering all the subcarriers, through which high range resolution radar detection can be achieved. Based on this method, narrow band spectral interferences can be easily eliminated by removing the dechirped signals of the interfered subcarriers. Numerical simulations are conducted with the results verifying the effectiveness of the multi-carrier fusion as well as the interference suppression capability.

articleTitle: An accumulation detection method based on energy dispersion of target echo in wideband radar
abstract: When the target size is fixed, the total number of weak scattering points will increase with the bandwidth increase. Because the total energy emitted by the radar is fixed, the energy is dispersed in more range units. Therefore, with the increasing bandwidth of wideband radar, the energy of a single echo will be dispersed to different distance units, resulting in echo splitting, and the reduction of signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) could be more conducive to target detection. In order to solve the problem of energy dispersion in wideband radar, an energy accumulation detection method with scattering point phase compensation is proposed in this paper. The method in this paper first analyzes the echo of the range-extended target. Then, it compensates for the echo signal by analyzing the phase relationship to realize the energy accumulation detection. The simulation results under the condition of low SNR show that compared with the radial accumulation detection method, the proposed accumulation detection method based on wideband radar energy dispersion has a higher target detection probability, which verifies the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Enhancing millimeter-wave radar object detection with a 3D transformer module on Range-Azimuth tensors
abstract: The millimeter-wave (mmWave) radar has been a robust and cost-effective sensor in the perception system. However, mmWave radar object detection is still a great challenge because radar signals contain far less semantic information than RGB images and are difficult to decipher directly by a human observer. Considering this, this letter presents an end-to-end network termed as 3D-Transformer-CNN (3D-T-CNN) for mmWave radar object detection using Range-Azimuth (RA) tensors. In this method, a non-local module transformer based on multi-head self-attention is introduced into a 3D vanilla convolutional neural network (CNN), which can make the best use of local and global features of sequential RA tensor frames. The experimental results show that the 3D-T-CNN significantly improves the accuracy of radar object detection, which achieves state-of-the-art performance.

articleTitle: Low-complexity DOA and polarization estimation via moving sparse nested array
abstract: To enhance the performance of direction of arrival (DOA) and polarization estimation, this paper presents a moving sparse nested array composed of cocentered orthogonal loop and dipole pairs, and then proposes a low-complexity method for parameter estimation with high-accuracy. A systematic procedure is applied for determining the inter-pair spacing of the original and shifted arrays and distance between such arrays for the synthetic polarization sensitive array, to efficiently increase degrees of freedom and enlarge array aperture. Owing to the array motion, the unique and high-precise DOA estimation is firstly achieved. Subsequently, the polarization state will be obtained by eigenvalue decomposition instead of multi-searching step. Numerical results are provided to show the advantages of the proposed approach over various existing methods in the presence of limited physical antennas.

articleTitle: ISAR sparse imaging exploiting the improved fully convolutional neural network
abstract: The fully convolutional neural network (FCNN) can cascade the shallow layer feature representations (SLFRs) and deep layer feature representations (DLFRs) to sparsely reconstruct ISAR target image. However, the FCNN adopts a series of nested, dense skip connections (SKs) to cascade the SLFRs and DLFRs directly, which inevitably leads to the semantic gap between the SLFRs and DLFRs and reduces the coherence of feature representations, and therefore the imaging performance of the FCNN is limited in deed. In this paper, we essentially re-design SKs using convolutional layers with the aim of reducing the semantic gap between the SLFRs and DLFRs. The FCNN with the re-designed SKs is referred to as improved FCNN (ImFCNN). Simulated ISAR data imaging results show that, the number of erroneous scatterers in the results obtained by ImFCNN is reduced by 18% on average, as compared with that in the results obtained by FCNN.

articleTitle: The optimal partition number estimation algorithm based on variational inference
abstract: The partition of individual targets into proper clusters is crucial in tracking group targets with complex spatial structures. However, most of the current clustering methods suffer from heavy computation burdens and unfitting a priori knowledge, resulting in the degradation of robustness. This paper proposes an optimal estimate of partition number based on the variational inference for group targets. By maximizing the variational evidence lower bound, which serves as the model-selected criterion, the optimal partition number can be estimated. The K-means++ algorithm is used to initialize the variation iteration. The proposed algorithm does not require a priori information and has low computation complexity, which benefits from the deterministic approximation character of variational inference. The effectiveness of the proposed method is verified by simulation results.

articleTitle: Characterization of corner reflector array in joint space-time-polarization domain
abstract: The corner reflector array has achieved wide applications in the radar field. It is important to study the scattering characteristics of the corner reflector array. It is currently common to research the scattering characteristics of the corner reflector in single-domain. However, one-dimensional information is difficult to reflect the real scattering characteristics of the target. There is rich information in the fully polarimetric high resolution range profiles (HRRP) sequence, which includes time information, space information and polarization information. This work is dedicated to reveal the scattering characteristics of the corner reflector array in joint space-time-polarization domain by using the polarimetric correlation pattern. The joint feature set with high separability is derived. Then, experimental studies with electromagnetic simulation data of corner reflector and typical scene are carried out. Experimental results show that the scattering characteristics of corner reflector array in space-time-polarization domain are roll-invariant and stable. The derived joint feature set has good separability.

articleTitle: Speckle-based optronic convolutional neural network for SAR target recognition in light scattering imaging
abstract: Light scattering has been a pervasive issue in past decades across many areas. The scattering medium not only destroys the imaging performance in remote sensing but also sets challenges in automatic target recognition (ATR). Recent deep learning (DL) approaches have made significant progress in ATR tasks based on the scattered speckle patterns. However, the DL methods encounter great challenges in computation speed and power consumption. Here, we develop a speckle-based optronic convolutional neural network (S-OPCNN) and realize the network in the optical platform for SAR ATR tasks. We specifically model the speckle patterns for Moving and Stationary Target Acquisition and Recognition (MSTAR) objects by random phase noise distortion. Then we train the S-OPCNN to execute the ATR tasks based on speckle patterns. In S-OPCNN, all computational operations are performed in optics with ultra-fast speed, low energy cost, and low space complexity. Experiments on MSTAR datasets demonstrate the S-OPCNN feasibility in SAR ATR under degraded imaging conditions.

articleTitle: Echo modeling for asteroids with rough surface in gound-based SAR imaging
abstract: With the development of radar imaging technology, asteroid imaging has become one of the focal points in astronomical radar research. However, in simulation and verification experiments for asteroids observation, the traditional point target approximation method is often inadequate in capturing geometric features and surface topography of asteroid. To address this issue, this paper proposes an improved method for generating asteroid echo specifically tailored for asteroid imaging tasks. Firstly, the relative motion between the radar and the asteroid is calculated to determine the slant range phase. Simultaneously, an amplitude factor that varies with the observation angle is introduced, correcting the isotropic scattering of traditional point target. Subsequently, considering the rough characteristic of asteroid surfaces, an echo generation process is presented based on the Monte Carlo method. Finally, computer simulation experiments are conducted to complete the echo generation and radar imaging of asteroid and its typical surface topography features. The experiments validate the correctness and effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Intelligent association algorithm for multi-angle SAR images based on multi-feature fusion
abstract: The multi-target association of synthetic aperture radar (SAR) remote sensing images in multiple views presents two key challenges. Firstly, the conventional association method based on state information is not applicable due to the diverse observation conditions. Secondly, relying only on image features for multi-target association causes ambiguity in the association. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a novel algorithm based on multi-feature fusion for multi-angle SAR image association. This approach integrates both image features and target position information to make more informed association judgments, effectively leveraging the complementary nature of these two types of information. As a result, it enhances association accuracy and enables adaptability in diverse and dynamic environments.

articleTitle: Surface acoustic wave reflective delay line as passive cooperative target for wireless sub-surface sensing in liquid using ground penetrating radar
abstract: Ground Penetrating RADAR (GPR) is a classical geophysical tool for detecting sub-surface dielectric interfaces. In this context, we complement this measurement by quantitatively sensing various quantities including temperature, stress, and most importantly, the concentration of chemical compounds in a liquid phase. This is achieved using dedicated cooperative targets designed as reflective surface acoustic wave delay lines which are manufactured on lithium tantalate oxide (LTO) piezoelectric substrates. LTO is chosen for detecting sub-surface chemical compounds in liquid phase due to its ability to generate and propagate pure shear acoustic waves, resulting in minimal insertion losses even in the presence of water. Furthermore, the high permittivity LTO leads to minimal impact of the presence of water over interdigitated transducer electrodes, removing the need for challenging microfluidic packaging otherwise needed to prevent capacitive short circuit. The reflective delay line design operating in the 100 to 500 MHz range induces echoes delayed beyond subsurface interface echoes – here associated to clutter – whose time difference is solely representative on the quantity under investigation, whether temperature, stress or chemical concentration depending on the surface functionalization, independently on the distance from the GPR to the sensor. This concept is demonstrated with the direct detection of protein physisorption without the need for sensor packaging.

articleTitle: An array calibration method based on iterative weighted least squares in radio astronomy
abstract: This paper focuses on array calibration in presence of noise in radio astronomy, involving estimating the time delay between different receiving channels. The received signals are modelled as complex Gaussian white noise with an under-estimated time delay between channels. A novel time delay estimation method is proposed, which utilizes an iterative weighted least squares method to the phase differences at different frequency. By establishing a linear relationship between phase differences and frequency, the desired time delay can be obtained. Simulations are conducted to evaluate the performance of the proposed method. The results demonstrate the advantages of the proposed method in accurate calibration.

articleTitle: Target localization for SIMO radar using tensor decomposition
abstract: This paper focuses on the problem of target localization for single input and multiple output (SIMO) radar. Firstly, the array structure and signal model are discussed. The transmitting array is shared for multiple receiving arrays, and a set of third order tensors with a common factor matrix are constructed. Then, the tensors are decomposed to separate the array manifold matrices by means of a modified alternating least square (ALS) method. Finally, the targets are located based on the baseline, the direction of departure (DOD) and direction of arrival (DOA), which can be estimated by spectrum analysis of each column of the array manifold matrices. The effectiveness and superiority of the proposed method is demonstrated by simulation results.

articleTitle: Identification and positioning of UAV in sheltered areas of buildings based on FMCW radar
abstract: The past few decades have witnessed the monumental success of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) in both military and civilian applications. However, this success has also led to the increased need for UAV detection and recognition, as improper management of UAVs can pose serious risks. Detecting UAVs is particularly challenging due to their small Radar Cross Section (RCS) and consequently low Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) in received signals. This difficulty is further compounded in urban environments where UAVs are often located in Non-Line-of-Sight (NLOS) areas, shielded by massive buildings. In this paper, we propose an approach to identify and locate UAVs in building shadow areas using a Frequency Modulated Continuous Wave (FMCW) radar system. Firstly, we extract the micro-Doppler spectrum of the drone rotor from the one-dimensional FFT spectrum of the echo signal. Then, we employ the peak extraction method to estimate the parameters of the drone rotor speed and blade length, facilitating drone identification. Subsequently, we extract range bins data capable of recognizing drones, which serves as input for the localization algorithm. By developing a multi-channel and multipath imaging fusion algorithm, we accumulate strong values corresponding to the drone location, thereby enabling its precise localization. Extensive simulations and experiments commendably validate the effectiveness and accuracy of the proposed method.

articleTitle: High-resolution radar ground clutter generation by denoising diffusion probability model
abstract: Environmental clutter significantly impacts the performance of High-Resolution Range Profiles (HRRP) in detection and recognition. Hence, it's crucial to model and simulate radar clutter for effective radar system design. However, traditional methods are limited to fixed probability distributions, struggle to accurately replicate clutter in complex real-world scenarios. In this paper, we propose to generate clutter based on the Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Model (DDPM). DDPM can learn the distribution of training data through its probabilistic modelling method, solving the limitations brought by traditional methods. In addition, in order to evaluate the amplitude characteristics of generated clutter, we propose to compare the fitting results of specific physical probability distributions of generated clutter with those of real clutter, as well as evaluate the distribution distance with real clutter. Experimental results on measured clutter data show that the clutter synthesized by DDPM can well match the distribution of the measured clutter. And it is able to demonstrate good performance in different scenarios.

articleTitle: Dual-polarized entropy extraction based on new scattering vector and its application in landslide detection
abstract: In analogy with the full-polarized (FP) synthetic aperture radar (SAR) data processing, this paper extracts the polarimetric entropy based on the reciprocity theorem from dual-polarized (DP) SAR data. Specifically, a new scattering vector conforming to the reciprocity assumption is constructed, based on which the entropy is derived via the classical entropy/alpha decomposition. The newly extracted entropy is analysed and compared not only with existing entropies for DP but also with that for FP, both theoretically and experimentally using the Gaofen-3 FP data. The results demonstrate that the entropy based on the new scattering vector has better consistency with target FP scattering characteristics, making it an effective descriptor of scattering randomness. Furthermore, experimental results on Sentinel-1 DP data obtained before and after the 2022 Luding earthquake show that the new entropy performs better for landslide detection than existing entropies.

articleTitle: A SCIL-based transformer for PolSAR image classification
abstract: Transformer has been applied for polarimetric synthetic aperture radar (PolSAR) image processing due to its ability to construct long-range dependency. However, Transformer lacks the learning of local spatial information within samples and correlation information among samples, which limits its performance in practical tasks. To address these issues, this paper proposes a novel Transformer structure based on spatial information learning and correlation information learning (SCIL-based Transformer) for PolSAR image classification. Firstly, a global-local spatial information learning (GL-SIL) module is constructed to fully extract the global-local spatial information within samples. Secondly, a correlation information learning (CIL) module is designed to achieve the learning of correlation information among samples by modeling the dependency across samples. Compared to the self-attention network in Transformer, the above two modules not only add the learning of local spatial information within samples and the correlation information among samples, but also greatly reduce the network complexity. Experiments on two real PolSAR datasets have shown that the proposed SCIL-based Transformer has better performance than other state-of-the-art algorithms.

articleTitle: An improved deep active learning method for SAR ship detection
abstract: In the task of Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) ship detection, data annotation is generally time-consuming and expensive. Active learning is a technique that iteratively selects the most informative images from a dataset. Therefore, it can reduce the number of samples required for training ship detection model. In this paper, an improved active learning method is proposed for SAR ship detection. This paper is based on the active learning method relying on the mixture density network, which estimates a probabilistic distribution for each localization and classification head’s output. The predicted parameters of distributions can be used to calculate the loss of a detection model during the training process and estimate the inputted SAR image’s informativeness score during selecting images for labelling. Since the network aims at predicting the distribution parameters, which are much more than the traditional detection network, it makes the model fitting more difficult. We improve the detection model by adding a localization head and classification head to this network. They aim to directly predict the potential target's bounding box positions and categories. The corresponding loss is named as bounding box loss. The final loss of model combines the bounding box with the mixture density loss. The model performance is evaluated on the SSDD dataset. For example, the network was first trained separately using initially less labelled SAR images. Then, new SAR images are labelled based on information scores and added to the training set to retrain the model. The results show that our method outperforms the mixed density network.

articleTitle: A dual-polarized maximum eigenvalue based target detection method for sea clutter environment
abstract: By making good use of the correlation information between the data via the covariance matrix, a matrix constant false alarm detector based on geometric measures is effective for detecting targets under a sea clutter environment with a small number of pulses. However, the existing matrix CFAR detector uses only a single polarization echo and has a high computational complexity, resulting in underutilization of correlation information and limited detection scenarios. This paper uses radar echoes from two channels of HH and VV polarization to construct eigenvalues of the cross-covariance matrix to capture correlations, and proposes a dual-polarized maximum eigen-value-based detection method with low computational complexity. The authors derive the detection statistic with the maximum eigenvalue as the main component, and further design the matrix CFAR detector based on the dual-polarized maximum eigenvalue, which can be used in real scenarios. In addition, the method is verified to achieve better practical detection performance with the measured sea clutter data.

articleTitle: Multilayer range migration based on autofocusing technology using GPR data
