abstract: Ground penetrate radar (GPR) migration imaging has important significance to underground target detection and recognition. In the actual environment, the underground medium often has a horizontal structure. Conventional migration imaging method for single medium is not applicable. Therefore, this paper proposes a multilayer range migration (MRM) imaging method, MRM combines the ideas of phase shift migration (PSM) and range migration (RM). Electromagnetic waves are discontinuous at the interface between layers, and MRM can solve the problem by phase continuation. The applicability of the RM from homogeneous medium extended to multilayer medium. Then, we use the autofocusing technique (AF) to estimate the relative permittivity (RP) of each layer of the medium based on the migrated image. Combining with MRM and AF enables accurately imaging the targets within a layered scene with unknown relative permittivity.

articleTitle: Model-based RAO and WALD detectors for range-spread targets in heterogeneous clutter environment
abstract: A significant advantage of the Random Frequency and Pulse Repetition Interval Agile (RFPA) radar system lies in its ability to reduce the correlation of sea clutter, subsequently enhancing the signal-to-clutter ratio (SCR). However, when the high- resolution RFPA radar operates in sea clutter environments, the backscattered energy from the target spreads across multiple range cells within a single pulse, leading to varying power levels among these cells. To address the challenge of detecting range-spread targets in such heterogeneous clutter environments, this paper introduces the Heterogeneous Autoregressive Rao (HTG-AR-Rao) detector and Heterogeneous Autoregressive Wald (HTG-AR-Wald) detector. These detectors are based on the Rao and Wald test, modeling the clutter as a 1st to 4th order AR process, so that no training data are required. The AR coefficients and the variances of the clutter for individual range cells are determined using Maximum Likelihood Estimation (MLE). Importantly, the asymptotic expressions for both the probability of false alarm and detection verify that the proposed detectors achieve an asymptotically constant false alarm rate (CFAR). Simulation results demonstrate that these detectors adeptly adapt to the heterogeneous clutter environment, delivering satisfactory detection performance and reduce computational cost compared to detectors based on the Generalized Likelihood Ratio Test (GLRT).

articleTitle: A self-supervised contrastive learning method for out-of-distribution detection in SAR images
abstract: This paper targets on an effective and self-supervised contrastive learning-based method for out-of-distribution (OOD) detection in Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) images. Due to the potential threats posed by unidentified targets in battlefield reconnaissance, it is crucial to determine whether the target category is known and prevent any misclassification. Existing deep-neural-network-based (DNN-based) methods for OOD detection have shown promising results, but their training process requires a significant amount of labeled data, which limits their application in SAR imagery. In this paper, we propose a label- free OOD detection framework for SAR images. By employing image augmentation techniques specifically designed for SAR images, we construct positive and negative samples. We utilize the contrastive learning framework for self-supervised training and employ Mahalanobis distance to distinguish unknown class data. After conducting numerous experiments and analysis, we have identified the optimal combination of augmentation techniques for SAR OOD detection. Experimental results on the MSTAR dataset demonstrate that our method outperforms existing DNN-based methods.

articleTitle: 3-D reconstruction of space target based on ISAR image sequences
abstract: 3-D reconstruction of spatial targets based on ISAR image sequences has important practical significance for spatial situational awareness and spatial security. The 3D reconstruction of image sequence needs to extract the coordinates of feature points on the target and correlate the same point in different images for matching, which requires that the feature points are present in the whole ISAR image sequence with a certain number so as to provide enough information to characterize the target. The current research mainly uses SIFT features, SURF features, Fast and other features commonly used in optical image matching. The number of feature points that can be extracted and matched between radar image sequences is relatively small, and it is difficult to reconstruct the target profile. To overcome this problem, this paper adopts Shi-Tomasi corner point detection and Kanade-Lucas-Tomasi (KLT) tracking to solve the problem of low number of feature point matching between radar images. After the matching of feature points in multiple sequence images, the 3D point cloud image of the target is obtained by using the factorization method. Compared with other related methods, the experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method can perform 3D reconstruction of spatial targets with high quality and obtain 3D dense point clouds of the targets.

articleTitle: Dynamic monitoring of mining subsidence using LT-1 DInSAR data in Datong
abstract: The Datong mining area is located in the northern part of Shanxi province. This area is significantly impacted by mining subsidence associated with mining activities. This work analyses the dynamics mining subsidence in some typical subsidence bowls. To achieve this goal, we utilized data from the LuTan-1(LT-1) mission, which is the first L-band bistatic spaceborne SAR mission for civil application in China. Firstly, we calculated displacements from LT-1 for the following time periods: 2 March 2022 to 18 April 2022, 18 April 2022 to 15 December 2022, 15 December 2022 to 28 January 2023, and 2 March 2022 to 28 January 2023. The results enabled the identification of four subsidence bowls with maximum subsidence areas and displacements of 10.604 m2 and -0.38 m, respectively, from 2 March 2022 to 28 January 2023. By overlapping the four DInSAR results from different dates, we derived the ground surface displacements that were a result of the dynamic mining process. As a result, the maximum horizontal displacement of the subsidence bowl was approximately 588.9 m during the one-year observation period. This approach opens the door to the dynamic monitoring of mining subsidence by LT-1 images.

articleTitle: Maritime moving target localization method based on multi-station GNSS-S radar SAR images
abstract: High precision real-time positioning of maritime moving ship targets has always been a research focus and challenge in the field of spaceborne radar remote sensing. Leveraging the advantages of all-weather, all-day, high-resolution imaging, the satellite-borne single-station Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) system has been widely employed for maritime ship localization. However, the movement of targets can lead to defocusing and positional shifts in SAR imaging, resulting in poor localization accuracy. This article proposes a method for maritime moving target localization based on multi-station SAR images using Global Navigation Satellite System-Scatterometry (GNSS-S) radar. The method establishes a dispersion evaluation function for detecting the positions of targets using multi-station GNSS-S radar. The dispersion value is utilized as an evaluation metric for iteratively optimizing and solving the target velocity, thereby obtaining the best velocity estimate for the target. The compensated imaging results are then fused across multiple stations to achieve high-precision uncontrolled positioning. Through simulation analysis, this method demonstrates that for moving targets with speeds around 8 m/s, the uncontrolled positioning accuracy can be improved from 680 meters to 98 meters, significantly enhancing the localization precision of maritime moving targets.

articleTitle: Remote sensing inversion of grass mowing based on time series SAR satellite images
abstract: Grass mowing is an important part of agricultural production and is vital for raising livestock and producing fodder. Therefore, accurate monitoring and prediction of the timing and scale of grass cutting is important for agricultural decision-making. Traditional monitoring methods are usually limited by weather conditions and geographical coverage. Time -series synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellite imagery, as an important remote sensing data source, can overcome these limitations and provide all-weather and all-time monitoring capabilities to capture the spatial and temporal variations of grassland mowing activities. In this paper, a remote sensing inversion method for grassland mowing based on time-series synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellite images is proposed. Firstly, relevant time-series synthetic aperture radar (SAR) image data are acquired and preprocessed to improve data quality. Then, sampling points were selected on the grassland in the study area to extract the relevant features of grass cutting: backward scattering coefficients, and establish the time series of SAR satellite images. Finally, the detection and identification of grass cutting was achieved using backscatter detection method.

articleTitle: Selection matrix design for sparse array signal processing
abstract: In sparse array signal processing, all the equivalent virtual signals vectorized from the covariance matrix are contained in the single-snapshot measurement vector. However, spatial smoothing technique is susceptible to repeated virtual sensors. In general, the array steering must be unique. This paper advances a selection matrix for extracting equivalent virtual signals received by such repeated virtual sensors. The elements of the selection matrix are determined by the weight function of the difference lags. We then popularize the method of constructing the selection matrix corresponding to arbitrary sparse arrays after analysing the weight function for nested array and coprime array. Compared with the previous binary selection matrix, the schemed selection matrix can preserve all the equivalent virtual signals, thus having better direction of arrival (DOA) es- timation performance.

articleTitle: Moving aircraft recognition with transformer based on radar trajectories
abstract: With the continuous development of intelligent military technology, aircraft recognition based on radar trajectories is of high significance. In this paper, we firstly carry out data cleaning for the radar trajectories of military and civilian aircraft to alleviate the impact of outliers. Due to the difficulty of data collection of military aircraft relative to civilian aircraft, the trajectories of military aircraft are augmented to achieve the same amount of samples as civilian aircraft for model training. Secondly, inspired by the global modelling capability of Transformer, we adopt a pooling-based attention Transformer to learn the long-term flying characteristics for the overall aircraft trajectory. Our results extensively validate the effectiveness of the proposed model.

articleTitle: Study on timeliness external DEM for open-pit mining area deformation monitoring using LuTan-1 SAR data
abstract: LuTan-1 SAR satellite is the first bistatic spaceborne SAR constellation for multiple applications in China, which consists of two identical multi-polarimetric L-band SAR. Surface deformation monitoring with centimeter even millimeter accuracy may be achieved based on LuTan-1 SAR data. For open-pit mining area, due to the extensive mining activities the topography of coal mine area generally changes obviously. Therefore, the high accuracy and timeliness external DEM has significant influence on deformation monitoring, especially for open-pit mining area. In order to effectively evaluate the effect of external DEM for InSAR deformation monitoring, SRTM DEM and GaoFen-7 satellite derived DEM were utilized for deformation extraction based on Lutan-1 SAR data. The results indicated that timeliness external DEM is significant for deformation monitoring over open-pit mining areas.

articleTitle: An applied OFDM chirp waveform design scheme for radar coincidence imaging
abstract: The imaging performance of traditional imaging radars is affected by platform motion factors or limited by hardware. For example, the focusing performance of synthetic aperture radar (SAR) will be lost due to the non-ideal motion state, and the improvement of azimuth resolution of real aperture radar (RAR) requires a very large array, which is obviously not advisable. Radar coincidence imaging (RCI) technology can well balance the shortcomings of SAR and RAR and can achieve super- resolution imaging results. The transmitted random noise waveform is an ideal waveform for RCI, but its hardware system and echo processing technology are complicated. In this paper, we use orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) chirp waveform instead of random noise waveform to realize RCI, which utilizes the advantages of OFDM technology and chirp signal to overcome the deficiency of noise waveform, and its orthogonality is higher than chirp signal. An OFDM chirp waveform optimization scheme based on the reference matrix condition number is proposed, which can further improve the imaging performance of RCI. The simulation results verify the effectiveness of the method proposed in this paper.

articleTitle: False target jamming identification based on CFAR with wideband distributed radar
abstract: Complex electromagnetism jamming plays an important role in modern combat system, which disturbs the normal radar probing. Especially for active deception jamming, it has strong coherence with radar transmitting signal to form indistinguishable false target, resulting in detection and tracking failure. In this paper, a false target jamming recognition method using wideband distributed radar is proposed based on scattering feature matching and statistical probability modelling. The scattering characteristics change with view angle for true target, but the false target keeps the same scattering characteristics due to the single directional modulation. Based on this consideration, the scattering characteristics of wideband echo among distributed radars are analysed, and the probabilistic discriminant model is derived to recognize false target. The simulated experiments are also given to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Statistical analysis of swarm targets radar echo
abstract: The statistical characteristics of radar target echoes play a critical role in target detection. Swarm targets, characterized by their substantial numbers, extensive distribution, and relative motion between entities, manifest echo properties notably different from conventional rigid point targets and range-spread targets. In this study, we examine the amplitude statistical attributes of crowd echoes, a prototypical swarm target, acquired through LFCW radar observations. We employ Rayleigh, Weibull, and K-distribution models to fit the collected data. The results demonstrate that the K-distribution model provides good data fitting than other statistical models for swarm target echoes.

articleTitle: ISAR refocusing algorithm for maneuvering ship targets SAR data based on parametric sparse Bayesian learning
abstract: SAR imaging of maneuvering ship targets under complex environment is a challenge problem. This paper proposed a ISAR refocusing algorithm for SAR data of maneuvering ship targets based on parametric SBL. The signal model of ship fluctuation in atrocious sea state is analysed firstly. The Doppler chirp rates of scatters vary with the position of scatters. The Doppler chirp rates is set as the parameters of the observation matrix. Then the hierarchical SBL model with Laplace prior is constructed. Variational inference and Quasi-Newton methos are applied to achieve Bayesian inference and updating parameters of the observation matrix, respectively. the experiment results have demonstrated that the proposed algorithm can obtain the focused image of maneuvering ship targets under the situation of low SNR and incomplete data.

articleTitle: Multi-frame track-before-detect for adjacent extended targets
abstract: This paper mainly studies the detection and tracking of the adjacent multi-extended targets in the low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) scene. Since the traditional multi-frame track-before-detect (MF-TBD) algorithm only considers the amplitude characteristics of the target, there are serious overlap and interference problems in the echo measurement of the adjacent extended targets, which causes the track confusion of multi-target tracking, bringing challenges to the MF-TBD algorithm. Therefore, a new algorithm named transfer cost MF-TBD (TC-MF-TBD) is proposed in this paper. Combined with the MF-TBD, a joint detection statistic based on the transfer cost function and the amplitude likelihood function is introduced. The TC-MF-TBD can effectually solve the difficulty of wrong data association of adjacent target trajectory by introducing transfer cost penalty in the process of multi-frame accumulation. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method is superiority in detecting performance and tracking accuracy.

articleTitle: Focusing spaceborne-missile bistatic forward-looking SAR using modified azimuth nonlinear chirp scaling
abstract: Spaceborne-missile bistatic forward-looking SAR (SMBF-SAR) can obtain high-precision images in front of the missile, using a spaceborne illuminator to provide a stable radar signal. However, the acceleration of the missile and the high speed of the spaceborne transmitter, cause a seriously spatial variant range cell migration (RCM) and azimuth frequency modulation (FM) rate in the echo signal. Therefore, in the range processing, the range preprocessing filtering and the second-order keystone transform (KT) are proposed to remove the large spatial variant RCM; in the azimuth processing, the modified azimuth nonlinear chirp scaling (NCS) is used to equalize the azimuth FM rate. The imaging results in simulation results verify the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Sea clutter parametric model modification based on measured data
abstract: To enhance the detection rate of small targets on the sea surface, it is crucial to characterize and model sea clutter. A new method is proposed in this paper to modify the parameterized sea clutter model which based on measured data. At first, the measured sea clutter data from an airborne radar is processed to obtain the data near the beam center. And then the measured data is fitted using various distribution models, such as the K distribution, generalized Pareto distribution, and Compound-Gaussian model with Inverse Gaussian texture distribution. The optimal distribution model is determined, and the parameters of this model are estimated to obtain the optimal parameters. At last, these optimal parameters are used to correct the parameterized model of sea clutter, thereby improving its performance.

articleTitle: Weak target detection via texture information on time-frequency manifolds
abstract: To improve the target detection performance in complex environments, this paper proposes a weak target detection method via texture information on time-frequency manifolds. Firstly, time-frequency distribution images are collected by the received data to capture non-stationary features. Meanwhile, based on the time-frequency distribution images, time-frequency manifolds are constructed. Then, the target and clutter can correspond to different objects on the manifold, and the target detection issues are transformed into the problem of measuring the distance between these geometric objects. For the complex scenario which the target and clutter are close on the manifold, the texture information is extracted to increase the difference between the target and clutter. Finally, an information geometry detector based on the texture information is put forward and experiment results show that the proposed method achieves a high detection performance in low SCNR.

articleTitle: A knowledge-assisted space-time spectrum compensation method for bistatic array radar clutter
abstract: When the spaceborne bistatic radar looks down, radar returns from ground, referred to as clutter, may be powerful and cause severe interferences. Space-time adaptive processing is an effective way to suppress the clutter for moving target detection. However, as the space-time spectrum of clutter in the bistatic radar system is rapidly changing in space, the space-time spectrum in a range gate may be severely spread, resulting in deterioration of processing performance. In order to solve this problem, a knowledge-assisted space-time spectrum compensation method for the bistatic radar system is proposed. Specifically, the detection area is divided into small-scale resolution units, and the space-time clutter model of the bistatic system is established according to the system geometry, platform relative motion and radar detection mechanism, which forms prior knowledge of the space-time vectors. Then, the knowledge-assisted space-time matrixes of the clutter units in the range gate to be compensated is constructed. Meanwhile, the space-time matrixes of the reference clutter units is searched by the Capon spectrum in the circular domain to fit the original clutter data. Based on the two matrixes, a transformation matrix is constructed to realize the space-time spectrum compensation. Finally, the validation of the proposed compensation algorithm is present by simulations.

articleTitle: A lightweight method for infrared small target detection
abstract: Infrared small target detection, as a technology for extracting faint targets from infrared feature maps, holds significant applications in fields such as search and rescue and wildfire prevention. However, conventional networks for infrared small target detection demand a substantial number of parameters. They impose high requirements on computational capability and storage space, thereby hindering their deployments on embedded devices. To address this issue, we proposed a bifurcated network model with two channels: one dedicated to capturing holistic image features, and the other focused on edge features, separately computing the network's loss function. Within both channels, we leveraged depthwise separable convolution and the Convolutional Block Attention Module to extract features. This approach effectively reduces the parameter count while ensuring precise target detection shapes. Our experimental results on the IRSTD-1k dataset demonstrate that, while maintaining accuracy and inference time comparable to the reference network model, our model has reduced the number of convolution parameters by 1.59x. Therefore, our method helps the deployment of complex neural networks for infrared small target detection in the context of resource-limited embedded systems.

articleTitle: Multi-source joint imaging method for shipborne GNSS-S radar
abstract: The signals of the Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) have the advantages of global coverage and full-time broadcast. By making full use of them as electromagnetic illuminators, the detection and imaging of maritime targets can be achieved, which can obtain multidimensional characteristic information about the target and enable the identification of maritime targets. However, conventional shore-based GNSS passive radar achieves synthetic aperture imaging through the movement of GNSS satellites, which requires a long observation time and is easily defocused by the movement of the target. In this study, a shipborne GNSS-S radar imaging method is proposed that realizes synthetic aperture imaging through the movement of the ship platform to shorten the observation time and improve the imaging quality by fusing multiple images. In view of the problems faced by shipborne GNSS passive radar imaging, such as three-dimensional spatial variation of geometric configuration and the influence of platform motion error, the imaging characteristics of shipborne GNSS-S radar are analyzed, and a shipborne multi-source GNSS-S imaging method is proposed. First, the imaging geometry is constructed on the basis of the position of the ship platform calculated from the direct GNSS signal to obtain a rough image of the target. Then, a three-dimensional image matrix is constructed from the imaging results of multiple GNSS satellites, and the energy distribution characteristics of multiple images are used to eliminate the image tailing phenomenon caused by motion residual errors and achieve fine focusing of the target image. Simulation and field experiments were conducted to verify that this method can obtain fine images of maritime ships with a synthetic aperture time of 3 s.

articleTitle: Exploiting the detection performance potential of hybrid PA-MIMO radar
abstract: This paper establishes a hybrid distributed phased-array multiple-input multiple-output (PA-MIMO) radar system model to explore the detection performance potential of the radar system. We derived a Neyman-Pearson based detection model with simultaneously considering the reciprocity of the channel induced by subarray transceiver sharing and the multi-pulse phase-coherent accumulation conditions. A closed-form solution for calculating detection probability is obtained by calculating the likelihood ratio test (LRT). Then, by comparing the performance with other three regimes, and the optimal element configuration PA-MIMO radar exhibits superior performance with a maximum detection probability of 0.9874. The simulation results validated the comprehensive utilization of coherent processing gain and waveform diversity gain will effectively enhancing the target detection capability of the radar system and thus successively exploring the detection performance of the radar system.

articleTitle: Scan performance of small boat RCS enhancers
abstract: Passive RCS enhancers are used to increase the return from small targets like green water fishing boats, increasing detectability and thus decreasing collisions. A small number of independent studies have qualified the performance of RCS enhancers in the horizontal plane. Here a set of RCS enhancers scaled to 12GHz to fit within a 200mm diameter sphere were assessed across the full working angular arc of each against the ISO recommendation using a commercially available antenna simulator. A commonly used trihedral reflector gave 7dBm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> or better across a ±12<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">°</sup> arc with 2dB variation. A 200mm diameter disk gave 13dBm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> on axis only, while a spherical lens reflector gave the same RCS across a ±30<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">°</sup> arc with 0.4dB variation. Changing from a spherical lens to a double convex lens halved the projected weight but reduced the scan range to a ±10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">°</sup> arc with 0.9dB variation.

articleTitle: Sparsity-based nonparametric phase error correction for THz SAR imaging
abstract: Terahertz synthetic aperture radar (THz SAR) has high imaging resolution even in complex environments. Due to the short wavelength, THz SAR is more sensitive to the complex motion error. The motion compensation methods for THz SAR mainly focus on the high frequency vibration error, which requires the presence of isolated strong scatterer in the scene and may fail when the actual motion error is inconsistent with the preset model. To address the above problems, an autofocusing framework based on sparse regularization is proposed for estimating complex phase error. Specifically, the phase error of each azimuth point is regarded as an independent variable, and the randomly sampled data from one range profile with high signal- to-noise ratio is used as the observation vector. The image of this range gate and phase error are reconstructed in an alternating iteration fashion. Furthermore, the phase error estimation is compensated to the original image to obtain a high-precision focused image. The performance of the proposed method is verified by the experimental data measured by a vehicle-borne SAR at 0.3THz band. Compared with the sinusoidal frequency modulated Fourier transform (SFMFT) algorithm, it does not require isolated strong scatterer and thus has better scene adaptability.

articleTitle: An enhanced iterative adaptive approach for automotive MIMO radar forward-looking imaging
abstract: Automotive radar forward-looking imaging is of great importance in scenarios like advanced driver assistance systems (ADASs). In this paper, an enhanced iterative adaptive approach (IAA) with two regularization terms is proposed for automotive MIMO radar forward-looking imaging. To tackle with the environmental noise in automotive radar, the additive noise term is taken into consideration, while the ill-posed problem of IAA is analysed and solved by introducing the diagonal loading method. When compared to IAA and regularized IAA, the proposed enhanced IAA is shown to provide resolution improvement. Numerical results illustrate the superior performance of the proposed enhanced IAA.

articleTitle: Design and implementation of a configurable parallel FFT processor in onboard SAR imaging system based on FPGA
abstract: Spaceborne Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) plays an important role in the field of emergency disaster reduction. In order to meet the stringent timeliness requirements in onboard SAR data processing, this paper proposes a configurable four-channel parallel FFT processor, which serves as the core of SAR imaging processing. This processor is capable of supporting up to 128K-point FFT operations. Additionally, it supports radix-2 time decimation FFT concatenation processing, radix-4 time decimation FFT concatenation processing, radix-2 frequency decimation FFT concatenation processing, and radix-4 frequency decimation FFT concatenation processing, all of which can be flexibly configured based on data structure . This processor is implemented on the Xilinx Virtex-7 XC7VX690T FPGA and can achieve a maximum FFT processing capability of 128K points at a frequency of 300MHz. The evaluation and analysis results demonstrate that the processor reaches a higher processing rate, effectively meeting the demanding requirements for efficient spaceborne processing.

articleTitle: Evaluation of the deformation measurement efficacy of GNSS-based InBSAR in vegetated areas: trials initiation
abstract: The surface-reflected signals from Global Navigation satellites (GNSS) contain a wealth of terrain information, which enable the extraction of deformations of the Earth's surface by bistatic Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InBSAR). However, the impact of vegetation on surface deformation measurement in GNSS-based InBSAR requires further investigation. In this paper, an initial trial of the evaluation of the deformation measurement efficacy of the GNSS-InBSAR is carried out. A methodological framework of this study considered multiple factors is proposed. Within vegetated landscapes, the interference coherence is particularly compromised due to the seasonal growth and decay of vegetation. Simultaneously, the intricate variety, complex structures, and stochastic distribution of vegetation impede the establishment of a comprehensive vegetation reflection model, thereby posing challenges to the retrieval of surface deformation. Moreover, a data acquisition experiment of Beidou Navigation Satellites (BDS) is designed and conducted.

articleTitle: Resolving range ambiguity in EPC SAR based on beampattern precise control
abstract: This paper aims to solve the problem of range ambiguity for Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) High-Resolution Wide-Swath (HRWS) imaging. At the modelling stage, an Element-Pulse Coding (EPC) SAR scheme is developed by encoding both the transmit antenna elements and slow-time pulses. In specific, the echoes from the desired range ambiguity region can be extracted according to the mainlobe of the equivalent transmit beampattern by nulling the undesired range ambiguity regions. Moreover, considering the amplitude-phase error, which induces a deviation from a presumed null, a Beampattern Precise Control (BPC) method is developed by adding artificial interferences on the beampattern to broaden the nulls for sufficient mitigation of undesired range ambiguity regions. Finally, the HRWS-SAR images can be achieved after conventional imaging processing in SAR system. Numerical results are provided to verify the effectiveness of the devised method in resolving the range ambiguity and obtaining the HRWS-SAR images.

articleTitle: Performance analysis of scanning gain for irregular ultra wideband phased array antennas based on subarrays
abstract: The irregular array based on subarrays can effectively improve the gain of antenna aperture. In response to the problem of large decrease in scanning gain of the irregular array based on subarrays, this paper comprehensively considers the antenna pattern and subarray form, and establishes a parabolic equivalent model for enhancing the gain of the irregular dual polarization array based on subarrays. Taking 6 GHz to 18 GHz as the object, the variation law of irregular array gain based on different number of subarrays and scanning angle changes was analysed. The simulation results showed that under the same number of TR channels, when operating in the ultra-wideband low-frequency or small scanning angle range, the irregular array gain based on subarrays was higher than the regular array gain; When operating in the ultra wideband high-frequency wide angle range, the gain of the irregular array based on the subarray is lower than that of the regular array; The HFSS simulation results of the Vivalid antenna array based on dual polarization are consistent with the model results in this paper. The paper can provide reference for the selection of ultra wideband phased array antenna array schemes.

articleTitle: A range and radial velocity measurement method based on up-chirp and down-chirp LFM signal in pulsed radar
abstract: Range accuracy and radial velocity accuracy are important indexes in pulsed radar. However, in pulsed radar using linear frequency modulation (LFM) pulse, the range-Doppler coupling of LFM signal will lead to large range error in high-speed target measurement. The target's radial velocity is computed using range differentiation in traditional method, which is also not accurate. This paper presents a measurement method based on up-chirp and down-chirp LFM signal to get the target's accurate range and radial velocity simultaneously. Experiments confirm that the proposed method outperforms traditional method in both range accuracy and radial velocity accuracy.

articleTitle: Innovative Pol-InSAR model system based on gamma distribution: theoretical unification of several models
abstract: This work unifies several polarimetric synthetic aperture radar interferometry (Pol-InSAR) models in theory based on the newly proposed Gamma form model to better describe forest vertical structure for height inversion. The proposed model system takes forest vertical heterogeneity and asymmetry into account, to which volume interferometric coherence is sensitive. The interferometric coherence associated with a volume where the vertical backscattered power varies following a Gamma distribution is derived. As special cases of Gamma distribution, Pol-InSAR models based on exponential distribution and chi-square distribution are derived, and their freedom degrees are lower than those based on Gamma distribution. Finally, the effect of scattering centre height standard deviation and mean elevation to the volume interferometric coherence is investigated.

articleTitle: Coherence feature modelling for single-baseline Pol-InSAR
abstract: In order to solve the problem that P-band polarimetric interferometric synthetic aperture radar (Pol-InSAR) observation is difficult to be modelled, this paper focuses on the analysis of Pol-InSAR coherence feature, in which polarimetric state is taken into consideration as a variable. To uniquely identify the Pol-InSAR coherence region, coherence feature modelling is carried out. Six parameters are used to determine the shape, direction and position of the coherence region in complex plane. Finally, the potential strategy of single-baseline based on the proposed coherence feature model for forest height inversion using P-band Pol-InSAR data is investigated.

articleTitle: Study on the three dimension imaging methods of fully-polarised array InSAR
abstract: Fully-polarised (FP) array interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (FP-Array-InSAR) is an important technology in three-dimensional (3D) reconstruction and image interpretation of various scattering mechanisms (SMs) by exploiting the structural and polarisation properties of the targets. There has been a solid foundation for multi-baseline PolInSAR, but lack of systematic comparison and analysis for FP-Array-InSAR. Relying on the UAV-borne FP-Array-InSAR system developed by our research team, this paper applies two 3D imaging methods, one based on polarisation decomposition and the other based on multi-baseline (MB) polarimetric coherence optimization, to four-channel FP-array-InSAR datasets from Suzhou, China. Finally, this paper compares and analyses the experimental results of these two methods, and then gives their applicable scenarios. Such comparative experiments are positive for the rational selection and application of different methods in FP-array-InSAR.

articleTitle: End-to-end global segmentation of PolSAR images with data augmentation
abstract: Deep neural networks have demonstrated impressive performance in PolSAR image classification. However, the lack of labelled data and the complexity of land boundaries hindering the mode's ability to achieve high-quality classification results. In order to address these inherent challenges, this paper introduces an augmentation method designed to maximize the utility of available labelled data. Furthermore, we present an end-to-end PolSAR image classification network, which we refer to as PolSARMixer. Our experimental results indicate that our proposed methodology significantly streamlines the classification process for PolSAR images when compared to traditional methods. Moreover, our proposed network exhibits superior performance in terms of classification accuracy and efficiency.

articleTitle: Inshore ship detection using high-resolution SAR images based on multi-feature fusion
abstract: The scattering characteristics of inshore ships in SAR images are similar to those of buildings and other man-made targets on land, making it difficult to detect them. In order to accurately detect the inshore ships in high-resolution SAR images, this paper proposes a multi-feature fusion method. Firstly, coarse sea-land segmentation is achieved by OTSU method and ROI (region of interest) is quickly determined by the maximum stability extremal region (MSER) method. After dividing the ROI into grid slices, the features of candidate targets and their surrounding backgrounds in the ROI are computed. And finally, background resolution (BR) is constructed by feature fusion to distinguish false alarm targets from real targets. Experiments based on satellite-based SAR data show that the method proposed in this paper has good detection accuracy and timeliness.

articleTitle: Steel reinforcement polarization characteristic calibration method based on Alford rotation
abstract: In civil engineering, investigating steel reinforcement defects through polarization characteristics is a critical focus in building safety research. However, some polarization characteristics exhibit variations due to rotation, diminishing disease detection accuracy. Calibrating the polarization characteristics for steel reinforcements with unknown azimuth angles is crucial. Our study introduces a novel method for calibrating steel reinforcement polarization characteristics using fully polarized ground-penetrating radar (FP-GPR) with Alford rotation. Initially, we calculate steel reinforcement azimuth angles with high precision. Then, Alford rotation is applied to fully polarized echoes, correcting them to the standard orientation. Finally, we extract polarization characteristics from the corrected echoes, effectively calibrating steel reinforcement characteristics with unknown azimuth angles. Simulation results show that the proposed method can effectively eliminate the influence of steel reinforcement azimuth angles on the rotation characteristics.

articleTitle: A special type of the passive radar imaging using the self-multipath signals on satellites
abstract: This paper investigates the feasibility of observing the satellite by its own transmitted signals. The system is a special type of the passive radar (PR) using the self-multipath signal (SMS) on satellites. Firstly, the geometry of the SMS-based PR (SMS-PR) is formulated and analysed, and then the direct signals containing self-multipath are modelled. Secondly, the in-pulse matched filtering and the direct-path cancellation are individually considered and corresponding processing algorithms are given. Thirdly, the process algorithms are proposed of the SMS-PR imaging of the satellite, based on the inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR) and the orthogonal matching pursuit (OMP). Finally is the post-processing of the proposed scheme is verified by the simulation results. In addition, the paper analyses also the conditions guaranteeing the successful imaging.

articleTitle: A sparse-based DOA estimation method based on deep learning
abstract: With the rapid advancement of assisted driving and automated driving, there is an increasing urgency for a super-resolution direction of arrival (DOA) estimation method in vehicular sensing systems. In this paper, a high-accuracy DOA estimation algorithm based on deep learning is proposed. The real and imaginary parts of normalized single snapshot received signals are used as the input of the proposed network, which makes the network robust. Different from the other existing DOA estimated network, the output of proposed is a vector, and the spatial spectrum is obtained after a simple transformation, leading to a smoother spatial spectrum and improved accuracy. The simulations are performed to demonstrate its effectiveness, and a frequency-modular continuous wave (FMCW) radar location system is established to validate it in practice.

articleTitle: An improved compressive sensing algorithm based on sparse Bayesian Learning for RFPA radar
abstract: The theory of Compressive Sensing (CS) has garnered significant attention in recent years due to its distinct advantages in mitigating the high sidelobe of Random Frequency and Pulse Repetition Interval Agile (RFPA) radar systems. Especially those CS algorithms based on Sparse Bayesian Learning (SBL), have played a pivotal role in enhancing signal recovery performance. Nevertheless, it is crucial to recognize that these algorithms possess certain limitations for RFPA radar, particularly in scenarios involving closely spaced targets, such as restricted dynamic range for target detection, slow convergence rates, and high computational complexity. To address these issues, this paper presents an improved SBL-based CS algorithm for RFPA radar systems. Specifically, the proposed algorithm enhances signal sparsity through the selection of a prior distribution, thereby improving its capability to detect between weak and strong targets. Additionally, the algorithm combines the Expectation-Maximization (EM) algorithm with a fixed-point update strategy, efficiently utilizing diagonal elements to expedite convergence while reducing computational complexity. Simulation results demonstrate that, in scenarios involving closely spaced targets, the proposed algorithm can effectively mitigate the masking of weak targets by strong target echoes, while exhibiting accelerated convergence with reduced computational overhead.

articleTitle: Translational acceleration compensation of space target via polynomial fitting
abstract: In order to obtain the micro-Doppler information of space targets, the high-speed translational component of radar echoes needs to be compensated accurately. The short-term observation of the space target is used to approximate the uniform acceleration motion, and the echo signal shows the characteristics of the linear frequency modulation signal. The time series of the linear frequency modulation slope of the target echo is estimated by the time segmentation method; Based on this, the variation law of the linear frequency modulation slope of the target echo is obtained by polynomial fitting, and then the high-order phase term compensation of the space target is completed to realize the translation acceleration compensation. Simulation results show the validity of the method proposed.

articleTitle: A fast implementation algorithm of GRFT for coherent integration of high-speed maneuvering targets
abstract: The generalized Radon-Fourier transform (GRFT) is a long-time coherent integration algorithm which is often used in radar detection of high-speed maneuvering targets. The principle of GRFT algorithm is to estimate the motion parameters of the target through multi-dimensional joint search, which can almost achieve the optimal detection performance, but its computation is huge, which is not conducive to the real-time detection of radar. To solve this problem, a fast GRFT implementation method based on genetic algorithm(GA)is proposed in this paper. We first encode the motion parameter set and set the initial population, then update the population iteratively through genetic algorithm, so that it can spontaneously and quickly approach the globa l optimal solution, and finally complete the coherent integration of the target to be detected. The simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A 2-D spectrum reconstruction method for spaceborne sliding-spotlight SAR with BV-PRI
abstract: Spaceborne sliding-spotlight synthetic aperture radar (SAR) can achieve high resolution and wide swath imaging. However, with the improvement of resolution and swath, the range migration of the echo signal is extremely large and the echo signal cannot be received by traditional fixed pulse repetition interval (F-PRI) receiving system effectively. To solve the problem, the block varying pulse repetition interval (BV-PRI) receiving system is designed, but it will lead to non-uniform sampling of echo signals in azimuth, making it impossible to be directly processed by traditional imaging algorithms. Thus, this article proposes a two-dimensional (2-D) spectrum reconstruction method which combines chirp scaling and sub-aperture process for spaceborne sliding-spotlight SAR with BV-PRI. Specifically, the proposed method includes three steps: range alignment, azimuth resampling, and 2-D spectrum recombination. Moreover, the proposed method can reconstruct a uniform 2-D spectrum without azimuth aliasing, and the focusing process can be completed by using traditional imaging algorithms. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is verified by simulation experimental results of point targets.

articleTitle: Design of mismatched filter with good Doppler tolerance via majorization minimization
abstract: The issue of Doppler sensitivity in phase-coded signals is a significant factor that leads to performance degradation in radar detection. To mitigate the sidelobes caused by Doppler shifts, we present an algorithm that converts the optimization problem into a quadratic constrained quadratic programming (QCQP) problem via Majorization Minimization (MM), allowing for solution by analysing the Karush–Kuhn–Tucker (KKT) conditions. The key steps of the algorithm are implemented through Fast Fourier transform (FFT), ensuring efficient computational performance. Numerical results demonstrate that our proposed algorithm outperforms the software-based algorithm in terms of both sidelobe suppression and computational efficiency.

articleTitle: Cramér-Rao bounds of direction-of-arrival estimation for end-fire array airborne radar
abstract: The application of end-fire array (EFA) antennas in airborne radar systems has garnered increasing attention in recent years. Owing to their low-profile design, EFA antennas possess unique advantages, particularly in compact detectors and sensors. This paper mainly study the estimation performance of direction-of-arrival (DOA) for EFA. Firstly, a target detection model for the EFA airborne radar was established. Subsequently, the Cramér-Rao bound (CRB) for parameter estimation under clutter background was derived. Furthermore, closed-form solutions for the CRBs of azimuth and elevation angles, as well as their coupling relationships in a clutter-free environment, are presented. The derivation and simulation results reveal that the CRBs for EFA are dependent on the DOA of the target and increase with the decrease of SNR, the number of array element or the pulses of coherent processing. Compared with conventional side-looking array antenna, EFA can maintain relatively stable DOA estimation performance when the target azimuth angle changes.

articleTitle: Designs of Earth-based Bi-station system combined with radar and radio telescope for PolIn-SAR application in radar astronomy
abstract: Earth-based synthetic aperture radar (SAR) system used for astronomic observation is of merits including large-scale imaging swath, all-day all-weather probing capability, high efficiency, low budget, etc. Beyond that, polarimetric SAR (PolSAR) and interferometric SAR (InSAR) can further expand its use and derive body’s information in polarity and height domain, respectively. Based on available radio facilities of China and/or huge-power radars of north Europe through international cooperation, here we introduce two designs of Bi-station SAR system which can have powerful application of PolIn SAR in radar astronomy, the first one with the transmitter as Qujing incoherent scatter radar (QJISR) and the receiver as five-hundred-meter-aperture spherical telescope (FAST), while the second one with power source of EISCAT 3D radar (E3D) and the receiver as Daocheng Solar Radio Imaging Telescope Array (DSRT). PolSAR can be realized in hybrid-polarity format in which QJISR transmits left-handed circular polarization (LCP) while FAST receives a pair of orthogonal linear polarizations, or E3D transmits a pair of orthogonal polarizations in alternate order, while DSRT receives both polarizations simultaneously. InSAR, on the other hand, can be fulfilled by formation of temporal-spatial baselines with repeat-pass interferometry for the first design or Earth-based radar interferometry for the second design. The imaging of the Moon is given as an example case.

articleTitle: Joint channel estimation and zero-Doppler clutter suppression for passive radar under multiplicative distortions via regularized ECA
abstract: In this paper, we consider the problem of suppressing the zero-Doppler clutters for the passive radar operating under the mul- tiplicative channel. In this scenario, channel distortion leads to the inconsistency between the echo and the reference signal, which deteriorates the performance of the conventional temporal clutter suppression algorithm. In this work, we propose a novel temporal method which can jointly estimate the channel distortion and suppress the zero-Doppler clutter. The proposed method modifies the conventional extended cancellation algorithm (ECA) by imposing two additional regularization items. The proposed optimization problem is non-convex and it is solved by a sequential iteration approach. In particular, we de- compose the original formulation into a smoothing regularization problem, which is for channel estimation, and a ridge re- gression, which is for clutter suppression. A final solution is achieved by iterating between these two regularized regression problems. The numerical results show that the proposed method can effectively estimate the channel distortion and can signif- icantly improve the performance of the clutter suppression compared with the conventional ECA.

articleTitle: Evaluation on extraction methods of tropical cyclone wind direction using SAR imagery
abstract: Refined wind direction extraction of tropical cyclones has been made possible by the development of high-resolution synthetic aperture radar (SAR). However, the accuracy and completeness of the extraction results are constrained by the complex events occurring within tropical cyclones and the weak wind streak characteristics. Based on a dataset of 15 Sentinel-1 tropical cyclone SAR images, this work conducts a comparative analysis of three conventional image processing methods for wind direction extraction, i.e., fast Fourier transform (FFT), local gradient (LG), and wavelet transform (WT). The study also investigates the impact of image resolution, window size, and polarization method on the extraction of wind streaks. Furthermore, the calculation of the percentage of effective wind direction was conducted based on the inflow angle, serving as an initial evaluation criterion. The results indicate that a resolution of about 100m and a window size of 100-150 are more suitable for extracting wind direction. Additionally, the VH-polarized image shows greater potential for wind direction extraction within 100km of tropical cyclones. Despite the optimal performance of the LG method, it fails to capture certain wind directions. Therefore, this paper proposes a multi-method wind direction extraction scheme that is more effective in comprehensively extracting multi-scale wind pattern information.

articleTitle: Analysis on future development demands of remote sensing information processing techniques based on the development of US Missile Defense System
abstract: This paper analyzed the diversifications, frameworks, and capability characteristics of the US Missile Defense System 2.0. For two types of threat targets, ballistic missiles and hypersonic missiles, relevant requirements for remote sensing information processing technology in defense tasks during the flight stages including the boost phase, mid-phase, glide phase, and terminal phase were analyzed. The main technical difficulties were analyzed, and the research results have a certain traction effect on the development of related technologies.

articleTitle: Radar target HRRP segmentation using diffusion model
abstract: High-resolution range profile (HRRP) formed by the extended target under high-resolution radar can reflect the detailed information of the target, which is one of the important means of target detection for air-to-ground radar. Accurately segmenting the target HRRP from the entire echo is of great significance for studying the target characteristics, target feature extraction and recognition. In this paper, a radar target HRRP segmentation algorithm using diffusion model is proposed. The disturbed position parameters of the target HRRP are generated according to the idea of adding noise by the diffusion model, and then the predicted segmentation results are obtained through the trained model to modify the disturbed parameters. The performance of the algorithm under different signal-to-noise ratios and polarization modes is evaluated in a measured dataset. The experimental results show that this method can effectively obtain target HRRPs and can be applied to the extended target segmentation of high-resolution radar.

articleTitle: System sensitivity testing based on L-band differential imterferometric SAR satellite
abstract: System sensitivity is among the critical indicators that impact the imaging quality of the Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) system. To begin, the typical test methods for the Noise Equivalent Sigma Zero (NESZ) are presented and an analysis to ascertain which testing method should be employed are conducted in the paper. Secondly, the proposed calculation method for the NESZ and the specific implementation process of the NESZ testing method are based on the L-band differential interferometric SAR (LuTan-1 SAR) satellite internal calibration mode. Finally, the NESZ is operated using the corresponding strip mode of the L-band SAR, resulting in the acquisition of corresponding test results. The quantitative analysis of the testing results indicate that the method employed in this paper can precisely determine the NESZ value. The L-band SAR system meets the requirements of the NESZ indicators, which can ensure that L-band SAR image has good image quality and high signal-to-noise ratio.

articleTitle: HRRP scattering center estimation based on modelled neural network
abstract: Scattering center estimation of HRRP is crucial for radar automatic target recognition (RATR). Traditional estimation algorithms either necessitate prior information of the signal or suffer from mismatch issues or possess excessive computational costs. In this paper, we propose an HRRP-modelled neural network (HNN), which addresses the mismatch problem and exhibits better accuracy. HNN combines the HRRP signal model with its layered structure, including input, output and activation function. It is initialized via orthogonal matching pursuit and optimized using back propagation algorithm with dual learning rate. The estimated position and amplitude can be obtained by the weights between layers. Through simulations and experiments, we demonstrate the superiority of HNN over traditional methods.

articleTitle: End-to-end radar signal sorting based on semantic segmentation
abstract: This research offers a semantic segmentation network-based signal clustering method to overcome the drawbacks of traditional radar signal sorting algorithms, which mainly rely on manually setup parameters and are limited by algorithm structures. Through this approach, end-to-end radar signal clustering is made possible by removing the aforementioned limits. This process uses the PDW of the combined radar pulses to produce a dot matrix image. DeepLab V3+ semantic segmentation network can be used to achieve pixel clustering. Then map the clustered pixels back to the pulse stream. It is evident from the simulation results that this method works well at clustering signals and maintains strong performance even in environments with pulse loss. Also, our method shows better accuracy when compared to conventional sorting algorithms.

articleTitle: Mainlobe deceptive interference mitigation in EPC-MIMO radar based on covariance matrix reconstruction
abstract: This paper deals with the problem of mainlobe deceptive interference mitigation via interference-plus-noise covariance matrix reconstruction in an element-pulse coding (EPC)-multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) radar. At the modelling stage, the EPC is implemented by introducing the phase coding in transmitted elements and slow-time pulses, which can provide more degrees of freedom (DOFs) in the joint transmit-receive (JTR) spatial domain. Hence, the mainlobe deceptive jammers are suppressed via a data-dependent beamformer based on the minimum variance distortionless response (MVDR) criterion. Furthermore, to solve the problem of training samples selection, a method of interference-plus-noise covariance matrix reconstruction based on sparse Bayesian learning algorithm (SBL) is developed. Numerical simulations are provided to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Combined corner reflector array interference recognition based on improved TCN and DGRU
abstract: Combined corner reflector is an important passive interference faced by radar in sea detection. Combined corner reflector recognition is the key for radar to achieve accurate countermeasures. At present, most combined corner reflector recognition methods rely on explicit feature extraction with physical connotations. For complex targets under the condition of low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), explicit features often cannot cover the full attitude when the number of samples is severely limited, resulting in a decrease in recognition accuracy. This paper proposes a combined corner reflector array interference recognition method based on improved Temporal Convolution Network (iTCN) and double-Gate Recurrent Unit (DGRU). TCN is used to improve the ability to extract deep features of the High Resolution Range Profile (HRRP) sequence. Improving the original activation layer structure and using the Swish activation function to place the activation layer in front of the weight layer, which provides greater nonlinear mapping capabilities for data, thus improving the anti-noise capability of the network. Combined with the DGRU network, deep and implicit features of HRRP sequence are extracted to make full use of ship attitude invariance. Experiments show that this model is capable for identifying combined corner reflector array interference under small samples and low SNR.

articleTitle: Low sidelobe pattern synthesis for airborne distributed coherent active phased array radar
abstract: Airborne distributed coherent active phased array radar can form a large aperture by combining multiple radar echoes scattered in the whole area of the aircraft, which can greatly improve the detection performance compared with the traditiona l single aperture radar. However, the array manifold of distributed coherent radar is complicated due to the influence of 3 - dimensional shadowing and array element anisotropy, which results in the traditional beamformer for the planar array is no longer applicable. Therefore, this paper proposes a beampattern synthesis algorithm that does not require specifying a lobe - level-mask and enables the optimization of array elements in terms of number and position. Numerical examples show that the proposed algorithm can attain a lower peak sidelobe level than the traditional beamformer.

articleTitle: Research on radar recognition technology for UAV target in migratory birds background
abstract: In recent years, the unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) has emerged as a significant risk factor in the field of low-altitude safety. Radar technology plays a crucial role in the detection of UAV within low-altitude airspace. During radar detection, avian targets, particularly migratory birds, share similarities with UAV in terms of flight characteristics, such as flight altitude, flight speed, course stability, radar cross-section, making it very difficult to distinguish UAV target from bird targets. In this paper, the flight mechanisms of UAV and migratory birds are analyzed, and a spatial migration intensity perception algorithm based on the trajectory is proposed. The target flight characteristics and spatial correlation characteristics are extracted from recent and historical radar trajectory data. The results of spatial migration intensity perception are combined with various trajectory characteristics, and five machine learning algorithms are used to realize the accurate recognition of UAV targets and birds. Finally, the effectiveness of the algorithm is verified by experimental data.

articleTitle: An autofocus framework based on combination of parametric and nonparametric methods for stripmap SAR
abstract: The autofocus algorithm is crucial in SAR imaging. However, it always become difficult when phase error reflects two-dimensional space-variance property. In this paper, a robust two-dimensional space-variant autofocus framework is proposed to improve the imaging performance of the stripmap SAR. This proposed autofocus framework based on combination of parametric and nonparametric autofocus methods. Firstly, the combined sub-blocks minimum entropy algorithm based on weighted least squares (WLS-CS-MEA) is proposed to estimate the range-variant phase error (RVPE) in the azimuth time domain before azimuth compression. Subsequently, the azimuth compressed SAR image is divided into several azimuth sub-images to eliminate the azimuth-variant phase error (AVPE). By introducing the Deskew function and azimuth window in the sub-image, the phase errors of different azimuth targets are aligned and can be estimated and compensated uniformly by the phase gradient autofocus (PGA) algorithm. The proposed autofocus framework can be applied to the stripmap SAR, and real measured data is employed to verify its effectiveness.

articleTitle: The UAV remote sensing vehicle tracking based on improved fairmot
abstract: Multi-object tracking (MOT) is an important problem in Earth-observation remote sensing task and has wide application. In recent years, UAV has been widely used in middle to high altitude remote sensing observation tasks, undertaking various tasks such as object detection and tracking, natural disaster monitoring and so on. The application of multi-object tracking to UAV platform has become one of the research trends. In this paper, a vehicle tracking algorithm based on UAV platform is proposed. In view of the size conflict between the network and the input image, bilinear interpolation method is adopted to resize the image and evaluate the loss. UAVDT dataset is used to train the algorithm and evaluate the model, thus achieving high-precision detection and tracking. At the same time, it has a high processing speed and achieves near-real-time performance.

articleTitle: Behavior state recognition of complex wingbeat patterns targets based on Bi-LSTM
abstract: Radar serves as a crucial tool for observing airborne biological targets, with wingbeat frequency being a vital parameter for distinguishing between different species of organisms. The wingbeat patterns of airborne biological targets are diverse. To improve the extraction of wingbeat frequencies from radar signals, it is necessary to identify the behavioral states of different wingbeat patterns and eliminate signals that cannot be used for wingbeat extraction. This paper presents an intelligent recognition algorithm based on wingbeat pattern behavioral states. Firstly, Doppler frequency modeling is performed on wingbeat pattern targets, and then simulated data is input into a Bi-LSTM network for pattern recognition training. Finally, the algorithm's performance is validated using field radar measurements after performing short-time Fourier transformation on the measured data. The validation results based on radar experimental data indicate that this algorithm can effectively recognize wingbeat pattern behavioral states.

articleTitle: Efficient multi-parameter estimation based on the reduced-dimension beam of vehicle radar
abstract: To Improve the performance of angle estimation and obtain efficient super-resolution for joint distance and velocity estimation, a joint multi-parameter estimation based on the reduced-dimension beamspace of vehicle radar is proposed. The proposed algorithm is implemented by the extended aperture of sparse arrays for the improved performance of angle estimation. The two-dimensional data in the space-time domain are converted into the frequency domain by fast Fourier transform, and the fast joint estimation of distance and velocity is achieved by a subspace-based approach with the equivalence of beamspace transform. Simulation results show that with greatly reduced computational complexity, the proposed method has both better estimation accuracy and high multi-parameter resolution.

articleTitle: Comparative analysis of reflectivity factors between GPM spaceborne dual-frequency precipitiation radar and S-band radar
abstract: The consistency of reflectivity factor data is compared and analyzed by using GPM satellite-borne dual-frequency precipitation radar data and Xiangtan S-band dual-polarization radar data. The accuracy of matching data is improved by geometric matching method. The comparison results of a precipitation process on February 9, 2023 show that the standard deviation of reflectivity factors between S-band dual-polarization radar and GPM satellite is 4.48dBZ, and the average deviation is 0.67dBZ, which indicates that the reflectivity factors of the two radars are in good consistency.

articleTitle: SAR two-dimensional beam scheduling method for azimuth large angle scanning
abstract: Spaceborne synthetic aperture radar achieve azimuth ultra-high resolution by scanning a large angle in the azimuth direction. Due to the influence of satellite orbit and earth curvature, beams on the ground will appear curved and offset and the shape of the belt will cause distortion when the radar beam azimuth scan angle is too large. It will bring difficulties to subsequent imaging processing at the same time. To get a continuous and straight observation band, the radar also needs to adjust the beam angle in the range direction when in the process of work. That means the two-dimensional beam scheduling at the same time. This paper analyzes the offset of the observation band of the radar in the case of azimuth large angle scanning. A two-dimensional beam scheduling method based on rotation center pushback is proposed. The effectiveness of the method is verified by simulation. The conclusions of this paper can provide reference for beam scheduling of high resolution imaging SAR.

articleTitle: Correlation analysis of entropy and scanning performance based on irregular subarray design
abstract: In this paper, the correlation between the information entropy value and scanning performance of polyomino subarray tiling is demonstrated. Firstly, the information entropy values and sidelobe level (SLL) of different tiling schemes via different scanning angles have been calculated. Then, a modified entropy calculating model is proposed to establish more accurate connection. Taking different tiling schemes of L-shaped octomino and Pistol-shaped subarrays as examples, the scanning performance and tiling entropy values are analyzed for reference. Numerical experiments are carried out to prove the positive correlation of modified entropy and scanning radiation performance.

articleTitle: Monitoring and analysis of landslide hazards in the Miaowei Reservoir area of the Lancang River based on time series InSAR technology
abstract: Reservoir projects are mostly located in mountainous and canyon areas, and often encounter problems with bank slope stability. Once a landslide occurs, it will cause great harm. To strengthen the monitoring and evaluation of potential landsl ides in the Miaowei Reservoir area of the Lancang River, this study uses 70 Sentinel-1A images from January, 2019 to December, 2021, and uses SBAS-InSAR technology to obtain deformation information in the Miaowei Reservoir area of the Lancang River. Combining multiple types of data such as geology, geomorphology, precipitation, etc., the identification and monitoring of landslide hazard points in the Miaowei Reservoir area of the Lancang River were studied. The study results indicate that a total of three potential landslide hazards have been identified in the Miaowei Reservoir area of the Lancang River, and the annual average subsidence rate of the study area during the study period ranges from -55.2 to 60.7mm/year. In addition, the study results provide data support and targeted governance suggestions for the monitoring of landslide hazard points in the study area.

articleTitle: Inverse synthetic aperture radar imaging of space target by using alternating direction method of multipliers
abstract: The compressive sensing (CS) based Inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR) imaging methods can obtain a good image using much less data as compared to the conventional ISAR imaging methods. The ISAR space target image can be reconstructed by solving a l1-minimization problem using greedy iteration strategies or convex optimization methods under the assumption that the target scene is sparse in a certain domain. Alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) is an efficient optimization algorithm for signal recovery with the superior convergence properties. In this paper, we present an ADMM based ISAR imaging method in the framework of CS. ADMM can decompose the l1-minimization problem of ISAR image reconstruction into several sub-problems and solve them alternately by dual-ascent strategy. We use the simulation data to demonstrate the performance of the ADMM based CS ISAR imaging method. The results show that the proposed ADMM based ISAR imaging method outperforms the state-of-the-art CS ISAR imaging methods in both image quality and computational efficiency.

articleTitle: High resolution ISAR imaging based on 2D-FMFSBL-net
abstract: In this article, a deep unfolded network, named 2D-FMFSBL-Net, is proposed for high resolution ISAR imaging. Firstly, the ISAR sparse observation model is established. Then the complex-valued 2D fast mean field sparse Bayesian learning(2D-FMFSBL) is derived to solve the model, and the iterative procedure of which is unrolled into a deep network, where all the adjustable parameters are learned through back-propagation. Since the optimal parameters of each layer can be learned separately, the proposed method exhibits more flexibility and achieves well-focused ISAR imaging with a shallow network. Experimental results on simulated and measured data demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in incomplete data and low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) scenarios.

articleTitle: Effective HRRP data augmentation by contrastive adversarial training
abstract: Recently, deep learning methods have significantly improved the recognition performance of high-resolution range profiles (HRRP). However, these methods often assume the availability of sufficient HRRP data, which is challenging in real-world applications, particularly for uncooperative targets. As a result, existing deep learning based HRRP recognition algorithms experience a significant drop in performance due to the limited availability of training data. To augment insufficient HRRP data, this paper proposes a solution by utilizing adversarial samples generated through a contrastive adversarial training algorithm (CAT), in order to augment the training data. Additionally, a diversity-based data transformation strategy (Dts) is introduced to enhance the effectiveness of the augmented data. The experimental results demonstrates that the proposed method is able to improve recognition performance after augmentation. The work presented in this paper provides an important advancement towards improving the reliability of deep learning-based radar recognition systems, particularly in scenarios were obtaining sufficient HRRP data is challenging.

articleTitle: A method for velocity estimation of moving targets based on multi-angle SAR image sequences
abstract: Multi-angle Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) is a new SAR working mode to acquire multi-dimensional information of target. By observing the target area from different observation angles, the multi-angle SAR has the ability to acquire moving target information. This paper constructs a multi-angle SAR moving target observation signal model, derives a method for estimating the speed of a moving target based on the SAR image acquired from forward and backward observation, and obtains the target azimuthal and radial speeds using this method. The validity of this method is verified through simulation experiment, and it can be used to accurately estimate the speed of moving targets.

articleTitle: Parallel FPGA-based processing for improved infrared target detection using VMD and SPWVD
abstract: Infrared sensors are widely used in target detection due to their small size and low cost. But the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) is very low and the range of action is short. In order to increase the probability of detecting a specific target, noise must be more thoroughly suppressed and signal features must be extracted more accurately. Algorithms such as variational mode decomposition (VMD) and smoothed pseudo-Wegener distribution (SPWVD) that have emerged in recent years can be used to solve this problem. VMD works well in suppressing noise in non-stationary and non-linear signals. SPWVD has high time-frequency resolution and clean spectra. However, infrared detection requires high real-time performance, so these methods are limited in use due to the large amount of calculation. This article builds a highly parallel processing system based on FPGA and introduces VMD and SPWVD into the scene of real-time infrared detection of moving targets. It meets real-time requirements while greatly improving detection accuracy.

articleTitle: A novel unscented particle filter for joint tracking and classification of maneuvering target
abstract: In order to solve the issue of low tracking accuracy and poor classification precision due to non-Gaussian noise and nonlinearity in the system when applying particle filter, in this paper, we propose an interactive multiple model unscented particle filter based on Kullback-Leibler distance (KLD) resampling improvement for joint tracking and classification of maneuvering targets. First, we apply unscented particle filter to the multiple model filtering process to reduce the effect of model switching noise. Second, to address the issue of computational complexity due to the application of UPF, we apply KLD sampling to adaptively determine the number of particles required at each iteration step, which reduces the computational amount of the algorithm. Simulation experiments demonstrate that the IMMKLUPF-JTC algorithm proposed in this paper can accurately track and classify maneuvering targets.

articleTitle: Clutter and interference cognitive suppression based on transmitter optimization
abstract: This paper employs a fast phase-only nullification algorithm to suppress strong clutter and interference, particularly in the sidelobes. In the presence of relative motion between ground clutter and the airborne radar, Doppler shifts are introduced, potentially masking weak targets. To address the challenge of clutter suppression, which is challenging to accomplish solely at the receiver end for backscatter clutter, the paper introduces pre-processing for clutter scene perception, with the removal of the main clutter component. Subsequently, optimization is applied at the transmitting end to create nulls in the direction of strong backscatter sidelobes and interference sources. The results are then subjected to space-time adaptive processing (STAP) to mitigate the adverse impact of strong scatterers and interference on target detection, improve the signal-to-clutter-plus-noise ratio(SCNR), and achieve low probability of intercept.

articleTitle: Transmission coefficients elimination for amplitude-only REV method in phased array calibration
abstract: The error of each channel at the probe can be solved by using the amplitude-only rotating electric vector (AOREV) method. However, since the transmission coefficients (TCs) between the probe and different antenna elements are different and unknown, the error of each channel at the antenna element cannot be determined.
