In this work, a transmission coefficient elimination technique is proposed for the AOREV method. It eliminates the TCs by forming two equations for each channel using the results obtained from AOREV method, so that the error of each channel at antenna element can be determined. The technique does not require any additional measurements. Simulated results show that, after eliminating the TCs by using the proposed technique, the errors of the channels at the antenna elements are below 0.2 dB (amplitude) and 2◦ (phase), respectively. Experimental results also confirm the proposed technique.

articleTitle: Data-dependent channel selection method for STAP based on MVDR criterion
abstract: Space-time adaptive processing (STAP) combines the returned signals from all elements of an antenna array and all coherent pulse trains during a CPI period to provide clutter suppression and target detection ability, which is a promising technique for acquiring small, slow, and moving targets. In this work, we proceed to the data-dependent channel selection method for Post- Doppler beam- space STAP to improve clutter suppression performance in sample starved environments, in which no additional a prior information is used in our framework. The main innovation of this manuscript lies in the characteristic th at the selected channels in the fully-dimension weight vector, which is inversely transformed from the RD weight vector, is sparse relative to the whole beam-Doppler channels. Compared with several existing methods, the proposed method significantly enhances the STAP performance in sample starved environments.

articleTitle: FDA radar transmit power allocation based on the Q_learning algorithm in spectrum-dense scenarios
abstract: The Frequency diversity arrays (FDA) radar has many new properties due to the frequency increment of its array elements, including its ability for flexible spectrum control through transmit power allocation. Under the assumption of spectrum density scenario, this paper proposes a narrowband spectrum jamming suppression method based on FDA radar transmit power allocation so that the radar system can maximize SINR while entirely using spectrum resources. By introducing the reinforcement learning framework, an interaction model between radar and the electromagnetic environment based on the Q_learning algorithm is established so that radar can sense and suppress jamming in the interaction process with the electromagnetic environment. Finally, simulation results confirm that the proposed algorithm can distribute the transmitted power, realize jamming suppression, and improve the radar performance.

articleTitle: Analysis of sea surface velocity vector inversion error based on multi-static ATI-SAR
abstract: Multi-static ATI SAR has significant potential for measuring sea surface velocity vectors. The system comprises one signal-transmitting satellite and two ATI signal-receiving satellites, with a substantial baseline between the receiving satellites and the transmitting satellite. This paper analyzes the accuracy of measuring sea surface velocity vectors using a multi-static spaceborne ATI SAR system, encompassing both velocity and direction measurements. To begin, we revisit the principles of sea surface velocity measurement based on the interferometric SAR's observation geometry to identify potential sources of error in the inversion of the sea surface current field. Subsequently, we derive formulas to quantify the impact of two types of errors: random errors and systematic errors, on the accuracy of vector inversion. Finally, we elucidate the satellite system requirements for multi-static ATI systems by utilizing a set of system parameters.

articleTitle: A receiving coherence method of airborne distributed radar based on joint search of strong scattering points
abstract: During ground target detection by airborne distributed radar, the received echoes are often inundated with a multitude of clutter signals. This saturation of clutter can lead to the confusion or even the masking of the target signal, significantly undermining the system's reception coherence performance. In response to this challenge, a novel receiving coherence method based on the joint identification of multiple scattering points is introduced.The method compensates for the time and phase synchronization errors between radars, distinguishes strong scattering points from ground clutter through two-dimensional imaging, and then uses the scattering point positions are coherently synthesized to achieve coherent reception of airborne distributed radar. The effectiveness of this method has been substantiated through simulations and practical experiments, showcasing its utility in improving the radar system's performance in scenarios characterized by the presence of strong ground clutter.

articleTitle: A model compression method based on multi-teacher distillation for SAR scene classification
abstract: In recent years, with the advancement of deep learning, convolutional neural networks tailored for processing image content have gained increasing attention within the remote sensing imagery domain. However, deep convolutional neural networks that exhibit exceptional performance often encompass a substantial number of parameters, thereby necessitating heightened computational resources and time for network training and prediction. Given the constraints posed by resource limitations in the realm of remote sensing, deploying such high-performance networks onto these devices becomes a challenging endeavor. To address this set of challenges, this paper introduces a methodology grounded in target differential probability for multi - teacher knowledge distillation. This approach effectively reduces the model's complexity while preserving the network models' commendable performance. By conducting a statistical analysis of the model's output probability distribution and computing the differential probabilities between teacher and student networks, we regulate the output pro portions of teachers within the multi-teacher model. As a result, a high-performing student network is cultivated. In aggregate, experimental validation on two distinct datasets substantiates the efficacy of this approach in facilitating efficient knowledge transfer, consequently yielding heightened performance outcomes.

articleTitle: The adaptive imaging of ocean scene based on high-resolution SAR sub-look analysis
abstract: This paper proposed an adaptive imaging algorithm for ocean scene based on both sub-look cross correlation and sub-look coherent entropy. The advantage of this algorithm is to improve the target signal-to-noise ratio and eliminate the influence of azimuth ambiguity through sub-look analysis indicators, thereby improving the SAR image quality of the ocean background. Sub-look analysis is a technique based on splitting a full synthetic aperture into two or more sub-apertures covering a short portion of Doppler bandwidth. Based on the analysis of measured data, a segmentation strategy is proposed in two-dimensional feature space to divide the sea surface into clutter, target and interference. Then, different reprocessing strategies are adopted for different signals. Images of GF-3 satellite UFS mode are utilized to verify the algorithm. The result shows good improvement of image quality. The azimuth ambiguity signal is greatly suppressed after adaptive imaging process, and the SCR of ship remains the same or slightly increases. In addition, the azimuth resolution is almost unaffected.

articleTitle: Quality validation of L-band SAR imagery based on point and distributed targets
abstract: The LT-1 marks a significant milestone as China L-band differential interferometric detection satellite, which has five Stripmap imaging mode with different resolutions, swath widths and polarization. For LT-1 SAR satellites, obtaining high-quality images is a prerequisite for applications in various industries and fields. This article conducts image quality validation of STRIP1 mode by point target and distributed target. More specifically, the initial step involves analysing the impulse response function (IRF) of corner reflectors in Xinjiang Hami calibration site. The IRF can reflect the response characteristics of the SAR system and the performance of the imaging algorithm. Then, the relative radiometric accuracy and elevation antenna pattern of LT1 were analysed using rainforest single look complex (SLC) data. The Amazon rainforest as a uniform distribution target can effectively reflect the quality of satellite radiometric quality. The experimental results indicate that the LT-1 satellite meets the expected design specifications in terms of resolution, sidelobe level and radiation accuracy. This confirms that the LT-1 satellite possesses a high-quality imaging capability, which will be a foundation for various applications.

articleTitle: Quantization analysis of frequency diverse arrays based on symmetric logarithms frequency offset
abstract: There is a difference between the ideal transmit frequency of the frequency diversity array and the frequency generated by the frequency generator, which will definitely make the performance indicators of the actual transmit beam deviate from the theoretically designed performance indicators. In this paper, a quantization strategy is adopted for the transmitter frequency offsets to simulate the actual frequency generated by the frequency generator, and on this basis, a small random frequency error is introduced to simulate the transmitter frequency perturbation, and then the effects of different quantization strategies on the antenna pattern are analyzed. Finally, the effectiveness of the analysis is verified by simulation.

articleTitle: Detection and resolution of UAV swarms based on KT and ANM
abstract: The unmanned aerial vehicle swarms are difficult to detect and distinguish given the weak signals, time-varying motion, and being too dense. In order to solve the problem, this paper proposes a target detection and resolution method based on a combination of keystone transform (KT) and atomic norm minimizeation (ANM). First, the KT based-algorithm is used to improve the signal-to-noise ratio of the target, and then the ANM is used to super-resolve the detected target. Compared with traditional accumulation methods and super-resolution methods, this method has better robustness and higher resolution. The subsequent simulation experiments verified the effectiveness of this method.

articleTitle: Interference mitigation method of automotive radar based on HF-S-LFM waveform
abstract: In light of the proliferation of Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS), 77GHz millimeter-wave automotive radars have become increasingly widespread, leading to a significant increase in the probability of mutual interference between radars. This paper proposes an agile radar waveform with strong ranging interference mitigation capability. Specifically, the waveform employs a sequence of Hopping Frequency Split-Frame Linear Frequency Modulation (HF-S-LFM) pulse signals. HF-S-LFM refers to the pulse signal where a frame of LFM signal is partitioned into multiple narrowband signals and transmitted in a randomized sequence. Employing the De-Chirping Time-Domain Wideband Synthesis (DTWS) algorithm, we synthesize the HF-S-LFM signals into a frame LFM signal, preserving inherent distance resolution characteristics. Theoretical analysis and simulations demonstrate that the HF-S-LFM waveform substantially enhances the anti-jamming capability of automotive radar. Under simulated conditions, the signal-to-interference ratio gain achieved is 19 dB with ten segments. Importantly, DTWS processing ensures that the ranging capabilities approximate those of original LFM signal while maintaining robust interference mitigation.

articleTitle: Gaussian distribution representation based knowledge distillation method for oriented SAR ship detection
abstract: In the Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) images, ship targets are usually arranged in arbitrary directions and have large aspect ratio. To address the sensitivity problem of localization precision to rotation angle affected by aspect ratio and output accurate prediction, we propose a knowledge distillation method based on Gaussian distribution representation for oriented object detection. By minimizing the Kullback-Leibler divergence between the Gaussian distributions of the student and teacher model output coordinates, adaptive optimization of angle parameter to the aspect ratio is achieved, and missed detection caused by inaccurate angle prediction can be reduced. Experiments on publicly available SAR ship detection dataset RSDD-SAR and SSDD demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method compared with existing state-of-the-art distillation methods.

articleTitle: Large-range and high-resolution 3-D and 4-D SAR imaging-the case study of Shanghai
abstract: The evolution of synthetic aperture radar (SAR) has given rise to tomographic synthetic aperture radar (TomoSAR), which integrates the synthetic aperture principle in the elevation direction to produce high-resolution three-dimensional images of architectural targets. This paper advances the discussion by introducing differential tomographic synthetic aperture radar (D-TomoSAR), a methodology that incorporates the synthetic aperture into the time dimension, thus enabling the acquisition of deformation information and facilitating the realization of four-dimensional imaging of urban structures. The employment of compressive sensing (CS) technology significantly refines the results of four-dimensional TomoSAR imaging, as elucidated in this paper. We applied TerraSAR-X complex image data for both TomoSAR and D-TomoSAR to achieve 3-D and 4-D imaging. A comprehensive exploration of the Pudong urban area in Shanghai exemplifies the ability to generate high-resolution 3-D and 4-D SAR images and substantiates the efficacy of this approach.

articleTitle: A novel range and azimuth scaling transform for squint spotlight SAR imaging with dechirp-on-receive
abstract: In this paper, a novel imaging algorithm of range and azimuth scaling transform (RAST) is proposed for squint spotlight synthetic aperture radar (SAR) with dechirp-on-receive. First, based on the planar wavefront assumption, a modified range linear scaling transform (MRLST) and an azimuth scaling transform (AST) are proposed to eliminate the coupling between range time and azimuth time. In addition, principle of chirp scaling (PCS) is used to implement MRLST to increase efficiency, which only involves complex multiplication and fast Fourier transforms (FFTs) and avoids interpolation operations. Meanwhile, a scaling factor is defined to adjust the range resampling interval, and a selection criteria of the scaling factor is formulated to avoid the possible aliasing of the range spectrum caused by PCS. Finally, point target simulation validates the algorithm.

articleTitle: Monitoring deformation of Baihetan hydropower station before and after reservoir impoundment by using TCP-InSAR technology
abstract: The Baihetan Hydropower Station, ranking as China's second-largest hydroelectric facility, deformation monitoring is very important for the operational safety of the reservoir. This study employs TCP-InSAR technology to extract ground deformations of about 100km² area, centered around the core of the dam, by using Sentiel-1 SAR images. The results show that there is no deformation at the dam body, however, a subsidence area along the east bank, and uplift area along the west bank of the reservoir are found, which are probably related to the impoundment of reservoir during the early of 2021.

articleTitle: SiamSTO: a novel method for object tracking with satellite videos
abstract: Object tracking algorithms have been widely applied to remote sensing systems, such as radar, sonar, and satellite. For satellite video tracking, traditional methods cannot capture high-quality features in case of small objects and tend to be unstable due to background interference. In this study, we propose a novel network, named as SiamSTO, for satellite video tracking by synchronously online and offline learning. First, a space-to-depth feature extraction network (SDN) is designed to reduce the loss of spatial information especially for small objects tracking. Then, an offline learning branch based on a Transformer-based information interaction (TFI) module is embedded in this SDN to enhance target-to-background discrimination. Furthermore, to overcome the limitation of the offline learning branch that it only utilizes the target region of the initial frame, the proposed method incorporates an online learning mechanism. This online learning mechanism is capable of extracting dynamic information from both the object and the background regions to acquire more discriminative representation. Hence, the proposed algorithm enhances the tracking performance on condition of severe background interference. Experimental results on the SatSOT dataset validate that the novel SiamSTO algorithm achieves state-of-the-art performance on satellite video tracking.

articleTitle: Passive anti-jamming decision-making based on deep reinforcement learning
abstract: Applying reinforcement learning to the selection of anti-jamming measures in multi-processing domains is an extremely attractive solution. However, current research mainly focuses on design of network optimization, with insufficient attention paid to the rational construction of scenarios, making it difficult to achieve engineering implementation. This paper aims to addr ess this issue by adding jamming parameter information to the discrete space of jamming state and expanding it into a continuous state space, which is in line with the influencing factors of anti-jamming measures. On this basis, based on the radar signal processing process, an anti-jamming index with target detection performance is designed, which is suitable for practical application scenarios. Simulation shows that compared to traditional manual anti-jamming strategies, the proposed method greatly improves the accuracy of selecting anti-jamming measures and analyzes the main factors that affect the accuracy.

articleTitle: DRFM-based repeater jamming cognition method based on ResNet with channel-attention mechanism
abstract: With the development of electronic countermeasure (ECM) technology, various kinds of digital radio frequency memory (DRFM)-based repeater jamming have been proposed, resulting in great influence on radar detection, localization and tracking. It is hard to obtain sufficient jamming samples, which brings difficulties to the jamming cognition. To solve this issue, a DRFM-based repeater jamming cognition method based on ResNet with channel-attention mechanism is proposed. In the proposed method, short-time Fourier transform (STFT) is utilized to generate the time-frequency maps of DRFM-based repeater jamming. Then, the 2D-wavelet transform is used to decompose the time-frequency maps and extract the texture feature. Moreover, the ResNet blocks with channel-attention mechanism are utilized to enhance the non-linear fitting ability of the network under small sample learning situation. Several simulations are conducted to illustrate that the proposed method achieves a higher classification accuracy for DRFM-based repeater jamming.

articleTitle: Sequential SAR images target detection based on SSD and 3D convolutional LSTM
abstract: Target detection is always a hot topic in Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) image interpretation. However, most of the current SAR target detection methods only use single-frame image for detection and can’t consider the time dimension of images, resulting in low accuracy of moving target detection. To solve this problem, this paper proposes a sequential SAR target detection method based on Single Shot Multibox Detector (SSD) and spatial-temporal feature fusion. Under the SSD framework, 3D convolutional LSTM network(3D-LSTM) is used to extract the temporal and spatial features of sequential SAR images. 3D-Convolution and self-attention mechanism are integrated into the 3D-LSTM memory unit, which can capture short-term and long-term motion information in space and time dimensions. The model is evaluated on the measured vehicle SAR image dataset. The experimental results prove that the proposed method can improve the SAR image target detection accuracy, solve the problems of missed and false detection.

articleTitle: A novel unsupervised anti-intermittent sampling jamming method for intra-pulse and inter-pulse frequency agile radar
abstract: The intermittent sampling jamming can generate several false targets with high flexibility and fidelity, posing a great threat on the effectiveness of the traditional anti-jamming methods, such as inter-pulse frequency agile radar. In order to improve radar’s ability to counter intermittent sampling jamming, the intra-pulse and inter-pulse frequency agile radar waveform is adopted in this paper since the sub pulses can cover each other. After receiving the radar echoes, the sub pulses can be obtained by setting narrow band filters. Considering there may be different types of intermittent sampling jamming in reality, the Hierarchical Density-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise (HDBSCAN) algorithm is utilized to figure out the sub pulses containing jamming. Due to its high adaptability, the algorithm is effective in the situation containing different jamming types. Instead of abandoning all the sub pulse echoes with jamming, a jamming suppression method based on the histogram-based contrast (HC) algorithm is proposed. In the proposed method, the jamming signals will be detected and suppressed in the time-frequency domain without loss of target information. Both the HDBSCAN and HC algorithms are unsupervised. The simulation experiments in typical scenarios indicate the validation of the method.

articleTitle: Estimation method of direction of departure via constant modulus constraint on multicarrier signal
abstract: Aiming at the problems of complicated installation and calibration, high power consumption and high cost in the current multi-antenna array device for measuring radio direction of arrival, this paper proposes a multi-carrier departure direction finding method with constant modulus constraints, which only uses one omni-directional receiving antenna to receive signals, and two omni-directional transmitting antennas simultaneously transmit multi-carrier signals, and extracts the departure direction from the constant modulus constraints of carrier frequency and amplitude of transmitted signals and received signals. The experimental results show that the standard deviation of the departure direction measured by the method proposed in this paper is 0.3673 degrees when the ratio of carrier power to noise power spectral density of a receiving antenna is 24dB.

articleTitle: Effective detection and localization of small maneuvering UAV swarm via coherent FDA radar
abstract: Detection and localization of unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) swarm are of great significance in industrial manufacture and critical aerial defense. It is a challenge for accurate detection and localization of UAV swarm, due to its characteristics of high spatial density, low altitude, small radar cross section (RCS) and high maneuverability. To address these issues, we propose an effective solution, which jointly considers the advanced radar system and signal processing strategies. Combining coherent frequency diverse array (FDA) radar and sparse representation, an accurate UAV swarm detection and localization method is proposed in this paper. Coherent FDA radar takes the advantages of wide spatial coverage and high angular resolution, which provides better performance in UAV swarm observation. Furthermore, a long-time coherent integration (LTCI) method based on Bayesian compressive sensing (BCS) technique is proposed to improve the received signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) in detection. To address the high spatial density problem, the BCS-based super-resolution is proposed to localize multiple UAV targets in a single discrimination unit. Numerical simulations validate the effectiveness and advantages of the proposed method in UAV swarm detection and localization.

articleTitle: A silicon-based frequency reconfigurable antenna design based on PINIP diodes
abstract: A silicon based frequency reconfigurable antenna is designed based on the solid plasma device PINIP diode, which uses a PINIP diode array instead of metal as the radiation part. By controlling the number of units in the PINIP diode array, the antenna can achieve frequency reconfigurability in four modes: 29.4 GHz, 22 GHz, 20.3 GHz, and 18.7 GHz. The overall antenna design is on a SOI silicon substrate and has been processed, providing a feasible solution for the high integration and miniaturization of silicon based solid plasma reconfigurable antennas.

articleTitle: An improved forward-backward spatial smoothing MUSIC algorithm for coherent signal direction finding
abstract: DOA estimation is an important technique in the field of radar. Traditional estimation algorithms often struggle with scenarios involving a significant number of coherent signals, making it difficult to identify the true signal. Therefore, we proposed an improved forward and backward spatial smoothing algorithm in covariance matrix estimation for performance improvement in coherent signal direction finding scenarios. Unlike other traditional methods, our algorithm generates an equivalent spatial smoothing matrix by performing weighted averaging of autocorrelation matrices, leveraging the inherent spatial correlation in the data to achieve more accurate parameter estimation and enhances the resolution of coherent signals. Our algorithm holds significant value across various engineering applications, such as radar angle estimation and passive radar localization. Experimental results show that our algorithm outperforms existing methods in terms of estimation success probability and RMSE. At a 6dB SNR, the RMSE is 0.2, and the estimation success probability reaches approximately 90%. Importantly, our algorithm maintains the lowest RMSE across different number of snapshots.

articleTitle: A multi-core image acquisition and storage system with low-light enhancement
abstract: This paper designs and implements an image acquisition and storage system based on the Feiteng processor FT2000/4, which includes five stages: acquisition, processing, compression, storage, and display: Real-time image acquisition through the USB camera, low-light enhancement processing of the captured image, storage of the captured image in the hard disk using JPEG compression coding, reading the image file, decoding and output to the monitor. The system software algorithms use pipelining and Ping-Pong caching methods to significantly optimize system processing speed. As tested, the total time for computing 500 frames of images using a multi-core five-stage pipeline is 8.139658s, with a processing speed of about 61.4fps, which is 3.12 times faster than that of single-core processing. This system achieves efficient operation of image acquisition and storage in the Feiteng processor, optimizes the performance of embedded real-time image acquisition and storage display, and has practical use value.

articleTitle: Elimination of ionospheric phase in SAR interferometry with deep convolutional neural network
abstract: Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR) technology has been widely used in land surface deformation monitoring due to its advantages including wide coverage, high spatial resolution, all-weather, all-day, and high precision. However, the interferogram will contain residual ionospheric phase in the process of InSAR, which can reduce the accuracy of elevation measurement results and even mask the deformation measurement results, especially at L-band frequencies. In this article, we proposed a standard supervised-trained method, which is based on a deep residual U-shaped network, to eliminate residual ionospheric phase. And the proposed method is evaluated on the computer simulation.

articleTitle: Improved axis rotation information geometry algorithm for high-speed time-varying target detection
abstract: Multiple pulse integration is an important and efficient method for weak target detection. However, if the target velocity is high enough, the received multiple-pulse signal will suffer from range migration. If the target character changes during the integration time, the integrated signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) will significantly reduce, and the detection performance of the weak target will be affected. In this article, a correction-detection algorithm for high-speed time-varying targets is proposed, based on the improved axis rotation method (IAR) and an information geometric detection method (IG). The detection method is a generalized constant false alarm rate method based on the metric on the Riemannian manifold of Hermitian positive-definite matrices. Avoiding the effects of the fast time-varying target character, this new algorithm has a much better performance than conventional methods. Finally, several simulations are performed and the results demonstrate the effectiveness of the new algorithm.

articleTitle: An automatic and accurate search method of spaceborne SAR images by ground control points
abstract: To solve the difficulty of automatic search of spaceborne SAR images by ground corner reflector, an automatic and accurate search method of spaceborne SAR images by ground control points is proposed. In this paper, the zero Doppler method based on iteration is used for rough location of the calibration point, and then the variable window of slant range orientation is adjusted according to the signal to clutter ratio of the current corner reflector on the basis of rough position. Thereafter, the SAR image data is intercepted for oversampling interpolation, and the precise coordinate position of the SAR image is extracted by the maximum position on oversampling SAR image in the end. At the same time, this method is used to test the actual data, and the test results verify the effectiveness of the proposed method. Moreover, software implementation is carried out based on the method in this paper, and the automatic extraction results of relevant software are given, which provides effective software support for the subsequent application of actual spaceborne SAR data in orbit test calibration.

articleTitle: Cooperative anti-jamming algorithm for networked radars based on stretch processing
abstract: With the increasing complexity of the electromagnetic environment, the limitations of single anti-jamming are gradually revealed. Especially with the development of Digital Radio Frequency Memory (DRFM) technology, the deception jamming caused by DRFM is difficult to be identified on stand-alone radar. Group countermeasure is the key to improve the detection ability of radars. For deception jamming, a cooperative anti-jamming method based on Stretch processing for networked radars is proposed. The trajectories (including the true target and the deception jamming) measured by the local radar are sent to the information fusion centre for fusion detection. The time delay and Doppler of the true target is estimated by the same-source-testing method. The estimated value is sent back to the local radar, and the baseband echo required by Stretch processing is constructed based on the linear frequency modulation slope known by the radars. After Stretch transform on the reconstructed baseband echo and the radar echo, the true target was separated from the deception jamming in the frequency domain, and the jamming signal is filtered out. Simulation and hardware test results show that the algorithm can effectively suppress the jamming signal and realize the target tracking in the jamming environment.

articleTitle: Optimization design of power density and comprehensive efficiency for Ka band solid state transmitting device
abstract: The miniaturization and lightweight development of radar transmitting device has become an inevitable trend. In order to improve its power density, the component adopts a stacked design as a whole. Firstly, the wave-guide spatial power division synthesis network and the component box are processed in an integrated manner, and then the multi-channel power amplifier module, power supply unit, and auxiliary unit are stacked on top of the power division synthesis network to achieve a high power density miniaturization design of the component; to improve the overall efficiency of the components, the power supply unit adopts a distributed power supply method, and the main power supply topology adopts a half bridge LLC+dual synchronous Buck. At the same time, innovative state trajectory control technology and synchronous rectification technology are introduced to reduce the switching and conduction losses of the power supply unit while further reducing the size of the power supply unit. Taking the 200W Ka band solid-state transmission component as a design example, the measured results show that the power density of the component reaches 1458W/in3 while meeting the basic indicators, which is nearly 18% higher than similar products. The overall efficiency of the component reaches 19.9%, which is nearly 2.1% higher.

articleTitle: DRP classifier for multi-class target recognition
abstract: In order to improve the recognition performance of the recognition algorithm for HRRP of multiple similar targets, we propose a multi-class target classification and recognition algorithm. By calculating the distance of each feature between the samples and calculating the ratio of the distances, the ratios of the distances of the different features are multiplied and finally the recognition result is obtained by voting. Since the main step consists of the calculation of distance, ratio and product, this classifier is called DRP classifier. In the paper, the DRP classifier is compared with other classification algorithms using five categories of target data with less feature differentiation, and the results show that the DRP classifier increases the accuracy of recognition and possesses higher accuracy than other classification algorithms when the target category increases.

articleTitle: 2D-DOA estimation with difference and sum coarray for L-shaped distributed array
abstract: This paper first constructs a novel L-shaped distributed array for two-dimensional (2-D) direction of arrival (DOA) estimation. Based on this, difference and sum coarrays (DSCAs) of the distributed nested array and the improved distributed array are obtained from the spatial and temporal information of the received data. And the closed-form expressions about the sensor locations, DSCA, and degree of freedom (DOF) are derived. The formed virtual array is composed of two orthogonal portions with identical distributed uniform linear arrays. While increasing DOF for the distributed nested array, the improved distributed array achieves a larger continuous aperture. Next, taking average of the repeat elements in the virtual array is equivalent to increasing the number of snapshots, which improves the estimation accuracy. Then, spatial smoothing is performed to restore the rank of each covariance matrix. Finally, the dual-size ESPRIT algorithm is applied to estimate the azimuth and elevation angles, respectively. Simulation results are conducted to demonstrated the effectivity of the proposed method and the high DOF of the improved distributed array.

articleTitle: Super-resolution target localization by fusing signals from multiple MIMO FMCW automotive radars
abstract: Achieving high azimuth resolution is one of the main bottleneck for automotive radars, which generally demands a large aperture of antenna array. However, building an automotive radar system with a large antenna array is a very challenging task from the perspective of both technological readiness and cost. To circumvent this problem, we propose to fuse signals from multiple small automotive radars placed over the facade of a car as an alternative solution with low system complexity, where each radar with a small Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) array operate independently without accurate synchronization. To (partially) coherently process the measurements from all the radars, a 2-D MUltiple Signal Classification (MUSIC) based algorithm is proposed for joint Direction-of-Arrival (DOA)-range estimation of targets in which spatial smoothing technique is exploited to tackle highly correlated signals. Taking advantage of the proposed estimation approach and multiple radars, it significantly improves the azimuth resolution of the system compared to that of a single MIMO radar. The performance of the proposed method is demonstrated through both numerical simulations and experimental results.

articleTitle: GPCNN: grouped pooling convolutional neural network for radar target detection
abstract: Radar target detection plays an important role in radar signal processing. Constant False Alarm Rate (CFAR) is the most widely used detection method, while its performance is easily affected by clutter and noise and greatly degrades in the condition with multiple targets. In this paper, we propose a Grouped Pooling Convolutional Neural Network (GPCNN) model to address the aforementioned issues. On one hand, this model extracts the deep features to detect targets from complex background. On the other hand, multiple tricks, including pooling module, replacement of fully connected layers, shuffle concatenation, and weight transfer, are introduced into CNN to improve the detection efficiency. Experimental results on the measured data demonstrate that the target detection probability of our proposed GPCNN model has increased by 10% compared with CFAR, and the operation speed has increased by 12 times compared with traditional CNN model.

articleTitle: Synthesis of sparse linear arrays with tensor decomposition
abstract: In this paper, tensors are innovatively applied to array optimization. Thus, an algorithm for synthesis of sparse linear arrays with multi-beampattern is proposed. Different from the traditional matrix pencil method (MPM), the proposed algorithm arranges the data obtained from the desired beampatterns into tensor form. Then a low-rank approximation is performed on this data tensor to obtain a new low-rank tensor, which is decomposed by higher-order singular value (HOSVD). By employing rotation invariance, we determine the element position of sparse array. Finally, the least square method is used to obtain the excitations corresponding to the new array, and the desired beampatterns are synthesized. Compared to MPM, our method accelerates running time while ensuring high accuracy in synthesizing beampatterns.

articleTitle: Ground-based radar three-dimensional imaging for moon under sparse observations
abstract: Ground-based radar system (GBRs) is a powerful tool to obtain three-dimensional (3-D) imagery of the interested celestial bodies, such as the moon. However, in 3-D moon imaging with GBRs, positions for observation are distributed sparsely, and it will lead to imaging ambiguity in height dimension. In this article, a ground-based radar 3-D imaging method for moon under sparse observation is proposed. First, baseline distribution is analyzed, and an optimal baseline selection algorithm based on spatial baseline density maximization is applied. Then, a tomographic 3-D imaging algorithm is discussed, and compressive sensing (CS) technique is used to recover the elevation signal under sparse observation. Moreover, computer simulations are conducted and validate the proposed method.

articleTitle: Joint design of the transmit and receive beamforming via ADMM for LPI radar
abstract: In view of the limitation of the phased-array on suppressing the range-dependent interference, a joint design of the transmit and receive beamforming for low probability of intercept (LPI) of multiple-input multiple-output with frequency diverse array (FDA-MIMO) radar is proposed. The problem of joint design is to maximize the performance of target parameter estimation, and simultaneously minimize the transmit energy at the target region which enhances LPI capability. Following a weighted sum of the performance metric, the original problem is converted into a multiple-ratio fractional programming (FP) problem. The resultant optimization problem is difficult to solve due to the multiple-ratio FP problem. To this end, we introduce two auxiliary variables to the objective function, and then utilize the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) technique to solve a linear optimization problem with respect to both quadratic equality constraints and multi-dimensional ratio constraint. Finally, numerical simulations are provided to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Target detection based on GIP for foliage penetration in signal domain
abstract: In this paper, targets under the dense foliage are seriously interfered by foliage clusters, leading to the invalid of conventional detection methods. To improve the detection probability, in this work, the approach of a two-step processing procedure based on coarse screening and precise detection is proposed. First, after conducting the range compression for echoes, the generalized inner product (GIP) values which are obtained by using the proposed method, where the GIP values are sorted descending and the range gates of some maximum value that be thought to targets are extracted for further analysis. Second, based on the range gates that contained suspected targets, the detection results with constant false alarm (CFAR) are obtained, in which the signal energy that exceeds the threshold value is thought to be the targets under the dense foliage. Finally, the effectiveness of this method is validated with the simulated data and measured data.

articleTitle: A novel MIMO-STAP filter for heterogeneous clutter suppression and joint transmit waveform design
abstract: Space-time adaptive processing in multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO-STAP) radar uses the clutter covariance matrix (CCM) as a crucial parameter for clutter suppression and transmit waveform design. However, in heterogeneous environments, a small number of independent and identically distributed training snapshots are available, leading to inaccurate estimation of CCM and poor performance of traditional MIMO-STAP filters. In this paper, we propose a novel MIMO-STAP filter for heterogeneous clutter suppression and transmit waveform design. First, a sparse recovery method based on structure-aware two- level block sparse characteristic is exploited for the robust CCM estimation and enhancing heterogeneous clutter suppression performance of MIMO-STAP. Based on that, a joint design problem of transmit waveform and STAP receiver filter is presented and solved by cycle optimization. Accordingly, the proposed method achieves satisfying performance on both clutter suppression and transmit waveform design in heterogeneous environments. Numerical experiments validate the superiority of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: A novel insect wingbeat frequency extraction algorithm based on ambiguity function
abstract: Accurate extraction of wingbeat frequency is crucial in insect radar for behavior analysis and species identification of migratory insects. However, the accuracy of extraction cannot be guaranteed due to the weak wingbeat signals and complex insect targets. To address this, this paper proposes an innovative method for enhancing insect wingbeat frequency extraction. This algorithm uses the periodic characteristics of wingbeat micro-motion signals to extract its delay frequency signal to locate its maximum value through the ambiguity function. Then, extract the insect wingbeat frequency by smoothing compensation and Fourier transform, which improves accuracy of insect wingbeat frequency extraction. The efficacy of our algorithm is validated through comprehensive simulations and field experiments, affirming its potential as a robust solution.

articleTitle: Calibration of DEM generation by using LuTan-1 bistatic SAR data
abstract: LuTan-1 (LT-1) is China's first L-band civil interferometric SAR satellite. It can overcome the influence of time decorrelation and atmospheric interference and generate high-precision DEM with bistatic mode. Calibration is an effective method to improve the accuracy of satellite parameters. In this paper, the geometric calibration and baseline calibration are conducted by processing LT-1 calibration cites data. The resulting calibration parameters are then applied to the bistatic data of the test cites, resulting in enhanced positioning accuracy within 5m, and improved elevation measurement accuracy within 5m. It is proved that both calibration methods can improve the quality of DEM.

articleTitle: A convolutional and variant visual transformer fusion network for small ship detection in SAR images
abstract: Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) has been widely recognized as an outstanding method for marine monitoring in recent years. With the rapid development of SAR technology and image processing field, significant progress has been made in ship detection techniques based on SAR images. However, detecting small target ships in SAR images remains a major challenge. In this study, we propose a convolutional and variant visual transformer fusion network specifically for small ship detection in SAR images. Primarily, we propose integrating a BiFormer-block at the end of the backbone network to enhance the network's feature extraction capability for small target ships. In addition, we propose a novel NormConv FPN, which for the first time adds new feature fusion layers and detection heads above the shallow layers to maximize retention of small object feature information, and we incorporate normalization-based Attention Modules during feature fusion to ensure focus on critical information. To validate the performance of the method in this paper, experiments were conducted on the SSDD dataset and compared with some state-of-the-art methods, obtaining the highest MAP (Mean Average Precision) score, 97.5%. In addition, ablation experiments were performed to validate the effectiveness of each enhancement element separately. Our code is available at https://github.com/shengyexu/BiFormer-Enabled-YOLOv5 (accessed on 10 August 2023).

articleTitle: Analysis of time-variant IPP and ISAR imaging for non-cooperative targets with highly maneuvering motion
abstract: Due to complex motion of translational motion (TM) and three-dimensional rotational motion (RM) co-exits for non-cooperative targets, existing inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR) imaging approaches cannot produce satisfactory performance, especially under low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). Therefore, an efficient inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR) imaging approach for non-cooperative targets is proposed in this work. First, the imaging geometry and signal model are reasonably established based on the highly maneuvering characteristic for non-cooperative targets. Second, based on the signal model, the resolution in range dimension and azimuth dimension, the time-variant Doppler frequency, the selection of pulse repetition frequency (PRF), and the non-stationary IPP are theoretically analyzed. Furthermore, aiming to the time-variant characteristic of echo signal, the smooth pseudo Wigner-Ville distribution (SPWVD) method is utilized to ISAR imaging for non-cooperative targets. Finally, both simulated and electromagnetic data validate the effectiveness of the signal model.

articleTitle: A MIMO millimeter-wave radar for high-resolution imaging
abstract: In recent years, the interest in active millimeter-wave radar imaging has gradually increased due to safety issues. The current mechanical scanning millimeter-wave radar has a low imaging rate, while the two-dimensional array electric scanning radar has a high hardware cost, making it difficult to apply in practice. Thus, a two-dimensional high-resolution millimeter-wave radar based on multiple input multiple output (MIMO) technology and linear array is introduced in this paper. Firstly, the antenna array model and the imaging geometry are introduced. Then, the key parameters of the antenna are designed, including the distance between antenna elements and the distance between transmitting and receiving arrays. Finally, the radar imaging experiment is conducted to verify the imaging ability of the radar on metal objects obstructed by paper and cloth.

articleTitle: Cross-domain SAR detection method based on salient object alignment
abstract: Deep learning based Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) object detection methods usually assume that the training data and the test data obey the same distribution. However, when the radar parameters change, the data distribution also changes, which will lead to a significant degradation in the performance of the detection network. To solve this problem, a cross-domain SAR detection method based on salient object alignment is proposed in this paper. Specifically, the module first calculates the saliency map of the SAR image. Combining the saliency map with the prediction of the model can obtain more accurate features of salient object. Therefore, we can pay more attention to the object in the process of feature alignment. Ablation experiments prove that the proposed object-saliency alignment module is effective. In addition, compared with several other methods in cross-domain detection task, this method has the best detection performance.

articleTitle: Assessment of thermal noise impact on sea ice classification using Sentinel-1 images and U-Net
abstract: Sea ice is one of the significant threats to high-latitude navigation and offshore operations. Accurate and timely classification of sea ice is very important for the safety of maritime navigation and other activities in polar region. Synthetic aperture radar (SAR), which has the merits of high resolution and all-time, all-weather observation capability, has been widely used for sea ice classification. However, thermal noise in SAR images, induced by platform and sensor system, imaging mechanism as well as scattering process, can significantly affect the sea ice classification. Thermal noise present in the Sentinel-1 cross-polarization images is thought to have a significantly affect. In this study, we investigated the impact of thermal noise on sea ice classification using Sentinel-1 extra-wide (EW) swath mode images and a deep learning (DL) model, U-Net. A denoising method was used to conduct sensitivity experiments for the U-Net and the comparing models, i.e., support vector machine (SVM), random forest (RF) and convolutional neural network (CNN). 15 Sentinel-1 EW model images were utilized for training and testing the models. The results indicate that the sea ice classification result of U-Net and CNN exhibit fewer discrepancies after applying denoising method, suggesting the noise immunity of DL models.

articleTitle: Data-driven SAR image reconstruction method using ADMM with deep plug-and-play priors
abstract: Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) image reconstruction fundamentally constitutes an ill-posed reconstruction conundrum, with the overarching objective of faithfully restoring the 'authentic' SAR scenes via radar echo measurements and a forward model. The conventional FFT-based approach, in conjunction with matched filtering, tends to yield undesirable sidelobes and speckle artifacts. Conversely, the reconstruction challenge can be cast as a minimization problem, seeking to enhance outcomes by merging data-term and prior-related terms. This composite problem is amenable to resolution via proximal methods. In this paper, a novel data-driven methodology is employed, leveraging the plug-and-play (PNP) technique to train a neural network for acquiring target image priors. In comparison to traditional manually crafted priors and PNP priors, the proposed PNP deep priors exhibit the capacity to achieve superior reconstruction results. Experimental assessments involving synthetic and real SAR scenes underscore the robustness and efficacy of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Deep SBL network-based DOA estimation for nested array with mutual coupling
abstract: Recently, deep unfolding networks have been widely used in direction of arrival (DOA) estimation because of the improved estimation accuracy and reduced computational cost. However, few consider the existence of nested array (NA) with mutual coupling. In this paper, we present a deep sparse Bayesian learning (DSBL) network to solve this problem. We first transform the array output with unknown mutual coupling coefficient (MCC) into real domain for neural networks. We then train the DSBL network to determine the MCC and obtain DOA spatial spectrum, where the loss function is calculated by using reconstruction error and the sparsity of network output, and the layers correspond to the steps of Expectation Maximization (EM) algorithm. We demonstrate that DSBL network can achieve better generalization ability without training labels and large-scale training data. Simulation results validate the effectiveness of DSBL network by comparing with the existing methods.

articleTitle: Tensor completion-based ISAR imaging with sparse sampling
abstract: With the extensive application of inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR) imaging in various practical contexts, there has been an increased demand for higher-performance algorithms in ISAR imaging, which has particularly sparked intense discussions regarding super-resolution imaging algorithms for sparse signal reconstruction. Conventional matrix completion (MC) applying matrix trace norm has provided a direction for enhancing imaging resolution. However, the traditional method fails to make full use of the structure of data, thus we propose a tensor completion-based matrix recovery (TCMR) method, which extends the matrix into higher-order dimensions by sliding windows method to better deliver the intrinsic structure of data. In this article, during the process of solving the model using the alternative direction method of multipliers (ADMM) algorithm, we utilize a singular value thresholding operator as a closed-form solution for iterative computations. The experimental evaluations were conducted using the measured data to perform performance analysis and comparison between the proposed algorithm and the conventional MC algorithm, thereby demonstrating the superiority of the algorithm.

articleTitle: Single-channel millimeter wave radar NLOS imaging based on multipath effect
abstract: Non-line-of-sight (NLOS) imaging technology of millimeter-wave (MMW) radar has the ability to detect targets hidden in corners that cannot be directly observed. A method of single-channel MMW radar NLOS imaging based on the multipath effect was presented in this manuscript. The synthetic aperture technique is used in the imaging scheme to reconstruct the detected target. A servo-driven slide is deployed to make the radar move at a constant velocity and used to obtain the vertical resolution. The system prototype is established based on the derived signal model of NLOS imaging. Simulation experiment results verify the effectiveness of the proposed imaging method.

articleTitle: Coherent motion compensation integrated with fast time domain algorithm for circular SAR imaging
abstract: Circular Synthetic Aperture Radar (CSAR) has attracted growing interest in recent years because it can obtain high-resolution imaging over a multi-angle observation along with the azimuth angle variation. To achieve high efficiency, fast time-domain algorithm (FTDA) segments the full-aperture into a number of sub-apertures, and the sub-apertures are processed individually by FTDA incorporated data-driven motion compensation (MOCO). However, data-driven MOCO will eventually introduce incoherent phase errors between sub-images and degrade the focusing quality of the final image. To address these problems, a coherent MOCO method is proposed by exploiting the spectral characteristics and recovering the coherence between adjacent sub-images. After restoring the coherence of sub-images, these sub-images are coherently processed to obtain the final SAR image with high quality. The processed results of simulations are provided to verify the performance of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Joint range and angle estimation with coprime FDA-MIMO radar
abstract: This paper deals with the problem of joint angle and range estimation for multiple targets in a Coprime frequency diverse array multiple-input multiple-output (FDA-MIMO) radar. At the design stage, a coprime array is utilized for both transmission and reception, where coprime frequency offsets are introduced in the transmit array elements. In order to obtain the range and angle information of the targets, the estimation problem is formulated resorting to the Maximum Likelihood (ML) criterion. Hence, a Linearized Array Manifold (LAM) method is developed by performing a tailored linearization of the array steering matrix around the nominal angles and ranges, where the array steering matrix is approximated at the first order. At the analysis stage, the Cramér-Rao Bound is derived, and the performance of the proposed method is assessed in terms of Root Mean Square Error (RMSE), where comparisons among other counterparts are carried out. Numerical results corroborate the effectiveness of the considered strategy in the background of Gaussian noise.

articleTitle: First validation of ocean current measurement by along-track interferometry mode of Luojia-2 satellite
abstract: Luojia-2 is the world's first Ka-band synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellite with along-track interferometry(ATI) capability. Its phased-array antenna can be splitted into two halves, and operates in full-transmitting two-halves-receiving mode, forming an effective baseline of 1.5 meters in the flight direction. To verify the current measurement capabilities of Luojia-2 ATI mode, the Kuroshio region where the world’s second largest ocean current exists is selected as the observation area. The ATI mode data was acquired on July 20, 2023, UTC time, and the current velocity component along the measurement direction was derived after some basic interferometic procedures and geometric projection. The "true" current for comparison was used from an ocean analysis products provided by the European Space Agency's Copernicus website. The results showed a correlation of 0.78 between the ATI measurement and the “true” current, with a current measurement accuracy of 0.09 m/s at a spatial resolution of 300 meters. This result validates the effectiveness of Luojia-2 ATI mode for ocean current field measurements of both high precision and resolution.

articleTitle: Low-oversampled staggered SAR imaging in present of a random PRI variation strategy
abstract: As an innovative concept of high-resolution and wide-swath systems, low-oversampled (LS) staggered synthetic aperture radar (SAR) combines SCan-On-REceive (SCORE) with continuous variation of the pulse repetition interval (PRI) to deal with the blind ranges over wide areas. Because the PRI variation leads to the nonuniformly sampled raw data being partially lost, the existing reconstruction algorithms mostly resample the nonuniformly sampled signal into a uniform grid and then perform traditionally focused processing. However, these algorithms ignore the accuracy of resampling with regard to the PRI strategies, especially under low oversampling or even sub-Nyquist sampling. In this paper, a reconstruction algorithm in the presence of a random PRI variation strategy is proposed. Due to the blind range distribution, which depends on the PRI variation strategy, affects the reconstructed performance, a random PRI variation strategy is optimized to further exploit the potential of non-uniform sampling. Then a reconstruction algorithm based on sparse Bayesian learning (SBL) is proposed to directly focus images using the nonuniform sampling for LS-SAR. Finally, the robustness and effectiveness of the proposed method are demonstrated by simulations and experiments.

articleTitle: Focused bistatic ISAR imaging demonstration with nonparametric autofocusing
abstract: Bistatic Inverse Synthetic Aperture Radar (Bi-ISAR) has been attracted more and more attentions in military and civil fields due to its spatially separated transmitter and receiver configuration. In this paper, the Bi-ISAR imaging model is established. To compensate the phase error, the modified autofocusing algorithm with nonparametric model under the minimum entropy criterion is proposed, and the Bi-ISAR imaging is performed and compared with that of conventional method. Finally, Bi-ISAR imaging experimental demonstration with sliding rail system is constructed. The effectiveness of the proposed algorithm is proved with the experimental data.

articleTitle: The application of the alternate descent conditional gradient method in tomographic SAR off-grid imaging
abstract: Compressed sensing (CS) technology has been applied to topographic synthetic aperture radar (TomoSAR) imaging due to the sparsity of elevation signals. The traditional CS algorithms discretize the elevation into many grids and assume that the scatterers are located on grids, therefore, the accuracy of the traditional CS algorithms is limited by the off-grid effect. Although there are currently methods to address the off-grid effect, such as atomic norm minimization (ANM), its application is limited by the baseline distribution form of TomoSAR, which only applies to uniformly observed scenarios. Alternating Descent Conditional Gradient (ADCG) has been applied in many fields as a gridless imaging algorithm. In this paper, we apply ADCG to TomoSAR imaging for the first time, achieving the reconstruction of non-uniform baseline observation scenes. The effectiveness of ADCG in TomoSAR imaging was verified by comparing it with iterative soft thresholding (IST) and orthogonal matching pursuit (OMP) through simulation experiments.

articleTitle: A 3-D imaging method based on phase-derived technology under squint model
abstract: The 3-D InISAR imaging results are degraded greatly under squint model because of the interferometric phase ambiguity. However, if the size of the target is large, the existing InISAR imaging algorithms under squint model cannot estimate the coordinates of target scatterers correctly which are not satisfied with the constraint condition of geometric between the target and radar system. Besides, they need to correct the slant-range coordinates, causing algorithm steps cumbersome. To overcome these disadvantages, a new 3-D imaging method based on phase-derived technology is proposed in this study. The angle measurement results of scatterers are obtained by phase-derived angle measurement (PDAM), in which phase-derived range measurement (PDRM) results of scatterers are used to resolve the interferometric phase ambiguity. Then, scatterers positioning by combining PDAM results and PDRM results are applied to estimate the coordinates of target scatterers which is not constrained by geometric between the target and radar system. Simulation results verified the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: First study of LT-1 SAR satellite for rock glacier deformation monitoring over Tibetan plateau periglacial environment
abstract: Rock glaciers are typical periglacial landforms that are almost ubiquitously present in the alpine mountain permafrost environment, extending downslope from talus cones, glaciers, or terminal moraines of glaciers. The displacement of rock glaciers serves as valuable indicators for landslide disaster prevention, changes in hydrological resources, and the evolution of periglacial environments. Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) interferometry (InSAR) is an effective approach for investigating rock glacier displacements. Lu Tan-1 (LT-1) is the first L-band SAR satellite constellation which was launched on January 26 and February 27, 2022, respectively. The LT-1 SAR data can provide a new data source for the deformation of rock glaciers. In this paper, a rock glacier landform deformation monitoring over the Nyainqêntanglha Range, Qinghai-Tibet Plateau (QTP) is conducted using newly launched LT-1 satellite SAR data. Firstly, a rock glacier inventory of the Nyainqêntanglha Range was derived from high-resolution Gaofen-2 images. Then, the deformation magnitude and velocity of rock glaciers were calculated using the differential interferometric synthetic aperture radar (DInSAR), Stacking method. Finally, the deformation characteristic of rock glaciers was extracted and analyzed in detail. The results demonstrated that the LT-1 could provide a new and powerful SAR data source for rock glacier deformation monitoring and will greatly enhance the level of periglacial landforms monitoring applications.

articleTitle: Generalized likelihood ratio test matched to fluctuation characteristics
abstract: The fluctuation of the target's Radar Cross Section(RCS) is influenced by factors such as radar line-of-sight, transmit carrier frequency. The effectiveness of traditional coherent integration detection and incoherent integration detection is contingent upon the extent of RCS fluctuation. In this paper, we employ the principles of generalized likelihood ratio test under the Neyman-Pearson(N-P) criterion to establish an optimal detector that matched to the first and second-order moment statistical characteristics of the complex RCS exhibited by a moving target. The selection of the optimal transmit frequency employs a selection approach that maximizes the detection probability for a given false alarm rate. Additionally, a fast Fourier transform implementation of the likelihood ratio test to solve the problem of the detector's reliance on Doppler frequency data. Experimental results demonstrate the detector's sustained optimality across varying degrees of target fluctuation characteristics.

articleTitle: Phase congruency based common feature saliency enhancement for optical and SAR image matching
abstract: Image matching plays a crucial role in integrating optical and synthetic aperture radar (SAR) image data. The presence of severe nonlinear radiation distortion (NRD) poses a significant challenge to the task of matching optical and SAR images. Existing methods fall short of effectively exacting common features from heterogeneous images, which limits the performance of image matching. Accordingly, we propose to use phase congruency to enhance the saliency of common features for improving image matching. We employ a U-Net architecture to extract high-level semantic information and low-level fine-grained information from intensity images. Meanwhile, the phase congruency feature maps are input into a shallow convolutional neural network (CNN) to refine the structural properties of the images. The features from both branches are combined and integrated across channels to produce a robust feature map. Finally, image matching is achieved through the use of a fast Fourier transform (FFT) correlation layer. Experiments on the publicly available SEN1-2 dataset show that the phase congruency prior branch significantly enhances matching accuracy. Furthermore, we establish the superiority of our proposed method compared to existing state-of-the-art approaches for optical and SAR image matching.

articleTitle: Detection of pre-seismic deformation of 2021 Maduo M7.4 earthquake by using ASF HYP3
abstract: On May 22, 2021, a seismic event of magnitude 7.4 struck the region of Maduo in Qinghai, China, with its epicenter located at approximately 34.59 degrees North latitude and 98.34 degrees East longitude. In this study, we employed an automated time-series InSAR (Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar) analysis technique. Building upon data processed within the ASF HYP3 cloud platform, we autonomously selected the necessary image pairs for our analysis. Subsequently, we utilized the MintPy software to process Sentinel-1 SAR (Synthetic Aperture Radar) image data covering the Maduo region in Qinghai, China, spanning from January 2018 to May 2021. This processing generated a time series of ground deformation leading up to the seismic event, enabling us to analyze the spatiotemporal distribution of regional crustal deformation in the pre-seismic phase. Our goal was to monitor any abnormal deformation signals preceding the strong earthquake. The research findings indicate that in the Maduo region, the pre-seismic LOS relative deformation rates are primarily concentrated at around 5 mm/yr, with an increase in velocity in proximity to the seismogenic fault.

articleTitle: Range-Doppler characteristics of multi-rotor unmanned aerial vehicle in low-frequency passive radar
abstract: Passive radar based on Frequency Modulation (FM) Broadcast, Digital Video Broadcasting for Terrestrial (DVB- T), Digital Terrestrial Multimedia Broadcast (DTMB) and other low-frequency signals is of great concern, which can be used for unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) detection. This paper establishes the echo model of the multi-rotor UAV and analyzes the range-Doppler characteristics with different flight states in the low-frequency passive radar. The results show that the micro- Doppler generated by the rotor in the low frequency is no longer the sinusoidal form, but the discrete frequency point, which produces multiple frequency lines in the range-Doppler image. The conclusion is confirmed by the field experiment, which has reference significance for multi-rotor UAV recognition.

articleTitle: An multilayer fusion strategy based on improved YOLOv5 for ship detection in SAR images
abstract: Since entering the era of deep learning, the single-stage detection algorithm represented by YOLO has achieved some progress in the detection of ship targets by synthetic aperture radar (SAR). However, the accuracy of single-stage detection is lower than that of two-stage detection, especially for small target detection. To this end, this paper proposes an improved YOLOv5 detection method based on convolutional bolck attention module(CBAM) and WPAN. At the same time, the focal efficient intersection over union (Focal EIoU) is introduced to optimize the calculation of bounding box regression loss. The experiment is verified on SAR ship detection dataset(SSDD). The results show that the proposed improved YOLOv5 algorithm can improve the false alarm and missing detection problems in multi-scale target detection, and improve the detection accuracy consequently.

articleTitle: Forward-looking high-resolution imaging using random stepped-frequency waveform
abstract: Radar forward-looking imaging is widely used in military reconnaissance, sea search, ground attack and other fields due to its all-weather and all-day advantages. However, the signal emitted by traditional forward-looking radar imaging is still the linear frequency modulated (LFM) signal with the large time-bandwidth product, and result of its simple waveform and fixed frequency, the radar is susceptible to interference in complex electromagnetic environments, thus affecting target imaging. In this paper, a forward-looking high-resolution imaging technique based on random stepped-frequency (RSF) waveforms is presented. Due to the agility of the waveform, it reduces the risk of radar being interfered in complex electromagnetic environment. In addition, compared with the traditional imaging algorithm, this method has better imaging.

articleTitle: Frequency coding waveform with non-uniform segmented LFM for MIMO radars
abstract: LFM (Linear Frequency Modulation) signal is commonly applied in MIMO (Multiple Input Multiple Output) radar system as its transmitting waveform because of high doppler tolerance. To address the issue of high autocorrelation sidelobes and enhance the characteristic of this designed waveform in searching low, slow and small targets, this paper proposes a frequency coding waveform with non-uniform segmented LFM design method. Based on a joint multi-parameter optimization model, this innovative approach optimizes not only the frequency coding of the transmitting signals but also the time duration and the bandwidth of sub-pulses simultaneously using the genetic algorithm. Compared to other different LFM waveform methods, the simulation results demonstrate that the OFD-LFM (Orthogonal Frequency Division-Linear Frequency Modulation) waveform optimized through this proposed method achieves significantly lower level of high autocorrelation sidelobes.

articleTitle: A novel approach to phase error estimation in multi-channel ScanSAR
abstract: The phase error between channels in azimuth multi-channel (AMC) synthetic aperture radar (SAR) system can deteriorate the reconstruction performance, leading to azimuth ambiguity in the final image. Therefore, phase error estimation is an essential step in AMC SAR imaging. However, due to the special beam scanning of AMC scanned-beam SAR (ScanSAR), the Doppler spectrum of the point target is incomplete and asymmetric, which makes the traditional phase error estimation methods unsuitable for ScanSAR. Taking the Doppler spectrum characteristics into account, a new method of multi-channel ScanSAR phase error estimation is proposed. The proposed method divides the Doppler centroid (DC) of the strong scattering point target into baseband DC and ambiguity DC. The spatial cross-correlation coefficient (SCCC) method is adopted to estimate the baseband DC. Then, the frequency cross-correlation coefficient (FCCC) method is proposed to estimate the DC ambiguity number. After estimating the precise DC, the frequency correlation method (FCM) is improved to estimate the phase error. Finally, the validation of the proposed method is demonstrated with the simulation data and GF-3 dual channel data.

articleTitle: Joint transmit signal and receiving filter design in barrage jamming with optimized received dynamic range
abstract: Improved dynamic range of the receiving filter output contributes to target detection performance of the radar system. In this paper, the problem of jointly designing the transmit signal and receiving filter in the presence of barrage jamming with optimized dynamic range is studied. The goal is to minimize the mean-square error (MSE) of a target's scattering coefficient estimate and obtain optimized dynamic range in the presence of barrage jamming at the same time. The problems of jointly designing the transmit signal and receiving filter in barrage jamming with optimized dynamic range are studied based on peak sidelobe level (PSL) metrics. The joint design problems are first split into transmit signal design and receiving filter design problems based on alternating direction method, and then iterative algorithms based on alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) are applied for solving the sub- optimization problem. Numerical examples show that the level of barrage jamming can be suppressed to peak sidelobe level by the optimized transmit signal and receiving filter.

articleTitle: An enhancing biological echo classification method with polarimetric weather radar using random forest classifiers
abstract: Polarimetric weather radar can enhance precipitation and biological scatter monitoring by measuring the polarization moments of targets, thus providing valuable shape information. This study employed five Random Forest classifiers to classify birds, insects, and precipitations at the five lowest elevation angles. The training and testing sets were artificially generated us ing typical cases of birds, insects, and precipitations captured by the polarimetric weather radar. A two-dimensional median filter was employed to reduce the volatility of polarization moments. To mitigate the impact of differential phase jumps, the centre of the probability distribution function for the differential phase in each volume scan was fixed at 180 degrees. The classification accuracy for each elevation angle and sample type exceeded 91%. The performance of the classifiers was assessed using two representative cases.

articleTitle: Rock glacier kinematic monitoring using the MT-INSAR method with high-resolution RADARSAT-2 images
abstract: In this paper, we developed an approach to maximize the ability for detecting rock glaciers deformation by a multi-baseline persistent scatterer (PS) and distributed scatterer (DS) combined MT-InSAR method and high-resolution Radarsat-2 SAR data. The design of the approach was to minimize the decorrelation effects from snow present, snow melt, and complex topography-induced atmospheric phase noises. The proposed method includes 3 steps: (1) evaluating the rock glacier interferometric coherence of all possible interferometric combinations and determining the multi-baseline network based on rock glacier coherence; (2) constructing a Delaunay triangulation network by exploiting both PS and DS points; (3) combing the Nelder-Mead algorithm with the M-estimator method to estimate the deformation rate variation at the arcs of the DTN and introduced a ridge-estimator-based weight least square method for the inversion of the deformation rate from the deformation rate variation; (4) Detecting the rock glacier activity and analyzing the deformation characteristics. The results indicate that more detailed activity characteristics were captured by using the Radarsat-2 data compared with Sentinel-1- derived results. The result demonstrated the application value of high-resolution SAR data on the rock glacier kinematic monitoring. We also found that the Ridge-and-furrow region of the rock glacier has obvious activity compared with the Front and Lateral Margins in some typical active rock glaciers.

articleTitle: Multi-observation scheme for arbitrary sparse array motion
abstract: Recently, sparse array motion has been proposed to increase the number of consecutive degrees of freedom (cDOFs). However, the moving strategy of half-wavelength are only suitable for certain types of sparse arrays. In this paper, a multi-observation scheme for arbitrary sparse array motion with displacements of half-wavelength multiples is presented to achieve a fully filled difference coarray (DCA). We first analyse the DCA of the synthetic array and turn out that it consists of the union of the original DCA and its multiple shifted versions to the left and right. Then, based on the maximum number of consecutive holes in the original DCA, we derive the number of moving observations to obtain a hole-free DCA structure for arbitrary sparse array motions. The numerical examples of direction of arrival (DOA) estimation are provided to demonstrate the superiority of the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: A novel method for refocusing swing ships on SAR images under long synthetic aperture time
abstract: Synthetic aperture radar can obtain images of ships at sea all day and all weather. However, moving ships exhibit azimuthal defocus on SAR images, especially swing ships at long synthetic aperture time. In order to solve this difficult problem, this paper proposes a new refocusing algorithm for swing ship SAR images at long synthetic aperture time. The algorithm first maps the SAR single-look complex image to the equivalent echo domain.
