Secondly, the Short Time Fourier Transform is applied to the signal of the range cell where the primary scatterer of the ship is located. Thirdly, the time-frequency ridge in the time-frequency plane is extracted, and then the smoothed time-frequency ridge is linearly segmented using the Douglas Pook algorithm to generate the subaperture images. Finally, the subaperture image is refocused using Fractional Fourier transform. The proposed algorithm is validated on real SAR ship images in HISEA-1 Spotlight mode. Experimental results show that the algorithm in this paper can effectively refocus 3D swing ship SAR images of long synthetic aperture time.

articleTitle: Difference pattern synthesis for subarrayed monopulse linear array via compressed sensing
abstract: An innovative and efficient technique based on Compressed Sensing (CS) is proposed for the difference pattern synthesis of monopulse linear arrays with the minimum number of subarrays. According to the fact that the difference excitations are the product of the sum excitations and the subarray weights, a sparse vector is first derived to represent the result of subarray partition generating the difference pattern from a fixed sum one. The related synthesis can be mathematically formulated as a sparse recovery problem with l1-norm minimization based on CS theory. The synthesis process is simple and efficient. The subarray number, configuration and weights corresponding to the desired difference pattern can be optimized jointly and determined simultaneously by convex optimization. Numerical experiments show the effectiveness and advantages of the proposed method.

articleTitle: SAR image simulation method for complex targets based on shadow geometry model
abstract: Since the synthetic aperture radar (SAR) has the advantages of strong permeability and long-range detection, target recognition based on SAR images is playing an increasingly critical role in reconnaissance and marine remote sensing applications. However, due to the high cost of acquiring real SAR images, it is hard to meet the requirements of target recognition in terms of quantity and conditional coverage. This paper presents a fast SAR image simulation method for complex targets to enlarge the dataset for SAR target recognition. In the process of simulating the SAR echo, the shadow effect between the target and the background environment along the direction of radar line-of-sight (RLOS) is considered, and the radar cross-section (RCS) data is obtained through Physical Optics (PO) method. Firstly, the surface of the established 3D model is divided into small surface elements to compute the backscattering coefficient of targets by PO method. Then, the shadow region can be determined by building the incidence angle geometry model. The speed of SAR echo simulation can be improved by fast convolution and the Deramp-Chirp Scaling (CS) algorithm is adopted for imaging processing. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method, which can generate the SAR simulated images of the specified target under different system parameters.

articleTitle: Analysis and compensation of Doppler shift effect of GNSS-S radar
abstract: In this paper, the influence of Doppler shift in GNSS-S radar detection due to platform movement or target movement is analyzed, and a compensation method is proposed. Different from traditional linear frequency modulation pulse signals, GNSS -S radar signals are continuously coded signals transmitted by GNSS satellites. When there is a large radial relative motion between the radar and the detected target, the Doppler shift caused by the motion will affect the compression characteristics of the enco ded signal, thus reducing the detection performance. Taking GNSS-S radar carried by aircraft and low orbit satellite platform as an example, the influence of Doppler difference between direct signal and scattered signal on detection performance is analyzed in detail. Then, the Doppler offset is calculated and compensated by combining direct signal positioning and antenna pointing geometry. The simulation results show that when the relative velocity between GNSS-S radar and target exceeds 30m/s, the signal-to-noise ratio is reduced by more than 10% in most geometries, and the detection performance can be improved close to the original level by Doppler offset compensation.

articleTitle: Joint ego-motion estimation and 3D imaging for forward-looking region using automotive radar
abstract: The problem of joint ego-motion estimation and 3D unambiguous Doppler beam sharpening in automotive multiple-input and multiple-output (MIMO) forward-looking radar has been studied. Based on the phase differences between the targets and the radar during the movement in different slow time bins, the 3-dimensional ego-estimation is performed and transferred into the 3D Doppler beam sharpening algorithm. The coupling between the azimuth and elevation estimation and the ambiguity problem of the Doppler beam sharpening are addressed in the proposed 3D Doppler beam sharpening algorithm. The joint algorithm performance has been studied in simulations, and possible limitations have been discussed. In addition, the method has been verified experimentally with point-like and extended targets to show the robustness of the whole process.

articleTitle: Transient observation for micro-Doppler of drones
abstract: Micro-Doppler is a critical technique for radar-based Automatic Target Recognition (ATR) in countering drones. However, capturing the intricate "blade flash" patterns in micro-Doppler spectrograms requires extended radar dwell times due to their time-domain nature, which exceeds many the limitations of single radar scans in counter-drone radars. This study introduces a fresh perspective by revealing that transient micro-Doppler signals equate to established Jet Engine Modulation (JEM) or Helicopter Rotor Modulation (HERM) lines in the micro-Doppler spectrum, and we re-define it as "transient micro-Doppler". Experimental assessments across various drones—quad-rotor, fixed-wing, and hybrid VTOL—amid diverse backgrounds using multiple radar systems, consistently disclose JEM signals. Unlike the "blade flash" pattern, JEM signals prove detectable within both short and adequate radar dwell times, thus enhancing ATR algorithms without temporal extensions.

articleTitle: Few-shot SAR target classification with CLPN: a prototypical network combining unsupervised contrastive learning
abstract: In the field of Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR), owing to the limitations of observation and imaging conditions, only a limited number of annotated samples are available for model training. Existing deep learning-based methods struggle to effectively extract discernible features, leading to degraded performance or even complete failure. To address these issues, this paper combines prototypical networks from meta-learning with unsupervised contrastive learning. By utilizing meta-learning, the proposed method ensures the model's classification performance under small sample conditions. Additionally, effective SAR data augmentation techniques are designed to incorporate unsupervised contrastive learning, enabling the model to better capture the similarities and differences between classes and enhance its generalization ability. Our proposed approach leverages both the supervised information from class labels and the unsupervised information inherent in the images, allowing the model to deeply explore the high-order information within the data and achieve accurate classification of few shot SAR targets. The recognition results on the MSTAR dataset, consisting of three target classes, demonstrate that the proposed method (CLPN) exhibits higher average recognition accuracy under the small sample condition and robustness to different depression angles.

articleTitle: Joint optimization algorithm for integrated transmission and reception of OFDM detection and communication on W-ADMM
abstract: This article proposes a dual-function of radar and communication (DFRC) OFDM waveform design method. This method utilizes the PSK method to modulate communication information on subcarrier complex weight, and consider adjust the location of phase of complex weight. It constructs a quadratic optimization problem with non-convex constraints based on minimizing the weighted integrated sidelobe level joint transmission and reception. The constraints include constant modulus constraints, signal-to-noise ratio loss, BER, and the mainlobe level of the cross-correlation between transmission and reception. Subsequently, the convergence and algorithm effectiveness of W-ADMM algorithm were demonstrated. The final exam results show that the designed waveform can effectively supress sidelobes and ensure communication error rate.

articleTitle: Separability analysis of ship targets based on compact polarimetric SAR features construction
abstract: Compact polarization is an emerging polarization SAR mode capable of effectively collecting polarimetric scattering information from targets in different polarization directions. Polarimetric features aid in delineating the geometric structure and analyzing the scattering characteristics of ships, thereby enabling the subsequent detection, classification, and identification of ship targets. To improve the separability between maritime ships and the background in compact polarimetric SAR images, this paper proposes a polarization feature λg based on the eigenvalue decomposition of the Stokes vector. This feature can not only reflect the polarization state between different targets but also evaluate the circular polarity of the ship target. In the experiments high-resolution GF-3 satellite fully polarized data is used to simulate right-handed CTLR mode compact polarimetric SAR data, in order to analyze the polarization characteristics of the ship target in the compact polarization mode. And the comparison is implemented with single-polarization amplitude and the four existing polarimetric features Span, Pg, A, Hω. The results show that the new feature has better performance in image contrast, local standard deviation than other polarization features, which can not only separate ship targets and background well, but also have better noise suppression performance.

articleTitle: Characterization and mitigation of RFI artifacts in operationally processed LuTan-1 imagery
abstract: LuTan-1 satellite is China's first L-band distributed spaceborne interferometric synthetic aperture radar (InSAR) mission, serving land resource management, mapping, forestry, and disaster preparedness purposes. However, the presence of radio frequency interference (RFI) in the shared L-band spectrum poses a significant threat to obtaining a high-quality digital elevation model (DEM) and deformation monitoring. This paper examines RFI issues in LuTan-1 InSAR mission, derives interference echo model, and analyses adverse impact on interferometric coherence. An automated RFI detection and mitigation pipeline is proposed for the Lutan-1 ground processing system, capable of managing massive image datasets without manual tuning parameters. Experiments with real LuTan-1 mission data, including various scenarios and RFI instances, demonstrate the proposed scheme's effectiveness in eliminating RFI artifacts and improving image quality and coherence. This solution has been integrated into LuTan-1's processing pipeline for practical use.

articleTitle: The fusion method of GB-MIMO radar images and 3D point cloud data based on high-precision coordinate system conversion
abstract: Ground-based multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) radar has the advantages of portability and high image frame rate, and has broad application prospects in monitoring landslides and other geological disaster early warning. The high-precision imaging of ground-based radar can obtain the scattering characteristics of the target in the scene, but the two –dimensional imaging in the line of sight direction,it’s difficult to reflect the three-dimensional structure of the target in the scene. With the help of three-dimensional point cloud data and based on the principle of radar imaging, this paper breaks through technologies of radar position estimation, coordinate system conversion, and matching of radar data and point cloud data. Achieved high - precision fusion of radar data and 3D point cloud.

articleTitle: Miniaturized phased array signal processing hardware design based on adaptive beamforming technology
abstract: This paper focuses on the challenges faced in hardware design for array signal processing using adaptive beamforming technology. Guided by the requirements of phased array radar systems, the study introduces various beamforming techniques and explores the criteria for adaptive beamforming. Specifically, it covers the classical Sample Matrix Inversion (SMI) adaptive beamforming algorithm. In environments that demand miniaturization and real-time operation, the paper considers the use of subarrays. It delves into the impact of subarrays on the performance of adaptive beamforming and offers computational methods tailored for subarray-level beamforming. Using Xilinx's High-Level Synthesis (HLS), an adaptive beamforming module has been implemented. The correctness was verified through C-based simulation analysis, and the functionality was further validated using the Zynq Ultrascale+ MPSOC platform.

articleTitle: An algorithm for sidelobe suppression of radar and communication integrated LFM-MSK signal
abstract: Radar communication integration has been a research hotspot in recent years. Waveform design is crucial for radar communication integration. A practicable waveform is to modulate the Minimum Shift Keying (MSK) signal onto a Linear Frequency Modulation (LFM) signal, which is called LFM-MSK for short. It has the advantages of constant envelope and continuous phase. However, the modulated sidelobe of the autocorrelation function is too high. The general windowing method is not valid for sidelobe suppression. In this paper, the spectrum modification algorithm is proposed for sidelobe suppression. Via the autocorrelation function, power spectrum density is estimated, which provides a reference for the design of the frequency window function in the proposed algorithm. Simulations show that the processed sidelobe around the main lobe is reduced by nearly 10 dB with SNR = 10 dB.

articleTitle: Research on segmented reconstruction multiple false targets suppression jamming technology based on improved quantum-real genetic algorithm
abstract: An improved quantum–real hybrid genetic algorithm (IQGA-RGA) with a segmental-reconstruction jamming-signal optimization model is proposed for the segmental reconstruction of a multi-false target jamming-signal optimization problem. The jamming evaluation function is set based on the mean-level constant false-alarm detection threshold, and the objective function is optimized using IQGA-RGA. The introduction of local quantum catastrophes at the early stage of evolution improves the optimization speed of the algorithm at an early stage. With improved optimization effect under the initial quantum coding condition, the optimization result of the real-coded genetic algorithm at the later stage is closer to the global optimal solution. Simulation results show that compared with the real number-coded genetic algorithm and quantum genetic algorithm, the IQGA-RGA has the characteristics of fast convergence speed and strong optimization searching ability, and it can effectively solve the optimization problem of segmented reconstructed jamming signals.

articleTitle: Time-varying electromagnetic scattering feature extraction and analysis for rotor targets
abstract: This paper mainly analyses the dominant degree of time-varying law of rotor weak scattering features of quadrotor UAVs in different motion processes, proposed evaluation factors to measure the dominant features of time-varying law, and evaluate the dominant law of rotor rotating time-varying features under multiple line-of-sight angles and multiple motion states. The evaluation results provide an effective angle range for subsequent simulation measurements and a theoretical basis for avoiding non-cooperative observation of rotor electromagnetic scattering characteristics.

articleTitle: Performance of logistic and tent chaotic sequences in direct spread spectrum communication application
abstract: To address the performance issues of different chaotic sequences in Direct Sequence Spread Spectrum (DSSS), The model and performance of logistic and tent chaotic sequences applied in DSSS is analyzed. Firstly, the chaotic properties and correlation function characteristics of Logistic and Tent chaotic sequences are introduced, and their error rate formulas applied in direct sequence spread spectrum systems are analyzed. Then, two simulation models of simulink were built, and the simulation results verified the correctness of the theory.

articleTitle: High transmitter-receiver isolation design of wide-beam array antennas
abstract: High transmitter-receiver isolation design of wide-beam array antennas based on a continuous wave radar is proposed in this paper. It is composed of a transmit antenna, five receive antennas, absorbing materials, metallic plates and ground plane. By loading metallic plates near the transmit and receive antennas, laying absorbing materials in the ground plane, and designing the shielding performance of the antennas, this proposed design achieves a larger isolation, a wider frequency working range, a more compact size. Both the simulations and measurements have been conducted to verify the design performance. The array antennas have a transmitter-receiver isolation of 85 dB between 10GHz and 12GHz.

articleTitle: Joint tracking and shape estimation method for targets with micro-motions
abstract: This paper established a triangular model and a rectangular model for extended targets based on Extended Gaussian Image (EGI) and proposed a joint tracking and shape estimation method for targets with micro-motions. Traditional methods for extended object tracking based on the EGI directly make the orientation of the target a state parameter. However, in cases where the target exhibits micro-motions, it's challenging to get an appropriate dynamic model for the orientation. For this reason, this paper takes the cosine and sine values of the target's orientation as state parameters and establishes a dynamic model of the orientation of the target. The simulation experiments show that the proposed method can estimate the size and orientation of targets effectively and simultaneously and have promising prospects for engineering applications in joint target tracking and classification.

articleTitle: Water level variation of Hongze Lake measured by Tiangong-2 interferometric imaging radar altimeter
abstract: In recent decades, the application of satellite radar altimeters has been extended from oceans to inland waters, especially for monitoring the water level variation (WLV) of lakes and rivers. The Tiangong-2 interferometric imaging radar altimeter (TG2-InIRA), launched in 2016, is a Ku-Band two-channel interferometric radar, which mainly aims to measure the sea surface height (SSH), as well as inland water. As a new-generation satellite radar altimeter with a wide swath, TG2-InIRA can obtain three-dimensional images of water bodies and land simultaneously because it takes near-nadir incidence (1°~8°), short interferometric baseline, aperture synthesis and the height tracker. Based on TG2-InIRA's unique advantage, a section of the solid bank of the lake as the permanent scatter (PS) is used to calibrate the water level measurement, using the idea of differential interferometry. In this paper, we present our new extraction method on the lake's high-precision WLV and report experimental results using TG2-InIRA two-pass observations of Hongze Lake, which show good agreement with in-situ measurements. The preliminary results demonstrate the capability of TG2-InIRA for inland water WLV monitoring very well, and the feasibility of using a man-made controllable calibrator enabling higher precision WLV measurements for future satellite missions as well.

articleTitle: Theoretical analysis of layover unmixing based on the attributed scattering center model
abstract: To address the issue in traditional multi-baseline interferometric methods, where the physical properties and geometric dimensions of the target cannot be inversely solved simultaneously, this study introduces the three-dimensional attribute scattering center model, which is internationally widely applied in parametric modeling. Considering the problem of multiple solutions in target parameter inversion based on the attribute scattering center model, we introduce the information matrix to quantitatively characterize the amount of information in the data that affects parameter inversion. We utilize the Cramér-Rao lower bound (CRLB) to quantitatively calculate the accuracy limit of interferometric data in inversion and conduct experiments and results analysis from the perspective of parameter inversion accuracy. After deriving the theoretical lower bound of parameter inversion based on the attribute scattering center model, we calculate the minimum signal-to-noise ratio of interferometric data corresponding to the local scattering mechanism when inverting physical parameters and geometric parameters. The Orthogonal Matching Pursuit (OMP) method is employed for overlapping separation experiments to verify the accuracy of this theory. The theoretical boundary analysis method in the inversion of Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) interferometric data proposed in this study can provide a reference for the observation design and actual measurement data selection of interferometric synthetic aperture radar.

articleTitle: Low-complexity algorithm for massive MIMO radar joint transmit waveform and receive filter design
abstract: This paper investigates the problem of joint transmit waveform and receive filter design for massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) radar equipped with one-bit digital-to-analog converters (DACs). In the presence of signal-dependent interferences, we formulate the optimization problem by maximizing the output signal to interference and noise ratio (SINR) of massive MIMO radar subject to one-bit waveform constraint. To effectively address this problem, we propose an alternating optimization method (AOM) that offers low computational complexity and memory consumption. Finally, simulation results show that the proposed method outperforms the state-of-the-art methods and can be applied to massive MIMO radar with hundreds or even thousands of antennas.

articleTitle: Multichannel spaceborne SAR squinted sliding spotlight imaging with nonlinear chirp scaling
abstract: The multichannel Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) squinted sliding spotlight data is difficult to process due to the extended Doppler spectrum and the spatial varied range cell migration. Conventional algorithms solve this problem by spectrum reconstruction and nonlinear chirp scaling to achieve a low resolution imaging with a three-order slant range model. However, in the case of a higher resolution case, e.g. 0.5 m, most existing conventional algorithms will fail due to insufficient accuracy. In this paper, a modified imaging algorithm based on a fourth-order slant range model is presented for the high-resolution multichannel spaceborne SAR squinted sliding spotlight imaging. Azimuth preprocess is firstly applied to recover an unambiguous azimuth spectrum. Based on the more accurate slant range model, a novel azimuth nonlinear chirp scaling process is proposed to compensate the phase more precisely, achieving a higher resolution imaging. The accuracy of the proposed algorithm is verified by the point simulation.

articleTitle: Unimodular sequence set design with low weighted correlation properties
abstract: In radar systems, there is a demand for the unimodular sequence set that exhibit excellent weighted correlation properties. In this paper, we propose an effective algorithm based on the memetic algorithm to minimize the weighted integrated sidelobe level (WISL) of the unimodular sequence set. The proposed algorithm takes evolutionary algorithm as the global search algorithm and majorization-minimization algorithm as the local refinement algorithm to design the unimodular sequence set. Compared to the previously proposed algorithms, this algorithm explores the solution space and improves solution accuracy more efficiently, leading to the attainment of the unimodular sequence set with significantly improved weighted correlation properties. Simulation results verify the performance of the proposed algorithm, which demonstrates that the proposed algorithm can generate the unimodular sequence set with much better weighted correlation properties compared with existing algorithms. In addition, the influence of key parameters on the performance of the proposed algorithm is investigated.

articleTitle: A design of phase-compensated periodic FMCW toward range estimation with limited bandwidth
abstract: The integration of range estimation architectures and communication frameworks has constituted a prevalent research point during the previous years, as the two mentioned systems are usually individually deployed to avoid potential disruption, which cause unexpected waste on spectrum and hardware resource. By restricting the bandwidth of the range estimation waveform, the communication system can transmit the waveform to complete range estimation. For this purpose, a phase-compensated periodic frequency modulated continuous wave (PC-PFMCW) is proposed to provide high-accuracy range estimation. The periodic waveform resembles an overlapped FMCW sequence which is sampled at a relatively low frequency and the process of range estimation with the periodic waveform is analyzed to propose a corresponding phase compensation algorithm. Simulations of the proposed scheme have been carried out, suggesting that the PC-PFMCW enables better range estimation accuracy than the typical FMCW under the same limited bandwidth. In the simulated situation where the PC-PFMCW with 10 MHz bandwidth is compared with a 1GHz FMCW, the result shows they can reach the same performance limitation of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−5</sup> while the 10 MHz narrow-band FMCW could not. A potential reason of phase compensation algorithm being sensitive to noise and the promising applications of PC-PFMCW have been discussed.

articleTitle: Design and implemenation of GNSS-INBSAR real-time preprocessing system based on SOC
abstract: The GNSS-InBSAR system, based on navigation satellites, utilizes on-orbit satellites as transmitters and combines radar with navigation signals to achieve continuous deformation monitoring of large-scale scenes. Due to the weak signal-to-noise ratio, low resolution, and poor coherence of the reflected signals from the scene, traditional reflection signal processing algorithms are time-consuming and inefficient in data processing. This paper designs and implements a real-time preprocessing system for GNSS-InBSAR based on SoC. It proposes a time-frequency phase synchronization method based on direct waves and segmented pulse compression technology. The problem of insufficient signal processing resources for multi-frequency point and multi-channel signals is solved through FFT multiplexing technology. The CORDIC algorithm is used to calculate compensation phase, improving phase accuracy. The proposed methods are validated in MATLAB. Finally, the reflection signal pulse compression results and backprojection (BP) imaging performance were tested and validated. The test results indicate that the system can efficiently and stably perform synchronous acquisition and preprocessing of direct wave and echo signals from 3 frequency points and 8 channels. SAR images with high point density and resolution are obtained through azimuth accumulation based on the preprocessed data, meeting the accuracy requirements for deformation measurement of large-scale scenes.

articleTitle: Efficient implementation of BP imaging algorithm on FPGA
abstract: The Back Projection (BP) imaging algorithm severely affects the efficiency of radar imaging operations due to its high computational complexity. As a parallel processor, Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) has significant advantages in parallel data processing. Therefore, this paper uses FPGA as the processing platform to optimize the BP imaging algorithm and shorten data processing time by setting reasonable parallel pipelines, fixed-point floating-point data, and on-chip memory technology. The proposed method validated the data through BP imaging processing and compared it with different methods, verifying the efficiency of the proposed method and achieving a large acceleration ratio, which to some extent improved the imaging processing efficiency.

articleTitle: Research on modelling motion echo and motion intention recognition of helicopter
abstract: This paper establishes and analyses a helicopter motion echo model. Based on the scattering coefficient and distribution of scattering points on helicopter blades, a helicopter motion micro motion echo model was constructed by establishing multiple coordinate systems, constructing a state matrix for transformation between coordinate systems, and vector decomposition of target velocity. Using the model for echo simulation, from the time-frequency results of the simulation, it can be seen that the micro motion echo of the helicopter will change when accelerating or decelerating, so there is a possibility of the helicopter's motion intention being recognized. Based on this characteristic, several machine learning algorithms and convolutional neural networks are used to identify the motion intention of helicopters. Simulation results show that the algorithm can effectively determine the motion intention of helicopters in a very short time, thereby further determining the combat intention of helicopters.

articleTitle: Method and implementation of region proposals extraction for complex scenes
abstract: Land remote sensing images are large in width, low in effective object density and complex in distribution. Using the existing detection strategies to finely process each pixel of the remote sensing images is difficult to meet the detection needs of high accuracy and fast speed for some tasks. It is necessary to extract regions proposals effectively. To this end, this paper designs a classification network based on embedded linear expansion features to achieve fast and accurate screening of region proposals. Specifically, we first optimally design the embedded linear expansion feature module to achieve lightweight convolution; secondly, we design the residual structure of the embedded linear expansion feature through the stacking module, to effectively extract feature; finally, we construct a classification network based on the embedded linear expansion feature through the combination of the proposed residual structure, which can classify the sliced image quickly and extract the region proposals effectively. The test results on the public dataset DOTA show that the proposed method with suitable detection has a significant improvement in accuracy and speed compared to the baseline model YOLOV4, with a 4% improvement in mAP and a reduction in computation to 16.8 times of the original.

articleTitle: An efficient fast factorized back-projected algorithm for bistatic forward-looking SAR imaging
abstract: Benefit from the flexible bistatic layout, bistatic forward-looking synthetic aperture radar (BFSAR) can form comprehensive observation of the forward-looking scene for a long duration. In the proposed algorithm, by using unified elliptical polar coordinate, the correction function of sub-aperture wavenumber-domain spectrum centre is derived to eliminate spectrum folding. Azimuth one-dimensional interpolation is applied to achieve coherent fusion of sub-images, and high-resolution forward-looking SAR images are obtained. Compared with conventional fast factorized back-projection (FFBP) algorithm, the proposed algorithm uses one-dimensional interpolation in a unified elliptical polar coordinate instead of two-dimensional interpolation in the local coordinate to improve efficiency. The simulations validate the superiorities of the proposed algorithm by comparing with the FFBP algorithm.

articleTitle: The design of RF-digital integrated microsystem for remote sensing applications
abstract: A RF-digital integrated microsystem has been designed according to the real-time processing requirements of intelligent and earth observation remote sensing tasks. Based on the RF-digital hybrid design of an ABF substrate and the RF-digital integration fusion design methodology, we realised an RF-digital integrated microsystem capable of converting RF signals into digital codes. Four-receiver and four-transmitter transceiver channels, programmable logic, processor, DDR, Flash and various interfaces are integrated into the microsystem. In response to the needs of ground-based remote sensing, airborne detection, small-satellite Earth observation and other tasks, the microsystem is suitable for ground-based rain radar, small-satellite SAR and other equipment. The application of this product can reduce the volume and weight of remote sensing payloads by more than 30 percents, and the cost of batch production can be reduced by more than 30 percents.

articleTitle: A dense false target jamming suppression method based on inter-pulse phase agility waveform
abstract: As a typical form of jamming, long-range support jamming with full-pulse dense forwarding, which has both blanketing and deception effects, significantly degrades the target detection performance of radar. Since long-range support jamming lags behind the target, this paper utilizes the range-gating characteristics of the inter-pulse phase agility waveform. It exploits the differences in energy distribution within the range-Doppler domain to distinguish between jamming and the target, facilitating the separation and reconstruction of both jamming and the target through alternating projection. Simulation results validate that the proposed method accurately reconstructs both jamming and the target, leading to a significant improvement in the Signal-to-Interference-plus-Noise Ratio (SINR) in the scene of strong jamming.

articleTitle: Coherent processing method for frequency agile radar
abstract: Coherent processing of frequency agile waveform can cause underdetermined estimation problems. Traditional matched filtering results in high sidelobes covering weak targets, which unable to satisfy the high-precision requirements of radar. This paper proposes a coherent processing method based on low-rank matrix completion to solve the underdetermined estimation problem for frequency agile waveform coherent processing. Firstly, this method formulates a model for the frequency agile waveform echo signal and represents it using a sparse observation matrix in the frequency domain. To ensure the low -rank of sparse observation matrix, we reconstruct the observation matrix into dual Hankel configurations. Then, the sparse observation matrix is efficiently reconstructed using matrix completion method based on Alternating Direction Multiplier Method, resolving the underdetermined estimation challenges arisen from coherent processing of frequency agile waveform. Finally, by means of simulation experiments, the effectiveness and feasibility of the proposed method based on matrix completion was validated.

articleTitle: Integrated sensing and communication system based on BOK-SLFM signal
abstract: To enhance the ranging accuracy of automotive radar and the utilization of spectrum resources, this paper introduces a novel integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems. The proposed system employs multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) radar to transmit a sequence of narrowband binary orthogonal keying stepped linear frequency modulation (BOK-SLFM) signals. At the radar receiver, we use the de-chirp time-domain wideband synthesis (DTWSS) algorithm to synthesize a wideband signal. At the communication receiver, we decode the binary data using matched filtering. Simulations results show that the synthetic wideband signal can improve the ranging accuracy by 4.28 dB and enhance the range resolution by 1.94 times compared to single SLFM signal under the parameters established in this paper. Furthermore, the information transmission rate is amplified by the number of antennas relative to traditional BOK communication.

articleTitle: Spaceborne active positioning and accuracy analysis using TDOA
abstract: Radar positioning is divided into active positioning and passive positioning according to different working modes. Active positioning has higher positioning accuracy. Passive positioning has more concealment. Combining the advantages of active detection and passive detection, and considering both range and angle constraint information, an active location model using time difference of arrival (AL-TDOA) based on spaceborne multi-static radar is proposed in this paper. Based on one transmit multiple receive radar system, passive time difference of arrival(TDOA) information is used to locate aerial targets in this model. From the point of view of geometric dilution of precision (GDOP), expressions of location accuracy for AL-TDOA location of one transmit three receive radar system are derived in detail. The expressions of location accuracy for active location and TDOA location are also given. Through the simulation, the positioning accuracy of AL-TDOA positioning, active positioning and TDOA positioning is compared and analyzed. It is found that the positioning accuracy of AL-TDOA is significantly higher than that of active positioning and far higher than that of TDOA positioning. Under the simulation conditions of this paper, compared with active location, the maximum location error of AL-TDOA is reduced by 30.5%, and the minimum location error is reduced by 15.8%.

articleTitle: Chaff jamming recognition based on pulse Doppler radar
abstract: In order to effectively combat the adverse effect of chaff jamming on ship detection by pulse Doppler rad ar, a chaff jamming recognition method based on range-Doppler image and deep target detection network is proposed in this paper. The chaff cloud diffusion model and the echo model of pulse Doppler radar are established, and the differences of two-dimensional range-Doppler images between ship target and chaff jamming echo are analysed. On this basis, convolutional neural network is utilized to extract the deep features of the image, and the classification and localization of chaff jamming are completed automatically. The performance of the model is verified by simulation and measured data. The results show that the proposed method can effectively solve the problem of chaff jamming recognition under high jamming to noise ratio, and the jamming range-Doppler information provided by the detection results is helpful for jamming suppression.

articleTitle: Space-surface bistatic SAR tomography: a promising approach for accurate local 3D reconstruction
abstract: With a flexibly deployed receiver, space-surface bistatic Synthetic Aperture Radar (SS-BiSAR) can increase the observation sensitivity in the north-south direction, which is a promising method for local high-precision three-dimensional deformation retrieval. However, in urban areas, the layover effect hinders the determination of the dominant scatterer in each resolution cell. Multi-baseline SAR tomography is an effective approach to solving overlaid scatterers. This paper presents the first experiment result of SS-BiSAR tomography. By estimating and removing the interferometric fringes, the repeat-track orbit errors are effectively corrected. The experiment was conducted based on the first L-band spaceborne twin SAR - the Chinese Lutan-1 (LT-1). A total of 11 repeat-track SAR images were acquired, and three-dimensional point clouds of a building area was recovered, with an accuracy of approximately 4 meters.

articleTitle: Satellite-missile bistatic forward-looking SAR imaging of ship target via hybrid SAR-ISAR algorithm
abstract: Satellite-missile bistatic SAR system can realize forward-looking imaging that cannot be achieved by monostatic SAR systems. In addition, the satellite can irradiate a wide range of scenes on the ground as a transmitter, which has a high military and civilian value. However, most research on the satellite missile bistatic SAR focuses on the imaging of static targets, the research on maneuvering target imaging is relatively less. In this article, a hybrid SAR-ISAR algorithm for ship target imaging in the satellite missile bistatic SAR system is proposed. Firstly, the modelling method of satellite missile bistatic SAR system based on coordinate system conversion is introduced. On this basis, the echo signal model is given and analysed. Next, the hybrid SAR-ISAR imaging method is described at length. Finally, the efficiency of the hybrid SAR-ISAR method is demonstrated by simulation results of the imaging of a ship target.

articleTitle: A ship detection method based on YOLOv7 in range-compressed SAR data
abstract: Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) is an exceptionally effective imaging technology capable of acquiring ground information regardless of weather conditions and time of day. SAR finds extensive applications in target detection, tracking, and recognition. Despite its wide imaging coverage and high resolution, ship target detection images face several challenges. The most prominent challenge is that both traditional methods such as constant false alarm rate (CFAR) detection and deep neural network methods require complex and time-consuming imaging processing, including but not limited to range migration correction and pulse compression processes. Consequently, real-time detection becomes arduous, leading to delayed results for subsequent applications such as target monitoring and tracking. To address this issue, this study proposes a novel ship detection method that leverages deep learning techniques along with range-compressed data from SAR images to enhance immediate target perception with a convolutional neural network algorithm. The aim is to improve the accurac y and timeliness of ship detection tasks. Given the limited availability of literature on this subject matter, this paper aims to provide an analysis of the proposed method's effectiveness through experimental results while also discussing future prospects.

articleTitle: Ship detection based on feature fusion for dual-pol SAR images
abstract: Ship detection in synthetic aperture radar (SAR) data, utilizing CNN-based detectors, has yielded remarkable results across diverse domains. These detectors swiftly identify targets in intricate marine settings by extracting and comprehending sample features, including structural and textural elements. However, in the face of the issue of complex image quality, there is still room for improvement in their detection performance. To this end, we propose a ship detection method based on feature fusion for dual-pol SAR images. This approach involves the rational exploration of complementary information concealed within co- polarization and cross-polarization images through the designed joint feature mining, cross enhancement module, and adaptive gate fusion module. It enhances and fuses the polarization features and feeds them into the detection head for regression, effectively reducing false alarms and comprehensively improving detection performance. Experiments on dual-polarization SAR datasets demonstrate its effectiveness and state-of-the-art performance.

articleTitle: Monopulse forward-looking 3D imaging algorithm based on STFT
abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) imaging of the forward-looking target is of great benefit for identifying and striking the target. However, due to the narrow Doppler bandwidth, the traditional high-resolution imaging techniques cannot be employed for the forward-looking imaging. The 3D information of forward-looking targets can be obtained by the monopulse technique, but there are also some problems, such as the angular glint. To solve these problems, this paper proposes a novel monopulse forward-looking 3D imaging algorithm based on the Short-Time Fourier Transform (STFT). Firstly, the STFT is utilized for each range unit of the three-channel compressed data and the results are spliced. Then the unit whose amplitude exceeds the threshold value in the sum channel is selected, and its azimuth and elevation angles are obtained by the monopulse technique. Finally, the energy projection is carried out to realize the 3D reconstruction of the target. The proposed method has the advantages of short accumulation time, low calculation, and high-quality results, and is conducive to the real-time imaging and target recognition. The simulation experiment is performed to demonstrate the validity of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Moving target detection based on a reduced-dimensional model in FDA-MIMO radar
abstract: In this paper, we study the problem of moving target detection for frequency diverse array multiple-input multiple-output (FDA-MIMO) radar in a Gaussian noise environment with an insufficient training data set. To address this issue, we adopt a reduced-dimensional method for constructing a novel data model to decrease the amount of training data required. Then, based on the new model, two detectors are proposed according to the generalized likelihood ratio test (GLRT) criterion, both one-step and two-step. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed detectors achieve good detection performance in the case of limited training data, validating the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Analysis of phase space-varing characteristics of circular aperture micro-deformation monitoring radar
abstract: Ground-based micro-deformation monitoring radar can be used for slope landslide monitoring and disaster emergency rescue in open-pit mines. Its outward circular imaging mode is being more and more widely used due to its all-round observation advantages. Aiming at the problem that the existing imaging processing mainly adopts oblique plane imaging, and the imaging quality is difficult to improve, this paper deeply analyses the relationship between the imaging quality and the influence of target elevation information under the circular imaging mode of ground-based micro-deformation monitoring radar. Firstly, the circular imaging geometric model of ground-based micro-deformation monitoring radar for stereo observation geometry is established, and the corresponding imaging echo model is given. Secondly, through theoretical deduction and computer simulation, we analysed the law of phase history changing with target elevation information. The space-varying phenomenon of the circular imaging target phase of the ground-based micro-deformation monitoring radar is confirmed. Finally, the imaging effect before and after considering the target elevation information is given by point target simulation, and the quantitative relationship between imaging focusing quality and pitch angle change in imaging observation is given.

articleTitle: A fast back-projection algorithm based on equivalent slant range model for high-squint SAR imaging
abstract: Because back-projection algorithm (BPA) is independent of the azimuth-invariant hypothesis of the echo signal, it has significant advantages for synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imaging with arbitrary trajectory. Although Cartesian fast back-projection algorithm (CFBPA) is proposed to improve the efficiency of BPA, for high-squint SAR (HS-SAR) imaging, the geometric configuration of HS-SAR greatly enhances the space-variant property of the spectrum, which leads to the ineffectively compressed spectrum and decreases the efficiency of the sub-image merging in CFBPA processing. In this paper, an equivalent slant range model (ESRM) based on hybrid coordinate system (HCS) is proposed for HS-SAR imaging. Benefiting from the designed ESRM, the space-variant property of the wavenumber spectrum can be significantly degraded to improve performance in spectrum compression and accelerates the sub-image merging. Promising results from simulation experiments are provided to validate the high performance of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: SAR tomography in urban areas: an approach based on sparse spectrum fitting
abstract: Tomography Synthetic Aperture Radar (TomoSAR) technology, as an extension of Interferometric SAR (InSAR), solves the inherent layover problem and provides three-dimensional (3D) imaging ability. Now, it is a promising technique in urban management and critical situation detection. However, in practical applications, the sparse and non-uniform distribution characteristics of the repeat-pass baselines make TomoSAR face the problem of low resolution and high sidelobes, which affect the 3D imaging effect. To address the above problems, a sparse spectrum fitting (SpSF) based TomoSAR processing approach is proposed in this paper. Compared with the traditional spatial spectrum estimation method, this method can achieve higher resolution and lower sidelobes, which is a significant advantage. The proposed method is also validated using computer simulation and the TerraSAR-X real data.

articleTitle: Polarization parameters estimation of radar jamming via four-probe two-dimensional golden section
abstract: Accurate estimation of polarization parameters of jamming signals is usually necessary for implementing effective radar anti-jamming measures in polarization domain. To improve estimation performance, this paper proposes a four-probe two-dimensional golden section method (FPGSM) based on the peak-to-sidelobe level (PSL) of the jamming signals. The mixed echo signal model of target and jamming is firstly built by the polarization representation method. Then, the four-probe two- dimensional golden section based jamming parameter evaluation model and its procedure is presented. The simulation results demonstrate that the proposed improved algorithm can achieve an estimation accuracy of over 90%, as well as a good resistance against noise.

articleTitle: Improved YOLOv5 for concealed object detection in human body millimeter wave images
abstract: Millimeter-wave radar is penetrating, can detect all kinds of items hidden under clothing, and does not have ionizing radiation, harmless to the human body, in recent years has been widely used in the field of security inspection. There is imaging noise in the millimeter wave security image, which will have an impact on the detection performance of small targets, and small targets carry little information, which can easily lead to information loss in the process of feature extraction, resulting in misdetection and missed detection. To address this problem, this paper improves the target detection model based on YOLOv5 by introducing the Double Attention module in the C3 module to better acquire the spatial global features; updating the original convolutional structure to the SPD-conv module, which reduces the loss of fine-grained information and thus improves the detection accuracy of the small targets; and finally, on the basis of the original detector head, replacing the de tector head for detecting large objects is replaced by the detection head for detecting extremely small targets. Experiments on the AMMW image dataset show that the improved model in this paper has significant improvement over the baseline model.

articleTitle: Intra-pulse modulation feature analysis and parameter estimation of phase and frequency multi-modulation signal
abstract: The parameter inversion of multi-modulation waveforms has always been a key and difficult problem in the field of electronic reconnaissance. To solve this problem, a method for intra-pulse modulation feature analysis and parameter estimation of phase and frequency multi-modulation signal is proposed in this paper. Firstly, we apply square preprocessing to eliminate the binary phase coded modulation information. Then, subpulse separation and subpulse parameter estimation are achieved by using the smooth pseudo-Wigner Ville distribution (SPWVD) and wavelet transform. Moreover, histogram statistics are introduced to improve the robustness of the method. Finally, the N-order phase difference is proposed for recovering binary phase coded sequences. Frequency domain filtering and sliding window averaging are also added to further improve the applicability of the proposed method under low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) conditions. Simulation results suggest that the method proposed in this paper can achieve accurate signal inversion and has good robustness.

articleTitle: Deep iterative network-based permittivity inversions for ground penetrating radar data
abstract: Ground penetrating radar full wave inversion offers high-resolution subsurface models but faces challenges of computational cost and sensitivity to initial values, constraining practical utility. This paper introduces AUFWI-Net, a novel method employing a learnable deep iterative network for joint full waveform inversion. AUFWI-Net converts GPR waveform inversion into a regularized optimization task, minimizing differences between simulated and observed waveforms. Employing a variational framework and rotation strategy, the complex optimization is deconstructed into three sub-problems, each with derived update formulas. These formulas are integrated into a neural network structure, where each phase addresses a sub- problem. Combined phases create a model-driven deep iterative unfolding network, enhancing GPR data inversion. Simulation outcomes underscore AUFWI-Net's efficacy, significantly improving permittivity inversion accuracy compared to alternatives, while meeting real-time application demands.

articleTitle: RFISM-Net: an interference segmentation and mitigation network for SAR
abstract: The existence of radio frequency interference (RFI) severely degrades the synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imaging quality and the subsequent image interpretation accuracy. To eliminate the effects of RFI on SAR, we present an RFI segmentation and mitigation method based on generative adversarial networks (RFISM-Net). The RFISM-Net consists of an RFI segmentation network, an RFI mitigation network, and an RFI adversarial network. The RFI segmentation network outputs the RFI position in the time-frequency domain. The RFI mitigation network can mitigate RFI and generate RFI-free SAR echo. Meanwhile, the RFI segmentation network shares the feature extraction network with the RFI mitigation network, which significantly boosts the RFI mitigation performance. The RFI adversarial network is designed to evaluate RFI mitigation performance and further improve the fidelity of RFI-free SAR echo. The effectiveness and superiority of the RFISM-Net are verified on the measured SAR data recorded by Sentinel-1 in the TOPS mode.

articleTitle: Quadrature phase-coded signal model and signal processing method for frequency diverse array radar
abstract: Frequency diverse array (FDA) radar can generate a three-dimensional time-range-angle correlation beam pattern. To address signal processing challenges in FDA radar systems, this paper constructs an array structure consisting of an FDA transmitter and a phased array receiver, while also establishing a signal model based on quadrature phase-coded signal. This paper presents the derivation of a signal model for point target echoes. Employing orthogonal matched filtering on the received signal for range dimensional echo separation, the echo signal is weighted in both the range and angle dimensions, enabling concurrent separation of sources situated at varying distances and angles. Simulations confirm the effectiveness of the proposed signal processing method.

articleTitle: Distributed joint sensor registration and resolvable-group target tracking based on hypergraph matching theory
abstract: The paper addresses the problem of distributed resolvable-group target tracking (RTT) over a peer-to-peer sensor network with different coordinates. In the local filtering stage, each sensor node employs the labeled multi-Bernoulli (LMB) filter. In the fusion stage, the presence of coordinate system differences, also known as drift, hinders direct fusion and can lead to diverging tracking performance. To address this issue, we propose a scheme called the distributed joint sensor registration a nd RTT (DJSR-RTT). Specifically, we first perform state estimates and then minimize the Wasserstein distance of different RFSs to find the matched targets, which is a prerequisite for estimating the drifts. To effectively estimate the drifts, we combine the hypergraph matching (HM) theory with Hungarian assignment. Lastly, the pairwise fusion under the generalized covariance intersection (GCI) rule is performed based on the calibrated coordinates. Simulation experiments are provided to validate the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: A domain adaptation detector for heterogenous SAR image object detection
abstract: Heterogenous Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) image object detection is the key to solve the challenge of inconsistent data distribution between the training and test sets, which is usually tackled with domain adaptation (DA) method. In response to the lack of prominence in detection accuracy of existing methods, this paper proposes a novel DA SAR image object detector. We utilize self-supervised learning to alleviate the problem of lack of ground truth in the target domain. First, the region with the highest detection confidence is identified in each target domain SAR image as the initial pseudo label. Then, the identified regions are cropped and a collection of their enhanced versions is generated and these enhanced versions are combined into a synthetic image. Next, the synthetic SAR images are used to adapt the network to the target domain. The experimental results confirm that the proposed method achieves the best detection performance among all state-of-the-art methods.

articleTitle: Design of SAR imaging system based on MPSoC + FPGA with optimization strategies for chirp scaling factor computation
abstract: Space-based remote sensing involves complex SAR imaging hardware design. This complexity arises from varied imaging modes and a convoluted imaging process. With the rapid advancement of embedded systems and Field Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGA), underscores their flexibility, efficiency, and reconfigurability for SAR imaging hardware implementation. This paper introduces a comprehensive SAR imaging system based on Multi-Processor System on Chip (MPSoC) and FPGA architectures. The system supports a multi-modal SAR imaging processing platform with large granularity, encompassing orbital parameter pro-cessing, Chirp Scaling (CS) factor computation, data transposition, complex multiplication, and FFT operations. An effi-cient data link between the host computer, MPSoC, and FPGA is also established. To address the challenges of multiple parameters, intricate computational flow, and various computational types in Chirp Scaling factor generation, the system utilizes Cortex A53 and Cortex R5 processors for computation and optimization. The results indicate an average accelera-tion ratio of 25.296, a relative error of 1.12×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-4</sup>, and an absolute error of 5.88×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup>, demonstrating that the “MPSoC+FPGA”-based imaging system meets the demands of imaging processing.

articleTitle: Rapid three-dimensional reconstruction for micro-motion target based on the low-rank state-space
abstract: This paper proposes a rapid three-dimensional (3D) reconstruction method for micro-motion target based on the low-rank state-space (LRSS). Firstly, considering the low-rank characteristics of the target echo data, an improved state-space algorithm based on randomized singular value decomposition (rSVD) is utilized to efficiently extract micro-range and micro-velocity information of the target. Then, the labeled multi-Bernoulli filter (LMB) algorithm accurately associates micro-range information from multiple scattering centers. Subsequently, a low-rank characteristic-based factorization 3D reconstruction algorithm is proposed for achieving 3D reconstruction of target scattering center positions. Finally, the experimental results on the real scenario verify the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Cultivated land extraction using short time series LT-1 SAR images
abstract: SAR images has been increasingly used in cultivated land extraction for less weather impact. It is common to apply long time series SAR to identify cultivated land and analyze its growing changes. However, within a short period, the growing change itself can be a key feature for cultivated land extraction. Therefore, in this research, we propose a method for extracting cultivated land through short time series SAR images (CLSTSS). We chose only three single polarization LT -1 images from April to June to form the times series. Then we conducted principal component analyse to get concentrated information of original images, and calculated texture features on it. Finally, support vector machine was utilized to obtain the cultivated land map. The results show that our proposed method performed well in cultivated land extraction, with a precision of 77.31% and a recall of 87.37%. And it can greatly improve the classification precision by single polarization SAR. Although in the fixed period, more images and shorter time interval can slightly improve the results, the significant increase in image costs is not conducive to regularly monitoring large areas of cultivated land. Hence, CLSTSS is very suitable. Besides, this research also demonstrates wider application prospects of LT-1.

articleTitle: Research on broadband undersampling ISAR Imaging method for vehicle targets
abstract: ISAR imaging of vehicle targets often faces complex multi-target scenes and wide band undersampling problem. In this case, the performance of traditional imaging algorithms is degraded or even invalid. This paper proposes an imaging method that combines UAMP-SBL algorithm, image domain line detection, minimum entropy criterion, and particle swarm optimization algorithm to address the issues of broadband undersampling and multi target imaging in vehicle target ISAR imaging. Firstly, the compressed sensing model of wide band undersampling signal is established, and then the complete echo of multiple targets is reconstructed by using UAMP-SBL algorithm; Based on the line detection in image domain, the first order phase term coefficient of each sub target are estimated to achieve coarse alignment of sub target envelope. Then, the joint parameter estimation of the remaining first-order and second-order phase terms of the sub target is completed based on the minimum entropy criterion and particle swarm optimization algorithm to achieve accurate alignment of the envelope of the sub target . Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is demonstrated by the simulations.

articleTitle: SAR ATR based on a deep feature fusion network with limited measured data
abstract: Deep neural networks have achieved remarkable success in the field of synthetic aperture radar (SAR) automatic target recognition (ATR). However, these algorithms face the challenge of limited SAR labeled data. Some researchers have developed methods for creating synthetic SAR data to overcome this issue. Furthermore, most of the existing research is based on network structures designed for optical images, which only considering the correlation between synthetic and measured data in amplitude. Therefore, we propose an approach based on a deep feature fusion network to fully utilize the information of SAR images, including amplitude, phase, and azimuth angle. With the aim to further improve the recognition accuracy with limited measured data, a transfer learning method is used to link the knowledge learned from synthetic data to measured data. Comparative experiments on the SAMPLE dataset demonstrate the superior performance of the proposed method when dealing with limited measured data in the SAR target recognition.

articleTitle: A sparse-prior-based dataset expansion method for microwave radar imaging
abstract: The deep neural networks (DNNs) are widely used to radar imaging problems in recent years. However, compared to the optical vision field, there are limited number of datasets for microwave radar imaging. Aiming at the lack of dataset, a novel method is proposed to convert the optical dataset. Based on the well-known assumption of target scattering centers, a Bernoulli-Gaussian distributed mask is added to the coefficients so that they possess the sparsity of targets’ scatterers in the microwave frequency band, hence, the optical targets become suitable for microwave radar imaging. Then, based on an imaging scenario with array radar, a two-channel DNN is proposed to validate the feasibility of the dataset expansion method. After training, the DNN could output high-quality imaging results compared to the traditional imaging method while largely decreases the computational complexity. The effectiveness of the proposed dataset expansion method is verified, and this method can also be widely applied to different kinds of microwave radar imaging problems.

articleTitle: Fast multiscale SAR images stitching based on improved APAP and OTSU algorithms
abstract: In marine synthetic aperture radar (SAR) remote sensing images, the land and ships often only occupy part of the images, and the rest are ocean or coastal backgrounds. Existing SAR image stitching algorithms often directly detect the entire SAR image, which consumes a lot of computing resources. In this paper, an automatic image stitching algorithm based on the As-Projective- As-Possible (APAP) and Otsu algorithm is proposed. Firstly, a new method of image size alignment is proposed to make multiple images have the same size for subsequent processing steps. Secondly, a threshold segmentation method is used to detect the positions of land or ships and filter out most of the sea backgrounds to reduce the computational requirements. Thirdly, a phase correlation algorithm is used to calculate the phase correlation between different images for determining the optimal stitching order and the scale-invariant feature transform (SIFT) algorithm is used to detect feature points from the thresholded images. Finally, the APAP algorithm is employed to perform the actual stitching at the source SAR image level using the order and feature points measured before, using the previously measured order and feature points. Experimental results conducted on the SSDD dataset demonstrate that the performance of our method is close to that of the traditional stitching algorithm, but the number of feature points and time are reduced by 46.83% and 27.87% of the traditional method, respectively.

articleTitle: Reinforcement learning based time-domain mutual interference avoidance for automotive radar
abstract: Due to the extensive usage of automotive radars on vehicles, mutual interference among radars on the road is becoming considerable. To address this, we propose a time domain strategy based on deep reinforcement learning (DRL). This approach helps avoid mutual interference for automotive radars in the time domain without extra communications. The numerical simulation results demonstrate that the proposed approach can avoid interference as effectively as frequency hopping. Moreover, the time domain strategy has more advantages than frequency hopping when encountering dynamic interference.

articleTitle: Influence of aperture fill time of wideband interference on anti-jamming method of multi-channel SAR
abstract: In the process of multi-channel SAR interference suppression, if the interference is wideband signal, the problem that the aperture fill time leads to the degradation of interference suppression performance should be considered. The incidence angle and bandwidth will affect aperture fill time and resulting distance gate offset between the signals received by each channel. Under the conditions of simulation experiment and measured data applied in this paper, when the signal bandwidth is 68MHz, whatever the incidence angle, the distance deviation is always less than one distance gate. In this case, the interference can be directly suppressed by ADBF. The output SNR after ADBF is not much different, and INR is reduced by about 14dB, indicating that ADBF can effectively suppress the interference without affecting the target signal. When the signal bandwidth is 150MHz, the distance gate offset begins to appear when the signal incidence angle is greater than 45°. At this time, the output SINR obtained by using ADBF-TDL to suppress interference is approximately 3dB higher than that obtained by ADBF method, and the TDL order-number is comprehensively determined by the interference suppression effect and the actual engineering application requirements.

articleTitle: Analysis of shipborne cross-eye jamming combined with range-gate pull-off jamming
abstract: Two-element retrodirective cross-eye jamming (TRCEJ), with its strong capability to counter monopulse radars, is well-suited for integration into ship platforms to enhance their self-defense ability. For a TRCEJ system installed on a ship, its jamming echoes must contend with the ship's skin echoes, imposing a stringent requirement for the jammer-to-signal ratio (JSR). Additionally, TRCEJ necessitates a long antenna baseline as the longer baseline introduces greater angular error in monopulse radars. However, the increased baseline length further differentiates the range information between the ship's skin echo and the jamming echo. Consequently, the range gate of the monopulse radar may capture the former but omit the latter, thus disabling the TRCEJ. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a combined jamming system that integrates range-gate pull-off (RGPO) into TRCEJ, referred to as CJRT, to achieve distance-angle joint deception. The structure of this jamming system is presented, along with a description of its three-stage jamming process. A mathematical model is developed to analyze the jamming performance in a conventional scenario. Simulation results demonstrate that the CJRT system is free from the baseline length restriction and induces greater angular error with less stringent requirements for parameter tolerance and JSR compared to the traditional TRCEJ.

articleTitle: 3D sparse imaging and point cloud enhancement for low sampling rates
abstract: Three-dimensional synthetic radar high-resolution imaging is widely used in indoor navigation, terrain detection and autonomous driving due to its low impact by certain natural conditions. In this paper, we use radar to acquire target echoes and combine compressed sensing (CS) based imaging method and deep learning network to extract a point cloud of the detected target. By combining the sparse imaging algorithm with the Iterative Shrinkage Thresholding Algorithm (ISTA), we acquire a sparse point cloud of the imaged target; we infer the feature profile information of the target through the point cloud up-sampling network, and ultimately obtain enhanced imaging results in point cloud acquisition at low sampling rates.

articleTitle: SAR ship target recognition combined with global scattering association features
abstract: Ship target recognition in SAR images has long been a focal issue in marine surveillance. Many scholars only improve the structure and loss function of deep learning networks and directly apply them to the field of SAR ship image interpretation, ignoring the ship target characteristics and scattering mechanisms, which cannot characterize the accurate feature of the target. To comprehensively characterize these features, a novel method combined with global scattering association features for SAR ship recognition is proposed. Firstly, fine segmentation is employed to separate the ship target from the background. Secondly, a local graph structure of the extracted scattering centers (SCs) is constructed by k Nearest Neighbors (KNN) algorithm, and then the global scattering topology structure of the ship can be represented by associating the local graph structure with edgeconv method. In addition, the deep features of the high-dimensional layer are extracted based on the improved A-ConvNet. Finally, the global scattering association features and deep features are fused to improve the recognition performance. Experimental results based on the FUSAR ship dataset demonstrate that the proposed method significantly enhances recognition performance compared to other classical approaches, thereby verifying the effectiveness of the proposed method in SAR ship target recognition.

articleTitle: ASC-SMCNN: SAR target classification method guided by attribute scattering center and separability measures
abstract: Deep learning has become a highly efficient method for Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) target classification, achieving ideal performance under most conditions. Unfortunately, commonly used deep learning-based models are often designed for optical images, while the imaging mechanism of SAR images is fundamentally different from optical images, which leads to poor performance under extended conditions. This paper proposes an Attribute Scattering Center based Separability Measured Convolutional Neural Network (ASC-SMCNN), which integrates the physical characteristics of SAR, introduces the ASC parameters and separability measure values into the model. The proposed model first extracts ASC parameters from complex SAR images, and then reconstructs SAR images. Then, the sample pairs composed of reconstructed images and amplitude images are inputted into a designed separability measure network. Finally, multiple features are fused together through Discriminant Correlation Analysis (DCA), and classification labels are output through the fully connected layers. The proposed method, guided by ASC parameters and separability measures, enables the model to focus on and extract unique causal features with clear physical meanings from SAR images, thereby achieving more competitive performance under extended conditions. Multiple experiments on the Moving and Stationary Target Acquisition and Recognition (MSTAR) dataset have verified the correctness and effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Adaptive thresholding for multi-temporal SAR interferometry
abstract: Multi-temporal interferometric synthetic aperture radar (MT-InSAR) is a standard tool for mapping large scale deformation with high precision. Most MT-InSAR methods select the scatterers with high coherence over the entire time series to improve the reliability of the phase unwrapping. However, the number of pre-selected scatterers obtained by the empirically thresholding varies with the number of acquisitions, which will cause the loss of scatterers in updating the results. In this work, we propose a simulation-based adaptive thresholding approach for MT-InSAR. The relationship between amplitude dispersion and phase noise is described using the numerical simulation. Then a statistical analysis is proposed to determine the relative optimal amplitude dispersion between different number of acquisitions. Experimental results using real SAR data show that the adaptive thresholding eliminate the loss of scatterers due to the fixed threshold, which can be further used in near real-time deformation monitoring.

articleTitle: Supervised learning-based generative adversarial network for target signature segmentation in GPR B-scan image
abstract: Ground-penetrating radar (GPR) is a non-destructive equipment effectively used for the characterization of surface targets. Underground target signature segmentation in GPR image is a preliminary step for further recognition and localization. However, most existing methods are time-consuming and susceptible to noise. Therefore, a novel deep learning-based method is proposed to segment GPR target characteristic. Due the advantage of migrating data distribution from input to output statistically, Generative adversarial networks (GAN) that combines generator and discriminator is employed as our main DL model. First, we perform GPR signature segmentation based on a supervised GAN model with paired images as input. Second, a loss function strategy is employed to improve the segmentation performance of GAN model, which combines L1 loss and conditional GAN loss. Therefore, the proposed method transfers our visual perception knowledge to the target instance segmentation task and is able to preserve key information.

articleTitle: Wideband jamming mitigation for target detection based on time-frequency analysis and sparse recovery method
abstract: Waveform agility technique in radar signal processing could effectively penalise a narrow-band jammer to some extent. However, with the increasing power of the jammer, Wideband jamming (WBJ) signal severely degrades the detection performance of the radar which uses the waveform agility technique. In this paper, WBJ signal transmitted by enemy jammer is defined as a broadband non-stationary interference characterised with a narrow instantaneous bandwidth. An anti-WBJ method based on time-frequency analysis and sparse recovery is proposed. By exploring the short-time Fourier transform domain as a pre-processing step and using a binary mask technique to suppress the major power of WBJ, and then an adaptive dictionary-based sparse recovery method is exploited to recover the useful target echo. Finally, a moving target detection (MTD) method is performed to obtain a traditional Range-Doppler imaging and target detection. Simulation results demonstrate the validation of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Analysis of the effect of vibration errors in arc array synthetic aperture radar
abstract: The Arc Array Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) is able to achieve wide-area observation under ideal conditions compared to conventional radars. However, helicopters equipped with arc-array SAR platforms are generally smaller in size and more sensitive to vibration, which greatly affects the imaging quality. In this paper, we study the vibration error of the arc-array SAR platform, establish a vibration error model of the arc-array SAR platform, analyse and compare the effect of vibration error on X, Y and Z axes with theoretical derivation, and verify the correctness of the theoretical results through simulation.

articleTitle: Fast block sparse Bayesian learning for recovery of block-sparse signal
abstract: Sparse Bayesian learning (SBL) has shown a superior capability for sparse signal recovery. In practice, block-sparse signals without knowledge of block structure are often encountered.
