To recover arbitrary block-sparse signals in a low-complexity manner, we extend the existing efficient SBL algorithm and propose a fast block SBL algorithm for block-sparse signal recovery. It adopts the pattern-coupled priors of entries to encourage block sparse structure and its update rules of the hyperparameters are derived by employing a joint sparsity assumption to deal with the hyperparameter coupling. Finally, numerical experimental results show that the proposed algorithm can efficiently recover block-sparse signal, especially in the case of low SNR when compared to some closely related SBL algorithms.

articleTitle: Clustering-based time-frequency domain adaptive SAR interference suppression
abstract: In the face of the current complex and variable electromagnetic interference environment, the broadband characteristics of synthetic aperture radar (SAR) make it extremely susceptible to other electromagnetic interference in the operating frequency band, which seriously restricts the information acquisition capability of SAR. Existing interference suppression methods based on notch filtering often rely on the interference a priori to set a fixed notch threshold, which suffers from poor adaptive ability and poor generalisation. Aiming at the aforementioned problems, this paper proposes a time-frequency domain adaptive SAR interference suppression method based on clustering, which makes use of the potential difference between the interference signal and the target signal in the time-frequency domain to adaptively locate the interference position in the time-frequency spectrum by unsupervised clustering, and then carries out zero-notch filtering to achieve the interference suppression on the basis of this method. The results of interference suppression from simulated and measured interference data show that the proposed method is able to overcome the need for interference a priori and effectively suppress different types of interference, with strong adaptive capability, generalisation to a wide range of interferences, and has value for practical application.

articleTitle: Classification of bird and drone based on radar time-frequency analysis
abstract: To address the classification of 'Low, Small, Slow' targets such as birds and drones, this paper proposes a classification algorithm based on target time-frequency spectrogram analysis. Firstly, radar-collected data is subjected to Short-Time Fourier Transform (STFT) to obtain target time-frequency spectrograms, followed by data preprocessing. Subsequently, these time-frequency spectrograms are fed into the designed neural network Residual Pyramid pooling Net (RPNet) for the classification of the two target classes. Validation results based on radar experimental data demonstrate that this algorithm can effectively classify birds and drones, thereby improving the classification performance of small targets.

articleTitle: Neural network aided fast coherent detection method for high-speed maneuvering target
abstract: The high-speed maneuvering target usually exhibits range cell migration (RCM) and Doppler spread (DS) effects in radar echo during the process of coherent detection, resulting in the degradation of coherent integration (CI) performance. To increase the energy accumulation gain and improve the radar detection ability, this paper proposes a fast implementation method via neural network to solve the problems of CI existed with RCM and DS. Particularly, this method constructs the data set to train the neural network and learn the features of target and clutter at first. Then, the trained network is utilized to extract the target energy trajectory from the clutter and the target parameters (including initial range cell, speed and acceleration) could be estimated via the polynomial fitting. Thus, the compensation function can be set up by using the estimated parameters and the RCM and DS can be removed simultaneously. At last, the Fourier transform is applied along the slow time direction to obtain the CI result. The effectiveness and feasibility of the proposed method are verified by the measured data.

articleTitle: Keyframe-based global localization in large-scale scenes
abstract: The purpose of scene recognition is to find keyframes from a known map that match the current frame. In large-scale scene positioning, the cumulative error of SLAM increases with the increase of the mileage of the unmanned vehicle due to the inevitable small error of inter-frame registration. Aiming at the localization problem of mobile robots in large-scale scenes, a global positioning method based on keyframes in large-scale scenes is proposed. First, the three-dimensional point cloud is transformed into single-line laser data, and key frames are selected from the single-line laser data to obtain a keyframe sequence. The trained laser spots then detect features and build databases and glossaries for efficient retrieval and location recognition. In order to verify the feasibility of the proposed method, multi-line lidar is used to conduct global positioning experiments in a wide outdoor environment. The experimental results show that the method can achieve a localization success rate of 61.2%, and the fastest speed is within 2ms. This method basically meets the accuracy and efficiency requirements of global positioning for autonomous driving in practical applications.

articleTitle: Maritime radar weak target detection against weather clutter based on FCOS network and dynamic ReLU
abstract: Sea exploration Radar is an important means in the field of ocean monitoring. The existence of weather clutter is also an important factor which degrades radar detection performance on maritime target. This phenomenon causes unsatisfied detection performance of traditional statistical detection algorithm such as Constant False Alarm Rate (CFAR). Inspired by excellent detection performance of deep learning methods, a novel maritime radar weak target detection method against weather clutter based on Fully Convolutional One-stage object detector (FCOS) network and dynamic Rectified Linear Unit (ReLU) is proposed in this paper. The proposed method extracts multi-dimensional features of radar target against sea exploration background with FCOS network. Besides, dynamic ReLU is combined with FCOS in order to adjust piecewise activation function according to global context encoding. In the part of experiment, real radar video data is utilized to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method. The proposed method performs better than tradition CFAR method and FCOS method on detecting weak target against weather clutter background.

articleTitle: Deformation monitoring of Datong coalfield based on LuTan-1
abstract: Long-term coal mining leads to surface subsidence, landslides, soil erosion and other problems, which has a potential threat to the lives and property of residents. Deformation monitoring of mining areas can effectively reduce the impact of disasters on people. Taking Datong coalfield as an application case, this paper uses SBAS method to monitor the surface deformation of the mining area with Lutan-1 as the data source, and finally compares it with three leveling data. From the monitoring results, 25 deformation areas can be seen, of which 4 subsidence reached more than 1m in a month. Compared with the leveling data, the subsidence trend is basically the same, and the average root mean square error is 10.9 mm, which provides a reference value for the application of land exploration satellite in the mining area.

articleTitle: A virtual reference station construction method based on TDOA prediction for IGSO tri-satellite TDOA geolocation system
abstract: Differential calibration (DC) achieves effective correction of ephemeris errors and synchronization errors of tri-satellite time difference of arrival (TDOA) geolocation system, but it needs a reference station which is near the object to be located emitting reference signals when the TDOA of the signal emitter is measured. In this paper a virtual reference station (VRS) construction method based on TDOA prediction for inclined geo-synchronous orbit (IGSO) tri-satellite TDOA geolocation system is proposed to solve above problem. The DC method is firstly described, then the method for constructing a VRS is explained, finally the method for TDOA prediction is shown. The simulations indicate that the method for TDOA prediction can predict TDOAs of reference stations well, and using the VRS constructed by these measured TDOAs or TDOA predictions can achieve effective correction of ephemeris errors and synchronization errors, enable the system to achieve higher localization accuracy.

articleTitle: Diffusion model in sea clutter simulation
abstract: The simulation of sea clutter has long been an attractive and challenging field. Sea clutter is formed by real scatterers and is different from noise in many respects. Hence simulated sea clutter with high fidelity promises to be crucial for the testing of related algorithms and the development of highly cognitive radar. Previous efforts to simulate sea clutter have been suffered from low fidelity, time-consuming calculation, etc. In this paper, we propose that up-to-date methods in artificial intelligence can be utilised to simulate high fidelity sea clutter within only a few seconds. A one-dimensional diffusion model is trained and implemented to generate sea clutter. The fidelity of the generated sea clutter is tested from perspectives including amplitude distribution, time correlation and fractal characteristics. The numerical analysis demonstrates the ability of neural networks like diffusion model to generate simulated data with high fidelity in a short time. Therefore, our research reveals the possibility to utilise simulated data generated by artificial intelligence for algorithm testing and the development of highly cognitive radar.

articleTitle: SAR-PC2AC: integrated phase congruency and CNN for aircraft classification in SAR imagery
abstract: Aircraft classification based on synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imagery plays a critical role in both military and civilian applications. However, the challenges arise from the sensitive attitude and discrete appearance of aircraft, which significantly impact the performance of aircraft classification in SAR images. To overcome these obstacles, an integrated phase congruency and CNN framework for aircraft classification (SAR-PC2AC) is proposed in this paper. The SAR-PC2AC consists of three main components: a basic deep classification network (BDCN), a phase congruency neural network (PCNN), and a feature fusion module (FFM). First, the BDCN takes the raw SAR image as input, which automatically gathers high-level semantic information from SAR images. Simultaneously, the PCNN is responsible for extracting phase congruency information from SAR images to enhance the correlation among the scattering points of the aircraft. Finally, PCNN is used via FFM to guide the BDCN in capturing inter-class and intra-class relation constraints, thereby improving classification performance. Experiments on the public SAR-ACD dataset with 1m resolution demonstrate the superiority of the proposed method over the baseline.

articleTitle: A self-attention armed lightweight optronic convolutional neural network for SAR target recognition
abstract: Deep learning has made significant progress in remote sensing and target recognition in recent decades. However, as a data-driven method, its development has encountered great challenges in computing speed and power consumption. Here, we propose a self-attention armed optronic neural network (SA-OPCNN) and realize the network in the optical platform for SAR target recognition. Based on the advantage of SA-OPCNN, all computation operations are executed in optics with ultra-fast speed, low computation cost, and low space complexity. Experiments on the Moving and Stationary Target Acquisition and Recognition (MSTAR) dataset demonstrate the feasibility and scalability of the proposed lightweight SAR target recognition method.

articleTitle: Sparse array pattern synthesis by phase-only control and regularized antenna switching
abstract: Pattern synthesis has always been an important issue in antenna array design. Traditional antenna array beamforming has obvious inefficiency and performance loss in many modern application scenarios. In order to improve the price-quality ratio of the antenna array, a sparse array beamforming strategy is proposed, and a reconfigurable antenna array using fewer antennas and front-end to generate high-performance beam patterns is designed. Furthermore, we propose a new method for designing sparse antenna arrays under phase-only control and regularized switching. The resulting sparse array synthesis problem is a nonconvex optimization problem with quadratic constraints. A simple but effective algorithm is proposed to solve the optimization problem. Simulation results are provided to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: A fusion algorithm with synchronous and asynchronous measurements for active and passive radar systems
abstract: In a collaborative detection system composed of active radar and passive radars, the arrival times of measurements from active and passive radars are not necessarily the same. However, traditional methods usually assume that the arrival times of measurements from these heterogeneous nodes are either synchronous or asynchronous, but do not consider both cases simultaneously. In this paper, a cubature Kalman filter (CKF) based fusion algorithm is proposed to deal with the aforementioned issue. Under this fusion algorithm, the measurements of active and passive radars are pre-processed and then filtered by the CKF, then the filtering results are sent to the fusion center, which determines whether the measurements of active radar and passive radar are synchronous or asynchronous through the timing sequence. Sequential fusion is used for asynchronous measurements and global fusion is used for synchronous measurements to form a state estimation of the target. The simulation results show that compared with the active radar systems, the active and passive radar systems can significantly improve the target angular tracking performance, radial velocity and acceleration tracking accuracy.

articleTitle: A biological echo identification method with single polarized weather radar using super-pixel segmentation
abstract: Weather radar networks, given their advantages of continental coverage and year-round operation, show great potential in the study of large-scale aerial biological migration. The precise identification and extraction of biological echoes from vast amounts of weather data serve as the essential metrics for assessing the biological monitoring capability of weather radar systems. However, complex weather conditions pose an obstacle to extracting biological information accurately. This study introduces super-pixel segmentation approach in the domain of weather radar-based biological recognition. A cluster-based method is proposed to extract biological information from localized spatial weather radar rendered images. From the perspective of colour space, we confirm the necessity and evident benefits of differentiating them at local spatial level. We collected 750,000 historical records from 108 weather radars nationwide and handpicked 36,000 representative migration cases for labelling, creating a large-scale trainable dataset for studying aerial ecological migration patterns with weather radars. We apply the proposed method to two typical scenes, and the results demonstrate that the accuracy of the proposed method is above 89.38% in the whole scenes.

articleTitle: Research on SAR imaging of hillside composite environment based on SBR-FBSM method
abstract: Using electromagnetic modelling to simulate radar imaging echo data and image has become one of the research hotspots in the field of radar imaging. This paper focuses on the application of shooting and bouncing racy - facet based scattering model (SBR-FBSM) method in synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imaging. Firstly, the modelling method of composite rough surface in hillside environment is introduced, then the basic principle of SBR-FBSM composite electromagnetic scattering method and SAR imaging are presented. Finally, the scattering echo of hillside environment and target is calculated by using the SBR-FBSM, and the echo data is brought into the Range-Doppler SAR imaging algorithm to complete the SAR imaging of the composite scene of hillside environment and targets, the physical phenomena presented in the simulation results can illustrate the rationality of the electromagnetic scattering algorithm proposed in this paper, and can provide necessary simulation data and technical theoretical support for target detection and recognition.

articleTitle: Experimental validations of insect 3D orientation extraction based on cooperative observation from two views of entomological radars
abstract: Individual trajectories are central to the study of insect migration. To realize fine-grained descriptions of migration, all information relevant to individual trajectories should be considered, especially the three-dimension (3D) orientation. The aim of this study is to demonstrate that insect 3D orientation can be effectively estimated by cooperative observation from two views of entomological radars. First, the 3D orientation extraction method based on dual radars is reviewed. This method shows that 3D orientation can be estimated by 2D orientations from two views of entomological radars. Then, three individual insects brought to the air by unmanned aerial vehicles are measured to prove the effectiveness of insect 3D orientation extraction.

articleTitle: Design of a non-uniform interpolator for real-time processing of flat earth removal of interferometric imaging radar altimeter
abstract: Interferometric imaging radar altimeter (InIRA) produces a large volume of data, which causes a need for real-time processing. In the current real-time processing algorithm of InIRA, the look angle of each point of the interferogram needs to be estimated using the slant range in flat earth removal step, which involves the problem of non-uniform interpolation. In this paper, an FPGA pipeline scheme is proposed for the non-uniform interpolation problem. In order to reduce resource consumption, the interpolation position is determined by sliding window comparison, and the window position is preset by simulation and obtained through table look-up. Meanwhile, only mantissa part of the floating-point number input by upstream module is intercepted for comparison. Finally, the interpolation position is determined. The design is testified on Xilinx Vertix-7 xc7vx690t FPGA. The pipeline calculation of flat earth phase for real-time processing algorithm is successfully implemented and verified with data from Tiangong-2 InIRA. Compared with the theoretical results, the final flat earth phase error is about 3×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-5</sup> degree, and the introduced error of sea surface height is of sub-millimetre level.

articleTitle: A novel dictionary-corrected sparse recovery stap algorithm based on prior knowledge
abstract: Sparse recovery space-time adaptive processing (SR-STAP) is prone to grid mismatch, which affects the clutter suppression performance. To cope with this problem, a dictionary correction sparse recovery STAP algorithm based on prior knowledge is proposed, which uses the principle of high power spectral value of clutter points. Firstly, the atoms matching the real clutt er points in the original dictionary are preliminarily selected by using the spectral value dimension reduction method. Then, around the selected atoms, the accurate clutter ridge is calculated by prior knowledge. Along parallel direction and vertical direction of the clutter ridge, space-time plane is evenly divided to form the local grid, and the optimal atoms to correct the original dictionary are searched in the local region. Finally, the modified clutter covariance matrix and the optimal STAP filtering weight are obtained. Simulation results show that, compared with the existing SR-STAP algorithm with dictionary-corrected, the proposed algorithm can find the grid points matching the real clutter ridge faster, effectively suppress the c lutter and improve the STAP performance.

articleTitle: Equivalent centroid-based method for velocity and position estimation of weak defocused maritime target
abstract: To position and track ships on the sea, conducting synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imaging of moving vessels and analyzing their speed and position parameters is necessary. However, due to the target's movement, SAR images will suffer from defocus blur and position shift. This paper explores the characteristics of target defocus blur and proposes a method to replace inaccurate imaging positions with equivalent centroids. To further obtain the speed and position parameters of the target, a target parameter estimation method based on the equivalent centroid is proposed. First, continuous imaging in the azimuth direction is performed, and multiple range-Doppler (R-D) equations are established by obtaining the imaging centroid position of the target. Then, the velocity parameters are estimated based on the Doppler shift of the target and then the target's Positional parameters. The simulation results verify the effectiveness of the method proposed in this article.

articleTitle: Robust joint association and registration under large sensor bias
abstract: Radar observation of group targets has recently received much attention in the flight mechanism research and many other applications. Group targets are usually closely spaced with lots of missed detections and false alarms, making it difficult for spatial reconstruction. Multisensor systems make use of data from multiple radars to provide more accurate measurements and robust tracks than a single radar, playing an important role in the group targets observation. In the data fusion processes, multisensor measurements are associated after transformed into a global coordinate system. However, large sensor bias makes it difficult to associate measurements of closely spaced targets given outliers, and nonideal association further increase the sensor bias estimation error. In this paper, we proposed a robust joint association and registration method to simultaneously acquire sensor bias estimates and association results. A nonlinear least median of squares estimator is used to achieve better accuracy and robustness of sensor bias estimation. Simulation results show the better bias estimation and association performance of the proposed method compared to other algorithms.

articleTitle: Velocity estimation of DRFM jamming source based on doppler differences in distributed array radar
abstract: Jamming sensing plays a crucial role in radar electronic countermeasure, requiring the estimation of parameters such as jamming type and motion state of jamming source. Among various jamming types, digital radio frequency memory (DRFM) jamming modulates false doppler phase and distance, making it challenging to estimate the true velocity of the jamming source. This paper proposes a method for estimating the velocity of DRFM jamming source using the doppler differences in distributed array radar. The radar units in distributed radar system are deployed sparsely and work cooperatively. The true doppler phase of DRFM jamming source varies across radars, while the modulated false phase remains consistent within radars. Collaborating multiple radars can effectively eliminate the false phase. Distributed array radar systems typically have long baselines, making precise localization of radar units and achieving system synchronization challenging. The algorithm proposed in this paper does not rely on the location of each radar and does not require coherence processing of echoes among radars, thereby reducing constraints on the distributed array radar system. The effectiveness of the algorithm is validated through simulations in this paper.

articleTitle: SSFEN: self-supervised feature extraction network for interrupted-sampling repeater jamming suppression
abstract: Interrupted-sampling repeater jamming (ISRJ), a form of main-lobe deception jamming, presents a significant obstacle for radar systems. Traditional anti-jamming techniques typically require the estimation of jamming parameters, which can introduce the potential for information loss regarding the target. In addition, methods based on convolutional neural networks (CNN) require a substantial amount of manually labeled data for training in order to achieve satisfactory results. However, obtaining a significant amount of labeled data in the radar domain poses a challenge. For the above problems, this article proposes a self-supervised feature extraction network (SSFEN) for jamming suppression. Localization and suppression of jamming is then formulated as a image processing problem and solved utilizing the classical GrabCut algorithm. In this approach, First, utilize the Short-Time Fourier Transform (STFT) to convert the one-dimensional signals into two-dimensional time-frequency representation. Next, employ the SSFEN to locate jamming and generate a mask. Finally, suppress the jamming by using the mask.

articleTitle: An arbitrary array passive localization algorithm using near-field effects
abstract: In order to solve the difficulty in engineering passive localization of large-aperture interferometers, an arbitrary array passive localization algorithm using near-field effects is proposed.In this method, the phase difference between the spatial position and the receiving array elements is used to construct a cost function for spatial matching search, and the particle swarm optimization algorithm is used for fast convergence iteration. Simulation results show that the proposed algorithm is not limited to the form of array elements. Localization of a radiation source target can be realized by using the phase difference information of the array elements, which brings the advantages of high localization accuracy and fast convergence speed.

articleTitle: Deep unfolding for sparse aperture ISAR imaging via compressed sensing: CIST+
abstract: The issue of inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR) imaging under sparse aperture (SA) conditions using compressed sensing (CS) techniques has garnered substantial attention. In this research, we amalgamate the explicability offered by the deep unfolding network (DUN) with the facile compression of the high-frequency component of the signal in the image domain. This fusion aims to unfold the iterative soft-thresholding algorithm (ISTA) into a trainable network model termed CIST+. Through end-to-end training, the model demonstrates its prowess in achieving robust reconstruction of low-compression-rate ISAR imaging even amidst noise interference, while also exhibiting exceptional operational efficiency. Our findings from simulations and measured data experiments demonstrate the efficacy and potential of the model.

articleTitle: DCAMM-Dynamic Clustering and Networking Algorithm for Mobile Agents in Manufacturing Scene
abstract: Due to the complex environment in large-scale manufacturing sites, cluster robots (intelligent agents) are required to participate in the work. The intelligent agents deployed in large-scale equipment manufacturing sites face challenges in communication such as multiple obstructions, agent mobility, and high latency requirements. In this paper, we propose DCAMM, a Dynamic Clustering Algorithm for Mobile Agents in Manufacturing Scene. The algorithm describes the latency model among mobile agents and between mobile agent and Console on the working conditions. It clusters the agents in a task-oriented manner, then selects cluster heads based on agent mobility strategies and signal quality, and further clusters them based on agent throughput limits. Simulation results compared to LEACH show better algorithm performance in the given scene, DCAMM achieves a 39.2% improvement (243ms) in cluster change delay and a 30.3% improvement (151ms) in transmission delay.

articleTitle: A fast SAR image template matching based on time-frequency analysis
abstract: To solve the time-consuming, low reliability, and fake matching problems among synthetic aperture radar(SAR) image template matching algorithm, a fast SAR template matching algorithm is proposed. It first multiplies the image and the template in the frequency domain to quickly locate the suspected targets. Then, it uses the template to correlate the location of the suspected targets in the time domain, thus improving reliability, speed, and accuracy. The experiment results show that the proposed algorithm is effective.

articleTitle: A frequency-domain sparse multi-functional anti-jamming waveform design and processing method
abstract: A frequency-domain sparse multifunctional anti-jamming waveform design and processing method is introduced. The anti-jamming waveform is transmitted using wide-to-narrow band transmission technique. By constructing the integrated Hidden Markov Model (HMM) for radar-jammer joint state, the jamming sub-band is predicted, and the corresponding receiving sub-band is determined to effectively mitigate the impact of jamming. Simulation experiments were conducted, demonstrating the pronounced efficacy of the proposed anti-jamming waveform in mitigating jamming effects.

articleTitle: A method for anti interrupted sampling and repeated jamming within main lobe based on fixed reflection array
abstract: The occurrence of intermittent sampling and repeater jamming within the main lobe will cause serious interference to radar detection. This article first analyzes the model of interference suppression by intra pulse frequency agile signals, and analyzes the characteristics of target echoes and repeater interference signals; An interrupted sampling repeater jamming cancellation method based on a fixed reflection array is proposed. On this basis, the geometric characteristics of the target=fixed reflection array provide positioning information in the echo, which can be used to solve the problem of height estimation. Simulation results shows that: Compared with the original signal-to-interference ratio is 11.11dB, the anti-interference algorithm based on cancellation, raised the signal-to-interference ratio to 31.12dB. Simulation shows that the proposed method has engineering application prospects for anti interrupted sampling and repeater jamming.

articleTitle: Closely spaced network-group target tracking using the Dirichlet GGIW-PHD filter
abstract: Network-group targets are a set of objectives that adhere to a common communication protocol, perform common tasks, and exhibit relatively coordinated movements. However, due to the short time slot of electromagnetic radiation generated by network-group targets, especially when the spatial distribution of these targets is dense, traditional tracking algorithms struggle to address the problem of association ambiguity. To tackle this issue, this paper introduces a method for tracking closely spaced network-group targets using the Dirichlet Gamma Gaussian inverse Wishart-probability hypothesis density (DGGIW-PHD) filter. In addition to utilizing position measurements, this method also takes into account the unit address, which is an attribute information. The state of the addresses is described by the Dirichlet model. The DGGIW-PHD method consistently performs as expected, as evidenced by the simulation results.

articleTitle: A heuristic detector for forward scatter radar with opportunistic signals from LEO satellites
abstract: In this work, a simple heuristic detector is proposed for the forward scatter radar with opportunistic signals from broadband low Earth orbit satellite communication systems, by utilizing the difference in the variances of the amplitude of the received signal in the ground station, when the target is present or not. The receiver operating characteristics is analyzed using a simplified model with the amplitude approximated as the summation of a signal term and a noise term. Simulation results for both a target crossing a single link and that crossing multiple links are presented, demonstrating the potential of such systems.

articleTitle: Gesture recognition for millimeter wave radar based on LocalPVT
abstract: Benefiting from the increasing development of deep learning, the deep learning-based millimeter wave radar gesture recognition method has been widely used in military and civil fields. Nonetheless, it faces problems such as scarcity of public datasets and lack of global information in traditional networks. To solve the above problems, a millimeter wave radar gesture recognition method based on LocalPVT is proposed in this paper. The proposed method consists of two stages: constructing the millimeter wave radar gesture recognition (MWRGR) dataset and implementing gesture recognition. In the first stage, we utilize a 77 GHz millimeter-wave radar to capture the echoes of gestures and perform preprocessing to generate the Micro-Doppler time spectrograms of dynamic gestures to facilitate the construction of the dataset. In the second stage, we propose a LocalPVT network for gesture recognition tasks that can not only capture global but also local information. We improve the global and local perception of time spectrograms of dynamic gestures in the LocalPVT network by introducing locality in the Transformer, which has only global perception. Experimental results based on the constructed MWRGR dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: On cyclic frequency sidelobe and range sidelobe reduction for LPI radar waveform
abstract: Design of radar waveform with low probability of intercept (LPI) performance has been a topic that has attracted much attention in recent years. In this paper, a new LPI radar waveform design scheme is proposed, which not only considers the LPI performance but also takes the integrated sidelobe level (ISL) into account to assure the radar detection performance. Based on the analysis of the cyclic spectrum, we develop a trade-off optimization model by minimizing the weighted summation of the cyclic frequency sidelobe level (CFSL) and ISL under energy constraint. Since the constructed problem is a non-convex quartic optimization problem, a majorization-minimization (MM) based low double sidelobes (MM-LDS) algorithm is proposed to transform it into a convex optimization problem for solving. Numerical simulation results verify LPI and low ISL performance of the designed waveform.

articleTitle: Target shadow profile retrieval from FSSR using LEO satellites as illuminators of opportunity
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the use of Low Earth Orbit satellites as the illuminators of opportunity within a forward scatter radar system to retrieve the shadow profiles of airborne targets. We provide a mathematical description of the forward scatter shadow ratio model specific to the application scenario and demonstrate how a plane wave equivalent model can be employed to retrieve the target shadow profile through an optimisation method. Simulations are conducted for a circular orbit with targets positioned 10 km above the ground and at elevation angles of 90, 70 and 40 degrees. The optimisation method employed to retrieve the target's shadow profile relies on a plane wave equivalent model with a fixed plane wave equivalent distance. For both the triangular and circular targets, the retrieved shadow profiles agrees with their true shapes at all tested elevation angles. It is suggested that the fixed plane wave equivalent distance does not significantly affect the performance of the retrieval. Nevertheless, with lower elevation angles, the fixed plane wave equivalent distance does introduce an error, slightly diminishing the accuracy of the retrieval.

articleTitle: Suppression of defocus along azimuth dimension for THz SAR imaging based on ADMM framework
abstract: Terahertz synthetic aperture radar (THz SAR) is used in numerous applications due to its unique properties. However, within the THz SAR systems, the tiny wavelength renders it more susceptible to the platform’s high frequency vibration. Hence, the THz SAR images will be seriously affected by the vibration error. To solve this problem, the platform vibration error compensation method based on the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) framework is employed to extract the instantaneous frequency (IF) precisely. Through the ADMM-based vibration compensation algorithm, the defocus arising from the vibration error is inhibited, then the focused images are acquired. The experimental results of simulated and real-measured data illustrate the validity of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Parameterized and structured 2-D controllable SAR jamming: new insights and framework
abstract: Imposing controllable barrage jamming against syn- thetic aperture radar (SAR) systems is a more technical challenge in electronic countermeasures. In this respect, a parameterized and structured two-dimensional (2-D) precise controllable SAR jamming technique is developed to assist in addressing such problems. Based on the characteristics of range-Doppler algo- rithm (RDA) under linear frequency modulation (LFM) case, the modulation framework has been established to impose the jamming signal with large-dynamic controllable coverage and high 2-D processing gain. Using the proposed technique, we can achieve the optimal power allocation and considerably decrease the jamming power. Finally, numerical simulations have been implemented to demonstrate the effectiveness and prospect of the proposed 2-D controllable jamming technique.

articleTitle: Optimization of radar waveform based on the weighted ambiguity function behavior
abstract: Aiming at the practical requirement of the waveform sequence with low sidelobes on the range-Doppler plane in radar systems, a method called as the weighted ambiguity function behavior optimization (WAFBO) algorithm is developed creatively to design a waveform with the desired ambiguity function behavior. The metric defined by the weighted ambiguity function with the quartic form is introduced for the first time. Furtherly, a new optimization problem under the constant constraint is formulated, which is hard to solve directly. To tackle this problem, two methods of WAFBO-1 and WAFBO-2 are employed. The former applies the existing convex optimization method to get the optimal solution, including two steps: convex approximation for the objective function and convex relaxation, the latter derives the closed-form solution at each iteration, which can improve the computational efficiency. Finally, the numerical simulations are carried out by comparing the ambiguity function behaviors of WAFBO-1 and WAFBO-2 with the existing noise waveform. The feasibility of the proposed algorithm is verified.

articleTitle: A quantized lobes reduction method based on thinned strategy for overlapped subarray architecture
abstract: Overlapped subarray plays an important role in low-cost multiple receive beamforming. Unexpected quantized lobes will deteriorate the performance of multiple beams. In this paper, we propose a thinned overlapped design strategy, which combines the idea of thinned array with overlapped subarray structure. The quantized lobe could be suppressed through optimizing the placements of antenna elements in subarray by solving an integer programming problem. The effectiveness of this design strategy is verified by numerical experiments.

articleTitle: Magnetic resonance eddy penetrating imaging for detecting reinforcement corrosion in concrete
abstract: Reinforcement corrosion is a popular hidden disease in concrete constructions and seriously threats to the structure safety, but effectively detecting it has still been challenging for its hidden nature. This work proposes a new principle of internal reinforcement corrosion detection: magnetic resonance eddy penetrating imaging (MREPI), which shows a large eddy detection depth because of resonance enhancement. By optimizing the parameters of the magnetic resonance eddy current sensor to make it more sensitive, the depth of investigation of MREPI has been significantly improved compared to conventional eddy current detection (ECT). The results show that the sensitivity of the resonance coil in the resonance state to the metal specimen is higher when a ferrite core is added between the excitation coil and the resonance coil, and the weaker the degree of coupling between the two coils. The location and direction of the corroded reinforcement under 50 mm concrete were also successfully obtained. These results provide an innovative method for the nondestructive detection of corroded reinforcement in concrete structure.

articleTitle: Contrastive learning-based prototype calibration method for few-shot HRRP recognition
abstract: High-resolution range profile (HRRP) recognition has been widely applied in radar automatic target recognition (RATR) due to its low computational cost, easy acquisition and rich information of target structure. For non-cooperative radar targets, obtaining sufficient data is a challenging task in real scenarios. To deal with this problem, metric-based few-shot learning methods dedicate to find better metric criteria to measure the distance relation between test samples and the prototypes. However, these methods tend to neglect the distribution of these prototypes in the feature space, which leads to overlapping classification boundaries. To alleviate this problem, we propose a contrastive learning-based prototype calibration method for few-shot HRRP recognition. During the learning process of the prototypes, feature-wised contrastive regularization is introduced to disperse prototypes and calibrate their distribution in the feature space. Experimental results indicate that the proposed method endows few-shot learning models with more separable classification boundaries and higher recognition accuracy compared with conventional metric learning methods.

articleTitle: Cooperative power allocation for radar and communication based on fixed condition optimization
abstract: Spectrum resources are becoming increasingly restricted as global wireless communication develops at a rapid pace. In order to effectively address the spectrum coexistence and resource allocation problem, a multi-carrier signal power allocation algorithm for radar and communication coexistence (RCC) system is proposed. First, signal models of radar and communication systems are built, and the performances of radar and communication in RCC are introduced. A dual-objective optimization model under power limitations and signal-to-interference-noise ratio (SINR) constraints is built, which is based on the criterion of maximizing radar mutual information (RMI) and communication data rate (CDR). The ideal solution for power allocation is then obtained by combining Taylor expansion and fixed condition optimization algorithm, and this optimization problem is solved using Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) optimal conditions. Finally, simulation results show that compared with other algorithms, the fixed optimization algorithm can obtain better radar and communication performances.

articleTitle: Analysis on spatial resolutions of low-frequency ultrawideband wide beamwidth SAR
abstract: Ultrawideband Synthetic Aperture Radar (UWB-SAR) is a high-resolution imaging radar with leaf-cluster penetration capability, which has broad application prospects in military and civilian fields. It can accurately map the terrain covered by the forest and imaging various targets hidden in forests. Compared with the conventional high-frequency narrow-band narrow- beamwidth (NBNB) SAR, the low-frequency UWB-SAR has the characteristics of large relative bandwidth and large imaging integral angle, and its imaging results will inevitably have new characteristics. Aiming at this phenomenon, this paper analyses the imaging characteristics of low-frequency ultrawideband wide beam SAR by point spread function. Firstly, the point spread function of low-frequency UWB-SAR is derived and its characteristics are analyzed. Then, the side-lobe direction and two-dimensional spatial resolution characteristics of the imaging results are analyzed according to the point spread function, and the relationship between spatial resolution, relative bandwidth and beamwidth is given by simulation.

articleTitle: DA-SSD: Domain Adaptation for 3D Single Stage Object Detector
abstract: Object detection on point cloud is an important task for autonomous driving technology. Long-distance detection is a major problem. Recent researches have demonstrated that good feature representation is the key to 3D object detection, especially for point-based methods. However, due to the physical characteristics of Lidar. Point clouds are densely distributed at short distance and sparsely distributed at long distance, which increases the difficulty for the points-representation learning. In this paper, a simple and effective single-stage detector, named Domain Adaptation for 3D Single Stage Object Detector (DA-SSD), is proposed with a range domain adaptor. Through the range domain adaptor, the knowledge learned on short-distance objects can be transferred to long-distance objects. The problem of uneven point cloud distribution can be alleviated by the proposed module. Extensive experiments show the effectiveness of the proposed DA-SSD.

articleTitle: Wideband pattern reconfigurable dielectric resonator antenna for Wi-Fi applications
abstract: A wideband pattern reconfigurable dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) based on the Yagi principle is developed in this paper. The proposed antenna is fed by a central metal probe to excite the desired resonant modes (TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01δ</sub>, TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">02δ</sub>, and TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11δ</sub> modes). Parasitic metal rods are employed at the appropriate positions to achieve end-fire radiation. Eight radiation patterns can be obtained by changing the position of the rods, which can be steered to cover all 360° horizontal orientation. The higher-order TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">02δ</sub> and TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11δ</sub> modes of the DR are introduced to achieve wider operating bandwidth. Combined with the resonance of the reflectors, the antenna with a wide -10 dB impedance bandwidth of 45.2% (4.05-6.42 GHz) is finally realized. A prototype of the proposed antenna is fabricated and measured, and its operating frequency band, return loss, and radiation pattern are presented. The proposed antenna is well poised to the 5G NR small cell and Wi-Fi 6 communication systems.

articleTitle: Optimization study on the siting of maintenance stations for distributed radars based on an improved K-means algorithm
abstract: In this study, the siting of radar maintenance stations was optimized concerning the distributed networking deployment patter n of high-precision radars. A genetic algorithm was introduced into the K-means algorithm, forming a GA-K-means algorithm. Besides, a K-means algorithm with constraints was designed to satisfy the actual task demands. With the global search ability of the genetic algorithm, the GA-K-means algorithm was provided with ideal initial centers of mass so that this algorithm became insensitive to the initial values and obtained a good clustering effect. By simulation experiments and changing the radar positions constantly, it was verified that the proposed GA-K-means algorithm was robust and generalized. The experimental results demonstrate that the maintenance station siting scheme based on the GA-K-means algorithm shortened the distance from a maintenance station to the corresponding radar sites and thus reduced the maintenance cost while satisfying the task constraint type.

articleTitle: Incorporating Doppler velocity measurements in orientation-based extended object tracking
abstract: For automotive radar-based extended object tracking (EOT), the Doppler velocity is not always fully exploited. Strong nonlinearities may exist due to the relative angle (or spatial position) between a scattering center and the radar sensor in the Doppler velocity measurement equation. To solve this problem, this paper introduces latent variables of positional noise-free measurements, which leads to a simplified form of the Doppler velocity measurement equation. Building upon the existing orientation-based EOT approach, we utilize a variational Bayesian approach to incorporate the improved Doppler velocity measurement and recursively estimate the object’s kinematic state, size, orientation, and yaw rate analytically. This approach avoids strong nonlinearities and has low computational complexity. The effectiveness of the proposed approach is demonstrated by using simulated data.

articleTitle: A dual-band micro-Doppler feature fusion recognition method based on self-attention mechanism in channel domain
abstract: Most research on radar target classification using micro-Doppler signature (MDS) involves single radar feature extraction, which makes it difficult to extract features comprehensively. In this work, we focus on fusing MDS from two radars and propose a novel network structure, which we term the "squeeze and excitation-double input convolutional neural network" (SE-DICNN). SE-DICNN combines the advantages of two radars by adaptively recalibrating radar-wise feature responses. The proposed SE-DICNN includes two input layers, two pre-trained ResNet50 network structures, a concatenated layer, a squeeze and excitation block (SE-Block), and a fully connected layer. We chose candence frequency diagrams (CFDs) as the inputs of the SE-DICNN because of their strong noise resistance. The data set contains three types of aerodynamic targets, which are observed by pulse Doppler radars operating in the HF band and VHF band frequency. The experimental results based on measured data show that the proposed method can excite channel weights in a highly class-specific manner, and achieves the best classification accuracy and anti-noise performance in the recognition task of three types of airplanes, compared to existing convolutional neural network (CNN) methods.

articleTitle: Frequency analysis method for SAR target classification using convolutional neural networks
abstract: This paper investigates Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) image processing, specifically examining the performance of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) under various SAR imaging conditions. ConvNeXt networks were trained using MSTAR and GOTCHA datasets, and the impact of using SAR images with different pitch angles and polarizations as input for deep learning models was analyzed. Frequency analysis methods were employed to uncover the frequency shortcut learning phenomenon in SAR images from a frequency perspective. The results indicate that neural networks initially ca pture and utilize significant spectral differences between classes during the learning process. and the frequency characteristics of the data play a crucial role. The analysis presented in this paper contributes to a better understanding of SAR image optimization for deep learning model applications. advances the development of algorithms for interpreting SAR images. and establishes atheoretical foundation for the effective integration of deep learning technology and SAR imaging.

articleTitle: An invalid deception-jammer area calculation method of Bistatic SAR
abstract: The problem of Bistatic SAR and deception-jamming countermeasure is studied, the signal model of Bistatic SAR and deception-jammer is established, the characteristics of deception-jamming signal in Bistatic SAR image are analysed, and an invalid deception-jammer area calculation method of Bistatic SAR is proposed. The effective jamming area of deception-jamming in Bistatic SAR image is estimated to determine whether the deception-jammer is effective, and the distribution area of invalid deception-jammer is obtained. The invalid deception-jammer area of Bistatic SAR is obtained by simulation, and the imaging results show that the deception-jammer cannot effectively jam Bistatic SAR when it is located in the invalid area. After changing the Bistatic SAR configuration, the change of the invalid area is consistent with the theory.

articleTitle: Multi-scenes SAR target classification network for class incremental learning
abstract: Deep learning has been widely applied in the field of synthetic aperture radar (SAR) image recognition. However, traditional deep learning approaches often struggle with dynamically incorporating new classification targets, given that acquiring all targets simultaneously is generally unfeasible. While incremental learning methodologies for SAR target classification have made noteworthy strides, they have largely neglected the challenges presented by multi-scenes classification. The problem of confusion between backgrounds results in suboptimal performance when addressing diverse classification scene. To remediate this deficiency, we introduce MSTC-Net, which employs a decoupling strategy to train target classifications from different scenes independently before integrating them into a unified network. This approach effectively segregates target information across varied scenes. The experiments demonstrate that MSTC-Net significantly improves the classification accuracy of SAR target in incremental learning.

articleTitle: A wake-sleep time extraction technique based on radar point clouds
abstract: Sleep is an integral part of human life and plays a very important role in maintaining human health. Adequate sleep duration and good sleep quality can maintain physical and mental health, enhance immunity, and promote learning and memory ability. Therefore, accurate sleep time extraction is crucial for health management. In order to achieve simple, lower-cost, long-term, and user-comfortable home wake-sleep time extraction, this paper proposes a millimetre-wave radar point cloud based sleep time extraction technique. Firstly, millimetre wave radar is used to obtain the raw echoes of human movement, and the point cloud of human activity is obtained after preprocessing. Then, count the number of human activity point clouds in the scene according to a certain time interval to form the concept of human activity level. Finally, by analysing the statistical features such as the mean value of the activity degree, the outliers are extracted, and their corresponding times are the wake-up time and sleep time. The algorithm can achieve non-contact, long-term stable and accurate extraction of human wake-sleep time and sleep duration, which provides effective basic information for the subsequent analysis of work and rest habits as well as life patterns.

articleTitle: Cavity filter with mixed electromagnetic coupling
abstract: In this paper, a two-order narrow bandpass filter with tunable transmission zeros and high out-of-band suppression is proposed based on mixed electromagnetic coupling. Through loading a metal circular plate on the coaxial cylinder, the loading capacitance is increased and the size of the cavity is greatly reduced. For the coupling portion, two metal discs are added to increase the capacitive coupling between the two resonant cavities, which can realize a transmission zero. The transmission zero can be adjusted to either side of the passband through tuning the gap between the discs and the resonant columns. The successful design has the fractional bandwidth of 0.7%, and the out-of-band rejection level of 55.0 dB.

articleTitle: Improved YOLOV5 for ship rotating frame target detection in SAR images
abstract: Aiming at the problem that the ship target in SAR remote sensing image has the characteristics of changeable direction and dramatic scale change, which leads to the low detection accuracy of ship target, this paper improves a ship target detection algorithm based on YOLOv5. Firstly, this paper introduces the detection layer to better detect small target ships in SAR remote sensing images. Then, CBAM is introduced into the backbone network. While the model is lightweight, the accuracy of ship target detection is improved. Finally, the rotation frame is introduced to better locate and detect the ship target. The experimental results show that the mAP (mean Average Precision) of the improved YOLOv5 ship target detection algorithm is 2.7 % higher than that of the original YOLOv5 algorithm on the SDD-SAR data set. Therefore, the improved algorithm can effectively improve the target detection accuracy of ship remote sensing images.

articleTitle: Improved YOLOv7 for small object detection in human body millimeter wave images
abstract: Aiming at the problem that the weak performance ability of small-sized contraband features in the target detection process of millimetre-wave security imaging affects the network detection rate, this paper, based on the original YOLOv7, firstly, by adding the ACmix attention mechanism in the backbone network and the feature fusion network, so as to make the detection network strengthen the sensitivity to the target in the millimetre-wave image and to reduce the noise brought by the background, and secondly, by referencing the C3 module in the model, so as to improve the model performance. It is proved that the improved YOLOv7 model achieves the expected results in detecting small-sized targets.

articleTitle: An identification algorithm of cross polarized jamming for single polarized radar
abstract: The high-power and cross polarized jamming is used in angular deception via maximizing the response distinction between main and cross polarization of a single polarized radar. When the radar suffers from the cross polarized jamming in the self- screening jamming case, the radar may neither have the target echo and jamming separated in spatial domain, nor identify and filter the jamming in polarization domain for lack of processing capacity. To cope with that, an identification algorithm aimed at cross polarized jamming based on spatial freedom is proposed. Firstly, the proposed algorithm gets a rough DOA estimation via traditional monopulse angle measurement. Then based on a series of beamforming weights pointing distinct angle, the mapping relation between the pointing angle and the weighted output of received data is established, along with a fitting curve called the received curve. The theoretical and homologous curve is created the same way, which is accord with the main polarization and known exactly by the radar. Finally, the geometry distinction between the received curve and the theoretical curve is regarded as the criterion of detecting cross polarized jamming. When the cross polarized jamming exists, the power of jamming provides additional power on the cross polarization, and causes the received curve derivate from the theoretical one in geometry. If not, the random noise leads to a smaller geometry distinction. The proposed algorithm is distinct and clear, and makes it possible for single polarized radar to identify the cross polarized jamming relying on making fully use of spatial freedom rather than loading multi-polarized hardware. The feasibility has been testified via simulation in multiple applications.

articleTitle: MGLI: an efficient index for RDW data in cloud environment
abstract: According to massive spatial-temporal data and high probability of granularity queries in RDW field, a multi-granularities and multi-levels index (MGLI) method is proposed for RDW data in Cloud environment. Chord and B+-tree are combined to index time dimension of data and R-tree is used to index space dimension of data. Then region encoding sequence which can use operation "AND" and "OR" is added to R-Tree, which forms the RCR-tree that is suitable for granularity query. In addition, the rowkey is designed depending on characteristics of index and data to make HBase store and query data conveniently. Pre- indexing mechanism is proposed to reduce the cost of updating data and support high insert throughput in RDW. Finally, we implemented a prototype based on HBase and did comprehensive experiments to test our solution's scalability and efficiency.

articleTitle: Doppler steering method based on pitch-yaw steering sequence
abstract: In space-borne SAR imaging, there are many factors that can affect the Doppler Center Frequency, such as the rotation of the earth and the non-circular orbit of the satellite. To offset the above effects, the satellite attitude needs to be constantly adjusted. The traditional instantaneous circular doppler steering method is to carry out yaw-pitch steering in the centroid orbit coordinate system, offset the influence of earth rotation by adjusting the yaw angle and offset the non-circular influence of satellite orbit by adjusting the pitch angle, but the premise of this is that the satellite orbit is nearly circular. With the continuous deepening of SAR satellite research and the continuous expansion of application fields, there may be large eccentricity orbital SAR satellites in the future, and the traditional doppler steering method cannot solve the problem effectively. Therefore, this paper deduced a pitch-yaw steering method for large eccentricity orbital SAR satellites and further expanded the future application scenarios of SAR satellites.

articleTitle: A novel target recognition method with polarimetric correlation phase for SAR images
abstract: While most contemporary target recognition techniques predominantly focus on single-polarization synthetic aperture radar (SAR) images and emphasize intensity information, this paper introduces an innovative target recognition approach for SAR images that harnesses the polarimetric correlation phase, minimally utilizing intensity data. The polarimetric correlation phase characterizes the phase disparity between co-polarization and cross-polarization, capturing the multifaceted scattering of target components. Through experiments conducted on both synthetic and actual images, we substantiate the efficacy and promise of our proposed method, illustrating its capacity to achieve high-precision target recognition solely through phase information, especially under conditions of elevated signal-to-clutter ratio (SCR).

articleTitle: A fast off-grid stap algorithm based on marginal likelihood maximization
abstract: Space-time adaptive processing (STAP) based on sparse recovery (SR) have become a promising algorithm for the benefit of reducing the training samples requirements. However, most SR-STAP approaches suffer the off-grid effect due to the discretization of the angle-Doppler plane. To mitigate the off-grid effect, an efficient clutter subspace estimation algorithm is proposed based on marginal likelihood maximization in this paper. The algorithm selects atoms from a dense dictionary incrementally to estimate clutter subspace, which avoids the effect of the strong coherence between the atoms. Moreover, the proposed algorithm only uses a part of the dictionary, leading to high computational efficiency. Numerical experiments are conducted to prove that the proposed algorithm has superior clutter suppression performance with low computational complexity.

articleTitle: Low-profile orbital angular momentum antenna with circular polarization based on polarization-conversion trifunctional metasurface for microwave imaging applications
abstract: A low-profile circularly polarized (CP) orbital angular momentum (OAM) antenna is presented in this paper. This antenna consists of a linearly polarized (LP) feed antenna on the bottom and is enabled by a polarization-conversion trifunctional metasurface on the top, together with an air-gap layer inserted between them. The lower part of the metasurface acts as a linear-to-circular polarization-conversion function meanwhile generates multiple-times wave reflection between the feed antenna and the metasurface. The upper part of the metasurface generates OAM wave with circular polarization. Additionally, it contributes to a function of focusing vortex beam. The meta-atoms of the metasurface consist of striplines, patches, metallic layers, and shorting pins. The striplines can be utilized to adjust or/and compensate the transmission phase, and the rotation of the slotted top patch can be applied to adjust the geometric phase. With a comprehensive interaction, a high-purity OAM wave with circular polarization is produced. The simulated results show that the antenna is operating over a bandwidth from 24.75 GHz to 26.75 GHz (7.8%). The peak gain for the OAM mode l=+2 can be up to 15.59 dBi. The OAM modes l=+1 and l=+2 can be transformed by changing the stripline structures in the meta-atoms. The antenna dimensions can be kept at 10λ0×10λ0× 2.16λ0, relatively performing a low-profile height.

articleTitle: Structural pruning for LiDAR 3D detection network by dependency graph
abstract: Multi-line LiDAR offers 3D environment perception and has been widely applied to autonomous driving. However, most deep neural networks for LiDAR 3D detection, exemplified by PointPillars, are excluded from real-time applications to on-board processors, as they require a huge set of parameters and cause heavy computational burden. Structural pruning can speed up detection by removing some groups of parameters, but the parameter-grouping patterns for detection networks have not been adequately analysed, leading to unsatisfying performance of the pruned models. In this work, a novel dependency graph strategy enhanced by grouped importance estimation, named as DepGraph-GIE, is proposed for structural pruning on PointPillars. For the first time, the DepGraph scheme is introduced to LiDAR 3D detection task to analyse parameter-grouping patterns by building dependency graph and consistent sparse training. Based on that, a group importance estimation method is employed to ensure the pruned groups are unimportant. In this way, DepGraph-GIE substantially improves inference efficiency and reduces parameter size at a negligible expense of accuracy. Experiments on a self-collected dataset and examinations for online deployment validate the superiorities of the proposed DepGraph-GIE method in reducing computational burden and meanwhile maintaining detection accuracy, in contrast to conventional structural pruning methods.

articleTitle: An incremental range and unambiguous velocity estimation approach with FDA-MIMO radar
abstract: This paper deals with the problem of incremental range and unambiguous velocity estimation for fast-moving targets in frequency diverse array (FDA) multiple-input and multiple-output (MIMO) radar. The FDA-MIMO radar signal model for fast-moving target scenarios is established at first, and the incoherence of the signals between different transmit elements due to the coupling of frequency offset and velocity is analyzed. Moreover, an iterative incremental range with the Doppler ambiguity index estimation method is proposed. Based on this, the estimated true velocity of the target is used to construct a compensation vector to further obtain the accurate incremental range. Numerical results are provided to validate the effectiveness of the proposed method for parameter estimation of fast-moving targets.

articleTitle: Experimental validations of insect species identification based on fully-polarimetric radar measurements
abstract: Accurate identification of migratory insect species is essential for effective pest forecasting and control strategies. Radar entomology presents challenges in insect identification, prompting the exploration of novel approaches. This paper addresses the issue by leveraging machine learning techniques to classify insect species based on their body mass and length, fundamental parameters for characterization. Four insect species were collected via searchlight traps, and their body mass and length were promptly measured. An Artificial Neural Network (ANN) was tailored to these parameters to construct a species identification model. Using a fully-polarimetric radar, 40 insects—10 from each of the four species—were monitored in the air. The insects were affixed to their backs with thin PE line and lifted by drones to a fixed position. The results demonstrate the efficacy of the trained identification models, achieving an average identification rate of 87.5% through estimated body mass and length parameters. This study validates the feasibility of species identification based on insect size parameters, offering promising insights for radar entomology applications.

articleTitle: A novel hybrid sparse SAR imaging algorithm based on L1/2-norm
abstract: Compressed sensing (CS) theory is widely used in the field of radar imaging. However, synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imaging cannot effectively reconstruct the non-sparse scene by the CS theory. Hence, a novel hybrid sparse SAR imaging method based on L1/2-norm is proposed. The method uses the approximate observation operator instead of the exact observation operator for SAR imaging. It performs the sparse representation of the spatial non-sparse scene with the discrete cosine transform and the curvelet transform. Then, the optimization problem based on the L1/2-norm is solved, so as to realize the reconstruction of the non-sparse scene in SAR imaging. The imaging experiments of simulated and actual scenes demonstrated that, the proposed method can achieve the effective reconstruction of non-sparse scenes under the condition of downsampling.

articleTitle: Robust waveform design for MIMO radar direction finding
abstract: This paper focuses on the design of transmit waveforms for a multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) radar with a uniform linear receive array. The purpose is to enhance the angle estimation performance of the multiple signal classification (MUSIC) algorithm. To improve the robustness of the designed waveforms in the presence of target amplitude uncertainties, we introduce an online stochastic framework to minimize the average asymptotic mean square error of the MUSIC algorithm. At each iteration of the online stochastic algorithm, we employ a minorization-maximization (MM) based technique to tackle the resultant nonconvex optimization problem. Numerical experiments are conducted to evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Optimized waveform design for distance sidelode suppression in NFMCW integrated radar and jamming systems
abstract: To realize the integration of radar and jammer in the waveform, we propose a noise FM continuous waveform (NFMCW). As a radar signal, it has a peg-type ambiguity function and excellent low interception probability and electron-opposition resistance, it hasn’t cyclic ranging ambiguity. As a jamming signal, it can continuously transmit electromagnetic signals for a long period of time to jam enemy radar, and it has a good suppression of jamming effect. In addition, against excessive NFMCW autocorrelation sidelobes, we adopt the optimization method of template matching, which reduces the autocorrelation sidelobe of the NFMCW while ensuring the jamming performance. Finally, the simulation results verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Spaceborne SAR image simulation based on multi-polarized SAR airborne data
abstract: SAR image simulation is a technology that simulates SAR image features or the working process of SAR systems on a computer platform to obtain simulated SAR images. It overcomes the high cost and long cycle of obtaining SAR images with different parameters in real SAR systems, and plays an important role in SAR system development and algorithm validation.This paper aims to solve the problems in existing technologies by providing a method for predicting multi-spaceborne polarimetric SAR images using airborne high-resolution SAR data. The correlation model between polarimetric distortion parameters, target polarimetric complex data information (including amplitude and phase), and the echoes of various polarimetric channels on board the satellite was reconstructed to generate and imaged the spaceborne SAR echoes. This simulation method was validated and evaluated through airborne and spaceborne SAR data. The results showed that the accuracy of typical scene similarity and polarimetric feature similarity estimation was better than 80%.

articleTitle: Suppression of mainlobe deceptive jammers with polarimetric FDA-MIMO
abstract: This paper aims to suppress mainlobe deceptive jammers, which are generated in the same transmit pulse with the true target after modulation, in a polarimetric frequency diversity array (PFDA)-multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) radar. At the modelling stage, a collocated PFDA-MIMO is considered with multiples pairs of crossed dipoles in a uniform linear array configuration for both transmission and reception. Specifically, due to the difference between polarization information matrices corresponding to the true target and mainlobe jammers, they are discriminated by performing the eigenvalue decomposition on the covariance matrix, where the rotation invariance of the eigenvectors is satisfied with the mainlobe jammers. Furthermore, a robust data-dependent beamforming is implemented to suppress mainlobe jammers based on jammer-plus-noise covariance matrix reconstruction. Numerical results as well as comparisons among different radar schemes are provided to verify the effectiveness of the devised method in suppression of mainlobe deceptive jammers.

articleTitle: A formal study of the Doppler tolerance of high freedom parameterized FM (HFPFM) code
abstract: The Doppler frequency shift caused by high -speed moving targets will severely damage the performance of pulse compression. For range profiling of high speed targets in a radar system, a novel Doppler tolerance optimization based on High Freedom Parameterized FM (HFPFM) Code is proposed which not only improves the signal-to-noise-rate(SNR) of match filter on high Doppler frequency, but also prevent the sidelobe level from increasing too much within a certain Doppler bandwidth. This method utilizes the method of alternating optimization of two parameters to obtain the low sidelobe level and adopts two metrics to measure and expand Doppler Tolerance. Therefore, it has a low sidelobe level and performs robustly in high Doppler shift. The performance of some typical methods is simulated and compared and the results proves the feasibility of the method proposed in this paper.

articleTitle: A spatial registration algorithm for networked radar based on grids merging
abstract: The spatial registration for networked radar is an important prerequisite to ensure the accurate implementation of fusion detection by associating the observations of the same target observed by different radar stations. Aiming at the problems of large registration errors and heavy computing burdens in current spatial registration algorithms, a method of grids merging for spatial registration is proposed in this paper. In this method, an optimization model concerning the trade-off between registration performance and computing burdens is established. The Fermat point is obtained as the mark point of grids to be merged, optimising the grid's size and the registration errors. The results of the proposed registration method can be intuitively shown in the forms of the off-line spatial registration information table, the registered position distribution map and the reconstructed overlapping regions of spatial sampling cells distribution map. The reliability of the proposed algorithm is also shown through some simulation results about registration under different conditions.

articleTitle: Convolutional neural network-based object classification for unmanned aerial vehicles using micro-Doppler features
abstract: In recent years, the number of Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) has increased dramatically, and the requirements for target-recognition radars have increased as well. In this paper, a UAV detection and classification method based on a convolutional neural network is designed by processing the radar echo signals and studying the micro-Doppler characteristics of UAVs. This study simulates and processes the echo signals of five UAVs to construct a larger dataset. Their micro-Doppler features are extracted by convolutional neural network and trained under different signal-to-noise ratio(SNR) conditions. After the training, the model is tested with the labeled datasets. The classification results of the five UAVs under the condition (signal-to-noise ratio of 20) have a score of more than 98%.

articleTitle: Simultaneous extraction-of-reference and direction-finding for coherent signals
abstract: In the process of radar detection, if the interference source signal is consistent with the radar signal, it will cause very serious interference to the radar. Therefore, how to achieve direction finding of coherent interference sources is of great significance to improving radar detection performance. Aiming at the direction-finding problem of coherent signals, this paper proposes an integrated reference signal extraction and coherent direction-finding method, which uses the antenna array snapshot received by the direction-finding equipment to simultaneously extract the reference signal known to the incoming wave direction of the radar and the coherent direction of the search direction by using the antenna array fast shot signal received by the direction-finding equipment, to achieve the purpose of improving the direction-finding accuracy of the coherent signal.

articleTitle: Correction of ionospheric dispersion for spaceborne SAR based on dual-antenna scheme
abstract: The propagation of spaceborne synthetic aperture radar (SAR) signal is affected by the ionosphere, which will lead to the degradation of the imaging quality, especially in the conditions of low frequency and wide bandwidth. A method of correcting ionospheric dispersion for SAR images based on the dual-antenna scheme is proposed in this paper. The ionospheric phase distortion is calculated by the time delay difference between the subband interferograms, which are obtained through split-spectrum and interference processing. It can be used in both single- and full-polarimetric SAR system. The simulation results show that the proposed method can estimate TEC in different ionospheric environments, and the performance is free from the constraint of the scene’s homogeneity.

articleTitle: Spaceborne SAR imaging system with high-performance polynomial engines
abstract: In recent years, with the development of Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) technology, the required resolution and imaging bandwidth for spaceborne SAR have been continuously increasing, posing stringent requirements on real-time imaging systems.
