To address the issue of uneven computing power allocation in implementing the Chirp Scaling (CS) algorithm on an FPGA+DSP platform, a spaceborne SAR imaging system with high-performance polynomial engines was designed, which enables the mapping of the Taylor series-based Chirp Scaling algorithm onto a hardware platform. The system is implemented using Xilinx's XC7VX690T FPGA and TI's TMS320C6678 DSP. The high-performance polynomial engine is designed with a parallel pipeline structure, supporting computation of polynomial up to seventh order. It offers flexible configuration and high versatility. The spaceborne SAR imaging system with high-performance polynomial engines can achieve SAR imaging in 16K×16K resolution with a time of 15.64 seconds, meeting the requirements of real-time SAR imaging applications in large-scale data scenarios.

articleTitle: FastICA based single-channel radar signal separation algorithm
abstract: Aiming at the traditional blind source separation for the received single-channel mixed radar signal makes it difficult to accurately recover the source signal, a single-channel radar signal comprehensive separation method based on the combination of the FastICA algorithm and the variational modal decomposition (VMD) algorithm is proposed. The method utilizes VMD to first perform modal separation of single-channel mixed Linear Frequency Modulation (LFM) signal, then selects the modal component signal with the largest correlation coefficient with the mixed signal and expands it with single-channel mixed LFM signal into a virtual multi-channel mixed signal, and finally inputs it into FastICA algorithm to obtain the source signal. The simulation experiment results show that the comprehensive separation algorithm can accurately separate the LFM signal, overcoming the limitation that the FastICA algorithm cannot directly separate the single-channel mixed radar signal.

articleTitle: A deep similarity-based network with compound regularization for unsupervised PolSAR image classification
abstract: Polarimetric SAR (PolSAR) image classification is a critical application of remote sensing image interpretation. Most of the early algorithms have a general classification performance, which use hand-crafted features to divide the image into various scattering categories. The Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) show superior performance in image proc essing with powerful nonlinear representation capabilities. However, they require a large amount of labeled training data, which limits the practical use of CNNs in PolSAR image classification scene where labeled data is rare and expensive. To address the previous issue, this paper proposes a deep similarity-based unsupervised classification network with compound regularization. The classification network combines a pre-trained feature extraction pipeline with convolutional autoencoder (CAE) and an unsupervised classification pipeline with deep feature similarity measurement. The regularization combines two ingredients to preserve both the sharpness of edges and the semantic continuity of the image contents. The first is the differential constraint based on pixel-level features, and the second is the graph model constraint based on superpixel-level features. Experiments prove the effectiveness of the proposed method on both spaceborne (RadarSat2) and airborne (E-SAR) PolSAR images. The visual results and quantitative scores show that our method outperforms the previous unsupervised classification methods with a large margin.

articleTitle: Sparse aperture ISAR imaging method based on DA-ISTA network
abstract: The use of sparse aperture echoes to reconstruct high-resolution Inverse Synthetic Aperture Radar (ISAR) images plays an important role in fields such as radar target recognition, space surveillance and ballistic missile defense. Aiming at the problem that traditional sparse aperture ISAR imaging algorithms are sensitive to parameters and slow in convergence, in this paper, inspired by the adaptive parameter learning and rapidly reconstruction of convolution neural network (CNN), a sparse recovery method for ISAR imaging, called deep augmented-iterative shrinkage thresholding algorithm (DA-ISTA) network. Firstly, high frequency components are considered in signal modeling, which increases the robustness of DA-ISTA. Specifically, DA-ISTA replaces the linear sparse transform with non-linear convolution operations. The iterative steps of ISTA are constructed as the hidden layer of the network, and DA-ISTA is capable of learning optimal parameters throughout the CNN training process, instead of being manually defined. Simulation experiments show that compared with traditional model-driven algorithms, the network avoids manual parameter adjustment process, has faster convergence speed, higher imaging quality, and has better generalization ability for data with large feature differences.

articleTitle: Nodes selection for area surveillance in noncoherent radar network based on numerical optimization
abstract: Compared to single-static radar, multi-static radar systems (MRS) can achieve better detection performance like larger surveillance area, more accurate object tracking, and higher detection probability, etc. For pursuing the above mentioned superiority, effective cooperation is needed for multiple radar nodes. However, there are too many parameters that can affect the detection performance, like transmitter and receiver node number, node locations, working mode, etc. Moreover, the detection gain estimation of noncoherent MRS is also more complicated than coherent radar systems. In order to select proper nodes for constructing netted radar system with better detection performance under resource constraints, we proposed an effective node selection method based on numerical optimization. The simulation results proved the effectiveness of the proposed method on node combination selection and working mode management.

articleTitle: Adaptive time-space-varying clutter suppression algorithm for handheld IR-UWB radar
abstract: The suppression of clutter, particularly in the time-space varying environments, is an obstacle that must be addressed by radar systems used in fire rescue to aid firefighters in locating and rescuing trapped individuals. However, traditional background clutter suppression methods are not well-suited to handle such situations due to their limitations in instantaneously responding to environmental changes with fixed parameter clutter suppression algorithms and pseudo-adaptive clutter suppression algorithms (algorithms requiring parameter tuning). This paper proposes a novel adaptive clutter suppression algorithm based on borrowing the SIGMOD activation function concept from neural networks, designed for fully adaptive clutter suppression in the time-space varying clutter background. Through experimental data processing analysis of six scenarios using handheld radar. The results demonstrate that compared to traditional clutter suppression methods, the proposed algorithm exhibits superior performance in target continuity, multi-target coexistence, and abrupt scene transitions under various scenarios such as handheld radar movement, handheld radar standing, and radar placement on a fixed platform.

articleTitle: Direct positioning algorithm based on frequency diverse MIMO radar
abstract: The combination of multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) radar and direct position determination techniques is a highly popular field in target positioning. However, existing direct localization methods based on MIMO radar rarely address the specific optimization of waveforms. In this paper, we propose a direct localization method based on orthogonal frequency division signals. By optimizing the steering vector according to the different wavelengths of each transmitted signal waveform, we further enhance the accuracy of target localization.

articleTitle: Holographic radar tracking algorithm for "low-slow-small" maneuvering targets
abstract: The proliferation of unauthorized flights and incidents involving "low-slow-small" maneuvering targets presents an increasing threat to national security and the normal progression of the national economy. Effectively addressing the threat has emerged as a vital task in upholding the security of the nation, society, and economy. This paper focuses on the attributes of “low-slow- small” targets and leverages the characteristics of holographic radar echoes to propose a Doppler-based Interaction Multiple Model Multiple Hypothesis Tracking (DIMM-TOMHT) algorithm. This algorithm yields the following advantages: 1) The tracking gate constructed by a single prediction step of the DIMM-TOMHT algorithm encompasses dimensions of Doppler velocity components. Owing to distinct disparities in position and velocity between targets and clutter, the multi-dimensional tracking gate containing Doppler components eliminates numerous irrelevant measurements, thereby reducing computational burden of the tracking algorithm while enhancing the accuracy of correlation and precision of target tracking. 2) To attain optimal global hypothesis trajectories, the DIMM-TOMHT algorithm computes scores for each hypothetical trajectory iteratively, which is employed for confirming transient trajectories and eliminating old tr ajectories. The algorithm inherently integrates aspects of trajectory management, thereby mitigating the complexity of multi-object tracking systems. Empirical data validate the efficacy of this algorithm in tracking "low-slow-small" targets.

articleTitle: Analysis of formation UAV targets' angular glint characteristics using phase gradient method
abstract: Detection of group targets is of great significance to social and national security. Due to the large individual number, obvious fluctuations, and dense distribution of group targets, angular glint phenomena may occur during radar detection of group targets. Angular glint is an inherent error generated by the superposition of individual echoes of group targets, which is an important factor affecting the tracking accuracy of group targets. This paper analyzes the mechanism of angular glint of group targets, calculates the angular glint of a typical UAV group targets using the phase gradient method. The amplitude-phase fluctuation characteristics of an individual UAV target is modelled. The statistical characteristics of UAV angular glint is analysed using the Q-Q plot. The simulation results show that the phase gradient method is capable of analyzing the angular glint characteristics of group targets.

articleTitle: Deformable convolution and global attention improve small ship target detection in SAR images
abstract: The rapid development of Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) imaging technology has provided a wealth of high-resolution SAR images for remote sensing information systems. Marine ship target detection is an important part of SAR image processing. In order to improve the detection accuracy of small target ships, this paper proposes an algorithm based on deformable convolution networks (DCN) and global attention mechanism (GAM). In order to solve the problem of low resolution and easy overlap of small target annotation frames, the DCN is used to improve the receptive field of detection points. At the same time, the GAM is added to the down-sampling stage, and a sampling module MP-GAM that captures global features is constructed to perform feature fusion in the channel dimension and spatial dimension to improve the ability to capture complex backgrounds. An ablation comparison experiment was conducted on the SSDD data set. Compared with the before improvement, the improved model's mAP@0.5 index increased by 5.7% and mAP@0.5:0.95 index increased by 8.7%, significantly improved the detection precision of small target ships.

articleTitle: SMSP jamming detection method for airborne radar in clutter environment
abstract: This paper solves the problem of smeared spectrum (SMSP) jamming detection for airborne radar under clutter conditions. A novel method based on mismatched filtering and sub-coherent processing interval (sub-CPI) space-time adaptive processing (STAP) is proposed. Firstly, the mismatched filter is designed to make it quadrature to the clutter and target signals in the time domain. Then, the sub-CPI STAP is given to reduce the clutter/noise energy and to improve the jamming-clutter-ratio (JCR) Finally, the constant false alarm rate (CFAR) detection for jamming is achieved in the range-Doppler domain. Simulation results about SMSP jamming detection of airborne radar are provided to confirm the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: ESA-Net: A network for enhancing small target detection performance in SAR imagery aircraft
abstract: In synthetic aperture radar (SAR) image aircraft target detection, aircraft small targets have a lower AP than aircraft targets and large targets due to the small number of pixel points they occupy and background clutter interference. To solve this problem, this paper proposes a network for enhancing the performance of aircraft small target detection for SAR images(ESA-Net). The network is designed based on yolov5s with a backbone network BH-CSPDarknet and a detection head TFA-Head.BH-CSPDarknet allocates more computational resources in the shallow layer of the network to process high-resolution feature maps, which effectively extracts richer feature information of aircraft small targets.TFA-Head provides appropriate feature preferences for classification and localisation tasks to provide TFA-Head provides appropriate feature information for classification and positioning task feature preferences, which can effectively suppress the background clutter interference while enhancing the aircraft small target features. The experimental results using the SAR-ADRD dataset show that the method improves the average accuracy of YOLOv5s by 1.9% and the average accuracy of aircraft small targets by 15.6%.

articleTitle: A CNN-based target component extraction method under jamming background
abstract: Intermittent Sampling Repeater Jamming (ISRJ), which leverages Digital Radio Frequency Memory (DRFM) to intercept and forward transmitted signals, poses a significant threat to modern radar due to its high flexibility and deceptive. Compared with the changing jamming characteristics, the target characteristics are more stable. Therefore, A Convolutional Neural Network (CNN)-based target component extraction method under jamming background is proposed. Firstly, the changeable characteristics of jamming and the stability characteristics of target are analysed by establishing the echo model. Then, the anti-jamming task is modelled by analogy with the speech signal separation task. Finally, the network structure and the loss function are designed to complete the task of extracting the target component in the mixed signal. Several experiments show the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Robust adaptive beamforming based on interference steering vector estimation and probability constrained under position errors
abstract: Adaptive beamforming plays a vital role in interference suppression. However, when sensor position errors are present, the output performance of adaptive beamformers degrades significantly, particularly if the desired signal component appears in the training data. To tackle this challenge, a robust adaptive beamforming method based on interference steering vector estimation and probability constrained is proposed. Firstly, the Capon spectrum is used to estimate the number of signal sources and the corresponding inaccurate directions of arrival (DOA). Then, the steering vector and the power of each interference are estimated based on the robust Capon beamforming principle, while the average value of the small eigenvalues of sampling covariance matrix (SCM) is used as the noise power estimation, which can be used to reconstruct the interference- plus-noise covariance matrix. Finally, the probability constrained method is utilized to maximize the power of the desired signal while suppressing interferences and noise, followed by the optimization of the weight vector. Numerical simulations illustrate that the proposed method can effectively improve the robustness of the beamformer against sensor position errors, and achieve higher output performance than the comparison methods.

articleTitle: A track association algorithm based on motion dynamics features in entomological radar
abstract: When tracking densely distributed targets such as insects, the traditional trajectory association algorithm exhibits poor correlation performance, leading to a decline in multi-target tracking efficiency. In this paper, based on the behavioral characteristics of insects gathering and co-orienting during aerial flight, a motion dynamic feature-assisted multi-target tracking method is proposed. Firstly, a three-dimensional biological distribution state matrix is constructed through spatial gridization. Then, a three-dimensional circular convolution is employed to estimate the target's motion dynamic feature, assisting in multi-target trajectory initialization. Finally, the improvement effect of the method on trajectory tracking accuracy is validated through simulations and migration insect data.

articleTitle: A ship imaging method with rotational motion based on empirical modal decomposition
abstract: Airborne synthetic aperture radar (SAR) provides high-resolution images of ships. Long synthetic aperture time ensures high resolution. The motion of the ship causes complex and small oscillatory changes in the range, which blurs the results of conventional imaging. To address this problem, this paper studies a ship imaging method with rotational motion based on Empirical Mode Decomposition (EMD). Firstly, the influence of ship's rotational motion on the range is analyzed. It can be approximated as the sum of multiple sinusoidal functions, and the signal model of the ship is given. And then the signal model is extended using the Bessel function and Euler formula. The imaginary part of its azimuth can be expressed as the sum of multiple sinusoidal functions. As a result, a ship imaging method based on EMD is proposed. (1) After migration correction, the signal is passed through the EMD to obtain some Intrinsic Mode Functions (IMFs). The frequencies of the sinusoidal functions are shown on the IMFs. (2) We match its other parameters by parameter search. After the influence of the sine is matched, the range-Doppler (R-D) map has a single focused image. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is verified by experimental simulation.

articleTitle: Micro-Doppler feature extraction through helicopter rotor modulation
abstract: The HERM lines can be used to classify and identify non-cooperative rotor-type targets. Compared to micro-Doppler generated by these targets, the sampling rate or pulse repetition frequency makes it difficult to meet the requirements of Nyquist sampling law. Therefore, the target echo appears aliasing and winding in the frequency domain or time-frequency domain, which makes it challenging to extract target features under low pulse repetition frequency. In order to extract the HERM line of the non-cooperative rotor-type targets, this paper not only studies the relationship between blade flash and HERM line but also studies the correspondence between HERM line and frequency, which is of great significance for the accurate extraction of the micro-motion parameters.

articleTitle: Asteroid shape reconstruction method based on convolutional neural network
abstract: Radar is the most powerful remote sensing tool for measuring the physical characteristics of near-Earth objects. In this paper, we propose an asteroid shape reconstruction method using convolutional neural networks, which can reconstruct the three-dimensional shape features of asteroids based on radar observation data. Compared to traditional methods, it has the advantages of automatic optimization and minimal manual intervention. Experimental results have been conducted to demonstrate the effectiveness of this method.

articleTitle: Target positioning with the MS-MU-MIMO-OFDM signal based on the unitary approximate message passing
abstract: In this paper we consider target sensing using the multistatic multiuser multiple input multiple output orthogonal frequency division multiplexing signal (MS-MU-MIMO-OFDM). The signals from different transmit nodes are at the same carrier frequency. This is a typical scenario for target sensing with the fifth generation (5G) communication network signals. Target position estimation in this circumstance can be casted into a block sparse vector reconstruction (BSVR) problem. Previous study uses the sparse Bayesian learning (SBL) for the BSVR. The traditional SBL involves repeated matrix inversion which takes huge computation time. In this paper we utilize the unitary approximate message passing based SBL (UMAP-SBL), which is a fast implementation of the SBL. Since the block sparsity nature of the representation vector in th is paper, we customize a block sparsity version of UMAP-SBL. Simulation demonstrates the effectives of the application of the UMAP- SBL to the target positioning considered in this paper.

articleTitle: RFI suppression method with improved eigen subspace decomposition for low-frequency radar
abstract: Due to the complex electromagnetic environment in the low-frequency band, both useful signals and other radio frequency (RF) signals enter the radar receiver indiscriminately, affecting the operation of the radar. Conventional radio frequency interference (RFI) suppression methods only have a good effect on narrowband interference (NBI). Faced with the complex RF environment, they cannot effectively suppress RFI, especially wideband interference (WBI) in the form of digital terrestrial multimedia broadcast (DTMB). To solve the problem of RFI suppression in the complex electromagnetic environment, an improved eigen subspace decomposition method is proposed in this paper. First, the echo signal matrix is implemented with eigendecomposition to obtain eigenvalues with different distribution characteristics, and the ratio of adjacent eigenvalues is used to detect whether there exists NBI in echo signal. Then, the NBI is modelled and estimated. According to the distribution characteristics of different eigenvalues after NBI suppression, those eigenvalues including WBI are determined by K-means clustering. Then, the interference subspace of WBI is accurately constructed, and the WBI can be suppressed. Through the processing of simulated and measured data, it can be proved that the proposed method can effectively suppress complex RFI.

articleTitle: Kullback-Leibler divergence based angle estimation in low SNR
abstract: Subspace-based and likelihood-based estimators are commonly used for direction of arrival (DOA) estimation. However, these methods exhibit performance degradation under low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), known as the threshold effect. We propose a generalized maximum likelihood estimation (MLE) approach, named KLD-based estimation, which considers MLE as the projection of the empirical distribution onto the Gaussian distribution using the Kullback-Leibler divergence (KLD). Additionally, a beam domain KLD (BDKLD) method is proposed to reduce computational complexity by exploiting beam domain echoes. We compare the KLD-based estimation with several popular methods in simulation, and the results demonstrate that the KLD-based estimation can reduce the threshold SNR of MLE method by more than 15dB under low SNR conditions. Under a -30dB SNR condition, the KLD-based estimation achieves approximately 10 times higher estimation accuracy compared to the MLE.

articleTitle: Three dimensional millimeter wave MIMO synthetic aperture radar imaging
abstract: A 3D millimeter wave synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imaging system is introduced, which is composed of AWR2243 cascade board multiple input multiple output (MIMO) radar of Texas Instruments (TI) company and mmWave cascade imaging radar digital signal processing evaluation module. The echo data can be obtained when the vertical disposition antenna array moves along a horizontal slide rail, thus a three dimensional (3D) imaging result can be derived using back projection (BP) algorithm. The elevation resolution is determined by the antenna aperture itself, as well as the azimuth resolution depends on the radar board sliding distance along the rail and the horizontal beam width. BP imaging algorithm is given combined the measurement geometrics. Real measurement imaging results are given to show the 3D imaging performance of the proposed imaging system.

articleTitle: Polarimetric holographic SAR 3-D imaging based on L2, 1-norm regularization: initial result
abstract: In order to accurately obtain the three-dimensional (3-D) scattering information of the interested target, the structural correlation between the collected echo of different polarimetric channels can be incorporated as priori knowledge into holographic synthetic aperture radar (HoloSAR) imaging. In this paper, we propose a novel “L2, 1-norm regularization, model selection and estimation reconstruction” method to construct the polarimetric HoloSAR imaging model, and achieve the 3-D imaging of the interested area by solving a mixed-norm regularization problem. Compared with traditional beamforming algorithm, the proposed method has the super-resolution imaging ability to recover the elevation position of scatterers. Compared with the single-channel compressive sensing (CS) method, it can suppress the interference from false targets, which makes the reconstruction of the backscattering coefficient more accurately. Experimental results based on Gotcha data validate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: An autonomous feature detection method for slow small targets on sea surface based on contextual bandit approach
abstract: This paper combines the contextual bandit approach with existing feature detection process, and then proposes an autonomous feature detection method of slow small targets on sea surface based on contextual bandit approach. The method is divided into the training stage and detection stage. In training stage, the method utilizes a large amount of sea clutter data collected in advance to generate the decision regions corresponding to existing feature detectors. In detection stage, every time the radar receives a frame of data, the method selects a feature detector in real time through the modified kernel-based upper confidence bound policy proposed in this paper. Finally, the decision region of real-time detector is used to detect the target in current frame. The superior performance of proposed method is verified by the measured sea clutter datasets.

articleTitle: Subsidence monitoring with polarimetric phase and multi-temporal InSAR techniques in Kunming Changshui International Airport
abstract: Recently developed multi-temporal InSAR techniques can be used to obtain the deformation of airports. However, due to the complex loading conditions and varying environments, make it hard to separate the dangerous signals and natural deformation. Aiming at this problem, we use polarized phase difference of the polarimetric channels and polarimetric decomposition to classification different features. Then, based on the physical properties of the features, we separate the natural deformation signals from the time series. In the case of Kunming Changshui International Airport, we identify a dihedral scatterer at the roof of terminal and separate its natural deformation using a thermal model. The results show the effectiveness.

articleTitle: Adaptive Doppler processing for folded clutter mitigation of inter-pulse phase-coded waveform
abstract: We provide a way to solve range ambiguity and mitigate clutter folding in airborne radar using inter-pulse phase coded waveform. We build the slow-time echo model for the considered waveform and explain why replica-correlation filtering does not work in heavy clutter. Further, we present the essential idea based on adaptive processing for folded clutter mitigation and derive the boundary condition associated. Finally, we derive a recursive approach to approximate the optimal filtering, which does not require loads of independent identically distributed samples. Simulation and experiment are conducted to validate the proposed method.

articleTitle: An efficient azimuth sampling design network for sparse SAR imaging
abstract: Conventional synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imaging methods based on the Nyquist sampling theorem encounters the dilemma of balancing imaging quality and resource consumption. In order to solve the problem, we propose a novel network to optimize the azimuth sampling pattern for sparse SAR imaging. We harness the impressive information extraction capabilities inherent in deep neural networks to efficiently segregate valuable information from clutter. This empowers us to extract more pertinent data while minimizing pulse utilization. Additionally, we have integrated the nonuniform fast Fourier transform (NUFFT) MF operator into the network-based SAR imaging framework, ensuring both efficiency and viability of the proposed approach. Experiments on real SAR scene data have been conducted, and both visual comparisons and numerical analysis demonstrate the efficiency and superiority of our method in the field of sparse SAR imaging.
